body.translated_text: <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>: <s>Buddhacarita</s> (Acts of the Buddha)
CANTO 1

children.text: aikṣvāka ikṣvākusamaprabhāvaḥśākyeṣvaśakyeṣu viśuddhavṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, equal in power to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, among the <s>Śākyas</s> who were unconquerable, of pure conduct —

children.text: priyaḥ śaraccandra iva prajānāṃ śuddhodano nāma babhūva rājā // Bc_1.1 //
children.translated_text: dear to his people like the autumn moon, there was a king named <s>Śuddhodana</s>. // 1.1 //

children.text: tasyendrakalpasya babhūva patnī dīptyā narendrasya samaprabhāvā /
children.translated_text: Of that king, equal to <s>Indra</s>, there was a wife, equal in splendor to the lord of men;

children.text: padmeva lakṣmīḥ pṛthivīva dhīrā māyeti nāmnānupameva māyā // Bc_1.2 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Padmā</s> (Lotus-goddess) to <s>Lakṣmī</s>, like the earth in steadfastness — <s>Māyā</s> by name, truly incomparable like <s>Māyā</s> (divine illusion). // 1.2 //

children.text: sārdha tayāsau vijahāra rājā nācintayadvaiśravaṇasya lakṣmīm /
children.translated_text: Together with her, that king took his pleasure, giving no thought to the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera);

children.text: tataśca vidheva samādhiyuktā garbha dadhe pāpavivarjitā sā // Bc_1.3 //
children.translated_text: and then, as if by divine ordinance, united in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration), she — free from sin — conceived a child. // 1.3 //

children.text: prāggarbhadhānnānmanujendrapatnī sitaṃ dadarśa dviparājamekam /
children.translated_text: Before conceiving, the queen of the lord of men beheld in a dream a single great white elephant-king

children.text: svapne viśantaṃ vapurātmanaḥ sā na tannimittaṃ samavāpa tāpam // Bc_1.4 //
children.translated_text: entering her body; she did not experience any distress on account of that. // 1.4 //

children.text: sā tasya devapratimasya devī garbheṇa vaṃśaśriyamudvahantī /
children.translated_text: She, the queen of that god-like [king], carrying in her womb the glory of the lineage —

children.text: śramaṃ na lebhe na śucaṃ na māyāṃ gantuṃ vanaṃ sā nibhṛtaṃ cakāṅkṣa // Bc_1.5 //
children.translated_text: felt no fatigue, no sorrow, no delusion; she longed to go to a secluded grove. // 1.5 //

children.text: sā lumbinī nāma vanāntabhūmiṃ citradrūmāṃ caitrarathābhirāmām /
children.translated_text: She desired a forest tract named <s>Lumbinī</s>, adorned with wondrous trees, beautiful as <s>Caitraratha</s> (Kubera's garden),

children.text: dhyānānukūlāṃ vijanāmiyeṣa tasyāṃ nivāsāya nṛpaṃ babhāṣe // Bc_1.6 //
children.translated_text: conducive to meditation, solitary — and for dwelling there, she spoke to the king. // 1.6 //

children.text: āryāśayāṃ tāṃ pravaṇāṃ ca dharme vijñāya kautūhalaharṣapūrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Recognizing her noble-hearted [nature] and her inclination toward <s>dharma</s>, filled with curiosity and delight,

children.text: śivāt purād bhūmipatirjagāma tatprītaye nāpi vihārahetoḥ // Bc_1.7 //
children.translated_text: the lord of the earth departed from the auspicious city — for her pleasure, not for the sake of recreation. // 1.7 //

children.text: tasminvane śrīmati rājapatnī prasūtikālaṃ samavekṣamāṇā /
children.translated_text: In that glorious grove, the royal wife, observing that the time of delivery had come,

children.text: śayyāṃ vitānopahitāṃ prapede nārīsahasrairabhinandyamānā // Bc_1.8 //
children.translated_text: took to a couch furnished with a canopy, attended with felicitations by thousands of women. // 1.8 //

children.text: tataḥ prasannaśca babhūva puṣyastasyāśca devyā vratasaṃskṛtāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation became auspicious, and from her — the queen consecrated by vows —

children.text: pārśvātsuto lokahitāya jajñe nirvedanaṃ caiva nirāmayaṃ ca // Bc_1.9 //
children.translated_text: a son was born from her side, for the welfare of the world, without pain and without ailment. // 1.9 //

children.text: ūroryathaurvasya pṛthośca hastānmāndhāturindrapratimasya mūrdhnaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Aurva</s> [was born] from the thigh, <s>Pṛthu</s> from the hand, <s>Māndhātṛ</s> — equal to <s>Indra</s> — from the head,

children.text: kakṣīvataścaiva bhujāṃsadeśāttathāvidhaṃ tasya babhūva janma // Bc_1.10 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Kakṣīvat</s> from the region of the shoulder — of such a kind was his birth. // 1.10 //

children.text: krameṇa garbhādabhiniḥsṛtaḥ san babhau cyutaḥ khādiva yonyajātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having emerged step by step from the womb, he shone as if fallen from the sky, not born from the womb;

children.text: kalpeṣvanekeṣu ca bhāvitātmā yaḥ saṃprajānansuṣuve na mūḍhaḥ // Bc_1.11 //
children.translated_text: for he, whose self had been cultivated through many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), was born with full awareness, not in delusion. // 1.11 //

children.text: dīptyā ca dhairyeṇa ca yo rarāja bālo ravibhūmimivāvatīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, though a babe, shone with brilliance and steadfastness, like the sun descended upon the earth —

children.text: tathātidīpto 'pi nirīkṣyamāṇo jahāra cakṣūṃṣi yathā śaśāṅkaḥ // Bc_1.12 //
children.translated_text: though exceedingly radiant, when gazed upon, he captivated the eyes, like the moon. // 1.12 //

children.text: sa hi svagātraprabhayojjvalantyā dīpaprabhāṃ bhāskaravanmumoṣa /
children.translated_text: For by the radiance blazing from his own body, he stole the light of lamps, like the sun;

children.text: mahārhajāmbūnadacāruvarṇo vidyotayāmāsa diśaśca sarvāḥ // Bc_1.13 //
children.translated_text: of the splendid color of fine <s>jāmbūnada</s> (river-gold), he illuminated all the quarters. // 1.13 //

children.text: anākulānyubjasamudgatāni niṣpeṣavadvyāyatavikramāṇi /
children.translated_text: Unhurried, firmly planted and raised high, with strides extended and impactful,

children.text: tathaiva dhīrāṇi padāni sapta saptarṣitārāsadṛśo jagāma // Bc_1.14 //
children.translated_text: thus with steady steps, seven [in number] — like the seven stars of the <s>Saptarṣi</s> (Great Bear) constellation — he walked. // 1.14 //

children.text: bodhāya jāto 'smi jagaddhitārthamantyā bhavotpattiriyaṃ mameti /
children.translated_text: 'I am born for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), for the welfare of the world; this is my last birth' —

children.text: caturdiśaṃ siṃhagatirvilokya vāṇī ca bhavyārthakarīmuvāca // Bc_1.15 //
children.translated_text: gazing in the four directions with a lion's gait, he uttered a speech that would bring about the meaning of what is to be. // 1.15 //

children.text: khātprasrūte candramarīciśubhre dve vāridhāre śiśiroṣṇavīrye /
children.translated_text: From the sky poured forth two streams of water, bright as moonbeams, of cool and warm potency,

children.text: śarīrasaṃsparśasukhāntarāya nipetaturmūrdhani tasya saumye // Bc_1.16 //
children.translated_text: for the pleasant bodily contact — they fell upon his gentle head. // 1.16 //

children.text: śrīmadvitāne kanakojjvalāṅge vaiḍūryapāde śayane śayānam /
children.translated_text: Upon a glorious canopied [couch], with limbs blazing like gold, with legs of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) — as he lay upon that bed,

children.text: yadgauravātkāñcanapadmahastā yakṣādhipāḥ saṃparivārya tasthuḥ // Bc_1.17 //
children.translated_text: the lords of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, with golden lotuses in hand, out of reverence, stood surrounding him. // 1.17 //

children.text: adṛśyabhāvāśca divaukasaḥ khe yasya prabhāvātpraṇataiḥ śīrobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: And the invisible celestial beings in the sky, with heads bowed by the force of his majesty,

children.text: ādhārayan pāṇḍaramātapatraṃ bodhāya jepuḥ paramāśiṣaśca // Bc_1.18 //
children.translated_text: held up a white parasol and uttered supreme blessings for his awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). // 1.18 //

children.text: mahoragā dharmaviśeṣatarṣād buddheṣvatīteṣu kṛtādhikārāḥ /
children.translated_text: The great serpents (<s>Mahoragas</s>), having rendered service to past <s>Buddhas</s> out of thirst for the distinction of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: yamavyajan bhaktiviśiṣṭanetrā mandārapuṣpaiḥ samavākiraṃśca // Bc_1.19 //
children.translated_text: fanned him with eyes distinguished by devotion and scattered <s>mandāra</s> flowers upon him. // 1.19 //

children.text: tathāgatotpādaguṇena tuṣṭāḥ śuddhādhivāsāśca viśuddhasattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Delighted by the merit of the birth of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the gods of pure abodes, of purified <s>sattva</s> (being),

children.text: devā nanandurvigate 'pi rāge magnasya duḥkhe jagato hitāya // Bc_1.20 //
children.translated_text: rejoiced — though free from passion — for the welfare of the world submerged in suffering. // 1.20 //

children.text: yasya prasūtau girirājakīlā vātāhatā nauriva bhūścacāla /
children.translated_text: At his birth, the earth — pinned by the king of mountains — trembled like a ship struck by wind,

children.text: sacandanā cotpalapadmagarbhā papāta vṛṣṭirgaganādanabhrāt // Bc_1.21 //
children.translated_text: and a rain, bearing sandalwood, produced from lotuses and water-lilies, fell from a cloudless sky. // 1.21 //

children.text: vātā vavuḥ sparśasukhā manojñā divyāni vāsāṃsyavapātayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Breezes blew, pleasant and delightful to the touch, wafting down divine garments;

children.text: sūryaḥ sa evābhyadhikaṃ cakāśe jajvāla saumyārciranīrito 'gniḥ // Bc_1.22 //
children.translated_text: the sun shone with even greater brilliance; fire blazed with gentle flames, unagitated. // 1.22 //

children.text: antaḥpurāṇyāgatavismayāni yasmin kriyāstīrtha iva pracakruḥ // Bc_1.23 //
children.translated_text: the women of the inner chambers, seized with wonder, performed rites at it as at a sacred <s>tīrtha</s> (pilgrimage site). // 1.23 //

body.translated_text: In the northeastern quarter of the dwelling-place, a well with clear water appeared of its own accord;

children.text: dharmārthibhirbhūtagaṇaiśca divyaistaddarśanārtha vanamāpupūre /
children.translated_text: The grove was filled with hosts of beings, both divine and those seeking <s>dharma</s>, [all] for the purpose of seeing him,

children.text: kautūhalenaiva ca pādapebhyaḥ puṣpāṇyakāle 'pyavapātayadbhiḥ // Bc_1.24 //
children.translated_text: and, out of sheer curiosity, even the trees shed flowers though it was not the season. // 1.24 //

children.text: bhūtairasaumyaiḥ parityaktahiṃsairnākāri pīḍā svagaṇe pare vā /
children.translated_text: By malevolent beings who had abandoned violence, no harm was done — neither to their own kind nor to others;

children.text: loke hi sarvāśca vinā prayāsaṃ rujo narāṇāṃ śamayāṃbabhūvuḥ // Bc_1.25 //
children.translated_text: and in the world, all the diseases of men were allayed without effort. // 1.25 //

children.text: kalaṃ praṇeduḥ mṛgapakṣiṇaśca śāntāmbuvāhāḥ sarito babhūvuḥ /
children.translated_text: The beasts and birds cried melodiously; the rivers flowed with tranquil waters;

children.text: diśaḥ prasedurvimale nirabhre vihāyase dundubhayo nineduḥ // Bc_1.26 //
children.translated_text: the quarters became clear; in the spotless, cloudless sky, celestial drums resounded. // 1.26 //

children.text: lokasya mokṣāya gurau prasūte śamaṃ prapede jagadavyavastham /
children.translated_text: When the guru was born for the liberation of the world, the disordered world found peace;

children.text: prāpyeva nāthaṃ khalu nītimantam eko na māro mudamāpa loke // Bc_1.27 //
children.translated_text: as if having obtained indeed a righteous lord — <s>Māra</s> alone in the world did not find joy. // 1.27 //

children.text: divyādbhutaṃ janma nirīkṣya tasya dhīro 'pi rājā bahukṣobhametaḥ /
children.translated_text: Observing his divine and wondrous birth, even the steadfast king was greatly agitated;

children.text: snehādasau bhītipramodajanye dve vāridhāre mumuce narendraḥ // Bc_1.28 //
children.translated_text: out of affection, that lord of men shed two streams of tears, born of fear and delight. // 1.28 //

children.text: amānuṣī tasya niśamya śaktiṃ mātā prakṛtyā karuṇārdracittā /
children.translated_text: Hearing of his superhuman power, the queen, by nature tender-hearted with compassion,

children.text: prītā ca bhītā ca babhūva devī śītoṣṇamiśreva jalasya dhārā // Bc_1.29 //
children.translated_text: became both gladdened and frightened — like a stream of water mixed with cold and warm. // 1.29 //

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇā bhayahetumeva dhyātuṃ na śekuḥ vanitāḥ pravṛddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gazing at what was indeed a cause for fear, the elder women could not bring themselves to reflect upon it;

children.text: pūtāśca tā maṅgalakarma cakruḥ śivaṃ yayācuḥ śiśave suraughān // Bc_1.30 //
children.translated_text: and they, purified, performed auspicious rites and invoked hosts of gods for the welfare of the child. // 1.30 //

body.text:
viprāśca khyātāḥ śrutaśīlavāgbhiḥ śrutvā nimittāni vicārya samyak /
mukhaiḥ praphullaiścakitaiśca dīptaiḥ / bhītaprasannaṃ nṛpametya procuḥ // Bc_1.31 //
body.translated_text: And the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, renowned for their learning, virtue, and speech, having heard and duly considered the omens, with faces beaming, astonished, and radiant, approached the king — both awed and reassured — and said: // 1.31 //

body.text:
śamepsavo ye bhuvi santi sattvāḥ / putraṃ vinecchanti guṇaṃ na kañcit /
tvatputra eṣo 'sti kulapradīpaḥ / nṛtyotsavaṃ tvadya vidhehi rājan // Bc_1.32 //
body.translated_text: 'Those beings on earth who desire peace wish for no quality other than a son; this son of yours is a lamp of the lineage — perform a celebration of dance today, O king! // 1.32 //

children.text: vihāya cintāṃ bhava śāntacitto modasva vaṃśastava vṛddhibhāgī /
children.translated_text: Abandon worry, be calm of mind, and rejoice — your lineage is a partaker of increase;

children.text: lokasya netā tava putrabhūtaḥ duḥkhārditānāṃ bhuvi eṣa trātā // Bc_1.33 //
children.translated_text: the leader of the world has become your son; he is the savior of those afflicted by suffering on earth.' // 1.33 //

children.text: dīpaprabho 'yaṃ kanakojjvalāṅgaḥ sulakṣaṇairyaistu samanvito 'sti /
children.translated_text: 'This one, radiant as a lamp, with limbs blazing like gold, endowed with auspicious marks —

children.text: nidhirguṇānāṃ samaye sa gatāṃ buddharṣibhāvaṃ paramāṃ śriyaṃ vā // Bc_1.34 //
children.translated_text: a treasury of virtues, in due time he will attain the supreme state of a <s>Buddha</s>-sage, or [else] supreme royal glory.' // 1.34 //

children.text: icchedasau vai pṛthivīśriyaṃ cet nyāyena jitvā pṛthivī samagrām /
children.translated_text: 'Should he desire the glory of sovereignty over the earth, having conquered the entire earth by righteousness,

children.text: bhūpeṣu rājeta yathā prakāśaḥ graheṣu sarveṣu ravervibhāti // Bc_1.35 //
children.translated_text: he would shine among kings as the light of the sun shines among all the planets.' // 1.35 //

body.text: mokṣāya cedvā vanameva gacchet / tattvena samyak sa vijitya sarvān /

children.text: matān pṛthivyāṃ bahumānametaḥ rājeta śaileṣu yathā sumeruḥ // Bc_1.36 //
children.translated_text: doctrines on earth — from this [would arise] great honor; he would stand supreme among [mountains] like <s>Sumeru</s> among peaks.' // 1.36 //

body.translated_text: 'Or if he goes to the forest for the sake of liberation, having truly conquered all

children.text: yathā hiraṇyaṃ śuci dhātumadhye merurgirīṇāṃ sarasāṃ samudraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As gold is pure among minerals, <s>Meru</s> among mountains, the ocean among lakes,

children.text: tārāsu candrastapatāṃ ca sūryaḥ putrastathā te dvipadeṣu varyaḥ // Bc_1.37 //
children.translated_text: the moon among stars, the sun among luminaries — so is your son the best among bipeds.' // 1.37 //

children.text: tasyākṣiṇī nirnimiṣe viśāle snigdhe ca dīpte vimale tathaiva /
children.translated_text: 'His eyes — wide, unblinking, tender yet radiant, spotless,

children.text: niṣkampakṛṣṇāyataśuddhapakṣme draṣṭuṃ samarthe khalu sarvabhāvān // Bc_1.38 //
children.translated_text: with steady, dark, long, and pure lashes — are indeed capable of seeing all things.' // 1.38 //

children.text: kasmānnu hetoḥ kathitānbhavadbhiḥ varānguṇān dhārayate kumāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For what reason does the prince bear the excellent qualities described by you?' —

children.text: prāpurna pūrve munayo nṛpāśca rājñeti pṛṣṭā jagadus dvijāstam // Bc_1.39 //
children.translated_text: asked the king; and the twice-born (<s>brāhmaṇas</s>), thus questioned, replied: 'Neither former sages nor kings attained [these].' // 1.39 //

children.text: khyātāni karmāṇi yaśo matiśca pūrva na bhūtāni bhavanti paścāt /
children.translated_text: 'Renowned deeds, fame, and wisdom — those not found in earlier [times] arise later;

children.text: guṇā hi sarvāḥ prabhavanti hetoḥ nidarśanānyatra ca no nibodha // Bc_1.40 //
children.translated_text: for all qualities arise from a cause — and here are the illustrations; attend to them: // 1.40 //

children.text: yadrājaśāstraṃ bhṛguraṅgirā vā na cakraturvaśakarāvṛṣī tau /
children.translated_text: 'The science of statecraft that neither <s>Bhṛgu</s> nor <s>Aṅgiras</s> composed — those two <s>ṛṣis</s> who could subdue —

children.text: tayoḥ sutau saumya sasarjatustatkālena śukraśca bṛhaspatiśca // Bc_1.41 //
children.translated_text: their sons, O gentle one, produced it in time: <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. // 1.41 //

children.text: sārasvataścāpi jagāda naṣṭaṃ vedaṃ punaryaṃ dadṛśurna pūrve /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sārasvata</s> too uttered again the lost <s>Veda</s> that earlier [sages] had not seen;

children.text: vyāsastathainaṃ bahudhā cakāra na yaṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ kṛtavānaśaktiḥ // Bc_1.42 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Vyāsa</s> divided it into many [parts] — which <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, though powerful, had not done. // 1.42 //

children.text: vālmīkirādau ca sasarja padyaṃ jagrantha yanna cyavano maharṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Vālmīki</s> first composed verse, which the great sage <s>Cyavana</s> did not compose;

children.text: cikitsitaṃ yacca cakāra nātriḥ paścāttadātreya ṛṣirjagāda // Bc_1.43 //
children.translated_text: and the medical science that <s>Atri</s> did not establish — the sage <s>Ātreya</s> later proclaimed. // 1.43 //

children.text: yacca dvijatvaṃ kuśiko na lebhe tadgādhinaḥ sunūravāpa rājan /
children.translated_text: 'And the status of being a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> that <s>Kuśika</s> did not obtain, the son of <s>Gādhi</s> attained, O king;

children.text: velāṃ samudre sagaraśca dadhre nekṣvākavo yāṃ prathamaṃ babandhuḥ // Bc_1.44 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Sagara</s> set a boundary to the ocean that the <s>Ikṣvākus</s> had not first established. // 1.44 //

children.text: ācāryakaṃ yogavidhau dvijānāmaprāptamanyairjanako jagāma /
children.translated_text: 'The mastership in the discipline of <s>yoga</s> among the twice-born, unattained by others — <s>Janaka</s> achieved;

children.text: khyātāni karmāṇi ca yāni śaureḥ śūrādayasteṣvabalā babhūvuḥ // Bc_1.45 //
children.translated_text: and the renowned deeds that belong to [the lineage of] <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — <s>Śūra</s> and others were incapable of them. // 1.45 //

children.text: tasmātpramāṇaṃ na vayo na vaṃśaḥ kaścitkvacicchraiṣṭhyamupaiti loke /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, neither age nor lineage is the standard — anyone, anywhere, attains supremacy in the world;

children.text: rājñāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca hi tāni tāni kṛtāni putrairakṛtāni pūrvaiḥ // Bc_1.46 //
children.translated_text: for those various deeds of kings and sages were accomplished by sons, not accomplished by forebears.' // 1.46 //

children.text: evaṃ nṛpaḥ pratyayitairdvijaistairāśvāsitaścāpyabhinanditaśca /
children.translated_text: Thus reassured and congratulated by those trustworthy twice-born,

children.text: śaṅkāmaniṣṭāṃ vijahau manastaḥ praharṣamevādhikamāruroha // Bc_1.47 //
children.translated_text: the king banished his unwelcome anxiety from his mind and ascended to even greater joy. // 1.47 //

children.text: prītaśca tebhyo dvijasattamebhyaḥ satkārapūrva pradadau dhanāni /
children.translated_text: And pleased, he gave wealth to those best of twice-born, preceded by due honor,

children.text: bhūyādayaṃ bhūmipatiryathokto yāyājjarāmetya vanāni ceti // Bc_1.48 //
children.translated_text: [praying:] 'May this one become a lord of the earth as foretold, and may he go to the forests only upon reaching old age.' // 1.48 //

children.text: atho nimittaiśca tapobalācca tajjanma janmāntakarasya buddhvā /
children.translated_text: Then, by omens and by the power of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), having learned of that birth of the one who would end [future] births,

children.text: śākyeśvarasyālayamājagāma saddharmatarṣādasito maharṣiḥ // Bc_1.49 //
children.translated_text: the great sage <s>Asita</s>, out of thirst for the true <s>dharma</s>, came to the abode of the lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>. // 1.49 //

children.text: taṃ brahmavidbrahmavidaṃ jvalantaṃ brāhmyā śriyā caiva tapaḥśriyā ca /
children.translated_text: Him — the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, radiant among the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, with both the glory of <s>Brahman</s> and the glory of <s>tapas</s> —

children.text: rājño gururgauravasatkriyābhyāṃ praveśāyāmāsa narendrasadma // Bc_1.50 //
children.translated_text: the king's preceptor, with due honor and veneration, ushered into the royal palace. // 1.50 //

children.text: sa pārthivāntaḥpurasaṃnikarṣa kumārajanmāgataharṣavegaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, upon approaching the inner quarters of the king, seized by a rush of joy at the birth of the prince,

children.text: viveśa dhīro vanasaṃjñayeva tapaḥprakarṣācca jarāśrayācca // Bc_1.51 //
children.translated_text: entered with composure, as if into a forest — by the eminence of his <s>tapas</s> and by his advanced age. // 1.51 //

children.text: tato nṛpastaṃ munimāsanasthaṃ pādyārdhyapūrvaṃ pratipūjya samyak /
children.translated_text: Then the king, properly honoring the sage who was seated, with the offering of water for feet and the <s>arghya</s> (respectful oblation),

children.text: nimantrayāmāsa yathopacāraṃ purā vasiṣṭhaṃ sa ivāntidevaḥ // Bc_1.52 //
children.translated_text: invited him with due hospitality — as <s>Antideva</s> once [honored] <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. // 1.52 //

children.text: ājñāpyatāṃ kiṃ karavāṇi saumya śiṣyo 'smi viśrambhitumarhasīti // Bc_1.53 //
children.translated_text: let it be commanded — what shall I do, O gentle one? I am your disciple; please trust [me].' // 1.53 //

body.translated_text: 'I am blessed; this lineage of mine is worthy of favor, since the Blessed One has come desiring to see me;

children.text: evaṃ nṛpeṇopanimantritaḥ sansarveṇa bhāvena muniryathāvat /
children.translated_text: Thus invited by the king with complete sincerity, the sage, fittingly,

children.text: sa vismayotphullaviśāladṛṣṭirgambhīradhīrāṇi vacāṃsyuvāca // Bc_1.54 //
children.translated_text: with eyes wide open in wonder, uttered words deep and solemn: // 1.54 //

children.text: mahātmani tvayyupapannametatpriyātithau tyāgini dharmakāme /
children.translated_text: 'This befits you, great soul — a cherished host, generous, devoted to <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: sattvānvayajñānavayo 'nurūpā snigdhā yadevaṃ mayi me matiḥ syāt // Bc_1.55 //
children.translated_text: it is fitting that such a gracious regard toward me should exist [in you], in accord with your <s>sattva</s> (noble nature), lineage, learning, and age.' // 1.55 //

body.text: etacca tadyena nṛparṣayaste / dharmeṇa sūkṣmeṇa dhanānyavāpya /

children.text: nityaṃ tyajanto vidhivadbabhūvustapobhirāḍhyā vibhavairdaridrāḥ // Bc_1.56 //
children.translated_text: constantly giving it away in due manner, became rich in austerities yet poor in possessions.' // 1.56 //

body.translated_text: 'And this is precisely that [quality] by which your royal sages, having obtained wealth through subtle <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: prayojanaṃ yattu mamopayāne tanme śṛṇu prītimupehi ca tvam /
children.translated_text: 'But the purpose of my coming here — hear that, and may you be pleased:',

children.text: divyā mayādityapathe śrutā vāgbodhāya jātastanayastaveti // Bc_1.57 //
children.translated_text: 'A divine voice was heard by me on the path of the sun: "Your son is born for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)."' // 1.57 //

children.text: śrutvā vacastacca manaśca yuktvā jñātvā nimittaiśca tato 'smyupetaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having heard that utterance and applied my mind, having ascertained it by signs — thence have I come,

children.text: didṛkṣayā śākyakuladhvajasya śakradhvajasyeva samucchritasya // Bc_1.58 //
children.translated_text: desiring to see the banner of the <s>Śākya</s> lineage, raised aloft like the banner of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>).' // 1.58 //

children.text: ityetadevaṃ vacanaṃ niśamya praharṣasaṃbhrāntagatinarendraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech, the king, his gait hurried with the rush of joy —

children.text: ādāya dhātryaṅkagataṃ kumāraṃ saṃdarśayāmāsa tapodhanāya // Bc_1.59 //
children.translated_text: Taking the prince who was seated in the nurse's lap, she showed [him] to the one rich in austerities. // 1.59 //

children.text: cakrāṅkapādaṃ sa tato maharṣirjālāvanaddhāṅgulipāṇipādam /
children.translated_text: Then the great sage [beheld] the king's son — his feet marked with wheels, his fingers and toes joined by webs,

children.text: sorṇabhruvaṃ vāraṇavastikośaṃ savismayaṃ rājasutaṃ dadarśa // Bc_1.60 //
children.translated_text: with golden brow-hair and a sheath-concealed member like an elephant's — he gazed upon the prince with wonder. // 1.60 //

children.text: dhātryaṅkasaṃviṣṭamavekṣya cainaṃ devyaṅkasaṃviṣṭamivāgnisūnum /
children.translated_text: And seeing him seated in the nurse's lap, like the son of <s>Agni</s> (Fire) seated in the lap of a goddess,

children.text: babhūva pakṣmāntavicañcitāśrurniśvasya caiva tridivonmukho 'bhūt // Bc_1.61 //
children.translated_text: tears quivered at the edges of his eyelashes, and sighing deeply, he turned his face toward heaven. // 1.61 //

children.text: sagadgadaṃ bāṣpakaṣāyakaṇṭhaḥ papraccha sa prāñjalirānatāṅgaḥ // Bc_1.62 //
children.translated_text: and with choked voice, throat astringent with tears, asked him with folded hands and bowed body: // 1.62 //

body.translated_text: Seeing <s>Asita</s> with eyes flooded with tears, the king trembled with affection for his son,

children.text: alpāntaraṃ yasya vapuḥ surebhyo bavhadbhutaṃ yasya ca janma dīptam /
children.translated_text: 'He whose body differs but little from the gods, whose birth was brilliant and abundantly wondrous,

children.text: yasyottamaṃ bhāvinamāttha cārtha taṃ prekṣya kasmāttava dhīra bāṣpaḥ // Bc_1.63 //
children.translated_text: and of whom you have declared a supreme future destiny — seeing him, O steadfast one, why do you weep? // 1.63 //

children.text: api sthirāyurbhagavan kumāraḥ kaccinna śokāya mama prasūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is the prince long-lived, O blessed one? Surely he was not born for my grief?

children.text: labdhaḥ kathaṃcitsalilāñjalirme na khalvimaṃ pātumupaiti kālaḥ // Bc_1.64 //
children.translated_text: This handful of water barely obtained by me — surely time does not approach to drink it up? // 1.64 //

children.text: apyakṣayaṃ me yaśaso nidhānaṃ kacciddhruvo me kulahastasāraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is he truly an imperishable treasure of my glory? Is the wealth in the hand of my family secure?

children.text: api prayāsyāmi sukhaṃ paratra supto 'pi putre 'nimiṣaikacakṣuḥ // Bc_1.65 //
children.translated_text: Shall I depart happily to the next world, I who even while sleeping keep an unblinking eye on my son? // 1.65 //

children.text: kaccinna me jātamaphullameva kulapravālaṃ pariśoṣabhāgi /
children.translated_text: 'Surely this tender shoot of my family, just born, is not destined to wither without blossoming?

children.text: kṣipraṃ vibho brūhi na me 'sti śāntiḥ snehaṃ sute vetsi hi bāndhavānām // Bc_1.66 //
children.translated_text: Tell me quickly, O mighty one, for I have no peace — you know the affection of kinsmen for a son.' // 1.66 //

children.text: ityāgatāvegamaniṣṭabuddhyā buddhvā narendraṃ sa munirbabhāṣe /
children.translated_text: Thus perceiving the king overcome with agitation from the thought of something undesired, the sage spoke:

children.text: mā bhūnmatiste nṛpa kācidanyā niḥsaṃśayaṃ tadyadavocamasmi // Bc_1.67 //
children.translated_text: 'Let no other thought be yours, O king — what I have said is beyond doubt. // 1.67 //

children.text: nāsyānyathātvaṃ prati vikriyā me svāṃ vañcanāṃ tu prati viklavo 'smi /
children.translated_text: 'My perturbation is not regarding any change in his [destiny], but rather I am distressed regarding my own deprivation;

children.text: kālo hi me yātumayaṃ ca jāto jātikṣayasyāsulabhasya boddhā // Bc_1.68 //
children.translated_text: for the time has come for me to depart, and this one has been born who will be the knower of the rarely attainable cessation of birth. // 1.68 //

children.text: vihāya rājyaṃ viṣayeṣvanāsthastīvraiḥ prayatnairadhigamya tattvam /
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned kingship, indifferent to sense-pleasures, having realized the truth through intense efforts,

children.text: jagatyayaṃ mohatamo nihantuṃ jvaliṣyati jñānamayo hi sūryaḥ // Bc_1.69 //
children.translated_text: he will blaze forth like a sun made of knowledge, to destroy the darkness of delusion in the world. // 1.69 //

children.text: duḥkhārṇavādvyādhivikīrṇaphenājjarātaraṅgānmaraṇogravegāt /
children.translated_text: 'From the ocean of suffering, with foam scattered as disease, with waves of old age, with the terrible current of death,

children.text: uttārayiṣyatyayamuhyamānamārta jagajjñānamahāplavena // Bc_1.70 //
children.translated_text: he will rescue the bewildered and afflicted world by the great raft of knowledge. // 1.70 //

body.text:
prajñāmbuvegāṃ sthiraśīlavaprāṃ samādhiśītāṃ vratacakravākām /
asyottamāṃ dharmanadī pravṛtāṃ / tṛṣṇārditaḥ pāsyati jīvalokaḥ // Bc_1.71 //
body.translated_text: 'The world of living beings, tormented by thirst, will drink from this supreme river of <s>Dharma</s> set flowing by him — whose current is the force of wisdom, whose banks are firm morality, which is cooled by <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration), and which has <s>vratas</s> (religious vows) as its <s>cakravāka</s> birds. // 1.71 //

children.text: duḥkhārditebhyo viṣayāvṛtebhyaḥ saṃsārakāntārapathasthitebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For he will proclaim the path of liberation to those afflicted by suffering, enveloped by sense-pleasures, standing on the road through the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> —

children.text: ākhyāsyati hyeṣa vimokṣamārga mārgapranaṣṭebhya ivādhvagebhyaḥ // Bc_1.72 //
children.translated_text: as to travelers who have lost their way. // 1.72 //

children.text: vidahyamānāya janāya loke rāgāgnināyaṃ viṣayendhanena /
children.translated_text: 'To the world of beings burning with the fire of passion fueled by sense-objects,

children.text: pralhādamādhāsyati dharmavṛṣṭyā vṛṣṭyā mahāmegha ivātapānte // Bc_1.73 //
children.translated_text: he will bring relief through a rain of <s>Dharma</s>, like a great cloud at the end of the hot season. // 1.73 //

children.text: tṛṣṇārgalaṃ mohatamaḥkapāṭaṃ dvāraṃ prajānāmapayānahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The door for beings' departure [from <s>saṃsāra</s>], bolted by craving, with delusion's darkness as its panels —

children.text: vipāṭayiṣyatyayamuttamena saddharmatāḍena durāsadena // Bc_1.74 //
children.translated_text: he will burst open with the supreme, unapproachable striking of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // 1.74 //

children.text: svairmohapāśaiḥ pariveṣṭitasya duḥkhābhibhūtasya nirāśrayasya /
children.translated_text: 'For the world, enmeshed in the bonds of its own delusion, overcome by suffering, without refuge —

children.text: lokasya saṃbudhya ca dharmarājaḥ kariṣyate bandhanamokṣameṣaḥ // Bc_1.75 //
children.translated_text: having awakened and becoming the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Dharma), he will bring about release from bondage. // 1.75 //

children.text: tanmā kṛthāḥ śokamimaṃ prati tvamasminsa śocyo 'sti manuṣyaloke /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore do not grieve regarding him; rather, pitiable in this world of mortals

children.text: mohena vā kāmasukhairmadādvā yo naiṣṭhikaṃ śroṣyati nāsya dharmam // Bc_1.76 //
children.translated_text: is he who, through delusion, or through the pleasures of desire, or through intoxication, will not hear the ultimate <s>Dharma</s> of this one. // 1.76 //

children.text: bhraṣṭasya tasmācca guṇādato me dhyānāni labdhvāpyakṛtārthataiva /
children.translated_text: 'And for me, having fallen from that virtue, even though I have attained the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), there is only unfulfilled purpose;

children.text: dharmasya tasyāśravaṇādahaṃ hi manye vipattiṃ tridive 'pi vāsam // Bc_1.77 //
children.translated_text: for because of not hearing that <s>Dharma</s>, I consider even a stay in heaven to be misfortune.' // 1.77 //

children.text: iti śrutārthaḥ sasuhṛtsadārastyaktvā viṣādaṃ mumude narendraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard these words, the king, together with his friends and queen, abandoned sorrow and rejoiced,

children.text: evaṃvidho 'yaṃ tanayo mameti mene sa hi svāmapi sāravattām // Bc_1.78 //
children.translated_text: thinking, 'Such is this son of mine!' — for he considered even his own [worldly] existence to be of value. // 1.78 //

body.text:
ārṣeṇa mārgeṇa tu yāsyatīti cintāvidheyaṃ hṛdayaṃ cakāra /
na khalvasau na priyadharmapakṣaḥ / saṃtānanāśāttu bhayaṃ dadarśa // Bc_1.79 //
body.translated_text: But [the thought] 'he will go by the path of the sages' made his heart subject to anxiety; for he was not indeed averse to the side of <s>Dharma</s>, but he foresaw danger from the destruction of the lineage. // 1.79 //

children.text: atha munirasito nivedya tattvaṃ sutaniyataṃ sutaviklavāya rājñe /
children.translated_text: Then the sage <s>Asita</s>, having communicated the truth to the king who was distressed about his son,

children.text: sabahumatumudīkṣyamāṇarūpaḥ pavanapathena yathāgataṃ jagāma // Bc_1.80 //
children.translated_text: being gazed upon with great respect, departed by the path of the wind just as he had come. // 1.80 //

children.text: kṛtamitiranujāsutaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā munivacanaśravaṇe ca tanmatau ca /
children.translated_text: Considering his purpose accomplished, and having seen his brother's son, and [having fulfilled] the hearing of the sage's words and the contemplation of their import,

children.text: bahuvidhamanukampayā sa sādhuḥ priyasutavadviniyojayāṃcakāra // Bc_1.81 //
children.translated_text: that virtuous one, with manifold compassion, had [the prince] cared for as if he were his own dear son. // 1.81 //

children.text: narapatirapi putrajanmatuṣṭo viṣayagatāni vimucya bandhanāni /
children.translated_text: The king too, delighted at the birth of his son, releasing the fetters imposed on those confined for offenses,

children.text: kulasadṛśamacīrakaradyathāvatpriyatanayastanayasya jātakarma // Bc_1.82 //
children.translated_text: performed for his son the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth-rite) as befitting the family, in due order, without delay. // 1.82 //

children.text: daśasu pariṇateṣvahaḥsu caiva prayatamanāḥ parayā mudā parītaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when ten days had elapsed, with a concentrated mind, surrounded by supreme joy,

children.text: akuruta japahomamaṅgalādyāḥ paramabhavāya sutasya devatejyāḥ // Bc_1.83 //
children.translated_text: he performed chanting, fire-oblation, auspicious rites, and other worship of the gods for the supreme well-being of his son. // 1.83 //

children.text: api ca śatasahasrapūrṇasaṃkhyāḥ sthirabalavattanayāḥ sahemaśṛṅgīḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, cows numbering a full hundred thousand, with sturdy and strong calves, with golden horns,

children.text: anupagatajarāḥ payasvinīrgāḥ svayamadadātsutavṛddhaye dvijebhyaḥ // Bc_1.84 //
children.translated_text: not yet touched by old age, rich in milk — he himself gave to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> for the flourishing of his son. // 1.84 //

children.text: bahuvidhaviṣayāstato yatātmā svahṛdayatoṣakarīḥ kriyā vidhāya /
children.translated_text: Then, being self-controlled, having performed various rites of many kinds that brought satisfaction to his heart,

children.text: guṇavati niyate śive muhūrte matimakaronmuditaḥ purapraveśe // Bc_1.85 //
children.translated_text: he joyfully set his mind on the entry into the city at an auspicious, blessed, and duly appointed moment. // 1.85 //

children.text: dviradaradamayīmatho mahārhā sitasitapuṣpabhṛtāṃ maṇipradīpām /
children.translated_text: Then a magnificent palanquin of great value, made of ivory, adorned with lamps of jewels,

children.text: abhajata śivikāṃ śivāya devī tanayavatī praṇipatya devatābhyaḥ // Bc_1.86 //
children.translated_text: bearing white and colored flowers — the queen, now a mother, mounted it for her welfare, having bowed to the deities. // 1.86 //

children.text: puramatha purataḥ praveśya patnīṃ sthavirajanānugatāmapatyanāthām /
children.translated_text: Then, having the queen enter the city first, attended by elderly women and protected by her offspring,

children.text: nṛpatirapi jagāma paurasaṃghairdivamamarairmaghavānivārcyamānaḥ // Bc_1.87 //
children.translated_text: the king too entered, honored by crowds of citizens, like <s>Maghavān</s> (<s>Indra</s>) [honored] by the gods in heaven. // 1.87 //

children.text: bhavanamatha vigāhya śākyarājo bhava iva ṣaṇmukhajanmanā pratītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, entering the palace, the <s>Śākya</s> king, overjoyed like <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) at the birth of <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> (six-faced <s>Kārttikeya</s>),

children.text: idamidamiti harṣapūrṇavaktro bahuvidhapuṣṭiyaśaskaraṃ vyadhatta // Bc_1.88 //
children.translated_text: with face full of joy [exclaiming] 'this! this!', performed various rites for prosperity and glory. // 1.88 //

children.text: iti narapatiputrajanmavṛddhyā sajanapadaṃ kapilāvhayaṃ puraṃ tat /
children.translated_text: Thus, through the birth and growth of the king's son, that city called <s>Kapilā</s> (<s>Kapilavastu</s>) together with its countryside

children.text: dhanadapuramivāpsaro 'vakīrṇa muditamabhūnnalakūbaraprasūtau // Bc_1.89 //
children.translated_text: became as joyful as the city of <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) strewn with <s>Apsarases</s> at the birth of <s>Nalakūbara</s>. // 1.89 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye bhagavatprasūtirnāma prathamaḥ sargaḥ // 1 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first canto named 'The Birth of the Blessed One' in the <s>Buddhacarita</s> <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem). // 1 //
CANTO II

children.text: ā janmano janmajarāntakasya tasyātmajasyātmajitaḥ sa rājā /
children.translated_text: From the birth of his son — who was the conqueror of birth, old age, and death — that king, who had conquered himself,

children.text: ahanyahanyarthagajāśvamitrairvṛddhiṃ yayau sindhurivāmbuvegaiḥ // Bc_2.1 //
children.translated_text: grew day by day in wealth, elephants, horses, and allies, like the ocean with currents of water. // 2.1 //

children.text: dhanasya ratnasya ca tasya tasya kṛtākṛtasyaiva ca kāñcanasya /
children.translated_text: Of wealth and jewels of every kind, both wrought and unwrought gold,

children.text: tadā hi naikānsa nidhīnavāpa manorathasyāpyatibhārabhūtān // Bc_2.2 //
children.translated_text: he found at that time many treasures, burdensome even for wishes. // 2.2 //

children.text: ye padmakalpairapi ca dvipendrairna maṇḍalaṃ śakyamihābhinetum /
children.translated_text: And those bull-elephants of the <s>Himālaya</s>, maddened with rut, whom even elephants equal to lotuses could not lead into the circle [of battle] here —

children.text: madotkaṭā haimavatā gajāste vināpi yatnādupatasthurenam // Bc_2.3 //
children.translated_text: they came to him of their own accord, without any effort. // 2.3 //

children.text: nānāṅkacinhairnavahemabhāṇḍairvibhūṣitairlambasaṭaistathānyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And with other horses too, marked with various brands, adorned with new golden trappings, with flowing manes,

children.text: saṃcukṣubhe cāsya puraṃ turaṅgairbalena maitryā ca dhanena cāptaiḥ // Bc_2.4 //
children.translated_text: obtained by strength, by friendship, and by wealth — his city was stirred. // 2.4 //

children.text: puṣṭāśca tuṣṭāśca tathāsya rājye sādhvyo 'rajaskā guṇavatpayaskāḥ /
children.translated_text: And in his kingdom, well-nourished, contented, virtuous, free from disease, of excellent milk,

children.text: udagravatsaiḥ sahitā babhūvurbavhyo bahukṣīraduhaśca gāvaḥ // Bc_2.5 //
children.translated_text: the cows were many, accompanied by tall-humped [bulls], yielding abundant milk. // 2.5 //

children.text: madhyasthatāṃ tasya ripurjagāma madhyasthabhāvaḥ prayayau suhṛttvam /
children.translated_text: His enemy assumed neutrality, the neutral one passed into friendship,

children.text: viśeṣato dārḍhyamiyāya mitraṃ dvāvasya pakṣāvaparastu nāsa // Bc_2.6 //
children.translated_text: and the friend in particular grew in firmness — thus there were only two parties for him; the third ceased to exist. // 2.6 //

children.text: tathāsya mandānilameghaśabdaḥ saudāminīkuṇḍalamaṇḍitābhraḥ /
children.translated_text: And for him, with gentle wind and cloud-thunder, with clouds adorned with lightning as earrings,

children.text: vināśmavarṣāśanipātadoṣaiḥ kāle ca deśe pravavarṣa devaḥ // Bc_2.7 //
children.translated_text: free from the faults of stone-rain and thunderbolt-fall, the sky rained at the proper time and place. // 2.7 //

children.text: ruroha sasyaṃ phalavadyathartu tadākṛtenāpi kṛṣiśrameṇa /
children.translated_text: Crops grew fruit-bearing, as if in season, even by labor of cultivation not intended for that [purpose];

children.text: tā eva cāsyauṣadhayo rasena sāreṇa caivābhyadhikā babhūvuḥ // Bc_2.8 //
children.translated_text: and those very herbs of his became superior in flavor and in essence. // 2.8 //

children.text: śarīrasaṃdehakare 'pi kāle saṃgrāmasaṃmarda iva pravṛte /
children.translated_text: Even at the time that endangers the body [i.e. childbirth], as if in the onset of a pitched battle,

children.text: svasthāḥ sukhaṃ caiva nirāmayaṃ ca prajajñire kālavaśena nāryaḥ // Bc_2.9 //
children.translated_text: women gave birth healthily, happily, and free from illness, by the power of that time. // 2.9 //

children.text: pṛthagvratibhyo vibhave 'pi garhye na prārthayanti sma narāḥ parebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Men did not seek wealth from others through [taking] separate vows, even when the wealth [to be gained] was blameless;

children.text: abhyarthitaḥ sūkṣmadhano 'pi cāryastadā na kaścidvimukho babhūva // Bc_2.10 //
children.translated_text: and even a nobleman solicited [for charity] whose wealth was modest — no one at that time turned away. // 2.10 //

children.text: nāgauravo bandhuṣu nāpyadātā naivāvrato nānṛtiko na hiṃsraḥ /
children.translated_text: There was no one disrespectful to kinsmen, nor a non-giver, nor one without vows, nor a liar, nor one who harmed —

children.text: āsīttadā kaścana tasya rājye rājño yayāteriva nāhuṣasya // Bc_2.11 //
children.translated_text: no one [of such character] existed at that time in his kingdom, as in that of king <s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>. // 2.11 //

children.text: udyānadevāyatanāśramāṇāṃ kūpaprapāpuṣkariṇīvanānām /
children.translated_text: Those devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, as if directly perceiving heaven,

children.text: cakruḥ kriyāstatra ca dharmakāmāḥ pratyakṣataḥ svargīmavopalabhya // Bc_2.12 //
children.translated_text: performed works for gardens, temples, hermitages, wells, drinking-places, pools, and groves. // 2.12 //

children.text: muktaśca durbhikṣabhayāmayebhyo hṛṣṭo janaḥ svarga ivābhireme /
children.translated_text: And the people, freed from famine, fear, and disease, rejoiced as if in heaven;

children.text: patnīṃ patirvā mahiṣī patiṃ vā parasparaṃ na vyabhiceratuśca // Bc_2.13 //
children.translated_text: and neither did a wife transgress against her husband, nor a chief queen against her lord. // 2.13 //

children.text: kaścitsiṣeve rataye na kāmaṃ kāmārthamarthaṃ na jugopa kaścit /
children.translated_text: No one pursued <s>kāma</s> (desire) for [mere] pleasure; no one guarded <s>artha</s> (wealth) for the sake of desire;

children.text: kaściddhanārthaṃ na cacāra dharma dharmāya kaścinna cakāra hiṃsām // Bc_2.14 //
children.translated_text: no one practiced <s>dharma</s> for the sake of wealth; no one committed <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) for the sake of dharma. // 2.14 //

children.text: steyādibhiścāpyaribhiśca naṣṭaṃ svasthaṃ svacakraṃ paracakramuktam /
children.translated_text: Free from theft and such, free from enemies, his own circle was secure, released from the circle of foes;

children.text: kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca babhūva tasya purānaraṇyasya yathaiva rāṣṭre // Bc_2.15 //
children.translated_text: prosperous and well-provisioned — his kingdom was as in the days of the ancient king <s>Manu</s>. // 2.15 //

children.text: tadā hi tajjanmani tasya rājño manorivādityasutasya rājye /
children.translated_text: For at that time, at the birth of that prince, in his kingdom,

children.text: cacāra harṣaḥ praṇanāśa pāpmā jajvāla dharmaḥ kaluṣaḥ śaśāma // Bc_2.16 //
children.translated_text: as in the reign of <s>Manu</s>, son of <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) — joy spread, sin vanished, <s>Dharma</s> blazed, and wickedness was pacified. // 2.16 //

children.text: evaṃvidhā rājakulasya saṃpatsarvārthasiddhiśca yato babhūva /
children.translated_text: Since such prosperity of the royal family and the accomplishment of all aims occurred,

children.text: tato nṛpastasya sutasya nāma sarvārthasiddhi 'yamiti pracakre // Bc_2.17 //
children.translated_text: the king gave his son the name '<s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>' (Accomplisher of All Aims). // 2.17 //

children.text: devī tu māyā vibudharṣikalpaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśālaṃ tanayaprabhāvam /
children.translated_text: But Queen <s>Māyā</s>, having seen the vast influence of her son, like that of a divine sage,

children.text: jātaṃ praharṣa na śaśāka soḍhuṃ tato nivāsāya divaṃ jagāma // Bc_2.18 //
children.translated_text: was unable to endure the surge of joy born [of it], and departed to heaven for her abode. // 2.18 //

children.text: tataḥ kumāraṃ suragarbhakalpaṃ snehena bhāvena ca nirviśeṣam /
children.translated_text: Then, his maternal aunt, equal in power to his mother,

children.text: mātṛṣvasā mātṛsamaprabhāvā saṃvardhayāmātmajavadbabhūva // Bc_2.19 //
children.translated_text: raised the prince, who was like a child of the gods, with affection and devotion without distinction, as if he were her own son. // 2.19 //

children.text: tataḥ sa bālārka ivodayasthaḥ samīrito vanhirivānilena /
children.translated_text: Then, like the young sun rising at the eastern mountain, or a fire fanned by wind,

children.text: krameṇa samyagvavṛdhe kumārastārādhipaḥ pakṣa ivātamaske // Bc_2.20 //
children.translated_text: the prince grew duly, step by step, like the lord of stars (moon) in the bright fortnight. // 2.20 //

children.text: tato mahārhāṇi ca candanāni ratnāvalīścauṣadhibhiḥ sagarbhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then from the houses of friends, they brought him precious sandalwood and garlands of jewels blended with herbs,

children.text: mṛgaprayuktān rathakāṃśca haimānācakrire 'smai suhṛdālayebhyaḥ // Bc_2.21 //
children.translated_text: and golden toy-chariots yoked with deer. // 2.21 //

children.text: vayo 'nurūpāṇi ca bhūṣaṇāni hiraṇmayān hastimṛgāśvakāṃśca /
children.translated_text: And ornaments appropriate to his age, golden elephants, deer, and horses,

children.text: rathāṃśca goputrakasaṃprayuktān putrīśca cāmīkararūpyacitrāḥ // Bc_2.22 //
children.translated_text: chariots yoked with small oxen, and dolls variously fashioned in gold and silver. // 2.22 //

children.text: evaṃ sa taistairviṣayopacārairvayo 'nurūpairupacaryamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, being attended with those various sense-gratifications appropriate to his age,

children.text: bālo 'pyabālapratimo babhūva dhṛtyā ca śaucena dhiyā śriyā ca // Bc_2.23 //
children.translated_text: even as a child he seemed beyond a child in steadfastness, purity, intelligence, and beauty. // 2.23 //

children.text: vayaśca kaumāramatītya samyak saṃprāpya kāle pratipattikarma /
children.translated_text: And having duly passed beyond the age of childhood, and reaching in due time the rite of investiture,

children.text: alpairahobhirbahuvarṣagāmyā jagrāha vidyāḥ svakulānurūpāḥ // Bc_2.24 //
children.translated_text: he mastered in a few days the sciences that take many years — those befitting his family. // 2.24 //

children.text: naiḥśreyasaṃ tasya tu bhavyamarthaṃ śrutvā purastādasitānmaharṣeḥ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Śākya</s> king, having heard beforehand from the great sage <s>Asita</s>

children.text: kāmeṣu saṅgaṃ janayāṃbabhūva vanāni yāyāditi śākyarājaḥ // Bc_2.25 //
children.translated_text: about the future destiny of his [son] toward the supreme good, sought to create in him attachment to pleasures, lest he depart to the forests. // 2.25 //

children.text: kulāttato 'smai sthiraśīlayuktātsādhvīṃ vapurhrīvinayopapannām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, from a family endowed with firm character, he summoned for him a bride —

children.text: yaśodharāṃ nāma yaśoviśālāṃ vāmābhidhānāṃ śriyamājuhāva // Bc_2.26 //
children.translated_text: one named <s>Yaśodharā</s>, of vast fame, also called <s>Vāmā</s>, a virtuous woman endowed with beauty, modesty, and propriety, [being herself] a <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune). // 2.26 //

children.text: vidyotamāno vapuṣā pareṇa sanatkumārapratimaḥ kumāraḥ /
children.translated_text: The prince, resplendent with surpassing beauty, like <s>Sanatkumāra</s>,

children.text: sārdha tayā śākyanarendravadhvā śacyā sahasrākṣa ivābhireme // Bc_2.27 //
children.translated_text: together with that bride of the <s>Śākya</s> king, took delight as <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> (<s>Indra</s>) with <s>Śacī</s>. // 2.27 //

children.text: kiṃcinmanaḥkṣobhakaraṃ pratīpaṃ kathaṃ na paśyediti so 'nucintya /
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'How might he not see anything disagreeable that would disturb his mind?'

children.text: vāsaṃ nṛpo vyādiśati sma tasmai harmyodareṣveva na bhūpracāram // Bc_2.28 //
children.translated_text: the king directed a dwelling for him in the upper chambers of the palace only, not on the ground. // Bc_2.28 //

children.text: tataḥ śarattoyadapāṇḍareṣu bhūmau vimāneṣviva rañjiteṣu /
children.translated_text: Then, in palaces white as autumn clouds, painted,

children.text: harmyeṣu sarvartusukhāśrayeṣu strīṇāmudārairvijahāra tūryaiḥ // Bc_2.29 //
children.translated_text: as if they were celestial mansions on the ground, providing comfort in all seasons, he reveled with the splendid music of women. // Bc_2.29 //

children.text: kalairhi cāmīkarabaddhakakṣairnārīkarāgrābhihatairmṛdaṅgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For with <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drums bound with gold girdles, struck by the fingertips of women,

children.text: varāpsaronṛtyasamaiśca nṛtyaiḥ kailāsavattadbhavanaṃ rarāja // Bc_2.30 //
children.translated_text: and with dances rivaling the dances of the best <s>Apsaras</s>, that palace shone like <s>Kailāsa</s>. // Bc_2.30 //

children.text: vāgbhiḥ kalābhirlīlataiśca hāvairmadaiḥ sakhelairmadhuraiśca hāsaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With melodious words, with playful gestures and coquetries, with intoxicating glances, with sweet laughter,

children.text: taṃ tatra nāryo ramayāṃbabhūvurbhūvañcitairardhīnarīkṣitaiśca // Bc_2.31 //
children.translated_text: the women there delighted him, with arched brows and sidelong glances. // Bc_2.31 //

children.text: tataḥ sa kāmāśrayapaṇḍitābhiḥ strībhirgṛhīto ratikarkaśābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he, seized by women skilled in the arts of love, fierce in passion,

children.text: vimānapṛṣṭhānna mahīṃ jagāma vimānapṛṣṭhādiva puṇyakarmā // Bc_2.32 //
children.translated_text: did not descend from the palace terrace to the earth, like one of meritorious deeds not descending from a celestial palace. // Bc_2.32 //

children.text: nṛpastu tasyaiva vivṛddhihetostadbhāvinārthena ca codyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the king, for the sake of his very growth and impelled by the destiny that was to be,

children.text: śame 'bhireme virarāma pāpādbheje damaṃ saṃvibabhāja sādhūn // Bc_2.33 //
children.translated_text: delighted in tranquility, refrained from evil, embraced self-restraint, and shared with the virtuous. // Bc_2.33 //

children.text: nādhīravatkāmasukhe sasañje na saṃrarañje viṣamaṃ jananyām /
children.translated_text: He did not cling to sensual pleasure like the unsteady, nor did he take delight improperly in women;

children.text: dhṛtyendriyāśvāṃścapalānvijigye bandhūṃśca paurāṃśca guṇairjigāya // Bc_2.34 //
children.translated_text: he conquered the restless horses of the senses by firmness, and surpassed kinsmen and citizens by his virtues. // Bc_2.34 //

children.text: nādhyaiṣṭa duḥkhāya parasya vidyāṃ jñānaṃ śivaṃ yattu tadadhyagīṣṭa /
children.translated_text: He did not pursue learning for the suffering of others; what knowledge was auspicious, that he studied;

children.text: svābhyaḥ prajābhyo hi yathā tathaiva sarvaprajābhyaḥ śivamāśaśaṃse // Bc_2.35 //
children.translated_text: just as for his own subjects, so for all beings he wished well-being. // Bc_2.35 //

children.text: bhaṃ bhāsuraṃ cāṅgirasādhidevaṃ yathāvadānarca tadāyuṣe saḥ /
children.translated_text: He duly worshipped the radiant star whose presiding deity is <s>Aṅgiras</s>, for the sake of his son's longevity;

children.text: juhāva havyānyakṛśe kṛśānau dadau dvijebhyaḥ kṛśanaṃ ca gāśca // Bc_2.36 //
children.translated_text: he offered oblations in a well-kindled fire, and gave gold and cows to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // Bc_2.36 //

children.text: sasnau śarīraṃ pavituṃ manaśca tīrthāmbubhiścaiva guṇāmbubhiśca /
children.translated_text: He bathed his body to purify his mind, with the waters of sacred places and with the waters of virtues;

children.text: vedopadiṣṭaṃ samamātmajaṃ ca somaṃ papau śāntisukhaṃ ca hārdam // Bc_2.37 //
children.translated_text: he drank the <s>Soma</s> prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s>, along with his son, and the heartfelt bliss of peace. // Bc_2.37 //

children.text: sāntvaṃ babhāṣe na ca nārthavadyajjajalpa tattvaṃ na ca vipriyaṃ yat /
children.translated_text: He spoke gently, yet not without substance; he uttered truth, yet nothing displeasing;

children.text: sāntvaṃ hyatattvaṃ paruṣaṃ ca tattvaṃ hriyāśakannātmana eva vaktum // Bc_2.38 //
children.translated_text: for gentle but untruthful speech, and harsh but truthful speech — he could not bring himself to utter either. // Bc_2.38 //

children.text: iṣṭeṣvaniṣṭeṣu ca kāryavatsu na rāgadoṣāśrayatāṃ prapede /
children.translated_text: In desirable and undesirable matters requiring action, he did not resort to attachment or aversion;

children.text: śivaṃ siṣeve vyavahāraśuddhaṃ yajñaṃ hi mene na tathā yathā tat // Bc_2.39 //
children.translated_text: he cultivated what was auspicious and pure in conduct; for he did not regard sacrifice as highly as that [purity of conduct]. // Bc_2.39 //

children.text: āśāvate cāhigatāya sadyo deyāmbubhistarṣamacecchidiṣṭa /
children.translated_text: To one who came hoping and was in need, he immediately quenched the thirst with waters of giving;

children.text: yuddhādṛte vṛttaparaśvadhena dviḍdarpamudvṛttamabebhidiṣṭa // Bc_2.40 //
children.translated_text: without resorting to war, he shattered with his well-wielded battle-axe the swollen pride of enemies. // Bc_2.40 //

children.text: ekaṃ vininye sa jugopa sapta saptaiva tatyāja rarakṣa pañca /
children.translated_text: He controlled the one [mind], protected the seven [constituents of the kingdom], abandoned seven [vices], guarded five [senses];

children.text: prāpa trivarga bubudhe trivarga jajñe dvivarga prajahau dvivargam // Bc_2.41 //
children.translated_text: he attained the triple group [of dharma, artha, kāma], understood the triple [Vedic] group, knew the dual group, and abandoned the dual group [of attachment and aversion]. // Bc_2.41 //

children.text: kṛtāgaso 'pi pratipādya vadhyānnājīghanannāpi ruṣā dadarśa /
children.translated_text: Even those who had committed offenses and were condemned to death, he did not execute, nor even look upon in anger;

children.text: babandha sāntvena phalena caitāṃstyāgo 'pi teṣāṃ hyanayāya dṛṣṭaḥ // Bc_2.42 //
children.translated_text: he bound them with kindness and reward, for even their release was seen as leading to no harm. // Bc_2.42 //

children.text: ārṣāṇyacārītparamavratāni vairāṇyahāsīccirasaṃbhṛtāni /
children.translated_text: He practiced the supreme vows of the ancient sages, he dissolved long-cherished enmities,

children.text: yaśāṃsi cāpadguṇagandhavanti rajāṃsyahārṣīnmalinīkarāṇi // Bc_2.43 //
children.translated_text: he gained glories untainted by the slightest defect, and swept away the impurities that defile. // Bc_2.43 //

children.text: na cājihīrṣidvalimapravṛttaṃ na cācikīrṣitparavastvabhidhyām /
children.translated_text: He did not wish to levy tribute that was unjust, nor did he desire to covet another's possessions;

children.text: na cāvivakṣīd dviṣatāmadharma na cāvivākṣīddhṛdayena manyum // Bc_2.44 //
children.translated_text: he did not wish to declare injustice against enemies, nor did he harbor wrath in his heart. // Bc_2.44 //

children.text: tasmiṃstathā bhūmipatau pravṛtte bhṛtyāśca paurāśca tathaiva ceruḥ /
children.translated_text: When that lord of the earth conducted himself thus, his servants and citizens likewise behaved,

children.text: śamātmake cetasi viprasanne prayuktayogasya yathendriyāṇi // Bc_2.45 //
children.translated_text: like the senses of one whose mind is tranquil and serene, who is engaged in <s>yoga</s>. // Bc_2.45 //

children.text: kāle tataścārupayodharāyāṃ yaśodharāyāṃ svayaśodharāyām /
children.translated_text: Then, in due time, from <s>Yaśodharā</s>, she of beautiful breasts, bearer of glory, who upheld his renown,

children.text: śauddhodane rāhusapatnavaktro jajñe suto rāhula eva nāmnā // Bc_2.46 //
children.translated_text: a son was born to the descendant of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, with a face like the rival of <s>Rāhu</s>, named <s>Rāhula</s>. // Bc_2.46 //

children.text: atheṣṭaputraḥ paramapratītaḥ kulasya vṛddhiṃ prati bhūmipālaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained a desired son, the lord of the earth, supremely delighted,

children.text: yathaiva putraprasave nananda tathaiva pautraprasave nananda // Bc_2.47 //
children.translated_text: rejoiced at the birth of a grandson just as he had rejoiced at the birth of a son. // Bc_2.47 //

children.text: putrasya me putragato mameva snehaḥ kathaṃ syāditi jātaharṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Filled with joy, thinking, 'How might the affection I have for my son extend to his son too?'

children.text: kāle sa taṃ taṃ vidhimālalambe putrapriyaḥ svargamivārurukṣan // Bc_2.48 //
children.translated_text: in due time he undertook this and that observance, fond of his son, as if aspiring to heaven. // Bc_2.48 //

children.text: sthitvā pathi prāthamakalpikānāṃ rājavarṣabhāṇāṃ yaśasānvitānām /
children.translated_text: Abiding on the path of the primordial royal bulls endowed with glory,

children.text: śuklānyamuktvāpi tapāṃsyatapta yajñaiśca hiṃsārahitairayaṣṭa // Bc_2.49 //
children.translated_text: though he did not put on white robes, he performed austerities and worshipped with sacrifices free from violence. // Bc_2.49 //

children.text: ajājvaliṣṭātha sa puṇyakarmā nṛpaśriyā caiva tapaḥśriyā ca /
children.translated_text: Then that man of meritorious deeds blazed forth with both the splendor of kingship and the splendor of asceticism,

children.text: kulena vṛttena dhiyā ca dīptastejaḥ sahasrāṃśurivotsisṛkṣuḥ // Bc_2.50 //
children.translated_text: radiant with lineage, conduct, and wisdom, like the thousand-rayed sun about to release its brilliance. // Bc_2.50 //

children.text: svāyaṃbhuvaṃ cārcikamarcayitvā jajāpa putrasthitaye sthitaśrīḥ /
children.translated_text: And having worshipped the <s>Ṛc</s> hymn of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, he of steadfast glory chanted for the stability of his son;

children.text: cakāra karmāṇi ca duṣkarāṇi prajāḥ sisṛkṣuḥ ka ivādikāle // Bc_2.51 //
children.translated_text: he performed difficult rites, like <s>Ka</s> (<s>Prajāpati</s>) at the beginning of creation desiring to create beings. // Bc_2.51 //

children.text: tatyāja śastraṃ vimamarśa śāstraṃ śamaṃ siṣeve niyamaṃ viṣehe /
children.translated_text: He abandoned the sword and pondered the scriptures; he cultivated peace and endured austerity;

children.text: vaśīva kaṃcidviṣayaṃ na bheje piteva sarvānviṣayāndadarśa // Bc_2.52 //
children.translated_text: like a self-controlled sage he did not indulge in any sense-object, yet like a father he watched over all sense-objects. // Bc_2.52 //

children.text: babhāra rājyaṃ sa hi putrahetoḥ putraṃ kulārthaṃ yaśase kulaṃ tu /
children.translated_text: For he bore the kingdom for the sake of his son, the son for the sake of the family, and the family for the sake of fame;

children.text: svargāya śabdaṃ divamātmahetordharmārthamātmasthitimācakāṅkṣa // Bc_2.53 //
children.translated_text: fame for the sake of heaven, heaven for the sake of the Self — he desired self-establishment for the sake of <s>dharma</s>. // Bc_2.53 //

children.text: evaṃ sa dharma vividhaṃ cakāra sidbhirnipātaṃ śrutitaśca siddham /
children.translated_text: Thus he performed <s>dharma</s> of various kinds, established through attainments and established from scripture,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kathaṃ putramukhaṃ suto me vanaṃ na yāyāditi nāthamānaḥ // Bc_2.54 //
children.translated_text: hoping, 'Having seen his son's face, my son will not go to the forest.' // Bc_2.54 //

children.text: rirakṣiṣantaḥ śriyamātmasaṃsthāṃ rakṣanti putrān bhuvi bhūmipālāḥ /
children.translated_text: Kings on earth protect their sons in order to guard the royal fortune that rests in them;

children.text: putraṃ narendraḥ sa tu dharmakāmo rarakṣa dharmādviṣayeṣu muñcan // Bc_2.55 //
children.translated_text: but that king, desiring <s>dharma</s>, protected his son from <s>dharma</s> [itself], releasing him among sensory pleasures. // Bc_2.55 //

children.text: vanamanupamasattvā bodhisattvāstu sarve viṣayasukharasajñā jagmurutpannaputrāḥ /
children.translated_text: But all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of incomparable courage, knowing the flavor of sensual pleasure, went to the forest after sons were born to them;

children.text: ata upacitakarmā rūḍhamūle 'pi hetau sa ratimupasiṣeve bodhimāpanna yāvat // Bc_2.56 //
children.translated_text: therefore, he of accumulated merit, even though the cause was deeply rooted, pursued pleasure until [the prince] would attain enlightenment. // Bc_2.56 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye antaḥpuravihāro nāma dvitīyaḥ sargaḥ // 2 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second canto, named 'The Pleasures of the Inner Apartments,' in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>. // 2 //
CANTO III

children.text: tataḥ kadācinmṛduśādvalāni puṃskokilonnāditapādapāni /
children.translated_text: Then, one day, he heard of groves adorned with lotus pools,

children.text: śuśrāva padmākaramaṇḍitāni gītairnibaddhāni sa kānanāni // Bc_3.1 //
children.translated_text: with soft green lawns, with trees resounding with the song of the male cuckoo, filled with music. // Bc_3.1 //

children.text: śrutvā tataḥ strījanavallabhānāṃ manojñabhāvaṃ purakānanānām /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing of the delightful nature of the city parks, dear to women,

children.text: bahiḥprayāṇāya cakāra buddhimantargṛhe nāga ivāvarūddhaḥ // Bc_3.2 //
children.translated_text: he resolved to go out, like an elephant confined within a house. // Bc_3.2 //

children.text: tato nṛpastasya niśamya bhāvaṃ putrābhidhānasya manorathasya /
children.translated_text: Then the king, learning the desire of his son — that wish of his heart —

children.text: snehasya lakṣmyā vayasaśca yogyāmājñāpayāmāsa vihārayātrām // Bc_3.3 //
children.translated_text: ordered a pleasure excursion suitable to his affection, his royal fortune, and his age. // Bc_3.3 //

children.text: nivartayāmāsa ca rājamārge saṃpātamārtasya pṛthagjanasya /
children.translated_text: And he had the royal road cleared of the encounter with any afflicted common person,

children.text: mā bhūtkumāraḥ sukumāracittaḥ saṃvignacetā iti manyamānaḥ // Bc_3.4 //
children.translated_text: thinking, 'Let not the prince, tender of heart, become agitated in mind.' // Bc_3.4 //

children.text: pratyaṅgahīnānvikalendriyāṃśca jīrṇāturādīn kṛpaṇāṃśca dikṣu /
children.translated_text: Those with missing limbs, those with impaired senses, the old, the sick, and the wretched in every direction —

children.text: tataḥ samutsārya pareṇa sāmnā śobhāṃ parāṃ rājapathasya cakuḥ // Bc_3.5 //
children.translated_text: these they removed with the utmost gentleness, and made the royal highway supremely beautiful. // Bc_3.5 //

children.text: tataḥ kṛte śrīmati rājamārge śrīmānvinītānucaraḥ kumāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, on the splendid royal road thus prepared, the glorious prince, with well-trained attendants,

children.text: prāsādapṛṣṭhādavatīrya kāle kṛtābhyanujño nṛpamabhyagacchat // Bc_3.6 //
children.translated_text: descended from the palace terrace at the proper time and, having received permission, approached the king. // Bc_3.6 //

children.text: atho narendraḥ sutamāgatāśruḥ śirasyupāghrāya ciraṃ nirīkṣya /
children.translated_text: Then the king, his eyes brimming with tears at his son's arrival, kissed him on the head and gazed at him long;

children.text: gaccheti cājñāpayati sma vācā snehānna cainaṃ manasā mumoca // Bc_3.7 //
children.translated_text: he commanded him with his voice, 'Go!' but in his heart, out of affection, he did not let him go. // Bc_3.7 //

children.text: tataḥ sa jāmbūnadabhāṇḍabhṛdbhiryuktaṃ caturbhirnibhṛtaisturaṅgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he mounted a golden chariot yoked with four gentle horses,

children.text: aklībavidvacchuciraśmidhāraṃ hiraṇmayaṃ syandanamāruroha // Bc_3.8 //
children.translated_text: driven by an attendant bearing gleaming golden vessels, skillful, brave, and holding radiant reins. // Bc_3.8 //

children.text: tataḥ prakīrṇojjvalapuṣpajālaṃ viṣaktamālyaṃ pracalatpatākam /
children.translated_text: Then, along a road strewn with a net of bright scattered flowers, hung with garlands, fluttering with banners,

children.text: mārgaṃ prapede sadṛśānuyātraścandraḥ sanakṣatra ivāntarīkṣam // Bc_3.9 //
children.translated_text: he proceeded with a fitting retinue, like the moon through the sky with its stars. // Bc_3.9 //

children.text: kautūhalātsphītataraiśca netrairnīlotpalārdhairiva kīryamāṇam /
children.translated_text: With eyes opened wider with curiosity, as if scattering half-opened blue lotuses,

children.text: śanaiḥ śanai rājapathaṃ jagāhe pauraiḥ samantādabhivīkṣyamāṇaḥ // Bc_3.10 //
children.translated_text: slowly, slowly he traversed the royal road, gazed upon from all sides by the citizens. // Bc_3.10 //

children.text: taṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ saumyaguṇena kecidvavandire dīptatayā tathānye /
children.translated_text: Some praised him for his gentle qualities; others saluted him for his radiance;

children.text: saumukhyatastu śriyamasya kecidvaipulyamāśaṃsiṣurāyuṣaśca // Bc_3.11 //
children.translated_text: some, seeing his gracious countenance, wished him abundant beauty and long life. // Bc_3.11 //

children.text: niḥsṛtya kubjāśca mahākulebhyo vyūhāśca kairātakavāmanānām /
children.translated_text: Hunchbacked women came forth from great households, and troops of <s>Kirāta</s> dwarfs,

children.text: nāryaḥ kṛśebhyaśca niveśanebhyo devānuyānadhvajavatpraṇemuḥ // Bc_3.12 //
children.translated_text: and women from humble dwellings bowed down, as if before the procession-banner of a god. // Bc_3.12 //

children.text: tataḥ kumāraḥ khalu gacchatīti śrutvā striyaḥ preṣyajanātpravṛttim /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing from the servants the news that the prince was passing by,

children.text: didṛkṣayā harmyatalāni jagmurjanena mānyena kṛtābhyanujñāḥ // Bc_3.13 //
children.translated_text: women, with permission from their elders, went to the palace terraces out of eagerness to see him. // Bc_3.13 //

children.text: tāḥ srastakāñcīguṇavighnitāśca suptaprabuddhākulalocanāśca /
children.translated_text: With their girdle-strings slipping and impeding them, with eyes drowsy and confused as if just awakened,

children.text: vṛttāntavinyastavibhūṣaṇāśca kautūhalenānibhṛtāḥ parīyuḥ // Bc_3.14 //
children.translated_text: with ornaments hastily put on, they crowded about restlessly with curiosity. // Bc_3.14 //

children.text: prāsādasopānatalapraṇādaiḥ kāñcīravairnūpuranisvanaiśca /
children.translated_text: With the sound of footfalls on palace stairways, the tinkling of girdle-bells, and the ringing of anklets,

children.text: vitrāsayantyo gṛhapakṣisaṅghānanyonyavegāṃśca samākṣipantyaḥ // Bc_3.15 //
children.translated_text: startling the flocks of household birds, and outpacing one another's speed. // Bc_3.15 //

children.text: kāsāṃcidāsāṃ tu varāṅganānāṃ jātatvarāṇāmapi sotsukānām /
children.translated_text: But some among those beautiful women, though hurrying eagerly,

children.text: gatiṃ gurutvājjagṛhurviśālāḥ śroṇīrathāḥ pīnapayodharāśca // Bc_3.16 //
children.translated_text: were held back in their gait by their large, broad hips and full, heavy breasts. // Bc_3.16 //

children.text: śīghraṃ samarthāpi tu gantumanyā gatiṃ nijagrāha yayau na tūrṇam /
children.translated_text: Another, though well able to go quickly, restrained her pace and did not go swiftly,

children.text: hriyāpragalbhā vinigūhamānā rahaḥprayuktāni vibhūṣaṇāni // Bc_3.17 //
children.translated_text: bashful and modest, concealing ornaments that had been put on in private. // Bc_3.17 //

children.text: parasparotpīḍanapiṇḍitānāṃ saṃmardasaṃkṣobhikuṇḍalānām /
children.translated_text: Of those women, pressed together in mutual crowding, their earrings clashing and agitated by the crush,

children.text: tāsāṃ tadā sasvanabhūṣaṇānāṃ vātayaneṣvapraśamo babhūva // Bc_3.18 //
children.translated_text: with their jingling ornaments, there was no stillness at the windows. // Bc_3.18 //

children.text: vātāyanebhyastu viniḥsṛtāni parasparāyāsitakuṇḍalāni /
children.translated_text: But their lotus-like faces, leaning out from the windows, with earrings displaced by mutual jostling,

children.text: strīṇāṃ virejurmukhapaṅkajāni saktāni harmyeṣviva paṅkajāni // Bc_3.19 //
children.translated_text: shone like lotuses clinging to the palaces. // Bc_3.19 //

children.text: tato vimānairyuvatīkarālaiḥ kautūhalodghāṭitavātayānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, with the palaces full of young women, the windows thrown open with curiosity,

children.text: śrīmatsamantānnagaraṃ babhāse viyadvimānairiva sāpsarobhiḥ // Bc_3.20 //
children.translated_text: the splendid city shone on all sides like the sky with celestial mansions filled with <s>Apsaras</s>. // Bc_3.20 //

children.text: vātāyanānāmaviśālabhāvādanyonyagaṇḍārpitakuṇḍalānām /
children.translated_text: Due to the narrowness of the windows, with their earrings pressed against each other's cheeks,

children.text: mukhāni rejuḥ pramodottamānāṃ baddhāḥ kalāpā iva paṅkajānām // Bc_3.21 //
children.translated_text: the faces of those supremely joyful women shone like a cluster of bound lotuses. // Bc_3.21 //

children.text: taṃ tāḥ kumāraṃ pathi vīkṣamāṇāḥ striyo babhurgāmiva gantukāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those women, gazing at the prince on the road, seemed as if they wished to descend to the earth;

children.text: ūrdhvonmukhāścainamudīkṣamāṇā narā babhurdyāmiva gantukāmāḥ // Bc_3.22 //
children.translated_text: and the men, gazing upward at him, seemed as if they wished to ascend to the sky. // Bc_3.22 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ rājasutaṃ striyastā jājvalyamānaṃ vapuṣā śriyā ca /
children.translated_text: And seeing that prince blazing with the splendor of his body and beauty,

children.text: dhanyāsya bhāryeti śanairavocañśuddhairmanobhiḥ khalu nānyabhāvāt // Bc_3.23 //
children.translated_text: the women said softly, 'Blessed is his wife!' — with pure hearts, indeed, and not from any other sentiment. // Bc_3.23 //

children.text: ayaṃ kila vyāyatapīnabāhū rūpeṇa sākṣādiva puṣpaketuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This one, they say, with long and mighty arms, in beauty like <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) incarnate,

children.text: tyaktvā śriyaṃ dharmamupaiṣyatīti tasmin hi tā gauravameva cakruḥ // Bc_3.24 //
children.translated_text: will abandon royal glory and pursue <s>dharma</s>' — therefore they regarded him with profound reverence. // Bc_3.24 //

children.text: kīrṇa tathā rājapathaṃ kumāraḥ paurairvinītaiḥ śucidhīraveṣaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The prince, seeing the royal road thus filled with well-mannered, pure-minded, and soberly attired citizens,

children.text: tatpūrvamālokya jaharṣa kiṃcinmene punarbhāvamivātmanaśca // Bc_3.25 //
children.translated_text: felt a certain joy and seemed to regard it as if a second birth for himself. // Bc_3.25 //

children.text: puraṃ tu tatsvargamiva prahṛṣṭaṃ śuddhādhivāsāḥ samavekṣya devāḥ /
children.translated_text: But the gods of pure abodes, seeing that city as joyful as heaven,

children.text: jīrṇaṃ naraṃ nirmamire prayātuṃ saṃcodanārthaṃ kṣitipātmajasya // Bc_3.26 //
children.translated_text: created an old man to pass before [the prince], in order to urge the son of the king forward. // Bc_3.26 //

children.text: tataḥ kumāro jarayābhibhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā narebhyaḥ pṛthagākṛtiṃ tam /
children.translated_text: Then the prince, seeing that man overwhelmed by old age, of form different from other men,

children.text: uvāca saṃgrāhakamāgatāsthastatraiva niṣkampaniviṣṭadṛṣṭiḥ // Bc_3.27 //
children.translated_text: spoke to the charioteer, his gaze fixed and unmoving upon that very spot, filled with wonder. // Bc_3.27 //

children.text: ka eṣa bhoḥ sūta naro 'bhyupetaḥ keśaiḥ sitairyaṣṭiviṣaktahaṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Who is this man, O charioteer, approached [by us], with white hair, his hand clinging to a staff,

children.text: bhrūsaṃvṛtākṣaḥ śithilānatāṅgaḥ kiṃ vikriyaiṣā prakṛtiryadṛcchā // Bc_3.28 //
children.translated_text: his eyes hidden beneath his brows, his limbs loose and bent — is this a transformation of nature, or chance?' // Bc_3.28 //

children.text: ityevamuktaḥ sa rathapraṇetā nivedayāmāsa nṛpātmajāya /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the chariot-driver disclosed to the prince,

children.text: saṃrakṣyamapyarthamadoṣadarśī taireva devaiḥ kṛtabuddhimohaḥ // Bc_3.29 //
children.translated_text: even that truth which was to be kept secret — his judgment deluded by those very gods, seeing no fault [in speaking]. // Bc_3.29 //

children.text: rūpasya hantrī vyasanaṃ balasya śokasya yonirnidhana ratīnām /
children.translated_text: Destroyer of beauty, calamity of strength, source of sorrow, end of pleasures,

children.text: nāśaḥ smṛtīnāṃ ripurindriyāṇāmeṣā jarā nāma yayaiṣa bhagnaḥ // Bc_3.30 //
children.translated_text: ruin of memories, enemy of the senses — this is called old age, by which this man is broken. // 3.30 //

children.text: pītaṃ hyanenāpi payaḥ śiśutve kālena bhūyaḥ parisṛptamurvyām /
children.translated_text: For even he once drank milk in infancy, in time he crawled upon the ground,

children.text: krameṇa bhūtvā ca yuvā vapuṣmān krameṇa tenaiva jarāmupetaḥ // Bc_3.31 //
children.translated_text: and gradually becoming a handsome youth — by that same gradual course he has arrived at old age. // 3.31 //

children.text: ityevamukte calitaḥ sa kiṃcidrājātmajaḥ sūtamidaṃ babhāṣe /
children.translated_text: When this was spoken, the prince was somewhat shaken, and said to the charioteer:

children.text: kimeṣa doṣo bhavitā mamāpītyasmai tataḥ sārathirabhyuvāca // Bc_3.32 //
children.translated_text: 'Will this affliction come upon me too?' — to which the charioteer then replied: // 3.32 //

children.text: āyuṣmato 'pyeṣa vayaḥprakarṣo niḥsaṃśayaṃ kālavaśena bhāvī /
children.translated_text: 'Even for one of long life, this advancing of age will inevitably come by the force of time;

children.text: evaṃ jarāṃ rūpavināśayitrīṃ jānāti caivecchati caiva lokaḥ // Bc_3.33 //
children.translated_text: thus the world knows old age, the destroyer of beauty, and yet desires [life all the same].' // 3.33 //

children.text: tataḥ sa pūrvāśayaśuddhabuddhirvistīrṇakalpācitapuṇyakarmā /
children.translated_text: Then he — whose intellect was pure by former dispositions, whose merit had been accumulated through vast <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) —

children.text: śrutvā jarāṃ savivije mahātmā mahāśanerghoṣamivāntike gauḥ // Bc_3.34 //
children.translated_text: hearing of old age, the great soul trembled, like a cow at the sound of a nearby thunderbolt. // 3.34 //

children.text: niḥśvasya dīrghaṃ svaśiraḥ prakampya tasmiṃśca jīrṇe viniveśya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: Sighing deeply, shaking his head, fixing his gaze upon that decrepit man,

children.text: tāṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā janatāṃ saharṣāṃ vākyaṃ sa saṃvigna idaṃ jagāda // Bc_3.35 //
children.translated_text: and seeing the crowd full of merriment — he, deeply stirred, spoke these words: // 3.35 //

children.text: evaṃ jarā hanti ca nirviśeṣaṃ smṛtiṃ ca rūpaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'Thus old age strikes without distinction — memory, beauty, and prowess;

children.text: na caiva saṃvegamupaiti lokaḥ pratyakṣato 'pīdṛśamīkṣamāṇaḥ // Bc_3.36 //
children.translated_text: yet the world feels no urgency, even while witnessing such a sight before its very eyes.' // 3.36 //

children.text: evaṃ gate sūta nivartayāśvān śīghraṃ gṛhāṇyeva bhavānprayātu /
children.translated_text: 'This being so, charioteer, turn the horses back — let us return swiftly to the palace;

children.text: udyānabhūmau hi kuto ratirme jarābhaye cetasi vartamāne // Bc_3.37 //
children.translated_text: for how can there be delight for me in the pleasure-grounds, when the fear of old age dwells in my heart?' // 3.37 //

children.text: athājñayā bhartusutasya tasya nivartayāmāsa rathaṃ niyantā /
children.translated_text: Then, by the command of the king's son, the driver turned back the chariot;

children.text: tataḥ kumāro bhavanaṃ tadeva cintāvaśaḥ śūnyamiva prapede // Bc_3.38 //
children.translated_text: and the prince entered that same palace, as if it were empty, his mind seized by thought. // 3.38 //

children.text: yadā tu tatraiva na śarma lebhe jarā jareti praparīkṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when he found no peace even there, constantly pondering 'old age, old age,'

children.text: tato narendrānumataḥ sa bhūyaḥ krameṇa tenaiva bahirjagāma // Bc_3.39 //
children.translated_text: then, with the king's permission, he went forth again by that same route. // 3.39 //

children.text: athāparaṃ vyādhiparītadehaṃ ta eva devāḥ sasṛjurmanuṣyam /
children.translated_text: Then those same gods created another man, one afflicted in body by disease;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ sārathimābabhāṣe śauddhodanistadgatadṛṣṭireva // Bc_3.40 //
children.translated_text: and seeing him, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, his gaze fixed upon that man, spoke to the charioteer: // 3.40 //
