children.text: sthūlodaraḥ śvāsacalaccharīraḥ srastāṃsabāhuḥ kṛśapāṇḍugātraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With swollen belly, body trembling with labored breathing, arms and shoulders drooping, limbs thin and pale,

children.text: ambeti vācaṃ karuṇaṃ bruvāṇaḥ paraṃ samāśritya naraḥ ka eṣaḥ // Bc_3.41 //
children.translated_text: crying out the word "mother" piteously, leaning upon another — who is this man?' // 3.41 //

children.text: tato 'bravītsārathirasya saumya dhātuprakopaprabhavaḥ pravṛddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the charioteer told him: 'O gentle one, a severe [affliction] arisen from the disturbance of the bodily humors,

children.text: rogābhidhānaḥ sumahānanarthaḥ śakto 'pi yenaiṣa kṛto 'svatantraḥ // Bc_3.42 //
children.translated_text: called disease — a very great misfortune — by which even this strong man has been rendered helpless.' // 3.42 //

children.text: ityūcivān rājasutaḥ sa bhūyastaṃ sānukampo naramīkṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The prince spoke again, gazing at that man with compassion:

children.text: asyaiva jāto pṛthageṣa doṣaḥ sāmānyato rogabhayaṃ prajānām // Bc_3.43 //
children.translated_text: 'Is this affliction peculiar to this man alone, or is the fear of disease common to all creatures?' // 3.43 //

children.text: tato babhāṣe sa rathapraṇetā kumāra sādhāraṇa eṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the chariot-driver replied: 'O prince, this is a common affliction;

children.text: evaṃ hi rogaiḥ paripīḍyamāno rujāturo harṣamupaiti lokaḥ // Bc_3.44 //
children.translated_text: for thus, the world — though tormented by diseases — though afflicted with sickness, still pursues pleasure.' // 3.44 //

children.text: iti śrutārthaḥ sa viṣaṇṇacetāḥ prāvepatāmbūrmigataḥ śaśīva /
children.translated_text: Having heard the import of this, his mind downcast, he trembled like the moon reflected in waves,

children.text: idaṃ ca vākyaṃ karuṇāyamānaḥ provāca kiṃcinmṛdunā svareṇa // Bc_3.45 //
children.translated_text: and moved by compassion, he uttered these words in a somewhat gentle voice: // 3.45 //

children.text: idaṃ ca rogavyasanaṃ prajānāṃ paśyaṃśca viśrambhamupaiti lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Seeing this calamity of disease among beings, the world yet reposes in confidence;

children.text: vistīrṇamajñānamaho narāṇāṃ hasanti ye rogabhayairamuktāḥ // Bc_3.46 //
children.translated_text: vast indeed is the ignorance of men — they laugh, though not freed from the fear of disease!' // 3.46 //

children.text: nivartyatāṃ sūta bahiḥprayāṇānnarendrasadmaiva rathaḥ prayātu /
children.translated_text: 'Let the chariot be turned back from this outing, charioteer; let it proceed to the royal palace;

children.text: śrutvā ca me rogabhayaṃ ratibhyaḥ pratyāhataṃ saṃkucatīva cetaḥ // Bc_3.47 //
children.translated_text: for having heard of the fear of disease, my mind recoils from pleasures and, as it were, contracts.' // 3.47 //

children.text: tato nivṛttaḥ sa nivṛttaharṣaḥ pradhyānayuktaḥ praviveśa veśma /
children.translated_text: Then he returned, his joy extinguished, absorbed in meditation, and entered the palace;

children.text: taṃ dvistathā prekṣya ca saṃnivṛttaṃ paryeṣaṇaṃ bhūmipatiścakāra // Bc_3.48 //
children.translated_text: and seeing him thus turned back for the second time, the lord of the earth made inquiry. // 3.48 //

children.text: śrutvā nimittaṃ tu nivartanasya saṃtyaktamātmānamanena mene /
children.translated_text: Hearing the cause of his return, the king felt that [his son] had given up attachment to himself;

children.text: mārgasya śaucādhikṛtāya caiva cukrośa ruṣṭo 'pi ca nogradaṇḍaḥ // Bc_3.49 //
children.translated_text: and he rebuked the officer charged with the cleanliness of the road — though angered, he [still] imposed no severe punishment. // 3.49 //

children.text: bhūyaśca tasmai vidadhe sutāya viśeṣayuktaṃ viṣayapracāram /
children.translated_text: And once more he arranged for his son a display of sensual pleasures endowed with special attractions,

children.text: calendriyatvādapi nāma sakto nāsmānvijahyāditi nāthamānaḥ // Bc_3.50 //
children.translated_text: hoping: 'Perhaps through the restlessness of his senses, being attached, he may not abandon us.' // 3.50 //

children.text: yadā ca śabdādibhirindriyārthairantaḥpure naiva suto 'sya reme /
children.translated_text: But when his son found no delight in the inner apartments even through the objects of the senses — sound and such —

children.text: tato bahirvyādiśati sma yātrāṃ rasāntaraṃ syāditi manyamānaḥ // Bc_3.51 //
children.translated_text: the king then ordered an excursion outside, thinking: 'Perhaps a change of enjoyment [would help].' // 3.51 //

children.text: snehācca bhāvaṃ tanayasya buddhvā sa rāgadoṣānavicintya kāṃścit /
children.translated_text: Out of affection, understanding the disposition of his son, and without reflecting on any faults of passion,

children.text: yogyāḥ samājñāpayati sma tatra kalāsvabhijñā iti vāramukhyāḥ // Bc_3.52 //
children.translated_text: he commanded chosen chief courtesans — skilled in the arts — to be stationed there. // 3.52 //

children.text: tato viśeṣeṇa narendramārge svalaṃkṛte caiva parīkṣite ca /
children.translated_text: Then, the king's road having been specially adorned and inspected,

children.text: vyatyasya sūtaṃ ca rathaṃ ca rājā prasthāpayāmāsa bahiḥ kumāram // Bc_3.53 //
children.translated_text: the king, having changed the charioteer and the chariot, sent the prince forth. // 3.53 //

children.text: tatastathā gacchati rājaputre taireva devairvihito gatāsuḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, as the prince was thus proceeding, those very gods fashioned a lifeless [corpse];

children.text: taṃ caiva mārge mṛtamuhyamānaṃ sūtaḥ kumāraśca dadarśa nānyaḥ // Bc_3.54 //
children.translated_text: and the charioteer and the prince — and no other — saw that dead man being carried along the road. // 3.54 //

children.text: athabravīdrājasutaḥ sa sūtaṃ naraiścaturbhihriyate ka eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the prince said to the charioteer: 'Who is this, being carried by four men,

children.text: dīnairmanuṣyairanugamyamāno yo bhūṣitaścāpyavarudyate ca // Bc_3.55 //
children.translated_text: followed by people in distress, who though adorned is being lamented?' // 3.55 //

children.text: tataḥ sa śuddhātmabhireva devaiḥ śuddhādhivāsairabhibhūtacetāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the chariot-driver, his mind overpowered by those very gods of pure nature and pure abode,

children.text: avācyamapyathīmimaṃ niyantā pravyājahārārthavadīśvarāya // Bc_3.56 //
children.translated_text: disclosed to his lord this matter — though it should not have been told — in words full of meaning: // 3.56 //

children.text: buddhīndriyaprāṇaguṇairviyuktaḥ supto visaṃjñastṛṇakāṣṭhabhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Deprived of intellect, senses, and vital breath, asleep, unconscious, become as straw and wood,

children.text: saṃvardhya saṃrakṣya ca yatnavadbhiḥ priyapriyaistyajyata eṣa ko 'pi // Bc_3.57 //
children.translated_text: though nourished and guarded with care by those who love [him] — he is now abandoned by dear and not-dear alike — who he may be.' // 3.57 //

children.text: iti praṇetuḥ sa niśamya vākyaṃ saṃcukṣubhe kiṃciduvāca cainam /
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the driver, he was somewhat shaken and said to him:

children.text: kiṃ kevalo 'syaiva janasya dharmaḥ sarvaprajānāmayamīdṛśo 'ntaḥ // Bc_3.58 //
children.translated_text: 'Is this the lot of this man alone, or is such an end [destined] for all creatures?' // 3.58 //

children.text: tataḥ praṇetā vadati sma tasmai sarvaprajānāmidamantakarma /
children.translated_text: Then the driver said to him: 'This is the final act of all creatures;

children.text: hīnasya madhyasya mahātmano vā sarvasya loke niyato vināśaḥ // Bc_3.59 //
children.translated_text: for the lowly, the middling, and the great-souled alike — destruction is certain for all in the world.' // 3.59 //

children.text: tataḥ sa dhīro 'pi narendrasūnuḥ śrutvaiva mṛtyuṃ viṣasāda sadyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the prince, though steadfast — the son of the king — upon merely hearing of death, sank into dejection;

children.text: aṃsena saṃśliṣya ca kūbarāgraṃ provāca nihrādavatā svareṇa // Bc_3.60 //
children.translated_text: and leaning his shoulder against the front of the chariot-pole, he spoke in a resonant voice: // 3.60 //

children.text: iyaṃ ca niṣṭhā niyatā prajānāṃ pramādyati tyaktabhayaśca lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This is the certain end appointed for all creatures, yet the world is heedless, having cast off fear;

children.text: manāṃsi śaṅke kaṭhināni nṝṇāṃ svasthāstathā hyadhvani vartamānāḥ // Bc_3.61 //
children.translated_text: hard indeed, I think, are the hearts of men, who remain at ease though traveling on such a road.' // 3.61 //

children.text: tasmādrathaḥ sūta nivartyatā no vihārabhūmerna hi deśakālaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, charioteer, let our chariot be turned back — this is not the time or place for a pleasure-ground;

children.text: jānanvināśaṃ kathamartikāle sacetanaḥ syādiha hi pramattaḥ // Bc_3.62 //
children.translated_text: for knowing destruction, how could one who is sentient be heedless at the time of [approaching] death?' // 3.62 //

children.text: iti bruvāṇe 'pi narādhipātmaje nivartayāmāsa sa naiva taṃ ratham /
children.translated_text: Even as the son of the king was speaking thus, the driver did not turn back that chariot,

children.text: viśeṣayuktaṃ tu narendraśāsanātsa padmaṣaṇḍaṃ vanameva niryayau // Bc_3.63 //
children.translated_text: but by the special command of the king, proceeded to the very grove of lotuses, the [pleasure-]forest. // 3.63 //

children.text: tataḥ śivaṃ kusumitabālapādapaṃ paribhramatpramuditamattakokilam /
children.translated_text: Then he beheld that auspicious grove, with young trees in blossom, with delighted intoxicated <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoos) roaming about,

children.text: vimānavatsa kamalacārudīrghikaṃ dadarśa tadvanamiva nandanaṃ vanam // Bc_3.64 //
children.translated_text: with beautiful pools adorned with lotuses, like celestial cars — a forest like the <s>Nandana</s> (garden of the gods). // 3.64 //

children.text: varāṅganāgaṇakalilaṃ nṛpātmajastato balādvanamatinīyate sma tat /
children.translated_text: The prince was then forcibly led into that grove, teeming with groups of beautiful women,

children.text: varāpsarovṛtamalakādhipālayaṃ navavrato muniriva vighnakātaraḥ // Bc_3.65 //
children.translated_text: like a newly vowed sage, fearful of obstacles, [led] into the pleasure-ground of the lord of <s>Alakā</s> (<s>Kubera</s>), surrounded by celestial <s>Apsarases</s>. // 3.65 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye saṃvegotpattirnāma tṛtīyaḥ sargaḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, [ends] the third canto, entitled 'The Arising of Disenchantment' (<s>Saṃvegotpatti</s>). // 3 //
CANTO IV

children.text: tatastasmātpurodyānātkautūhalacalekṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, from that city-garden, with eyes restless with curiosity,

children.text: pratyujjagmurnṛpasutaṃ prāptaṃ varamiva striyaḥ // Bc_4.1 //
children.translated_text: the women came forth to meet the prince, as if to greet a beloved. // 4.1 //

children.text: abhigamya ca tāstasmai vismayotphullalocanāḥ /
children.translated_text: And having approached him, with eyes wide open in wonder,

children.text: cakrire samudācāraṃ padmakośanibhaiḥ karaiḥ // Bc_4.2 //
children.translated_text: they performed courteous greetings with hands [soft] like lotus buds. // 4.2 //

children.text: tasthuśca parivāryainaṃ manmathākṣiptacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: And they stood surrounding him, their minds agitated by <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love),

children.text: niścalaiḥ prītivikacaiḥ pibantya iva locanaiḥ // Bc_4.3 //
children.translated_text: with motionless eyes opened wide in delight — as if drinking [him in] with their glances. // 4.3 //

children.text: taṃ hi tā menire nāryaḥ kāmo vigrahavāniti /
children.translated_text: For those women regarded him as <s>Kāma</s> (Love) in bodily form,

children.text: śobhitaṃ lakṣaṇairdīptaiḥ sahajairbhūṣāṇairiva // Bc_4.4 //
children.translated_text: adorned with radiant marks that were like innate ornaments. // 4.4 //

children.text: saumyatvāccaiva dhairyācca kāścidenaṃ prajajñire /
children.translated_text: Due to his gentleness and his steadfastness, some perceived him

children.text: avatīrṇo mahī sākṣād guḍhāṃśuścandramā iti // Bc_4.5 //
children.translated_text: as the moon descended bodily upon the earth, with his rays hidden. // 4.5 //

children.text: tasya tā vapuṣākṣiptā nigṛhītaṃ jajṛmbhire /
children.translated_text: Captivated by his beauty, they restrained their yawns,

children.text: anyonyaṃ dṛṣṭibhirhatvā śanaiśca viniśaśvasuḥ // Bc_4.6 //
children.translated_text: struck one another with their glances, and softly sighed. // 4.6 //

children.text: evaṃ tā dṛṣṭimātreṇa nāryo dadṛśureva tam /
children.translated_text: Thus, the women saw him with their glance alone,

children.text: na vyājahurna jahasuḥ prabhāveṇāsya yantritāḥ // Bc_4.7 //
children.translated_text: but spoke not, nor laughed — held fast by his majesty. // 4.7 //

children.text: tāstathā nu nirārambhā dṛṣṭvā praṇayaviklavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing them thus without initiative, flustered by affection,

children.text: purohitasuto dhīmānudāyī vākyamabravīt // Bc_4.8 //
children.translated_text: the wise <s>Udāyin</s>, son of the royal priest, spoke these words: // 4.8 //

children.text: sarvāḥ sarvakalājñāḥ stha bhāvagrahaṇapaṇḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are all accomplished in all arts, skilled in capturing hearts,

children.text: rupacāturyasaṃpannāḥ svaguṇairmukhyatāṃ gatāḥ // Bc_4.9 //
children.translated_text: endowed with beauty and charm — by your own qualities you have attained preeminence. // 4.9 //

children.text: śobhayeta guṇairebhirapi tānuttarān kurūn /
children.translated_text: 'With these qualities, you could adorn even those exalted <s>Kurus</s>,

children.text: kuberasyāpi cākrīḍaṃ prāgeva vasudhāmimām // Bc_4.10 //
children.translated_text: even the pleasure-ground of <s>Kubera</s> — how much more this earth! // 4.10 //

children.text: śaktāścaliyituṃ yūyaṃ vitarāgānuṣīnapi /
children.translated_text: 'You are capable of shaking even passionless sages,

children.text: apsarobhiśca kalitān grahītuṃ vibudhānapi // Bc_4.11 //
children.translated_text: and of captivating even the gods, though attended by <s>Apsarases</s>. // 4.11 //

children.text: bhāvajñānena hāvena rūpacāturyasaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: 'By your knowledge of moods, your coquetry, your wealth of beauty and charm,

children.text: strīṇāmeva ca śaktāḥ stha saṃrāge kiṃ punarnṛṇām // Bc_4.12 //
children.translated_text: you are capable [of conquering] even women — how much more men! // 4.12 //

children.text: tāsāmevaṃvidhānāṃ vo viyuktānāṃ svagocare /
children.translated_text: 'Yet for you — of such qualities, united with your domain [of expertise] —

children.text: iyamevaṃvidhā ceṣṭā na tuṣṭo 'smyārjavena vaḥ // Bc_4.13 //
children.translated_text: this kind of behavior! I am not satisfied with your straightforwardness. // 4.13 //

children.text: idaṃ navavadhūnāṃ vo hrīnīkuñcitacakṣuṣām /
children.translated_text: 'Such conduct would be fitting for newly married women with eyes shyly downcast,

children.text: sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ hi syādapi vā gopāyoṣitām // Bc_4.14 //
children.translated_text: or perhaps for the women of the cowherds. // 4.14 //

children.text: yadapi syādayaṃ dhīraḥ śriprabhāvānmahāniti /
children.translated_text: 'Even if this one is steadfast and great through the power of <s>Śrī</s> (fortune) —

children.text: strīṇāmapi mahatteja itaḥ kāryo 'tra niścayaḥ // Bc_4.15 //
children.translated_text: the splendor of women too is great — hence a resolve must be made here. // 4.15 //

children.text: purā hi kāśisundaryā veśavadhvā mahānṛṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For formerly, the great sage [<s>Vyāsa</s>], invincible even to the gods,

children.text: tāḍito 'bhūtpadā vyāso durdharṣo devatairapi // Bc_4.16 //
children.translated_text: was struck on the foot by a beautiful courtesan of <s>Kāśī</s>. // 4.16 //

children.text: manthālagautamo bhikṣurjaṅghayā vāramukhyayā /
children.translated_text: 'The mendicant <s>Manthāla-Gautama</s>, by a chief courtesan's leg —

children.text: piprīṣuśca tadarthārthaṃ vyasūnniraharatpurā // Bc_4.17 //
children.translated_text: and wishing to please her, he formerly extorted money. // 4.17 //

children.text: gautamaṃ dīrghatapasaṃ maharṣi dīrghajīvinam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Gautama</s>, the great sage of long austerity and long life —

children.text: yoṣitsaṃtoṣayāmāsa varṇasthānāvarā satī // Bc_4.18 //
children.translated_text: a woman of lower station gratified him. // 4.18 //

children.text: ṛṣyaśṛṅgaṃ munisutaṃ tathaiva strīṣvapaṇḍitam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, the sage's son, likewise unversed in women —

children.text: upāyairvividhaiḥ śāntā jagrāha ca jahāra ca // Bc_4.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śāntā</s> captured and carried him away by various stratagems. // 4.19 //

children.text: viśvāmitro maharṣiśca vigāḍho 'pi mahattapaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, though deeply immersed in great <s>tapas</s> —

children.text: daśa varṣāṇyaharmene ghṛtācyāpsarasā hṛtaḥ // Bc_4.20 //
children.translated_text: was carried away by the <s>Apsaras</s> <s>Ghṛtācī</s> for ten years — he forgot [all else]. // 4.20 //

children.text: evamādīnṛṣīstāṃstānanayanvikriyāṃ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, women led such sages as these to states of perturbation;

children.text: lalitaṃ pūrvavayasaṃ kiṃ punarnṛpateḥ sutam // Bc_4.21 //
children.translated_text: how much more then the son of a king, who is of tender youth! // 4.21 //

children.text: tadevaṃ sati viśrabdhaṃ prayatadhvaṃ tathā yathā /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, this being so, exert yourselves boldly, in such a way

children.text: iyaṃ nṛpasya vaṃśaśrīrito na syātparāṅmukhī // Bc_4.22 //
children.translated_text: that this glory of the king's lineage may not turn away from here. // 4.22 //

children.text: yā hi kāścidyuvatayo haranti sadṛśaṃ janam /
children.translated_text: 'For those young women who attract men of their own kind — [that is natural];

children.text: nikṛṣṭotkṛṣṭayorbhāvaṃ yā gṛhṇanti tu tāḥ striyaḥ // Bc_4.23 //
children.translated_text: but those who capture the hearts of both the lowly and the exalted — they are [true] women! // 4.23 //

children.text: ityudāyivacaḥ śrutvā tā viddhā iva yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Udāyin</s>, those women, as if stung,

children.text: samāruruhurātmānaṃ kumāragrahaṇaṃ prati // Bc_4.24 //
children.translated_text: steeled themselves for the task of winning the prince. // 4.24 //

children.text: tā bhrūmiḥ prekṣitairhāvairhasitailīḍitairgataiḥ /
children.translated_text: With brow-play, glances, coquetry, laughter, lip-biting, and gaits,

children.text: cakrurākṣepikāśceṣṭā bhītabhītā ivāṅganāḥ // Bc_4.25 //
children.translated_text: the women performed provocative gestures, as if half-afraid. // 4.25 //

children.text: rājñastu viniyogena kumārasya ca mārdavāt /
children.translated_text: But by the king's directive and the prince's gentleness,

children.text: jahuḥ kṣipramaviśrambhaṃ madena madanena ca // Bc_4.26 //
children.translated_text: they swiftly shed their diffidence, through intoxication and through love. // 4.26 //

children.text: atha nārījanavṛtaḥ kumāro vyacaradvanam /
children.translated_text: Then the prince, surrounded by the throng of women, wandered through the grove,

children.text: vāsitāyūthasahitaḥ karīva himavadvanam // Bc_4.27 //
children.translated_text: like a bull elephant in the <s>Himavat</s> forest accompanied by a herd of females. // 4.27 //

children.text: sa tasmin kānane ramye jajvāla strīpuraḥsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: In that delightful grove, he blazed forth, preceded by women,

children.text: ākrīḍa iva vibhrāje vivasvānapsarovṛtaḥ // Bc_4.28 //
children.translated_text: shining splendidly like <s>Vivasvat</s> (the Sun) surrounded by <s>Apsarases</s> in his pleasure-ground. // 4.28 //

children.text: madenāvarjitā nāma taṃ kāścittatra yiṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some women there, overpowered by desire, in order to captivate him,

children.text: kaṭhinaiḥ paspṛśuḥ pīnaiḥ saṃhatairvalgubhiḥ stanaiḥ // Bc_4.29 //
children.translated_text: touched him with their hard, full, firm, and shapely breasts. // 4.29 //

children.text: srastāṃsakomalālambamṛdubāhulatābalā /
children.translated_text: One tender girl, with a soft creeper-like arm drooping from her slipped shoulder —

children.text: anṛtaṃ skhalitaṃ kācitkṛtvainaṃ sasvaje balāt // Bc_4.30 //
children.translated_text: One woman, having feigned a stumble, forcibly embraced him. // Bc_4.30 //

children.text: kācittāmrādharoṣṭhena mukhenāsavagandhinā /
children.translated_text: Another, with her mouth whose lips were red as copper,

children.text: viniśaśvāsa karṇe 'sya rahasyaṃ śrūyatāmiti // Bc_4.31 //
children.translated_text: fragrant with wine, whispered in his ear, 'Let a secret be heard!' // Bc_4.31 //

children.text: kācidājñāpayantīva provācārdrānulepanā /
children.translated_text: Another, as if commanding, her body moist with unguent, spoke:

children.text: iha bhaktiṃ kuruṣveti hastasaṃśleṣalipsayā // Bc_4.32 //
children.translated_text: 'Apply your devotion here!' — desiring the clasp of his hand. // Bc_4.32 //

children.text: muhurmuhurmadavyājasrastanīlāṃśukāparā /
children.translated_text: Yet another, her dark blue garment repeatedly slipping as if from intoxication,

children.text: ālakṣyaraśanā reje sphuradvidyudiva kṣapā // Bc_4.33 //
children.translated_text: her girdle barely visible, shone like a night lit by flashing lightning. // Bc_4.33 //

children.text: kāścitkanakakāñcībhirmukharābhiritastataḥ /
children.translated_text: Some wandered here and there, with tinkling golden girdle-belts,

children.text: babhramurdarśayantyo 'sya śroṇīstanvaṃśukāvṛtāḥ // Bc_4.34 //
children.translated_text: displaying to him their hips covered by thin garments. // Bc_4.34 //

children.text: cūtaśākhāṃ kusumitāṃ pragṛhyānyā lalambire /
children.translated_text: Others hung from a blossoming mango branch, grasping it,

children.text: suvarṇakalaśaprakhyāndarśayantyaḥ payodharān // Bc_4.35 //
children.translated_text: displaying breasts resembling golden pitchers. // Bc_4.35 //

children.text: kācitpadmavanādetya sapadmā padmalocanā /
children.translated_text: One, coming from a lotus pond, holding a lotus, lotus-eyed,

children.text: padmavaktrasya pārśve 'sya padmaśrīriva tasthuṣī // Bc_4.36 //
children.translated_text: stood at his side like <s>Padmaśrī</s> (the goddess of the lotus) beside him whose face was a lotus. // Bc_4.36 //

children.text: madhuraṃ gītamanvarthaṃ kācitsābhinayaṃ jagau /
children.translated_text: One sang a sweet and fitting song with gestures,

children.text: taṃ svasthaṃ codayantīva vañcito 'sītyavekṣitaiḥ // Bc_4.37 //
children.translated_text: as if urging him who was self-possessed, with glances saying 'You are deceived!' // Bc_4.37 //

children.text: śubhena vadanenānyā bhrūkārmukavikarṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: Another, with her lovely face drawing the bow of her brows,

children.text: prāvṛtyānucakārāsya ceṣṭitaṃ dhīralīlayā // Bc_4.38 //
children.translated_text: turned and imitated his movements with graceful playfulness. // Bc_4.38 //

children.text: pīnavalgustanī kāciddhāsāghūrṇitakuṇḍalā /
children.translated_text: One, with full and shapely breasts, her earrings swaying with laughter,

children.text: uccairavajahāsainaṃ samāpnotu bhavāniti // Bc_4.39 //
children.translated_text: laughed aloud at him, saying 'May you attain [your desire]!' // Bc_4.39 //

children.text: apayāntaṃ tathaivānyā babandhurmālyadāmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Others, as he turned to leave, bound him with garlands;

children.text: kāścitsākṣepamadhurairjagṛharvacanāṅkuśaiḥ // Bc_4.40 //
children.translated_text: some detained him with words that were rebuking yet sweet, like goads. // Bc_4.40 //

children.text: pratiyogārthinī kācid gṛhītvā cūtavallarīm /
children.translated_text: One, seeking a rival contest, took hold of a mango spray

children.text: idaṃ puṣpaṃ tu kasyeti papraccha madaviklavā // Bc_4.41 //
children.translated_text: and asked, bewildered with intoxication, 'Whose is this flower?' // Bc_4.41 //

children.text: kācitpuruṣavatkṛtvā gatiṃ saṃsthānameva ca /
children.translated_text: One, assuming a man's gait and bearing,

children.text: uvācainaṃ jitaḥ strībhīrjaya bho pṛthivīmimām // Bc_4.42 //
children.translated_text: said to him, 'Conquered by women! Come, conquer this earth, O lord!' // Bc_4.42 //

children.text: atha lolekṣaṇā kācijjighrantī nīlamutpalam /
children.translated_text: Then one with darting eyes, smelling a blue lotus,

children.text: kiṃcinmadakalairvākyai rnṛpātmajamabhāṣata // Bc_4.43 //
children.translated_text: addressed the prince with words somewhat softened by intoxication: // Bc_4.43 //

children.text: paśya bhartīścitaṃ cūtaṃ kusumairmadhugandhibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'See this mango tree laden with honey-scented blossoms,

children.text: hemapañjararuddho vā kokilo yatra kūjati // Bc_4.44 //
children.translated_text: where a cuckoo, as if confined in a golden cage, sings! // Bc_4.44 //

children.text: aśoko dṛśyatāmeṣa kāmiśokavivardhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Behold this <s>aśoka</s> tree, which increases the sorrow of lovers,

children.text: ruvanti bhramarā yatra dahyamānā ivāgninā // Bc_4.45 //
children.translated_text: where bees hum as if burning with fire! // Bc_4.45 //

children.text: cūtayaṣṭyā samāśliṣṭo dṛśyatāṃ tilakadrumaḥ /
children.translated_text: See this <s>tilaka</s> tree embraced by a mango shoot,

children.text: śuklavāsā iva naraḥ striyā pītāṅgarāgayā // Bc_4.46 //
children.translated_text: like a man in white garments [embraced] by a woman whose limbs are anointed with yellow pigment! // Bc_4.46 //

children.text: phullaṃ kurubakaṃ paśya nirbhuktālaktakaprabham /
children.translated_text: Behold the blossoming <s>kurubaka</s>, glowing like chewed lac,

children.text: yo nakhaprabhayā strīṇāṃ nirbhīrtsata ivānataḥ // Bc_4.47 //
children.translated_text: which bows down as if put to shame by the luster of women's nails! // Bc_4.47 //

children.text: bālāśokaśca nicito dṛśyatāmeṣa pallavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And see this young <s>aśoka</s>, laden with tender sprouts,

children.text: yo 'smākaṃ hastaśobhābhirlajjamāna iva sthitaḥ // Bc_4.48 //
children.translated_text: which stands as if embarrassed by the beauty of our hands! // Bc_4.48 //

children.text: dīrghikā prāvṛtāṃ paśya tīrajaiḥ sinduvārakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: See the pool covered with <s>sinduvāra</s> trees growing on its banks,

children.text: pāṇḍurāṃśukasaṃvītāṃ śayānāṃ pramadāmiva // Bc_4.49 //
children.translated_text: like a woman lying down, clothed in a white garment! // Bc_4.49 //

children.text: dṛśyatāṃ strīṣu māhātmyaṃ cakravāko hyasau jale /
children.translated_text: Behold the devotion among females: that <s>cakravāka</s> drake in the water

children.text: pṛṣṭhataḥ preṣyavadbhāryāmanuvartyanugacchati // Bc_4.50 //
children.translated_text: follows his mate from behind, attending her like a servant! // Bc_4.50 //

children.text: mattasya parapuṣṭasya ruvataḥ śrūyatāṃ dhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: Listen to the call of the intoxicated cuckoo as it cries —

children.text: aparaḥ kokilo 'nvakṣaṃ pratiśrutkeva kūjati // Bc_4.51 //
children.translated_text: another cuckoo sings after it as if in echo! // Bc_4.51 //

children.text: api nāma vihaṅgānāṃ vasantenāhṛto madaḥ /
children.translated_text: Is it not that even among birds, spring stirs their passion,

children.text: na tu cintayato 'cintyaṃ janasya prājñamāninaḥ // Bc_4.52 //
children.translated_text: but not the mind of a man who ponders the imponderable and considers himself wise?' // Bc_4.52 //

children.text: ityevaṃ tā yuvatayo manmathoddāmacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus those young women, their hearts unbound by desire,

children.text: kumāraṃ vividhaistaistairupacakramire nayaiḥ // Bc_4.53 //
children.translated_text: approached the prince with various such stratagems. // Bc_4.53 //

children.text: evamākṣipyamāṇo 'pi satu dhairyāvṛtendriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: But he, though thus assailed, his senses veiled by steadfastness,

children.text: martavyamiti sodvego na jaharṣa na vivyathe // Bc_4.54 //
children.translated_text: agitated by the thought 'one must die,' neither rejoiced nor trembled. // Bc_4.54 //

children.text: tāsāṃ tattve 'navasthānaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa puruṣottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing their lack of grounding in truth, that best of men

children.text: samaṃ vignena dhīreṇa cintayāmāsa cetasā // Bc_4.55 //
children.translated_text: reflected with a mind both agitated and resolute: // Bc_4.55 //

children.text: kiṃ tvimā nāvagacchanti capalaṃ yauvanaṃ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Do these women not understand the fleeting nature of youth,

children.text: yato rūpeṇa saṃmattaṃ jarā yannāśayiṣyati // Bc_4.56 //
children.translated_text: intoxicated by their beauty, which old age will destroy? // Bc_4.56 //

children.text: nūnametā na paśyanti kasyacidrogasaṃplavam /
children.translated_text: Surely they do not see the onrush of disease in anyone,

children.text: tathā hṛṣṭā bhayaṃ tyaktvā jagati vyadhidharmiṇi // Bc_4.57 //
children.translated_text: for they are so joyful, having cast aside fear, in a world subject to illness! // Bc_4.57 //

children.text: anabhijñāśca suvyaktaṃ mṛtyoḥ sarvāpahāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And clearly they are unaware of death, which carries away all;

children.text: tataḥ svasthā nirudvignāḥ krīḍanti ca hasanti ca // Bc_4.58 //
children.translated_text: therefore they are at ease, untroubled, and play and laugh. // Bc_4.58 //

children.text: jarāṃ vyādhiṃ ca mṛtyuṃ ca ko hi jānansacetanaḥ /
children.translated_text: For who, knowing of old age, disease, and death, and being conscious,

children.text: svasthastiṣṭhenniṣīdedvā śayedvā kiṃ punarhaset // Bc_4.59 //
children.translated_text: could remain at ease, or sit, or lie down, much less laugh? // Bc_4.59 //

children.text: yastu dṛṣṭvā paraṃ jīrṇa vyādhitaṃ mṛtameva ca /
children.translated_text: But one who, seeing another grown old, diseased, and even dead,

children.text: svastho bhavati nodvigno yathācetāstathaiva saḥ // Bc_4.60 //
children.translated_text: remains at ease and untroubled — he is like one without consciousness. // Bc_4.60 //

children.text: viyujyamāne hi tarau puṣpairapi phalairapi /
children.translated_text: For when a tree is being stripped of its flowers and fruits,

children.text: patati cchidyamāne vā taruranyo na śocate // Bc_4.61 //
children.translated_text: or when it is being felled, another tree does not grieve.' // Bc_4.61 //

children.text: iti dhyānaparaṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣayebhyo gataspṛham /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him absorbed in meditation, free from desire for sense-objects,

children.text: udāyī nītiśāstrajñastamuvāca suhṛttayā // Bc_4.62 //
children.translated_text: <s>Udāyin</s>, who was learned in statecraft, spoke to him with the affection of a friend: // Bc_4.62 //

children.text: ahaṃ nṛpatinā dattaḥ sakhā tubhyaṃ kṣamaḥ kila /
children.translated_text: 'I was appointed by the king as your companion, deemed worthy;

children.text: yāsmāttvayi vivakṣā me tayā praṇayavattayā // Bc_4.63 //
children.translated_text: therefore I have this desire to speak to you, out of that friendly intimacy. // Bc_4.63 //

children.text: ahitātpratiṣedhaśca hite cānupravartanam /
children.translated_text: Dissuasion from what is harmful, encouragement toward what is beneficial,

children.text: vyasane cāparityāgastrividhaṃ mitralakṣaṇam // Bc_4.64 //
children.translated_text: and not abandoning [a friend] in adversity — these are the threefold marks of a friend. // Bc_4.64 //

children.text: so 'haṃ maitrīṃ pratijñāya puruṣārthātparāṅmukhaḥ /
children.translated_text: If I, having professed friendship, were to overlook you

children.text: yadi tvā samupekṣeya na bhavenmitratā mayi // Bc_4.65 //
children.translated_text: while you turn away from the aims of life — there would be no friendship in me. // Bc_4.65 //

children.text: tadbravīmi suhṛdbhūtvā taruṇasya vapuṣmataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore I speak to you as a friend: for one who is young and handsome,

children.text: idaṃ na pratirūpaṃ te strīṣvadākṣiṇyamīdṛśam // Bc_4.66 //
children.translated_text: this kind of discourtesy toward women is not fitting for you. // Bc_4.66 //

children.text: anṛtenāpi nārīṇāṃ yuktaṃ samanuvartanam /
children.translated_text: Even by falsehood, one should comply with women;

children.text: tadvrīḍāparihārārthamātmaratyarthameva ca // Bc_4.67 //
children.translated_text: that is for the sake of removing their bashfulness and for the sake of one's own pleasure. // Bc_4.67 //

children.text: saṃnatiścānuvṛttiśca strīṇāṃ hṛdayabandhanam /
children.translated_text: Deference and compliance are what bind women's hearts;

children.text: snehasya hi guṇā yonirmānakāmāśca yoṣitaḥ // Bc_4.68 //
children.translated_text: for the qualities of affection are their source, and women desire honor. // Bc_4.68 //

children.text: tadarhasi viśālākṣa hṛdaye 'pi parāṅmukhe /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O wide-eyed one, even if your heart is averse,

children.text: rūpasyāsyānurūpeṇa dākṣiṇyenānuvartitum // Bc_4.69 //
children.translated_text: you should respond with a courtesy befitting this beauty of yours. // Bc_4.69 //

children.text: dākṣiṇyamauṣadhaṃ strīṇāṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ param /
children.translated_text: Courtesy is the remedy for women; courtesy is the supreme ornament;

children.text: dākṣiṇyarahitaṃ rūpaṃ niṣpuṣpamiva kānanam // Bc_4.70 //
children.translated_text: beauty without courtesy is like a garden without flowers. // Bc_4.70 //

children.text: kiṃ vā dākṣiṇyamātreṇa bhāvenāstu parigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: But why merely courtesy? Let there be attachment with genuine feeling;

children.text: viṣayāndurlabhāṃllabdhvā na hyavajñātumarhasi // Bc_4.71 //
children.translated_text: having obtained sense-pleasures that are hard to obtain, you should not disregard them. // Bc_4.71 //

children.text: kāmaṃ paramiti jñātvā devo 'pi hi puraṃdaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing desire to be supreme, even the god <s>Puraṃdara</s> (<s>Indra</s>)

children.text: gautamasya muneḥ patnīmahalyāṃ cakame purā // Bc_4.72 //
children.translated_text: formerly desired <s>Ahalyā</s>, the wife of the sage <s>Gautama</s>. // Bc_4.72 //

children.text: agastyaḥ prārthayāmāsa somabhāryā ca rohiṇīm /
children.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s> desired <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the wife of <s>Soma</s> (the Moon);

children.text: tasmāttatsadṛśī lebhe lopāmudrāmiti śrutiḥ // Bc_4.73 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the tradition says, he obtained <s>Lopāmudrā</s>, who was her equal. // Bc_4.73 //

children.text: utathyasya ca bhāryāyāṃ mamātāyaṃ mahātapaḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, of great austerity, in the wife of <s>Utathya</s>,

children.text: mārutyāṃ janayāmāsa bharadvājaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ // Bc_4.74 //
children.translated_text: begot <s>Bharadvāja</s> upon <s>Mārutī</s>. // Bc_4.74 //

children.text: bṛhaspatermahiṣyāṃ ca juvhatyāṃ juvhatāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: And upon <s>Juhu</s> (<s>Tārā</s>), the queen of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the Moon (<s>Candra</s>),

children.text: budhaṃ vibudhakarmāṇaṃ janayāmāsa candramāḥ // Bc_4.75 //
children.translated_text: best of offerers, begot <s>Budha</s>, whose deeds were divine. // Bc_4.75 //

children.text: kālīṃ caiva purā kanyāṃ jalaprabhavasaṃbhavām /
children.translated_text: And long ago, <s>Parāśara</s>, his passion aroused,

children.text: jagāma yamunātīre jātarāgaḥ parāśaraḥ // Bc_4.76 //
children.translated_text: approached the maiden <s>Kālī</s>, born of the water, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>. // Bc_4.76 //

children.text: mātaṅgayāmakṣamālāyāṃ garhitāyāṃ riraṃsayā /
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, out of desire to sport

children.text: kapiñjalādaṃ tanayaṃ vasiṣṭho 'janayanmuniḥ // Bc_4.77 //
children.translated_text: with <s>Akṣamālā</s>, a woman of the <s>Mātaṅga</s> caste, though despised, begot his son <s>Kapiñjalāda</s>. // Bc_4.77 //

children.text: yayātiścaiva rājarṣirvayasyapi vinirgate /
children.translated_text: And <s>Yayāti</s>, the royal sage, even when his youth had departed,

children.text: viśvācyāpsarasā sārdhaṃ reme caitrarathe vane // Bc_4.78 //
children.translated_text: sported with the <s>Apsaras</s> <s>Viśvācī</s> in the forest of <s>Caitraratha</s>. // Bc_4.78 //

children.text: strīsaṃsarga vināśāntaṃ pāṇḍurjñātvāpi kauravaḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, the <s>Kaurava</s>, though knowing that union with women ends in destruction,

children.text: mādrīrūpaguṇākṣiptaḥ siṣeve kāmajaṃ sukham // Bc_4.79 //
children.translated_text: overcome by the beauty and qualities of <s>Mādrī</s>, pursued the pleasure born of desire. // Bc_4.79 //

children.text: karālajanakaścaiva hṛtvā brāhmaṇakanyakām /
children.translated_text: And <s>Karālajana</s>, even though he incurred his downfall by carrying off a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> maiden,

children.text: avāpa bhraṃśamapyevaṃ na tu seje na manmatham // Bc_4.80 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless did not abandon desire. // Bc_4.80 //

children.text: evamādyā mahātmāno viṣayān garhitānapi /
children.translated_text: Thus these and other great souls pursued even censured pleasures

children.text: ratihetorbubhujire prāgeva guṇasaṃhitān // Bc_4.81 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of love — how much more those endowed with good qualities! // Bc_4.81 //

children.text: tvaṃ punarnyāyataḥ prāptān balavān rūpavānyuvā /
children.translated_text: But you, though strong, handsome, and young, disdain the sense-pleasures

children.text: viṣayānavajānāsi yatra saktamidaṃ jagat // Bc_4.82 //
children.translated_text: that have come to you rightfully, to which this world is attached! // Bc_4.82 //'

children.text: iti śrutvā vacastasya ślakṣṇamāgamasaṃhitam /
children.translated_text: Having heard his smooth words, supported by scriptural precedent,

children.text: meghastanitanirghoṣaḥ kumāraḥ pratyabhāṣata // Bc_4.83 //
children.translated_text: the prince, whose voice was deep as the rumbling of thunder, replied: // Bc_4.83 //

children.text: upapannamidaṃ vākyaṃ sauhārdavyañjakaṃ tvayi /
children.translated_text: 'This speech befitting you, expressive of friendship, is well-placed;

children.text: atra ca tvānuneṣyāmi yatra mā duṣṭhu manyase // Bc_4.84 //
children.translated_text: and in this matter I will persuade you where you think me wrong. // Bc_4.84 //

children.text: nāvajānāmi viṣayān jāne lokaṃ tadātmakam /
children.translated_text: 'I do not despise sense-pleasures; I know the world to be of their nature;

children.text: anityaṃ tu jagamatvā nātra me ramate manaḥ // Bc_4.85 //
children.translated_text: but knowing this world to be impermanent, my mind does not delight in them. // Bc_4.85 //

children.text: jarā vyādhiśca mṛtyuśca yadi na syādidaṃ trayam /
children.translated_text: If old age, disease, and death — if this triad did not exist,

children.text: mamāpi hi manojñeṣu viṣayeṣu ratirbhavet // Bc_4.86 //
children.translated_text: even my mind would take pleasure in delightful sense-objects. // Bc_4.86 //

children.text: nityaṃ yadapi hi strīṇāmetadeva vapurbhavet /
children.translated_text: If indeed the beauty of women were to remain constant forever,

children.text: doṣavatsvapi kāmeṣu kāmaṃ rajyeta me manaḥ // Bc_4.87 //
children.translated_text: my mind might well be attached even to flawed pleasures. // Bc_4.87 //

children.text: yadā tu jarayāpītaṃ rūpamāsāṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: But when their beauty shall be drunk up by old age,

children.text: ātmano 'pyanabhipretaṃ mohāttatra ratirbhavet // Bc_4.88 //
children.translated_text: even undesired by their own selves — attachment to that would be delusion. // Bc_4.88 //

children.text: mṛtyuvyādhijarādharmā mṛtyuvyādhijarātmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is subject to the law of old age, disease, and death, and yet,

children.text: ramamāṇo hyasaṃvignaḥ samāno mṛgapakṣibhiḥ // Bc_4.89 //
children.translated_text: sporting with those who are themselves subject to old age, disease, and death, feels no agitation — he is no different from beasts and birds. // Bc_4.89 //

children.text: yadapyāttha mahātmānaste 'pi kāmātmakā iti /
children.translated_text: And as for your saying that even great souls were given to desire —

children.text: saṃvego 'traiva kartavyo yadā teṣāmapi kṣayaḥ // Bc_4.90 //
children.translated_text: urgency should be felt in this very matter, since even they came to destruction. // Bc_4.90 //

children.text: māhātmyaṃ na ca tanmanye yatra sāmānyataḥ kṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: I do not consider that greatness, where there is a common destruction,

children.text: viṣayeṣu prasaktirvā yuktirvā nātmavattayā // Bc_4.91 //
children.translated_text: or attachment to sense-objects — or fitness either — when there is no self-mastery. // Bc_4.91 //

children.text: yadapyātthānṛtenāpi strījane vartyatāmiti /
children.translated_text: And as for your saying that one should comply with women even by falsehood —

children.text: anṛtaṃ nāvagacchāmi dākṣiṇyenāpi kiṃcana // Bc_4.92 //
children.translated_text: I understand no falsehood whatsoever, even in the guise of courtesy. // Bc_4.92 //

children.text: na cānuvartanaṃ tanme rucitaṃ yatra nārjavam /
children.translated_text: Nor does that compliance please me where there is no straightforwardness;

children.text: sarvabhāvena saṃparko yadi nāsti dhigastu tat // Bc_4.93 //
children.translated_text: if there is no connection in every aspect of one's being — fie upon it! // Bc_4.93 //

children.text: adhṛteḥ śraddadhānasya saktasyādoṣadarśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who is unsteady, credulous, attached, and blind to faults —

children.text: kiṃ hi vañcayitavyaṃ syājjātarāgasya cetasaḥ // Bc_4.94 //
children.translated_text: what would there be to deceive in a mind already seized by passion? // Bc_4.94 //

children.text: vañcayanti ca yadyevaṃ jātarāgāḥ parasparam /
children.translated_text: And if those seized by passion thus deceive each other,

children.text: nanu naiva kṣamaṃ draṣṭuṃ narāḥ strīṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ striyaḥ // Bc_4.95 //
children.translated_text: then surely it is not fitting for men to look upon women, nor women upon men! // Bc_4.95 //

children.text: tadevaṃ sati duḥkhārta jarāmaraṇabhāginam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, being thus afflicted by suffering, subject to old age and death,

children.text: na māṃ kāmeṣvanāryeṣu pratārayitumarhasi // Bc_4.96 //
children.translated_text: you should not seek to lead me astray into ignoble pleasures. // Bc_4.96 //

children.text: aho 'tidhīraṃ balavacca te manaścaleṣu kāmeṣu ca sāradarśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, how exceedingly resolute and strong is your mind, which sees substance in fleeting pleasures!

children.text: bhaye 'titīvre viṣayeṣu sajjase nirīkṣamāṇo maraṇādhvani prajāḥ // Bc_4.97 //
children.translated_text: You cling to sense-objects while beholding creatures on the road of death, in the midst of terrible fear! // Bc_4.97 //

children.text: ahaṃ punarbhīruratīvaviklavo jarāvipadvyādhibhayaṃ vicintayan /
children.translated_text: But I, timid and exceedingly agitated, contemplating the danger of old age, calamity, and disease,

children.text: labhe na śāntiṃ na dhṛtiṃ kuto ratiṃ niśāmayandīptamivāgninā jagat // Bc_4.98 //
children.translated_text: find neither peace, nor steadiness, much less delight — seeing the world as if ablaze with fire. // Bc_4.98 //

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ mṛtyuriti prajānato narasya rāgo hṛdi yasya jāyate /
children.translated_text: When desire arises in the heart of a man who knows that death is certain,

children.text: ayomayīṃ tasya paraimi cetanāṃ mahābhaye rajyati yo na roditi // Bc_4.99 //
children.translated_text: I consider his consciousness to be made of iron — who delights and does not weep in the face of great danger!' // Bc_4.99 //

children.text: atho kumāraśca viniścayātmikāṃ cakāra kāmāśrayaghātinīṃ kathām /
children.translated_text: Then the prince made a speech of firm resolve, destructive of the abode of desire;

children.text: janasya cakṣurgamanīyamaṇḍalo mahīdharaṃ cāstamiyāya bhāskaraḥ // Bc_4.100 //
children.translated_text: and the sun, whose orb was pleasing to the eyes of all, set behind the mountain. // Bc_4.100 //

children.text: tato vṛthādhāritabhūṣaṇasrajaḥ kalāguṇaiśca praṇayaiśca niṣphalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, their ornaments and garlands worn in vain, their skills and charms and affections fruitless,

children.text: sva eva bhāve vinigṛhya manmathaṃ puraṃ yayurbhagnamanorathāḥ striyaḥ // Bc_4.101 //
children.translated_text: suppressing desire within themselves, the women returned to the city, their hopes shattered. // Bc_4.101 //

children.text: tataḥ purodyānagatāṃ janaśriyaṃ nirīkṣya sāyaṃ pratisaṃhṛtāṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, observing the beauty of the people who had gone to the pleasure garden in the city now withdrawn at evening,

children.text: anityatāṃ sarvagatāṃ vicintayanviveśa dhiṣṇayaṃ kṣitipālakātmajaḥ // Bc_4.102 //
children.translated_text: reflecting on the impermanence pervading everything, the son of the king entered his dwelling. // Bc_4.102 //

children.text: tataḥ śrutvā rājā viṣayavimukhaṃ tasya tu mano
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that his son's mind was averse to sense-pleasures, the king

children.text: na śiśye tāṃ rātriṃ hṛdayagataśalyo gaja iva /
children.translated_text: did not sleep that night, like an elephant with a dart lodged in his heart;

children.text: atha śrānto mantre bahuvividhamārge sasacivo
children.translated_text: and then, wearied in counsel with his ministers over many diverse strategies,

children.text: na so 'nyatkāmebhyo niyamanamapaśyatsutamateḥ // Bc_4.103 //
children.translated_text: he could see no other restraint for his son's resolve than pleasures. // Bc_4.103 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye strīvighātano nāma caturthaḥ sargaḥ // 4 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth canto, named 'The Repelling of Women,' in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>. // 4 //
CANTO V

children.text: sa tathā viṣayairvilobhyamānaḥ paramārhairapi śākyarājasūnuḥ /
children.translated_text: Though thus enticed with the most exquisite sense-pleasures, the son of the <s>Śākya</s> king —

children.text: na jagāma dhṛtiṃ na śarma lebhe hṛdaye siṃha ivātidigdhaviddhaḥ // Bc_5.1 //
children.translated_text: he found no firmness, nor did he find peace — in his heart, like a lion deeply pierced by a poisoned [arrow]. // 5.1 //

children.text: atha mantisutaiḥ kṣamaiḥ kadācitsakhibhiścitrakathaiḥ kṛtānuyātraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, at some time, accompanied by capable sons of ministers and friends skilled in entertaining tales,

children.text: vanabhūmididṛkṣayā śamepsurnaradevānumato bahiḥ pratasthe // Bc_5.2 //
children.translated_text: desiring to see the forest land, wishing for peace, with the permission of the god among men, he set forth. // 5.2 //

children.text: navarukmakhalīnakiṅkiṇīkaṃ pracalaccāramaracāruhemabhāṇḍam /
children.translated_text: Having mounted <s>Kanthaka</s>, a noble steed, with a bridle of new gold, tinkling bells,

children.text: abhiruhya sa kanthakaṃ sadaśvaṃ prayayau ketumiva drumābjaketuḥ // Bc_5.3 //
children.translated_text: and beautiful swaying golden trappings — he rode forth like a banner, like a tree adorned with lotuses. // 5.3 //

children.text: sa vikṛṣṭatarāṃ vanāntabhūmiṃ vanalobhācca yayau mahīguṇācca /
children.translated_text: He went to a more distant tract of forest, from love of the forest and from the virtues of the earth;

children.text: salilormivikārasīramārgāṃ vasudhāṃ caiva dadarśa kṛṣyamāṇām // Bc_5.4 //
children.translated_text: and he saw the earth being ploughed, with furrows like the ripples of water. // 5.4 //

children.text: halabhinnavikīrṇaśaṣpadarbhā hatasūkṣmakrimikīṭajantukīrṇām /
children.translated_text: The soil was torn by the plough, its grass and <s>darbha</s> scattered, strewn with slain tiny worms, insects, and creatures —

children.text: samavekṣya rasāṃ tathāvidhāṃ tāṃ svajanasyeva vadhe bhṛśaṃ śuśoca // Bc_5.5 //
children.translated_text: beholding the earth in such a state, he grieved deeply as if at the slaughter of his own people. // 5.5 //

children.text: kṛṣataḥ puruṣāṃśca vīkṣamāṇaḥ pavanārkāśurajovibhinnavarṇān /
children.translated_text: And seeing the men who were ploughing, their complexions marred by wind, sun, and dust,

children.text: vahanaklamaviklavāṃśca dhuryān paramāryaḥ paramāṃ kṛpāṃ cakāra // Bc_5.6 //
children.translated_text: and the draft-oxen bearing fatigue and distress — the supremely noble one felt supreme compassion. // 5.6 //

children.text: avatīrya tatasturaṅgapṛṣṭhācchanakairgā vyacaracchucā parītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dismounting from the horse's back, he walked slowly, overcome with sorrow,

children.text: jagato jananavyayaṃ vicinvan kṛpaṇaṃ khalvidamityuvāca cārtaḥ // Bc_5.7 //
children.translated_text: reflecting on the birth and decay of the world, and in distress he said: 'Pitiable indeed is this!' // 5.7 //

children.text: manasā ca viviktatāmabhīpsuḥ suhṛdastānanuyāyino nivārya /
children.translated_text: And desiring solitude with his mind, turning away the friends who accompanied him,

children.text: abhitaścalacāruparṇavatyā vijane mūlamupeyivān sa jambvāḥ // Bc_5.8 //
children.translated_text: he approached the root of a <s>jambū</s> tree in a secluded spot, with beautiful trembling leaves all around. // 5.8 //

children.text: niṣasāda sa yatra śaucavatyāṃ bhuvi vaidūryanikāśaśādvalāyām /
children.translated_text: He sat down there upon the pure ground, on a sward resembling <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl),

children.text: jagataḥ prabhavavyayau vicinvanmanasaśca sthitimārgamālalambe // Bc_5.9 //
children.translated_text: and reflecting on the arising and passing away of the world, he took hold of the path of steadiness of mind. // 5.9 //

children.text: samavāptamanaḥsthitiśca sadyo viṣayecchādibhirādhibhiśca muktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having at once attained steadiness of mind, freed from the afflictions of desire for sense-objects and such,

children.text: savitarkavicāramāpa śāntaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamanāsravaprakāram // Bc_5.10 //
children.translated_text: he attained the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), peaceful, accompanied by deliberation and reflection, of the type free from impurities. // 5.10 //

children.text: adhigamya tato vivekajaṃ tu paramaprītisukhaṃ manaḥsamādhim /
children.translated_text: Then, having attained the supreme joy and happiness of mental <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) born of discernment,

children.text: idameva tataḥ paraṃ pradadhyau manasā lokagatiṃ niśāmya samyak // Bc_5.11 //
children.translated_text: from that point he reflected thus further, having rightly observed the course of the world: // 5.11 //

children.text: kṛpaṇaṃ bata yajjanaḥ svayaṃ sannavaśo vyādhijarāvināśadharmā /
children.translated_text: 'Pitiable it is that humankind, itself being subject to the law of disease, old age, and destruction, helpless —

children.text: jarayārditamāturaṃ mṛtaṃ vā paramajño vijugupsate madāndhaḥ // Bc_5.12 //
children.translated_text: blinded by pride, looks with disgust upon another who is stricken by age, sick, or dead, being supremely ignorant!' // 5.12 //

children.text: iha cedahamīdṛśaḥ svayaṃ sanvijugupseya paraṃ tathāsvabhāvam /
children.translated_text: 'If I, being myself of such a nature, were to look with disgust upon another who is of such a nature,

children.text: na bhavetsadṛśaṃ hi tatkṣamaṃ vā paramaṃ dharmamimaṃ vijānato me // Bc_5.13 //
children.translated_text: that would be neither fitting nor proper for me, who knows this supreme <s>dharma</s>.' // 5.13 //

children.text: iti tasya vipaśyato yathāvajjagato vyādhijarāvipattidoṣān /
children.translated_text: Thus, as he rightly perceived the faults of disease, old age, and calamity of the world,

children.text: balayauvanajīvitapravṛtto vijagāmātmagato madaḥ kṣaṇena // Bc_5.14 //
children.translated_text: the intoxication born of strength, youth, and life departed from him in an instant, [absorbed] within his own self. // 5.14 //

children.text: na jaharṣa na cāpi cānutepe vicikitsāṃ na yayau na tandrinidre /
children.translated_text: He neither rejoiced, nor did he regret; he did not fall into doubt, nor into torpor or sleep;

children.text: na ca kāmaguṇeṣu saṃrarañje na vididveṣa paraṃ na cāvamene // Bc_5.15 //
children.translated_text: he neither delighted in the qualities of sensual pleasures, nor did he hate or despise another. // 5.15 //

children.text: iti buddhiriyaṃ ca nīrajaskā vavṛdhe tasya mahātmano viśuddhā /
children.translated_text: Thus this pure, dustless understanding grew in that great soul;

children.text: puruṣairaparairadṛśyamānaḥ puruṣaścopasasarpa bhikṣuveṣaḥ // Bc_5.16 //
children.translated_text: and unseen by other men, a man in the guise of a mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) approached him. // 5.16 //

children.text: naradevasutastamabhyapṛcchadvada ko 'sīti śaśaṃsa so 'tha tasmai /
children.translated_text: The son of the god among men questioned him: 'Tell me, who are you?' And he declared to him:

children.text: narapuṃgava janmamṛtyubhītaḥ śramaṇaḥ pravrajito 'smi mokṣahetoḥ // Bc_5.17 //
children.translated_text: 'O bull among men, frightened by birth and death, I am a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic wanderer), gone forth for the sake of liberation. // 5.17 //

children.text: jagati kṣayadharmake mumukṣarmṛgaye 'haṃ śivamakṣayaṃ padaṃ tat /
children.translated_text: 'In this world subject to the law of decay, I seek that auspicious, imperishable state — desiring liberation;

children.text: svajane 'nyajane ca tulyabuddhirviṣayebhyo vinivṛttarāgadoṣaḥ // Bc_5.18 //
children.translated_text: equal-minded toward my own people and others, with passion and aversion turned away from sense objects. // 5.18 //

children.text: nivasan kvacideva vṛkṣamūle vijane vāyatane girau vane vā /
children.translated_text: 'Dwelling here and there — at the root of a tree, in a deserted temple, on a mountain, or in a forest —

children.text: vicarāmyaparigraho nirāśaḥ paramārthāya yathopapannabhaikṣaḥ // Bc_5.19 //
children.translated_text: I wander possessionless, without expectations, for the supreme goal, subsisting on whatever alms come my way.' // 5.19 //

children.text: iti paśyata eva rājasūnoridamuktvā sa nabhaḥ samutpapāta /
children.translated_text: Having said this, even as the prince watched, he rose up into the sky;

children.text: sa hi tadvapuranyabuddhadarśī smṛtaye tasya sameyivāndivaukāḥ // Bc_5.20 //
children.translated_text: for he was a celestial being who, perceiving [the prince's] readiness for another <s>Buddha</s>-vision, had come to remind him. // 5.20 //

children.text: gaganaṃ khagavadgate ca tasminṛvaraḥ saṃjahṛṣe visismiye ca /
children.translated_text: When that one had gone into the sky like a bird, the best of men was both delighted and astonished;

children.text: upalabhya tataśca dharmasaṃjñāmabhiniryāṇavidhau matiṃ cakāra // Bc_5.21 //
children.translated_text: and having thereby obtained the concept of <s>dharma</s>, he formed the resolve to go forth. // 5.21 //

children.text: tata indrasamo jitendriyāśvaḥ pravivikṣuḥ puramaśvamāruroha /
children.translated_text: Then, like <s>Indra</s>, he whose steed was his conquered senses, wishing to enter the city, mounted his horse;

children.text: parivārajanaṃ tvavekṣamāṇastata evābhimataṃ vanaṃ na bheje // Bc_5.22 //
children.translated_text: but looking at the retinue of attendants, he did not go to the beloved forest from that point. // 5.22 //

children.text: sa jarāmaraṇakṣayaṃ cikīrṣurvanavāsāya matiṃ smṛtau nidhāya /
children.translated_text: He, desiring to destroy old age and death, having placed in his memory the resolve for forest-dwelling,

children.text: praviveśa punaḥ puraṃ na kāmādvanabhūmeriva maṇḍalaṃ dvipendraḥ // Bc_5.23 //
children.translated_text: entered the city again — not from desire, like a lord of elephants [returning] from the forest-land to the enclosure. // 5.23 //

children.text: sukhitā bata nirvṛtā ca sā strī patirīdṛkṣa ihāyatākṣa yasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Happy indeed, and content is that woman whose husband is such as this, with wide eyes!' —

children.text: iti taṃ samudīkṣya rājakanyā praviśantaṃ pathi sāñjalirjagāda // Bc_5.24 //
children.translated_text: thus said a royal maiden, with palms joined, seeing him entering on the road. // 5.24 //

children.text: atha ghoṣamimaṃ mahābhraghoṣaḥ pariśuśrāva śamaṃ paraṃ ca lebhe /
children.translated_text: Then he, of thundercloud-deep voice, heard this proclamation and attained supreme peace;

children.text: śrutavānsa hi nirvṛteti śabdaṃ parinirvāṇavidhau matiṃ cakāra // Bc_5.25 //
children.translated_text: for having heard the word <s>nirvṛtā</s> ('content' / 'extinguished'), he formed the resolve regarding the path of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation). // 5.25 //

children.text: atha kāñcanaśailaśṛṅgavarṣmā gajamegharṣabhabāhunisvanākṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he, whose body was like the peak of a golden mountain, whose arms, voice, and eyes were like an elephant, a cloud, a bull,

children.text: kṣayamakṣayadharmajātarāgaḥ śaśisiṃhānanavikramaḥ prapede // Bc_5.26 //
children.translated_text: with passion arisen for the imperishable <s>dharma</s> of destruction [of suffering], with the gait, face, and prowess of the moon and a lion — entered [the palace]. // 5.26 //

children.text: mṛgarājagatistato 'bhyagacchannṛpatiṃ mantrigaṇairupāsyamānam /
children.translated_text: With the gait of a king of beasts, he then approached the king, who was attended by groups of ministers,

children.text: samitau marutāmiva jvalantaṃ maghavantaṃ tridive sanatkumāraḥ // Bc_5.27 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Sanatkumāra</s> [approaching] <s>Maghavat</s> (<s>Indra</s>), blazing in the assembly of the <s>Maruts</s> in the third heaven. // 5.27 //

children.text: praṇipatya ca sāñjalirbabhāṣe diśa mahyaṃ naradeva sādhvanujñām /
children.translated_text: And bowing down, with palms joined, he said: 'Grant me, O god among men, your gracious permission;

children.text: parivivrajiṣāmi mokṣahetorniyato hyasya janasya viprayogaḥ // Bc_5.28 //
children.translated_text: I wish to go forth for the sake of liberation, for the separation of this being [from loved ones] is certain.' // 5.28 //

children.text: iti tasya vaco niśamya rājā kariṇevābhihato drumaścacāla /
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of his, the king trembled like a tree struck by an elephant;

children.text: kamalapratime 'ñjalau gṛhītvā vacanaṃ cedamuvāca bāṣpakaṇṭhaḥ // Bc_5.29 //
children.translated_text: and grasping his lotus-like joined hands, he spoke this utterance, his throat choked with tears: // 5.29 //

children.text: pratisaṃhara tāt buddhimetāṃ na hi kālastava dharmasaṃśrayasya /
children.translated_text: 'Withdraw this intention, my son — for it is not the time for you to resort to <s>dharma</s> [as a renunciant];

children.text: vayasi prathame matau calāyāṃ bahudoṣāṃ hi vadanti dharmacaryām // Bc_5.30 //
children.translated_text: for they say that the practice of <s>dharma</s> [as renunciation] in the first stage of life, when the mind is unsteady, has many faults. // 5.30 //

children.text: viṣayeṣu kutūhalendriyasya vratakhedeṣvasamarthīniścayasya /
children.translated_text: 'For one young in years, whose senses are curious about objects, who lacks the capacity for the hardships of vows,

children.text: taruṇasya manaścalatyaraṇyādanabhijñaśca viśeṣato viveke // Bc_5.31 //
children.translated_text: the mind wanders from the forest — especially for one unacquainted with the distinctions of discernment. // 5.31 //

children.text: mama tu priyadharma dharmakālastvayi lakṣmīmavasṛjya lakṣmabhūte /
children.translated_text: 'But for me, O lover of <s>dharma</s>, it is the time for <s>dharma</s>; having released sovereignty to you, who are fit for sovereignty,

children.text: sthiravikrama vikrameṇa dharmastava hitvā tu guruṃ bhavedadharmaḥ // Bc_5.32 //
children.translated_text: O steadfast hero — for to pursue <s>dharma</s> by heroic stride while abandoning one's elder would be <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness). // 5.32 //

children.text: tadimaṃ vyavasāyamutsṛja tvaṃ bhava tāvannirato gṛhasthadharme /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, abandon this resolution; be devoted for now to the <s>dharma</s> of a householder;

children.text: puruṣasya vayaḥsukhāni bhuktvā ramaṇīyo hi tapovanapraveśaḥ // Bc_5.33 //
children.translated_text: for having enjoyed the pleasures appropriate to one's age, entry into the ascetic forest is delightful.' // 5.33 //

children.text: iti vākyamidaṃ niśamya rājñaḥ kalaviṅkasvara uttaraṃ babhāṣe /
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of the king, he of the <s>kalaviṅka</s>-bird's (sparrow's) voice spoke in reply:

children.text: yadi me pratibhūtaścaturṣu rājan bhavasi tvaṃ na tapovanaṃ śrayiṣye // Bc_5.34 //
children.translated_text: 'If you will be my guarantor in four matters, O king, I will not resort to the ascetic forest: // 5.34 //

children.text: na bhavenmaraṇāya jīvitaṃ me viharetsvāsthyamidaṃ ca me na rogaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That my life shall not lead to death; that this my health shall not be [undermined by] disease;

children.text: na ca yauvanamākṣipejjarā me na ca saṃpattimimāṃ haredvipattiḥ // Bc_5.35 //
children.translated_text: that old age shall not seize my youth; and that misfortune shall not rob me of this prosperity.' // 5.35 //

children.text: iti durlabhamarthamūcivāṃsaṃ tanayaṃ vākyamuvāca śākyarājaḥ /
children.translated_text: To his son, who had spoken of [this] difficult-to-obtain goal, the king of the <s>Śākyas</s> said:

children.text: tyaja buddhimimāmatipravṛttāmavahāsyo 'timanoratho 'kramaśca // Bc_5.36 //
children.translated_text: 'Abandon this excessively extravagant intention — you are to be laughed at; this is a fantasy and out of order.' // 5.36 //

children.text: atha merugururguruṃ babhāṣe yadi nāsti krama eṣa nāsmi vāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he, weighty as <s>Meru</s>, said to his father: 'If this course [of renunciation] does not exist, I should not be restrained;

children.text: śaraṇājjvalanena dahyamānānna hi niścikramiṣuḥ kṣamaṃ grahītum // Bc_5.37 //
children.translated_text: for it is not right to hold back one who seeks to escape from a burning house.' // 5.37 //

children.text: jagataśca yadā dhruvo viyogo nanu dharmāya varaṃ svayaviyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And since separation from the world is certain, is not voluntary separation for the sake of <s>dharma</s> better?

children.text: avaśaṃ nanu viprayojayenmāmakṛtasvārthamatṛptameva mṛtyuḥ // Bc_5.38 //
children.translated_text: For would not death forcibly separate me, with my purpose unfulfilled and my desires unsatisfied?' // 5.38 //

children.text: iti bhūmipatirniśamya tasya vyavasāyaṃ tanayasya nirmumukṣoḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the resolution of his son who wished to be liberated, the lord of the earth,

children.text: abhidhāya na yāsyatīti bhūyo vidadhe rakṣaṇamuttamāṃśca kāmān // Bc_5.39 //
children.translated_text: declaring 'He shall not go,' arranged yet again guards and the highest sensual pleasures. // 5.39 //

children.text: sacivaistu nidarśito yathāvad bahumānātpraṇayācca śāstrapūrvam /
children.translated_text: But having been shown by the ministers, as was fitting, [the path of duty] preceded by scripture, with respect and affection,

children.text: guruṇā ca nivārito 'śrupātaiḥ praviveśāvasathaṃ tataḥ sa śocan // Bc_5.40 //
children.translated_text: and having been restrained by his elder with a shedding of tears — he then entered his dwelling, grieving. // 5.40 //

children.text: calakuṇḍalacumbitānanābhirghananiśvāsavikampitastanībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By women with trembling earrings kissing their cheeks, their breasts heaving with deep sighs,

children.text: vanitābhiradhīralocanābhimṛrgaśāvābhirivābhyudīkṣyamāṇaḥ // Bc_5.41 //
children.translated_text: with restless eyes — like young fawns — he was gazed upon. // 5.41 //

children.text: sa hi kāñcanaparvatāvadāto hṛdayenmādakaro varāṅganānām /
children.translated_text: For he, fair as a mountain of gold, captivating the hearts of the beautiful women,

children.text: śravaṇāṅgavilocanātmabhāvānvacanasparśavapurguṇairjahāra // Bc_5.42 //
children.translated_text: stole their hearing, limbs, eyes, and very selves — by his voice, touch, form, and virtues. // 5.42 //

children.text: vigate divase tato vimānaṃ vapuṣā sūrya iva pradīpyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, when the day had passed, blazing in beauty like the sun, into the palace,

children.text: timiraṃ vijighāṃsurātmabhāsā ravirudyanniva merumāruroha // Bc_5.43 //
children.translated_text: wishing to dispel the darkness with his own radiance — like the sun rising and ascending <s>Meru</s> — he ascended. // 5.43 //

children.text: kanakojjvaladīptadīpavṛkṣaṃ varakālāgurudhūpapūrṇagarbham /
children.translated_text: The [palace], with trees of lamps blazing bright with gold, its interior filled with the smoke of fine dark <s>aguru</s> (aloe) incense,

children.text: adhiruhya sa vajrabhakticitraṃ pravaraṃ kāñcanamāsanaṃ siṣeve // Bc_5.44 //
children.translated_text: having ascended [it], he sat upon the excellent golden seat, variegated with diamond inlay. // 5.44 //

children.text: tata uttamamuttamāṅganāstaṃ niśi tūryairupatasthurindrakalpam /
children.translated_text: Then, at night, the finest women attended him — like <s>Indra</s> — with instruments,

children.text: himavacchirasīva candragaure draviṇendrātmajamapsarogaṇaughāḥ // Bc_5.45 //
children.translated_text: like hosts of <s>Apsaras</s> [attending] the son of the lord of riches (<s>Kubera</s>) upon the moon-white peak of <s>Himavat</s>. // 5.45 //

children.text: paramairapi divyatūryakalpaiḥ sa tu tairnaiva ratiṃ yayau na harṣam /
children.translated_text: But even with those [instruments], equal to the finest divine music, he felt neither delight nor pleasure;

children.text: paramārthasukhāya tasya sādhorabhiniścikramiṣā yato na reme // Bc_5.46 //
children.translated_text: for that virtuous one, whose desire was to go forth for the sake of supreme truth, found no enjoyment. // 5.46 //

children.text: atha tatra suraistapovariṣṭhairakaniṣṭhairvyavasāyamasya buddhvā /
children.translated_text: Then, the gods of the highest <s>tapas</s>, the <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s>, having understood his resolve,

children.text: yugapatpramadājanasya nidrā vihitāsīdvikṛtāśca gātraceṣṭāḥ // Bc_5.47 //
children.translated_text: caused sleep to fall simultaneously upon the crowd of pleasure-women, and [caused] distorted postures of their limbs. // 5.47 //

children.text: abhavacchayitā hi tatra kācidviniveśya pracale kare kapolam /
children.translated_text: For one [woman] there lay sleeping, having placed her cheek upon her unsteady hand,

children.text: dayitāmapi rukmapattracitrāṃ kupitevāṅkagatāṃ vihāya vīṇām // Bc_5.48 //
children.translated_text: as if in anger, having cast aside even her beloved <s>vīṇā</s>, beautiful with gold-leaf designs, which had been upon her lap. // 5.48 //

children.text: vibabhau karalagnaveṇuranyā stanavisrastasitāṃśukā śayānā /
children.translated_text: Another lay sleeping, a bamboo flute gripped in her hand, with her white garment slipped from her breasts,

children.text: ṛjuṣaṭpadapaṅktijuṣṭapadmā jalaphenaprahasattaṭā nadīva // Bc_5.49 //
children.translated_text: like a river with lotuses attended by a line of straight-flying bees, with foam laughing on its banks. // 5.49 //

children.text: navapuṣkaragarbhakomalābhyāṃ tapanīyojjvalasaṃgatāṅgadābhyām /
children.translated_text: With arms tender as the interior of fresh lotuses, gleaming with ornaments of burnished gold,

children.text: svapiti sma tathāparā bhujābhyāṃ parirabhya priyavanmṛdaṅgameva // Bc_5.50 //
children.translated_text: another slept thus, embracing a drum as if it were a beloved, with both her arms. // 5.50 //

children.text: navahāṭakabhūṣaṇāstathānyā vasanaṃ pītamanuttamaṃ vasānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others, adorned with new gold ornaments, wearing supreme yellow garments,

children.text: avaśā ghananidrayā nipeturgajabhagnā iva karṇikāraśākhāḥ // Bc_5.51 //
children.translated_text: fell helpless in deep sleep, like branches of the <s>karṇikāra</s> tree broken by an elephant. // 5.51 //

children.text: avalambya gavākṣapārśvamanyā śayitā cāpavibhugnagātrayaṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Another, leaning against the side of a window, lying with her body-staff bent like a bow,

children.text: virarāja vilambicāruhārā racitā toraṇāśālabhañjikeva // Bc_5.52 //
children.translated_text: shone with her beautiful necklace hanging down, like a sculpted <s>śālabhañjikā</s> (bracket-figure) fashioned on an arched gateway. // 5.52 //

children.text: maṇikuṇḍaladaṣṭapattralekhaṃ mukhapadmaṃ vinataṃ tathāparasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The lotus-face of yet another, bent down, with the lines of its painted leaf-designs scratched by her jeweled earrings,

children.text: śatapattramivārdhavakranāḍaṃ sthitakāraṇḍavaghaṭṭitaṃ cakāśe // Bc_5.53 //
children.translated_text: gleamed like a hundred-petaled [lotus], half-bent on its stalk, struck by a hovering <s>kāraṇḍava</s> duck. // 5.53 //

children.text: aparāḥ śayitā yathopaviṣṭāḥ stanabhārairavanamyamānagātrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others, sleeping as if seated, their bodies bent by the weight of their breasts,

children.text: upaguhya parasparaṃ virejurbhujapāśaistapanīyaparihāryaiḥ // Bc_5.54 //
children.translated_text: embracing one another, shone with arm-fetters [adorned] with gold ornaments. // 5.54 //

children.text: mahatī parivādinī ca kācidvanitāliṅgya sakhīmiva prasuptā /
children.translated_text: And one, having embraced a large <s>parivādinī</s> (long-necked lute) like a friend, lay fast asleep,

children.text: vijughūrṇa calatsuvarṇasūtrā vadanenākulakarṇikojjvalena // Bc_5.55 //
children.translated_text: rolling about, with her golden thread-chain swaying, her face bright with ear-ornaments in disarray. // 5.55 //

children.text: paṇavaṃ yuvatirbhujāṃsadeśādavavisraṃsitacārūpāśamanyā /
children.translated_text: Another young woman, with a <s>paṇava</s> (small drum) that had slipped from the region of her shoulder, its beautiful strap loosened,

children.text: savilāsaratāntatāntamūrvorvivare kāntamivābhinīya śiśye // Bc_5.56 //
children.translated_text: having drawn it to the space between her thighs — languid from playful love-exertion — as if a beloved, lay sleeping. // 5.56 //

children.text: aparā babhūvurnimīlitākṣyo vipulākṣyo 'pi śubhabhruvo 'pi satyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Others lay with their eyes closed, though their eyes were large, and their brows were beautiful —

children.text: pratisaṃkucitāravindakośāḥ savitaryastamite yathā nalinyaḥ // Bc_5.57 //
children.translated_text: like lotus-pools with their lotus-buds contracted when the sun has set. // 5.57 //

children.text: śithilākulamūrdhajā tathānyā jaghanasrastavibhūṣaṇāṃśukāntā /
children.translated_text: Another lay there, her hair loosened and disheveled, her ornaments and garment-edges fallen from her hips,

children.text: aśayiṣṭa vikīrṇakaṇṭhasūtrā gajabhagnā pratiyātanāṅganeva // Bc_5.58 //
children.translated_text: her necklace scattered — like a woman whose limbs have been trampled by an elephant at a waystation. // 5.58 //

children.text: aparāstvavaśā hriyā viyuktā dhṛtimatyo 'pi vapurguṇairupetāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others still, helpless, bereft of modesty — though women of firmness and endowed with bodily virtues —

children.text: viniśaśvasurulbaṇaṃ śayānā vikṛtāḥ kṣiptabhūjā jajṛmbhire ca // Bc_5.59 //
children.translated_text: lay breathing heavily, their bodies distorted, arms flung out, and they yawned. // 5.59 //

children.text: vyapaviddhavibhūṣaṇasrajo 'nyā visṛtāgranthanavāsaso visaṃjñāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others, their ornaments and garlands cast aside, their garments loosened and untied, unconscious —

children.text: animīlitaśuklaniścalākṣyo na virejuḥ śayitā gatāsukalpāḥ // Bc_5.60 //
children.translated_text: with unblinking, white, motionless eyes, they did not shine — sleeping, they appeared as if lifeless. // Bc_5.60 //

children.text: vivṛtāsyapuṭā vivṛddhagātrī prapatadvaktrajalā prakāśaguhyā /
children.translated_text: Another, with gaping mouth, limbs spread wide, saliva falling from her face, her private parts exposed,

children.text: aparā madaghūrṇiteva śiśye na babhāse vikṛtaṃ vapuḥ pupoṣa // Bc_5.61 //
children.translated_text: lay as if stupefied by drink — she did not shine, her body having assumed a distorted form. // Bc_5.61 //

children.text: iti sattvakulānvayānurūpaṃ vividhaṃ sa pramadājanaḥ śayānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, those women of pleasure, sleeping in various [postures] corresponding to their lineage of character and family,

children.text: sarasaḥ sadṛśaṃ babhāra rūpaṃ pavanāvarjitarugnapuṣkarasya // Bc_5.62 //
children.translated_text: bore the appearance of a lotus pond whose lotuses had been broken and bent down by the wind. // Bc_5.62 //

children.text: samavekṣya tathā tathā śayānā vikṛtāstā yuvatīradhīraceṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having observed the young women lying thus and thus, distorted and of unsteady movements,

children.text: guṇavadvapuṣo 'pi valgubhāṣā nṛpasūnuḥ sa vigarhayāṃbabhūva // Bc_5.63 //
children.translated_text: the prince, though their bodies were endowed with qualities and their speech was charming, felt disgust. // Bc_5.63 //

children.text: aśucirvikṛtaśca jīvaloke vanitānāmayamīdṛśaḥ svabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Impure and distorted — such is the nature of women in the world of the living;

children.text: vasanābharaṇaistu vañcyamānaḥ puruṣaḥ strīviṣayeṣu rāgameti // Bc_5.64 //
children.translated_text: yet, deceived by garments and ornaments, a man develops passion for the objects of women. // Bc_5.64 //

children.text: vimṛśedyadi yoṣitāṃ manuṣyaḥ prakṛtiṃ svapnavikāramīdṛśaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: If a man were to consider the true nature of women and this kind of transformation in sleep,

children.text: dhruvamatra na vardhayetpramādaṃ guṇasaṃkalpahatastu rāgameti // Bc_5.65 //
children.translated_text: surely he would not increase his heedlessness — but struck by the fancy of [their] qualities, he develops passion." // Bc_5.65 //

children.text: iti tasya tadantaraṃ viditvā niśi niścikramiṣā samudbabhūva /
children.translated_text: Having perceived that opening, his desire to depart in the night arose;

children.text: avagamya manastato 'sya devairbhavanadvāramapāvṛtaṃ babhūva // Bc_5.66 //
children.translated_text: and the gods, having understood his mind, caused the doors of the palace to be opened. // Bc_5.66 //

children.text: atha so 'vatatāra harmyapṛṣṭhādyuvatīstāḥ śayitā vigarhamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he descended from the palace roof, disdaining those sleeping women,

children.text: avatīrya tataśca nirviśaṅko gṛhakakṣyāṃ prathamāṃ vinirjagāma // Bc_5.67 //
children.translated_text: and having descended, without hesitation he passed through the first enclosure of the palace. // Bc_5.67 //

children.text: turagāvacaraṃ sa bodhayitvā javinaṃ chandakamitthamityuvāca /
children.translated_text: Having awakened his swift horse-attendant <s>Chandaka</s>, he spoke to him thus:

children.text: hayamānaya kanthakaṃ tvarāvānamṛtaṃ prāptumito 'dya me yiyāsā // Bc_5.68 //
children.translated_text: "Bring the horse <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, quickly — my desire is to depart from here today to attain the deathless." // Bc_5.68 //

children.text: hṛdi yā mama tuṣṭiradya jātā vyavasāyaśca yathā matau niviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The contentment that has arisen in my heart today, and the resolve that has settled in my mind,

children.text: vijane 'pi ca nāthavānivāsmi dhruvamartho 'bhimukhaḥ sameta iṣṭaḥ // Bc_5.69 //
children.translated_text: and that even in solitude I feel as if protected — surely the desired goal has come to meet me. // Bc_5.69 //

children.text: hriyameva ca saṃnatiṃ ca hitvā śayitā matpramukhe yathā yuvatyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since these young women have cast aside modesty and propriety, sleeping before me thus,

children.text: vivṛte ca yathā svayaṃ kapāṭe niyataṃ yātumato mamādya kālaḥ // Bc_5.70 //
children.translated_text: and since the doors have opened by themselves — surely this is the time for my departure. // Bc_5.70 //

children.text: pratigṛhya tataḥ sa bharturājñāṃ viditārtho 'pi narendraśāsanasya /
children.translated_text: Then, receiving his master's command, though aware of the king's orders,

children.text: manasīva pareṇa codyamānasturagasyānayane matiṃ cakāra // Bc_5.71 //
children.translated_text: as if impelled by another force in his mind, he set his thoughts to bringing the horse. // Bc_5.71 //

children.text: atha hemakhalīnapūrṇavaktraṃ laghuśayyāstaraṇopagūḍhapṛṣṭham /
children.translated_text: Then he brought to his master that excellent horse, whose mouth was filled with a golden bit,

children.text: balasattvajavānvayopapannaṃ sa varāśvaṃ tamupānināya bhartre // Bc_5.72 //
children.translated_text: whose back was covered with a light saddle-cloth, endowed with strength, spirit, speed, and noble lineage. // Bc_5.72 //

children.text: pratatrikapucchamūlapārṣṇi nibhṛtahṛsvatanūjapucchakarṇam /
children.translated_text: With outstretched tail-base and heels, with quietly [set] short offspring-tail and ears,

children.text: vinatonnatapṛṣṭhakukṣipārśva vipulaprothalalāṭakaṭyuraskam // Bc_5.73 //
children.translated_text: with back, belly, and flanks alternately depressed and raised, with broad nostrils, forehead, hips, and chest — // Bc_5.73 //

children.text: upaguhya sa taṃ viśālavakṣāḥ kamalābhena ca sāntvayan kareṇa /
children.translated_text: embracing him, the broad-chested [prince], soothing him with a lotus-like hand,

children.text: madhurākṣarayā girā śaśāsa dhvajinīmadhyamiva praveṣṭukāmaḥ // Bc_5.74 //
children.translated_text: commanded him with words of sweet syllables, as if wishing to enter the midst of an army: // Bc_5.74 //

children.text: bahuśaḥ kila śatravo nirastāḥ samare tvāmadhiruhya pārthivena /
children.translated_text: "Many times have enemies been repelled in battle by the king riding upon you;

children.text: ahamapyamṛtaṃ padaṃ yathāvatturagaśreṣṭha labheya tatkuruṣva // Bc_5.75 //
children.translated_text: O best of horses, may I too properly attain the deathless state — do so! // Bc_5.75 //

children.text: sulabhāḥ khalu saṃyuge sahāyā viṣayāvāptasukhe dhanārjane vā /
children.translated_text: Companions are easily found in battle, in pleasures obtained from sense objects, or in the acquisition of wealth;

children.text: puruṣasya tu durlabhāḥ sahāyāḥ patitasyāpadi dharmasaṃśraye vā // Bc_5.76 //
children.translated_text: but companions are hard to find for a man who has fallen into misfortune or who has taken refuge in <s>dharma</s>. // Bc_5.76 //
