children.text: iha caiva bhavanti ye sahāyāḥ kaluṣe karmaṇi dharmasaṃśraye vā /
children.translated_text: Those who are companions here — whether in an impure deed or in taking refuge in <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: avagacchati me yathāntarātmā niyataṃ te 'pi janāstadaṃśabhājaḥ // Bc_5.77 //
children.translated_text: as my inner self understands, those people too are surely sharers of a portion of that [fruit]. // Bc_5.77 //

children.text: tadidaṃ parigamya dharmayuktaṃ mama niryāṇamito jagaddhitāya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, understanding this departure of mine as righteous and for the welfare of the world,

children.text: turagottama vegavikramābhyāṃ prayatasvātmahite jagaddhite ca // Bc_5.78 //
children.translated_text: O best of horses, strive with your speed and valor — for the good of yourself and the good of the world!" // Bc_5.78 //

children.text: iti suhṛdamivānuśiṣya kṛtye turagavaraṃ nṛvaro vanaṃ yiyāsuḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed the excellent horse in his duty, as one would a friend, the best of men, wishing to go to the forest,

children.text: sitamasitagatidyutirvapuṣmān raviriva śāradamabhramāruroha // Bc_5.79 //
children.translated_text: resplendent in form, with the brilliance of both the white and the dark courses [of the moon], mounted him like the sun mounting an autumn cloud. // Bc_5.79 //

children.text: atha sa pariharanniśīthacaṇḍaṃ parijanabodhakaraṃ dhvanīṃ sadaśvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that noble horse, avoiding the fierce sounds of the night that would awaken the attendants,

children.text: vigatahanuravaḥ praśāntaheṣaścakitavimuktapadakramo jagāma // Bc_5.80 //
children.translated_text: with suppressed jaw-sounds, with stilled neighing, proceeded with steps released as if startled. // Bc_5.80 //

children.text: kanakavalayabhūṣitaprakoṣṭhaiḥ kamalanibhaiḥ kamalāniva pravidhya /
children.translated_text: Bowing down, the <s>Yakṣas</s>, with forearms adorned with golden bracelets, with lotus-like hands as if parting lotuses,

children.text: avanatatanavastato 'sya yakṣāścakitagatairdīdhare khurān karāgraiḥ // Bc_5.81 //
children.translated_text: held his hooves with their fingertips, moving with startled steps. // Bc_5.81 //

children.text: guruparighakapāṭasaṃvṛtā yā na sukhamapi dviradairapāvriyante /
children.translated_text: The city gates, secured with heavy bars and doors, which could not easily be opened even by elephants,

children.text: vrajati nṛpasute gatasvanāstāḥ svayamabhavanvivṛtāḥ puraḥ pratolyaḥ // Bc_5.82 //
children.translated_text: as the prince departed, became soundlessly opened by themselves. // Bc_5.82 //

children.text: pitaramabhimukhaṃ sutaṃ ca bālaṃ janamanuraktamanuttamāṃ ca lakṣmīm /
children.translated_text: Having made his resolve, without attachment, leaving behind his father who loved him, his young son,

children.text: kṛtamatirapahāya nirvyapekṣaḥ pitṛnagarātsa tato vinirjagāma // Bc_5.83 //
children.translated_text: the devoted people, and his supreme fortune, he departed from his father's city. // Bc_5.83 //

children.text: atha sa vimalapaṅkajāyatākṣaḥ puramavalokya nanāda siṃhanādam /
children.translated_text: Then he, of pure, wide, lotus-like eyes, looking back at the city, roared a lion's roar:

children.text: jananamaraṇayoradṛṣṭapāro na puramahaṃ kapilāvhayaṃ praveṣṭā // Bc_5.84 //
children.translated_text: "Until I have seen the far shore of birth and death, I shall not enter the city called <s>Kapilā</s>." // Bc_5.84 //

children.text: iti vacanamidaṃ niśamya tasya draviṇapateḥ pariṣadgaṇā nananduḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of his, the hosts attending <s>Dhanapati</s> (Kubera) rejoiced;

children.text: pramuditamanasaśca devasaṅghā vyavasitapāraṇamāśaśaṃsire 'smai // Bc_5.85 //
children.translated_text: and the assemblies of gods, their minds delighted, praised him for his resolve to cross over. // Bc_5.85 //

children.text: hutavahavapuṣoḥ divaukaso 'nye vyavasitamasya suduṣkaraṃ viditvā /
children.translated_text: Other celestial beings of fire-like splendor, knowing his resolve to be exceedingly difficult,

children.text: akṛṣata tuhine pathi prakāśaṃ ghanavivaraprasṛtā ivendupādāḥ // Bc_5.86 //
children.translated_text: cast light upon the frosty path — like moonbeams emerging from gaps in the clouds. // Bc_5.86 //

children.text: harituragaturaṅgavatturaṅgaḥ sa tu vicaranmanasīva codyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that horse, swift as the wind-coursing steeds of <s>Hari</s> (Indra), as if driven by his master's mind,

children.text: aruṇaparuṣatāramantarikṣaṃ sa ca subahūni jagāma yojanāni // Bc_5.87 //
children.translated_text: traversed a vast number of <s>yojanas</s>, under a sky of reddish, harsh stars. // Bc_5.87 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye 'bhiniṣkramaṇo nāma pañcamaḥ sargaḥ // 5 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth canto, named 'The Great Departure,' in the <s>Buddhacarita</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>. // 5 //
CANTO VI

children.text: tato muhūrtābhyudite jagaccakṣuṣi bhāskare /
children.translated_text: Then, when the sun, the eye of the world, had risen for a moment,

children.text: bhārgavasyāśramapadaṃ sa dadarśa nṛṇāṃ varaḥ // Bc_6.1 //
children.translated_text: that best of men beheld the hermitage of <s>Bhārgava</s>. // Bc_6.1 //

children.text: suptaviśvastahariṇaṃ svasthasthitavihaṅgamam /
children.translated_text: Seeing it — with its deer sleeping in trust, its birds calmly perched —

children.text: viśrānta iva yaddṛṣṭvā kṛtārtha iva cābhavat // Bc_6.2 //
children.translated_text: he became as if refreshed, as if he had attained his purpose. // Bc_6.2 //

children.text: sa vismayanivṛttyartha tapaḥpūjārthameva ca /
children.translated_text: For the sake of dispelling his wonder, for the worship of asceticism,

children.text: svāṃ cānuvartitā rakṣannaśvapṛṣṭhādavatārat // Bc_6.3 //
children.translated_text: and to protect his own follower, he dismounted from the horse's back. // Bc_6.3 //

children.text: avatīrya ca pasparśa nistīrṇamiti vājinam /
children.translated_text: Having dismounted, he stroked the horse, [saying] "you have crossed over,"

children.text: chandakaṃ cāvravītprītaḥ snāpayanniva cakṣuṣā // Bc_6.4 //
children.translated_text: and spoke to <s>Chandaka</s> with joy, as if bathing him with his eyes: // Bc_6.4 //

children.text: imaṃ tārkṣyopamajavaṃ turaṅgamanugacchatā /
children.translated_text: "By following this horse of speed equal to <s>Tārkṣya</s> (Garuḍa),

children.text: darśitā saumya madbhaktirvikramaścāyamātmanaḥ // Bc_6.5 //
children.translated_text: you have shown, O gentle one, your devotion to me, and this is your own valor. // Bc_6.5 //

children.text: sarvathāsmyanyakāryo 'pi gṛhīto bhavatā hṛdi /
children.translated_text: Though I am occupied with other purposes altogether, you have held me in your heart;

children.text: bhartusnehaśca yasyāyamīdṛśaḥ śaktireva ca // Bc_6.6 //
children.translated_text: such is your love for your master, and such indeed is your ability. // Bc_6.6 //

children.text: asnigdho 'pi samartho 'sti niḥsāmarthyo 'pi bhaktimān /
children.translated_text: One without affection may be capable, and one without capacity may be devoted;

children.text: bhaktimāṃścaiva śaktaśca durlabhastvadvidho bhuvi // Bc_6.7 //
children.translated_text: but one who is both devoted and capable — such as you — is rare on earth. // Bc_6.7 //

children.text: tatprīto 'smi tavānena mahābhāgena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, I am pleased by this noble deed of yours,

children.text: yasya te mayi bhāvo 'yaṃ phalebhyo 'pi parāṅmukhaḥ // Bc_6.8 //
children.translated_text: for your disposition toward me is indifferent even to [personal] rewards. // Bc_6.8 //

children.text: ko janasya phalasthasya na syādabhimukho janaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who would not be well-disposed toward a person who is intent on [obtaining] results?

children.text: janībhavati bhūyiṣṭhaṃ svajano 'pi viparyaye // Bc_6.9 //
children.translated_text: Even one's own people mostly become strangers in adversity. // Bc_6.9 //

children.text: kulārtha dhāryate putraḥ poṣārtha sevyate pitā /
children.translated_text: A son is maintained for the sake of the family; a father is served for the sake of sustenance;

children.text: āśayācchilaṣyati jagannāsti niṣkāraṇā svatā // Bc_6.10 //
children.translated_text: the world desires out of expectation — there is no affinity without a cause. // Bc_6.10 //

children.text: kimuktvā bahu saṃkṣepātkṛtaṃ me sumahatpriyam /
children.translated_text: What more shall I say? In brief, you have done me a very great kindness.

children.text: nivartasvāśvamādāya saṃprāpto 'smīpsitaṃ padam // Bc_6.11 //
children.translated_text: Return now, taking the horse — I have reached the desired state." // Bc_6.11 //

children.text: ityuktvā sa mahābāhuranuśaṃsacikīrṣayā /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed one, wishing to show his gratitude,

children.text: bhūṣaṇānyavamucyāsmai saṃtaptamanase dadau // Bc_6.12 //
children.translated_text: removed his ornaments and gave them to that grief-stricken one. // Bc_6.12 //

children.text: mukuṭāddīpakarmāṇaṃ maṇīmādāya bhāsvaram /
children.translated_text: Taking from his crown a brilliant gem of radiant luster,

children.text: bruvanvākyamidaṃ tasthau sāṃditya iva mandaraḥ // Bc_6.13 //
children.translated_text: he stood, uttering these words, like <s>Mandara</s> mountain touching the sun. // Bc_6.13 //

children.text: anena maṇinā chanda praṇamya bahuśo nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: "With this gem, <s>Chanda</s>, bowing many times before the king,

children.text: vijñāpyo 'muktaviśrambhaṃ saṃtāpavinivṛttaye // Bc_6.14 //
children.translated_text: he should be informed, with unshaken confidence, for the removal of his sorrow: // Bc_6.14 //

children.text: janmamaraṇanāśārtha praviṣṭo 'smi tapovanam /
children.translated_text: 'For the sake of destroying birth and death, I have entered the ascetic grove —

children.text: na khalu svargatarṣeṇa nāsnehena na manyunā // Bc_6.15 //
children.translated_text: not from a thirst for heaven, not from lack of affection, not from anger. // Bc_6.15 //

children.text: tadevamabhiniṣkrāntaṃ na māṃ śocitumarhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore you should not grieve for me who have departed thus;

children.text: bhūtvāpi hi ciraṃ śleṣaḥ kālena na bhaviṣyati // Bc_6.16 //
children.translated_text: for even a long-lasting union will, in time, cease to be. // Bc_6.16 //

children.text: dhruvo yasmācca viśleṣastasmānmokṣāya me matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since separation is certain, therefore my intention is toward liberation;

children.text: viprayogaḥ kathaṃ na syād bhūyo 'pi svajanāditi // Bc_6.17 //
children.translated_text: how could there not be separation from one's own people again and again?' // Bc_6.17 //

children.text: śokatyāgāya niṣkrāntaṃ na māṃ śocitumarhasi /
children.translated_text: 'You should not grieve for me who have departed for the abandonment of sorrow;

children.text: śokahetuṣu kāmeṣu saktāḥ śocyāstu rāgiṇaḥ // Bc_6.18 //
children.translated_text: those who are attached to desires, which are the causes of sorrow — they, the passionate, are to be grieved for. // Bc_6.18 //

children.text: ayaṃ ca kila pūrveṣāmasmākaṃ niścayaḥ sthiraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And this, they say, was the firm resolve of our forebears;

children.text: iti dāyādyabhūtena na śocyo 'smi pathā vrajan // Bc_6.19 //
children.translated_text: therefore I, who walk the path that is my inheritance, should not be mourned. // Bc_6.19 //

children.text: bhavanti hyarthadāyādāḥ puruṣasya viparyaye /
children.translated_text: 'There are indeed heirs to wealth when a man changes [his state];

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ dharmadāyādāḥ durlabhāstu na santi vā // Bc_6.20 //
children.translated_text: but heirs to <s>dharma</s> are rare on earth — or do not exist at all. // Bc_6.20 //

children.text: yadapi syādasamaye yāto vanamasāviti /
children.translated_text: 'And if it be said that he has gone to the forest at an untimely age —

children.text: akālo nāsti dharmasya jīvite cañcale sati // Bc_6.21 //
children.translated_text: there is no untimely moment for <s>dharma</s>, when life is so uncertain. // Bc_6.21 //

children.text: tasmādadyaiva me śreyaścetavyamiti niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, my resolve is that I must seek the supreme good this very day;

children.text: jīvite ko hi viśrambho mṛtyau pratyarthini sthite // Bc_6.22 //
children.translated_text: for who can have confidence in life, when death stands as an adversary? // Bc_6.22 //

children.text: evamādi tvayā saumya vijñāpyo vasudhādhipaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Such and similar things, O gentle one, should be conveyed by you to the lord of the earth;

children.text: prayatethāstathā caiva yathā māṃ na smaredāpi // Bc_6.23 //
children.translated_text: and strive also so that he may not even think of me. // Bc_6.23 //

children.text: api nairguṇyamasmākaṃ vācyaṃ narapatau tvayā /
children.translated_text: "Moreover, you should tell the king of my faults;

children.text: nairguṇyāttyajyate snehaḥ snehatyāgānna śocyate // Bc_6.24 //
children.translated_text: from [perceived] faults, affection is abandoned; from the abandonment of affection, there is no grieving." // Bc_6.24 //

children.text: iti vākyamidaṃ śrutvā chandaḥ saṃtāpaviklavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing these words, <s>Chandaka</s>, overcome with anguish,

children.text: bāṣpagrathitayā vācā pratyuvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ // Bc_6.25 //
children.translated_text: replied with voice choked by tears, with hands joined in reverence: // Bc_6.25 //

children.text: anena ta va bhāvena bāndhavāyāsadāyinā /
children.translated_text: "By this intention of yours, which brings distress to your kinsmen,

children.text: bhartaḥ sīdati me ceto nadīpaṅka iva dvipaḥ // Bc_6.26 //
children.translated_text: O master, my heart sinks — like an elephant in the mud of a river. // Bc_6.26 //

children.text: kasya notpādayedbāṣpaṃ niścayaste 'yamīdṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Whose [eyes] would this resolve of yours not cause to shed tears —

children.text: ayomaye 'pi hṛdaye kiṃ punaḥ snehaviklave // Bc_6.27 //
children.translated_text: even in a heart made of iron, how much more in one overcome with affection? // Bc_6.27 //

children.text: vimānaśayanārhaṃ hi saukumāryamidaṃ kva ca /
children.translated_text: "This tenderness, worthy of palace couches and aerial seats — where [does it belong]?

children.text: kharadarbhāṅkuravatī tapovanamahī kva ca // Bc_6.28 //
children.translated_text: And where is the ground of the ascetic grove, rough with blades of <s>darbha</s> grass? // Bc_6.28 //

children.text: śrutvā tu vyavasāyaṃ te yadaśvo 'yaṃ mayāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: "That I brought this horse, having heard of your resolve —

children.text: balātkāreṇa tannātha daivenaivāsmi kāritaḥ // Bc_6.29 //
children.translated_text: O lord, I was compelled to that by force — by fate itself. // Bc_6.29 //

children.text: kathaṃ hyātmavaśo jānan vyavasāyamimaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: "For how could I, of my own will, knowing this resolve of yours,

children.text: upānayeyaṃ turagaṃ śokaṃ kapilavāstunaḥ // Bc_6.30 //
children.translated_text: bring the horse — [which would bring] grief to the people of <s>Kapilavastu</s>? // Bc_6.30 //

children.text: tannārhasi mahābāho vihātuṃ putralālasam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, O mighty-armed one, you should not abandon the king who is old,

children.text: snigdhaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca rājānaṃ saddharmamiva nāstikaḥ // Bc_6.31 //
children.translated_text: affectionate, and longing for his son — as an atheist [abandons] the true <s>dharma</s>. // Bc_6.31 //

children.text: saṃvardhanapariśrāntāṃ dvitīyāṃ tāṃ ca mātaram /
children.translated_text: "You should not forget that queen — your second mother,

children.text: devīṃ nārhasi vismartu kṛtaghna iva satkriyām // Bc_6.32 //
children.translated_text: exhausted from raising you — as an ingrate [forgets] a good deed. // Bc_6.32 //

children.text: bālaputrāṃ guṇavartī kulaślādhyāṃ pativratām /
children.translated_text: "You should not abandon the queen — who has a young son, is virtuous, of praiseworthy lineage, devoted to her husband —

children.text: devīmarhasi na tyaktuṃ klībaḥ prāptāmiva śriyam // Bc_6.33 //
children.translated_text: as a coward [abandons] fortune that has come to him. // Bc_6.33 //

children.text: putraṃ yāśodharaṃ ślādhyaṃ yaśodharmabhṛtāṃ varam /
children.translated_text: "You should not abandon the praiseworthy <s>Yaśodhara</s>, your son, the best of those who bear the burden of fame and <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: bālamarhasi na tyaktuṃ vyasanīvottamaṃ yaśaḥ // Bc_6.34 //
children.translated_text: though a child — as a wastrel [abandons] supreme fame. // Bc_6.34 //

children.text: atha bandhuṃ ca rājyaṃ ca tyaktumeva kṛtā matiḥ /
children.translated_text: "But if your mind is set on abandoning kinsmen and kingdom,

children.text: māṃ nārhasi vibho tyaktuṃ tvatpādau hi gatirmama // Bc_6.35 //
children.translated_text: you should not, O Lord, abandon me — for your feet are my refuge. // Bc_6.35 //

children.text: nāsmi yātuṃ puraṃ śakto dahyamānena cetasā /
children.translated_text: "I am unable to go to the city with a burning heart,

children.text: tvāmaraṇye parityajya sumantra iva rāghavam // Bc_6.36 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned you in the forest — like <s>Sumantra</s> [abandoning] <s>Rāghava</s> (Rāma). // Bc_6.36 //

children.text: kiṃ hi vakṣyati māṃ rājā tvadṛte nagaraṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: "For what will the king say to me, who has returned to the city without you?

children.text: vakṣyāmyucitadarśitvātkiṃ tavāntaḥpurāṇi vā // Bc_6.37 //
children.translated_text: And what shall I say — discerning what is proper — to your women's quarters? // Bc_6.37 //

children.text: yadapyātthāpi nairguṇyaṃ vācyaṃ narapatāviti /
children.translated_text: "And as for what you said — that faults should be told to the king —

children.text: kiṃ tadvakṣyāmyabhūtaṃ te nirdoṣasya muneriva // Bc_6.38 //
children.translated_text: what false fault shall I speak of you, who are faultless, like a sage? // Bc_6.38 //

children.text: hṛdayena salajjena jivhayā sajjamānayā /
children.translated_text: "With an ashamed heart and a tongue that falters,

children.text: ahaṃ yadapi vā brūyāṃ kastacchraddhātumarhati // Bc_6.39 //
children.translated_text: even if I were to say something — who could believe it? // Bc_6.39 //

children.text: yo hi candramasastaikṣṇyaṃ kathayecchraddadhīta vā /
children.translated_text: "For he who would speak of harshness in the moon, or would believe it —

children.text: sa doṣāṃstava doṣajña kathayecchraddadhīta vā // Bc_6.40 //
children.translated_text: he would tell your faults, O knower of faults, or believe them. // Bc_6.40 //

children.text: sānukrośasya satataṃ nityaṃ karuṇavedinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who is always compassionate, ever aware of others' suffering,

children.text: snigdhatyāgo na sadṛśo nivartasva prasīda me // Bc_6.41 //
children.translated_text: an unkind abandonment is not fitting — turn back, be gracious to me! // Bc_6.41 //

children.text: iti śokābhibhūtasya śrutvā chandasya bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Chandaka</s>, who was overcome with grief,

children.text: svasthaḥ paramayā dhṛtyā jagāda vadatāṃ varaḥ // Bc_6.42 //
children.translated_text: the best of speakers, composed, replied with supreme steadfastness: // Bc_6.42 //

children.text: madviyogaṃ prati cchanda saṃtāpastyajyatāmayam /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Chandaka</s>, abandon this anguish over my departure;

children.text: nānābhāvo hi niyataṃ pṛthagjātiṣu dehiṣu // Bc_6.43 //
children.translated_text: for separation of states is inevitable among embodied beings born in different births. // Bc_6.43 //

children.text: svajanaṃ yadyapi snehānna tyajeyamahaṃ svayam /
children.translated_text: Even if I myself would not willingly abandon my own people out of affection,

children.text: mṛtyuranyonyamavaśānasmān saṃtyājayiṣyati // Bc_6.44 //
children.translated_text: death will forcibly separate us from one another. // Bc_6.44 //

children.text: mahatyā tṛṣṇayā duḥkhairgarbheṇāsmi yayā dhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: My mother, who bore me in her womb with great longing and suffering —

children.text: tasyā niṣphalayatnāyāḥ kvāhaṃ mātuḥ kva sā mama // Bc_6.45 //
children.translated_text: where am I to her now, and where is she to me, her efforts rendered fruitless? // Bc_6.45 //

children.text: vāsavṛkṣe samāgamya vigacchanti yathāṇḍajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as birds, having gathered on a roosting tree, depart,

children.text: niyataṃ viprayogāntastathā bhūtasamāgamaḥ // Bc_6.46 //
children.translated_text: so the meeting of beings inevitably ends in separation. // Bc_6.46 //

children.text: sametya ca yathā bhūyo vyapayānti balāhakāḥ /
children.translated_text: And just as clouds, having come together, again disperse,

children.text: saṃyogo viprayogaśca tathā me prāṇināṃ mataḥ // Bc_6.47 //
children.translated_text: so, in my view, is the union and separation of living beings. // Bc_6.47 //

children.text: yasmādyāti ca loko 'yaṃ vipralabhya paraṃparam /
children.translated_text: Since this world passes away, deceiving one another,

children.text: mamattvaṃ na kṣamaṃ tasmātsvapnabhūte samāgame // Bc_6.48 //
children.translated_text: attachment is not fitting in a meeting that is dream-like. // Bc_6.48 //

children.text: sahajena viyujyante parṇarāgeṇa pādapāḥ /
children.translated_text: Trees are separated from the color of their leaves, which is innate;

children.text: anyenānyasya viśleṣaḥ kiṃ punarna bhaviṣyati // Bc_6.49 //
children.translated_text: will not the parting of one from another, which is not innate, surely come to pass? // Bc_6.49 //

children.text: tadevaṃ sati saṃtāpaṃ mā kārṣī saumya gamyatām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this being so, do not grieve, gentle one — go;

children.text: lambate yadi tu sneho gatvāpi punarāvraja // Bc_6.50 //
children.translated_text: but if affection lingers, then having gone, return again. // Bc_6.50 //

children.text: brūyāścāsmatkṛtāpekṣaṃ janaṃ kapilavāstuni /
children.translated_text: And tell the people in <s>Kapilavastu</s> who are concerned about me:

children.text: tyajyatāṃ tagdataḥ snehaḥ śrūyatāṃ cāsya niścayaḥ // Bc_6.51 //
children.translated_text: let affection for me be abandoned from that direction, and let my resolve be heard. // Bc_6.51 //

children.text: kṣiprameṣyati vā kṛtvā janmamṛtyukṣayaṃ kila /
children.translated_text: Either he will quickly return, having brought about the destruction of birth and death,

children.text: akṛtārtho nirārambho nidhanaṃ yāsyatīti vā // Bc_6.52 //
children.translated_text: or, having failed in his purpose and abandoned effort, he will go to his end.' // Bc_6.52 //

children.text: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā kanthakasturagottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard his words, <s>Kanthaka</s>, the best of horses,

children.text: jivhayā lilihe pādau bāṣpamuṣṇaṃ mumoca ca // Bc_6.53 //
children.translated_text: licked his feet with his tongue and shed hot tears. // Bc_6.53 //

children.text: jālinā svastikāṅkena cakramadhyena pāṇinā /
children.translated_text: With his hand marked with a net, a <s>svastika</s>, and a wheel at the center,

children.text: āmamarśa kumārastaṃ babhāṣe ca vayasyavat // Bc_6.54 //
children.translated_text: the prince stroked him and spoke as to a companion: // Bc_6.54 //

children.text: muñca kanthaka mā bāṣpaṃ darśiteyaṃ sadaśvatā /
children.translated_text: 'Shed no tears, <s>Kanthaka</s>; you have shown the true nature of a noble horse;

children.text: mṛṣyatāṃ saphalaḥ śīghraṃ śramaste 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati // Bc_6.55 //
children.translated_text: bear with it — this toil of yours will soon bear fruit.' // Bc_6.55 //

body.text: maṇitsaruṃ chandakahastasaṃsthaṃ tataḥ sa dhīro niśitaṃ gṛhītvā

children.text: kośādasiṃ kañcanabhakticitraṃ bilādivaśīviṣamudbabarha // Bc_6.56 //
children.translated_text: drew it from its scabbard — golden-plated and ornate — like a serpent from its hole. // Bc_6.56 //

body.translated_text: Then that resolute one, taking the sharp sword with its jeweled hilt that rested in <s>Chandaka</s>'s hand,

children.text: niṣkāsya taṃ cotpalapattranīlaṃ ciccheda citraṃ mukuṭaṃ sakeśam /
children.translated_text: Drawing it out, blue as a lotus petal, he cut his brilliant diadem together with his hair,

children.text: vikīryamāṇāṃśukamantarīkṣe cikṣepa cainaṃ sarasīva haṃsam // Bc_6.57 //
children.translated_text: and flung it, with its cloth scattering, into the sky — like a swan into a lake. // Bc_6.57 //

children.text: pūjābhilāṣeṇa ca bāhumānyāddivaukasastaṃ jagṛhuḥ praviddham /
children.translated_text: The celestial beings, out of desire for worship and great reverence, seized it as it was cast away;

children.text: yathāvadenaṃ divi devasaṅghā divyairviśeṣairmahayāṃ ca cakruḥ // Bc_6.58 //
children.translated_text: and the hosts of gods in heaven honored it duly with divine distinctions. // Bc_6.58 //

children.text: muktvā tvalaṃkārakalatravattāṃ śrīvipravāsaṃ śirasaśca kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the state of being adorned with ornaments and wife, and having made his head bereft of beauty,

children.text: dṛṣṭvāṃśukaṃ kāñcanahaṃsacinhaṃ vanyaṃ sa dhīro 'bhicakāṅkṣa vāsaḥ // Bc_6.59 //
children.translated_text: seeing his garment marked with the golden swan, that resolute one desired a forest garment. // Bc_6.59 //

children.text: tato mṛgavyādhanapurdivaukā bhāvaṃ viditvāsya viśuddhabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then a celestial being in the guise of a hunter, of pure intent, understanding his disposition,

children.text: kāṣāyavastro 'bhiyayau samīpaṃ taṃ śākyarājaprabhavo 'bhyuvāca // Bc_6.60 //
children.translated_text: approached wearing an ochre robe; and the scion of the <s>Śākya</s> king addressed him: // Bc_6.60 //

children.text: śivaṃ ca kāṣāyamṛṣidhvajaste na yujyate hiṃsramidaṃ dhanuśca /
children.translated_text: 'This ochre robe, the banner of the sages, befits you well, but this violent bow does not;

children.text: tatsaumya yadyasti na saktiratra mahyaṃ prayacchedamidaṃ gṛhāṇa // Bc_6.61 //
children.translated_text: therefore, gentle one, if you have no attachment to it, give this to me and take [my garment].' // Bc_6.61 //

children.text: vyādho 'bravītkāmada kāmamārādanena viśvāsya mṛgāgnihanmi /
children.translated_text: The hunter said, 'O bestower of desires, by this [garment] I lure deer nearby and kill them;

children.text: arthastu śakropama yadyanena hanta pratīcchānaya śuklametat // Bc_6.62 //
children.translated_text: but if your purpose is served by it, O equal of <s>Śakra</s>, take it — and give me that white one.' // Bc_6.62 //

children.text: pareṇa harṣeṇa tataḥ sa vanyaṃ jagrāha vāso 'śukamutsasarja /
children.translated_text: Then, with exceeding joy, he took the forest garment and released the fine cloth;

children.text: vyādhastu divyaṃ vapureva bibhrattacchuklamādāya divaṃ jagāma // Bc_6.63 //
children.translated_text: and the hunter, resuming his divine form, took that white garment and ascended to heaven. // Bc_6.63 //

children.text: tataḥ kumāraśca sa cāśvagopastasmiṃstathā yāti visismiyāte /
children.translated_text: Then the prince and the horse-keeper marveled greatly

children.text: āraṇyake vāsasi caiva bhūyastasminnakārṣṭā bahumānamāśu // Bc_6.64 //
children.translated_text: at his departure, and their reverence for the forest garment increased all the more. // Bc_6.64 //

children.text: chandaṃ tataḥ sāśrumukhaṃ visṛjya kāṣāyasaṃbhṛddhṛtikīrtibhṛtsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, dismissing the tearful <s>Chandaka</s>, clad in ochre, bearing firmness and glory,

children.text: yenāśramastena yayau mahātmā saṃdhyābhrasaṃvīta ivoḍurājaḥ // Bc_6.65 //
children.translated_text: that great soul went toward the hermitage, like the king of stars veiled by twilight clouds. // Bc_6.65 //

children.text: tatastathā bhartari rājyaniḥspṛhe tapovanaṃ yāti vivarṇavāsasi /
children.translated_text: Then, when that lord, free from desire for the kingdom, went to the ascetic grove in his faded garment,

children.text: bhujau samutkṣipya tataḥ sa vājibhṛd bhṛśaṃ vicukrośa papāta ca kṣitau // Bc_6.66 //
children.translated_text: the horse-keeper, raising his arms, cried out loudly and fell upon the ground. // Bc_6.66 //

children.text: vilokya bhūyaśca ruroda sasvaraṃ hayaṃ bhujābhyāmupaguhya kanthakam /
children.translated_text: And looking again, he wept aloud, embracing the horse <s>Kanthaka</s> with both arms;

children.text: tato nirāśo vilapananmuhurmuhuryayau śarīreṇa puraṃ na cetasā // Bc_6.67 //
children.translated_text: then, despairing, lamenting again and again, he went to the city with his body, but not with his mind. // Bc_6.67 //

children.text: kvacitpradadhyau vilalāpa ca kvacit kvacitpracaskhāla papāta ca kvacit /
children.translated_text: Now he reflected, now he lamented; now he stumbled, now he fell;

children.text: ato vrajan bhaktivaśena duḥkhitaścacāra bavhīravaśaḥ pathi kriyāḥ // Bc_6.68 //
children.translated_text: thus, journeying in grief from devotion, he involuntarily performed many actions on the road. // Bc_6.68 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye chandakanivartano nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ // 6 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth canto, named 'The Dismissal of <s>Chandaka</s>,' in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>. // 6 //
CANTO VII

children.text: tato visṛjyāśrumukhaṃ rudantaṃ chandaṃ vanacchandatayā nirāsthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having dismissed the weeping, tearful <s>Chandaka</s>, desiring the forest out of longing for it,

children.text: sarvārthasiddho vapuṣābhibhūya tamāśramaṃ siddha iva prapede // Bc_7.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, overpowering [all] by his appearance, entered that hermitage like a perfected being. // Bc_7.1 //

children.text: sa rājasūnurmṛgarājagāmī mṛgājiraṃ tanmṛgavatpraviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: That prince, walking with the gait of the king of beasts, having entered the deer-ground like a deer,

children.text: lakṣmīviyukto 'pi śarīralakṣmyā cakṣūṃṣi sarvāśramiṇāṃ jahāra // Bc_7.2 //
children.translated_text: though bereft of royal splendor, captivated the eyes of all the hermitage-dwellers by the beauty of his person. // Bc_7.2 //

children.text: sthitā hi hastasthayugāstathaiva kautūhalāccakradharāḥ sadārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who stood with yokes in their hands, and the wheel-bearing householders with their wives,

children.text: tamindrakalpaṃ dadṛśurna jagmurdhuryā ivārdhāvanataiḥ śirobhiḥ // Bc_7.3 //
children.translated_text: gazed at him who was like <s>Indra</s> but did not move on, like draft animals with their heads half-bowed. // Bc_7.3 //

children.text: viprāśca gatvā bahiridhmahetoḥ prāptāḥ samitpuṣpavitrahastāḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who had gone out for firewood, having returned with sacrificial fuel, flowers, and kuśa grass in hand,

children.text: tapaḥpradhānāḥ kṛtabuddhayo 'pi taṃ draṣṭumīyurna maṭhānabhīyuḥ // Bc_7.4 //
children.translated_text: though devoted to austerity and of resolved minds, went to see him and did not enter their huts. // Bc_7.4 //

children.text: hṛṣṭāśca kekā mumucurmayūrā dṛṣṭvāmbudaṃ nīlamivonnamantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Peacocks joyfully uttered their cries, raising their necks as at the sight of a dark cloud;

children.text: śaṣpāṇi hitvābhimukhāśca tasthurmṛgāścalākṣā mṛgacāriṇaśca // Bc_7.5 //
children.translated_text: and the deer, with their beautiful eyes, leaving the grass, stood facing him, as did those who lived the life of deer. // Bc_7.5 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tamikṣvākukulapradīpaṃ jvalantamudyantamivāṃśumantam /
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the lamp of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> race, blazing like the rising sun,

children.text: kṛte 'pi dohe janitapramodāḥ prasusruvurhomaduhaśca gāvaḥ // Bc_7.6 //
children.translated_text: even the cows that yielded milk for the <s>homa</s> (fire-oblation), filled with delight though already milked, let their milk flow forth. // Bc_7.6 //

children.text: kaścidvasūnāmayamaṣṭamaḥ syātsyādāviśvanoranyataraścyuto vā /
children.translated_text: 'Could this be the eighth of the <s>Vasus</s>? Or one of the two <s>Aśvins</s>, fallen from heaven?'

children.text: ucceruruccairiti tatra vācastaddarśanādvismayajā munīnām // Bc_7.7 //
children.translated_text: Such exclamations, born of wonder at his sight, arose loudly from the sages there. // Bc_7.7 //

children.text: lekharṣabhasyeva vapurdvitīyaṃ dhāmeva lokasya carācarasya /
children.translated_text: Like a second body of the bull of the gods, the very radiance of the world of movable and immovable beings,

children.text: sa dyotayāmāsa vanaṃ hi kṛtsnaṃ yadṛcchayā sūrya ivāvatīrṇaḥ // Bc_7.8 //
children.translated_text: he illuminated the entire forest, like the sun descended of its own accord. // Bc_7.8 //

children.text: tataḥ sa tairāśramibhiryathāvadabhyarcitaścopanimantritaśca /
children.translated_text: Then, duly honored and invited by those hermitage-dwellers,

children.text: pratyarcayāṃ dharmabhṛto babhūva svareṇa sāmbho 'mbudharopamena // Bc_7.9 //
children.translated_text: he honored in return those bearers of <s>dharma</s>, with a voice deep as a rain cloud charged with moisture. // Bc_7.9 //

children.text: kīrṇaṃ tathā puṇyakṛtā janena svargābhikāmena vimokṣakāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: That forest, thronged with people who performed meritorious acts and desired heaven — he, desiring liberation,

children.text: tamāśramaṃ so 'nucacāra dhirastapāṃsi citrāṇi nirīkṣamāṇaḥ // Bc_7.10 //
children.translated_text: traversed that hermitage with composure, observing their various austerities. // Bc_7.10 //

children.text: tapovikārāṃśca nirīkṣya saumyastapovane tatra tapodhanānām /
children.translated_text: And the gentle one, having observed the distortions caused by austerity among those rich in austerity in the ascetic grove,

children.text: tapasvinaṃ kaṃcidanuvrajantaṃ tattvaṃ vijijñāsuridaṃ babhāṣe // Bc_7.11 //
children.translated_text: addressed the following to a certain ascetic who was accompanying him, wishing to learn the truth: // Bc_7.11 //

children.text: tatpūrvamadyāśramadarśanaṃ me yāsmādimaṃ dharmavidhiṃ na jāne /
children.translated_text: 'Since this is my first sight of a hermitage, and I do not know this method of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: tasmādbhavānarhati bhāṣituṃ me yo niścayo yatprati vaḥ pravṛttaḥ // Bc_7.12 //
children.translated_text: therefore you should tell me: what is the resolve toward which you are engaged?' // Bc_7.12 //

children.text: tato dvijātiḥ sa tapovihāraḥ śākyarṣabhāyarṣabhavikramāya /
children.translated_text: Then that twice-born one, experienced in ascetic life, to the bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>, who had the stride of a bull,

children.text: krameṇa tasmai kathayāṃcakāra tapoviśeṣāṃstapasaḥ phalaṃ ca // Bc_7.13 //
children.translated_text: described in sequence the particular forms of austerity and the fruit of asceticism: // Bc_7.13 //

children.text: agrāmyamannaṃ salile prarūḍhaṃ parṇīna toyaṃ phalamūlameva /
children.translated_text: 'Food not from the village, grown in water, or leaves, water, fruits, and roots alone —

children.text: yathāgamaṃ vṛttiriyaṃ munīnāṃ bhinnāstu te te tapasāṃ vikalpāḥ // Bc_7.14 //
children.translated_text: this is the livelihood of sages according to tradition; but the types of austerity differ in various ways. // Bc_7.14 //

children.text: uñchena jīvanti khagā ivānye tṛṇāni kecinmṛgavaccaranti /
children.translated_text: Some live by gleaning, like birds; some graze on grass, like deer;

children.text: kecidbhujaṅgaiḥ saha vartayanti valmīkabhūtā vanamārutena // Bc_7.15 //
children.translated_text: some live with serpents, having become ant-hills, [sustained] by forest wind. // Bc_7.15 //

children.text: āśmaprayatnārjitavṛttayo 'nye kecitsvadantāpahatānnabhakṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others obtain their sustenance by effort with stones; some eat food crushed by their own teeth;

children.text: kṛtvā parārtha śrapaṇaṃ tathānye kurvanti kāryaṃ yadi śeṣamasti // Bc_7.16 //
children.translated_text: and others, having cooked for others first, eat what remains, if any. // Bc_7.16 //

children.text: kecijjalaklinnajaṭākalāpā dviḥ pāvakaṃ juvhati mantrapūrvam /
children.translated_text: Some, with their matted locks wet with water, offer oblations to the fire twice, preceded by <s>mantras</s>;

children.text: mīnaiḥ samaṃ kecidapo vigāhya vasanti kūrmollikhitaiḥ śarīraiḥ // Bc_7.17 //
children.translated_text: some plunge into water with the fishes and dwell there, their bodies scratched by tortoises. // Bc_7.17 //

children.text: evaṃvidhaiḥ kālacitaistapobhiḥ parairdivaṃ yāntyaparairnṛlokam /
children.translated_text: By such austerities, accumulated over time, some go to heaven, others to the world of men;

children.text: duḥkhena mārgeṇa sukhaṃ hyupaiti sukhaṃ hi dharmasya vadanti mūlam // Bc_7.18 //
children.translated_text: for happiness is attained by a path of suffering — they say that happiness is the root of <s>dharma</s>.' // Bc_7.18 //

body.text:
ityevamādi dvipadendravatsaḥ śrutvā vacastasya tapodhanasya /
adṛṣṭatattvo 'pi na saṃtutoṣa / śanairidaṃ cātmagataṃ babhāṣe // Bc_7.19 //
body.translated_text: Having heard these and other words of that man rich in austerity, the calf of the bull among men, though he had not yet seen the truth, was not satisfied, and softly spoke this within himself: // Bc_7.19 //

children.text: duḥkhātmakaṃ naikavidhaṃ tapaśca svargapradhānaṃ tapasaḥ phalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'Austerity is of the nature of suffering, and of many kinds; and the fruit of austerity is primarily heaven;

children.text: lokāśca sarve pariṇāmavantaḥ svalpe śramaḥ khalvayamāśramāṇām // Bc_7.20 //
children.translated_text: and all worlds are subject to change — truly, this effort of the hermitages is for a small [reward]. // Bc_7.20 //

children.text: priyāṃśca bandhūnviṣayāṃśca hitvā ye svargahetorniyamaṃ caranti /
children.translated_text: Those who, having abandoned dear ones, kinsmen, and sense-objects, practice discipline for the sake of heaven —

children.text: te viprayuktāḥ khalu gantukāmā mahattaraṃ bandhanameva bhūyaḥ // Bc_7.21 //
children.translated_text: they, having been separated [from all], desiring to go [to heaven], seek what is merely a greater bondage again! // Bc_7.21 //

children.text: kāyaklamairyaśca tapo 'bhidhānaiḥ pravṛttimakāṅkṣati kāmahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, through bodily afflictions called austerity, seeks activity for the sake of desire,

children.text: saṃsāradoṣānaparīkṣamāṇo duḥkhena so 'nvicchati duḥkhameva // Bc_7.22 //
children.translated_text: without examining the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — he seeks suffering through suffering itself. // Bc_7.22 //

children.text: trāsaśca nityaṃ maraṇātprajānāṃ yatnena cecchanti punaḥprasūtim /
children.translated_text: Beings are constantly in fear of death, yet they strive for rebirth;

children.text: satyāṃ pravṛttau niyataśca mṛtyustatraiva magnā yata eva bhītāḥ // Bc_7.23 //
children.translated_text: while activity continues, death is certain — they are sunk in the very thing from which they are afraid. // Bc_7.23 //

children.text: ihārthameke praviśanti khedaṃ svargārthamanye śramamāpnuvanti /
children.translated_text: Some undergo hardship for the sake of this world, others toil for the sake of heaven;

children.text: sukhārthamāśākṛpaṇo 'kṛtārthaḥ patatyanarthe khalu jīvalokaḥ // Bc_7.24 //
children.translated_text: the living world, wretched with hopes and unfulfilled, falls into what is worthless, seeking happiness. // Bc_7.24 //

children.text: na khalvayaṃ garhita eva yatno yo hīnamṛtsṛjya viśeṣagāmi /
children.translated_text: This effort is not to be censured, indeed, since it abandons the inferior and moves toward the superior;

children.text: prājñaiḥ samānena pariśrameṇa kāryaṃ tu tadyatra punarna kāryam // Bc_7.25 //
children.translated_text: but the wise should direct the same exertion toward that from which there is no further action needed. // Bc_7.25 //

children.text: śarīrapīḍā tu yadīha dharmaḥ sukhaṃ śarīrasya bhavatyadharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: If bodily mortification is <s>dharma</s> here, then bodily comfort would be <s>adharma</s>;

children.text: dharmeṇa cāpnoti sukhaṃ paratra tasmādadharma phalatīha dharmaḥ // Bc_7.26 //
children.translated_text: but since one attains happiness in the next world through <s>dharma</s>, therefore <s>dharma</s> [by this logic] bears the fruit of <s>adharma</s> here. // Bc_7.26 //

children.text: yataḥ śarīraṃ manaso vaśena pravartate cāpi nivartate ca /
children.translated_text: Since the body acts and ceases to act under the control of the mind,

children.text: yukto damaścetasa eva tasmāccittādṛte kāṣṭhasamaṃ śarīram // Bc_7.27 //
children.translated_text: discipline of the mind alone is therefore appropriate; without the mind, the body is like a log of wood. // Bc_7.27 //

children.text: āhāraśuddhyā yadi puṇyamiṣṭaṃ tasmānmṛgānāmapi puṇyamasti /
children.translated_text: If merit is desired through purity of food, then even animals would have merit;

children.text: ye cāpi bāhyāḥ puruṣāḥ phalebhyo bhāgyāparādhena parāṅmukhārthāḥ // Bc_7.28 //
children.translated_text: and those people also who are excluded from [the fruits], turned away from wealth by the fault of their destiny. // Bc_7.28 //

children.text: duḥkhe 'bhisaṃdhistvatha puṇyahetuḥ sukhe 'pi kāryo nanu so 'bhisaṃdhiḥ /
children.translated_text: If intention directed toward suffering is the cause of merit, then should not that same intention be directed toward happiness?

children.text: atha pramāṇaṃ na sukhe 'bhisaṃdhirduḥkhe pramāṇaṃ nanu nābhisaṃdhiḥ // Bc_7.29 //
children.translated_text: And if intention toward happiness is not authoritative, then surely intention toward suffering is not authoritative either. // Bc_7.29 //

children.text: tathaiva ye karmaviśuddhihetoḥ spṛśantyapastīrthamiti pravṛttāḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, those who touch water with the idea that it is a sacred ford, believing it purifies <s>karma</s> —

children.text: tatrāpi toṣo hṛdi kevalo 'yaṃ na pāvayiṣyanti hi pāpamāpaḥ // Bc_7.30 //
children.translated_text: in that too, the satisfaction is in the heart alone; for waters will not purify sin. // Bc_7.30 //

children.text: spṛṣṭaṃ hi yadyadguṇavadbhirambhastattatpṛthivyāṃ yadi tīrthamiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: If whatever is touched by the waters frequented by the virtuous is a sacred ford on earth,

children.text: tasmādguṇāneva paraimi tīrthamāpastu niḥsaṃśayamāpa eva // Bc_7.31 //
children.translated_text: then I consider virtues alone to be the true sacred ford — water is assuredly just water.' // Bc_7.31 //

children.text: iti sma tattadbahuyuktiyuktaṃ jagāda cāstaṃ ca yayau vivasvān /
children.translated_text: Thus he spoke, with many well-reasoned arguments on this and that point; and the sun set;

children.text: tato havirdhūmavivarṇavṛkṣaṃ tapaḥpraśāntaṃ sa vanaṃ viveśa // Bc_7.32 //
children.translated_text: then he entered that forest, whose trees were dimmed by the smoke of oblation-fires, and where austerity was at peace. // Bc_7.32 //

children.text: abhyuddhṛtaprajvalitāgnihotraṃ kṛtābhiṣekarṣijanāvakirṇam /
children.translated_text: Where the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation) blazed with raised flames, thronged with sages who had performed their ablutions,

children.text: jāpyasvanākūjitadevakoṣṭhaṃ dharmasya karmāntamiva pravṛttam // Bc_7.33 //
children.translated_text: with the shrines buzzing with the murmur of <s>japa</s> (recitation) — as if the workshop of <s>dharma</s> were in operation. // Bc_7.33 //

children.text: kāścinniśāstatra niśākarābhaḥ parīkṣamāṇaśca tapāṃsyuvāsa /
children.translated_text: Having spent some nights there, resembling the moon, and examining their austerities,

children.text: sarva parikṣepya tapaśca matvā tasmāttapaḥkṣetratalājjagāma // Bc_7.34 //
children.translated_text: he assessed all their asceticism and, having reflected, departed from that ground of the austerity-field. // 7.34 //

children.text: anvavrajannāśramiṇastatastaṃ tadrūpamāhātmyagatairmanobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the hermitage-dwellers followed him, their minds captivated by his beauty and greatness,

children.text: deśādanāryairabhibhūyamānānmaharṣayo dharmamivāpayāntam // Bc_7.35 //
children.translated_text: like great sages [following] <s>Dharma</s> departing from a region overrun by the ignoble. // 7.35 //

children.text: tato jaṭāvalkalacīrakhelāṃstapodhanāṃścaiva sa tāndadarśa /
children.translated_text: Then he beheld those ascetics, rich in austerities, with matted hair, bark garments, and antelope-skin robes,

children.text: tapāṃsi caiṣāmanurudhyamānastasthau śive śrīmati vṛkṣamūle // Bc_7.36 //
children.translated_text: and showing regard for their austerities, he stood at an auspicious, beautiful tree-root. // 7.36 //

children.text: athopasṛtyāśramavāsinastaṃ manuṣyavarya parivārya tasthuḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the hermitage-dwellers approached and stood around him, the best of men;

children.text: vṛddhaśca teṣāṃ bahumānapūrvaṃ kalena sāmnā giramityuvāca // Bc_7.37 //
children.translated_text: and the eldest among them, with precedence of esteem, gently spoke these words in due time: // 7.37 //

children.text: tvayyāgate pūrṇa ivāśramo 'bhūtsaṃpadyate śūnya eva prayāte /
children.translated_text: 'When you arrived, the hermitage seemed full; when you depart, it becomes as if empty;

children.text: tasmādimaṃ nārhasi tāta hātuṃ jijīviṣordehamiveṣṭamāyuḥ // Bc_7.38 //
children.translated_text: therefore, dear one, you should not abandon this [hermitage], just as one who desires to live [should not abandon] his beloved life-span. // 7.38 //

children.text: brahmarṣirājarṣisurarṣijuṣṭaḥ puṇyaḥ samīpe himavān hi śailaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the auspicious <s>Himālaya</s> mountain nearby is frequented by <s>brahmarṣis</s> (Brahman-sages), <s>rājarṣis</s> (royal sages), and <s>surarṣis</s> (divine sages);

children.text: tapāṃsi tānyeva tapodhanānāṃ yatsaṃnikarṣādbahulībhavanti // Bc_7.39 //
children.translated_text: whose very proximity multiplies the austerities of the ascetics. // 7.39 //

children.text: juṣṭāni dharmātmabhirātmavadbhirdevarṣibhiścaiva maharṣibhiśca // Bc_7.40 //
children.translated_text: frequented by dharma-minded, self-possessed beings, by divine sages and great sages. // 7.40 //

body.translated_text: 'And likewise nearby are sacred fords, like stairways to the vault of heaven,

children.text: itaśca bhūyaḥ kṣamamuttaraiva diksevituṃ dharmīvaśeṣahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And from here, it is still more fitting to proceed northward for the sake of further dharma;

children.text: na tu kṣamaṃ dakṣiṇato budhena padaṃ bhavedekamapi prayātum // Bc_7.41 //
children.translated_text: but for a wise man, it would not be fitting to take even a single step southward. // 7.41 //

children.text: tapovane 'sminnatha niṣkriyo vā saṃkīrṇadharmāpatito 'śucirvā /
children.translated_text: 'Or if in this ascetic grove, someone inactive, or one of mixed practices, or fallen, or impure,

children.text: dṛṣṭastvayā yena na te vivatsā tadbrūhi yāvadrucito 'stu vāsaḥ // Bc_7.42 //
children.translated_text: has been seen by you, because of whom you have no desire to stay — tell [us], so that your dwelling may be to your liking. // 7.42 //

children.text: ime hi vāñchanti tapaḥsahāyaṃ taponidhānapratīmaṃ bhavantam /
children.translated_text: 'For these [ascetics] desire as a companion in austerity you, who are like a treasury of austerity;

children.text: vāsastvayā hīndrasamena sārdha bṛhaspaterabhyudayāvahaḥ syāt // Bc_7.43 //
children.translated_text: for a stay with you, who are equal to <s>Indra</s>, would bring the prosperity of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. // 7.43 //'

children.text: ityevamukte sa tapasvimadhye tapasvimukhyena manīṣimukhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: When thus addressed by the chief of ascetics in the midst of the ascetics, the chief of the wise,

children.text: bhavapraṇāśāya kṛtapratijñaḥ svaṃ bhāvāmantargatamācacakṣe // Bc_7.44 //
children.translated_text: who had made his resolve for the destruction of <s>bhava</s> (worldly existence), disclosed his inner thought: // 7.44 //

children.text: ṛjvātmanāṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ munīnāmiṣṭātithitvātsvajanopamānām /
children.translated_text: 'The supreme affection and the honor that have been born in me by such sentiments

children.text: evaṃvidhairmā prati bhāvajātaiḥ prītiḥ parā me janitaśca mānaḥ // Bc_7.45 //
children.translated_text: from sages who are upright in soul, who uphold <s>Dharma</s>, and who are like one's own people because of their welcome hospitality — // 7.45 //

children.text: snigdhābhirābhirhṛdayaṃgamābhiḥ samāsataḥ snāta ivāsmi vāgbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'by your words, affectionate, pleasant, and heart-touching — in short, I am as if bathed;

children.text: ratiśca me dharmanavagrahasya vispanditā saṃprati bhūya eva // Bc_7.46 //
children.translated_text: and my delight in my fresh resolve for <s>Dharma</s> has now been stirred even more. // 7.46 //

children.text: evaṃ pravṛttān bhavataḥ śaraṇyānatīva saṃdarśitapakṣapātān /
children.translated_text: 'That I shall leave you, who have acted thus, who are worthy of refuge, who have shown such extreme partiality —

children.text: yāsyāmi hitveti mamāpi duḥkhaṃ yathaiva bandhūṃstyajatastathaiva // Bc_7.47 //
children.translated_text: my grief at that is like that at abandoning kinsmen. // 7.47 //

children.text: svargāya yuṣmākamayaṃ tu dharmo mamābhilāṣastvapunarbhavāya /
children.translated_text: 'But this <s>dharma</s> of yours is for the attainment of heaven; my aspiration, however, is for the cessation of rebirth;

children.text: asminvane yena na me vivatsā bhinnaḥ pravṛttyā hi nivṛttidharmaḥ // Bc_7.48 //
children.translated_text: hence my desire not to stay in this grove — for the <s>dharma</s> of cessation is different in its direction from the <s>dharma</s> of activity. // 7.48 //

children.text: tannāratirme na parāpacāro vanādito yena parivrajāmi /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore it is not displeasure, nor any fault of others, for which I leave this grove;

children.text: dharme sthitāḥ pūrvayugānurūpe sarve bhavanto hi maharṣikalpāḥ // Bc_7.49 //
children.translated_text: for you are all like great sages, established in the <s>dharma</s> befitting a former age. // 7.49 //'

children.text: tato vacaḥ sūnṛtamarthavacca suślakṣṇamojasvi ca garvita ca /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the prince's speech — truthful, meaningful, smooth, powerful, and yet free of pride —

children.text: śrutvā kumārasya tapasvinaste viśeṣayuktaṃ bahumānamīyuḥ // Bc_7.50 //
children.translated_text: those ascetics went to an especially high regard [for him]. // 7.50 //

children.text: kaściddvijastatra tu bhasmaśāyī prāṃśuḥ śikhī dāravacīravāsāḥ /
children.translated_text: But a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s> there, who slept in ashes, tall, with a crest of hair, clad in wooden bark garments,

children.text: āpiṅgalākṣastanudīrghaghoṇaḥ kuṇḍaikahasto giramityuvāca // Bc_7.51 //
children.translated_text: tawny-eyed, thin with a long nose, holding a water-pot in one hand, spoke these words: // 7.51 //

children.text: dhīmannudāraḥ khalu niścayaste yastvaṃ yuvā janmani dṛṣṭadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O wise one, your resolution is indeed noble — you who, though young, have seen the faults of birth;

children.text: svargāpavargau hi vicārya samyagyasyāpavarge matirasti so 'sti // Bc_7.52 //
children.translated_text: for one who, having duly considered heaven and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), has his mind set upon liberation — he truly exists. // 7.52 //

children.text: yajñaistapobhirniyamaiśca taistaiḥ svarga yiyāsanti hi rāgavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the passionate seek heaven through sacrifices, austerities, and observances;

children.text: rāgeṇa sārdha ripuṇeva yuddhvā mokṣaṃ parīpsanti tu sattvavantaḥ // Bc_7.53 //
children.translated_text: but the resolute, having fought with passion as with an enemy, seek <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). // 7.53 //

children.text: tadbuddhireṣā yadi niścitā te tūrṇaṃ bhavān gacchatu vindhyakoṣṭham /
children.translated_text: 'If this resolve of yours is firm, then go quickly to the region of <s>Vindhya</s>;

children.text: asau munistatra vasatyarāḍo yo naiṣṭhike śreyasi labdhacakṣuḥ // Bc_7.54 //
children.translated_text: there dwells the sage <s>Arāḍa</s>, who has attained insight into the ultimate good. // 7.54 //

children.text: tasmādbhavāñcchroṣyati tattvamārga satyāṃ rucau saṃpratipatsyate ca /
children.translated_text: 'From him you will hear the path of truth, and if it pleases you, you will also attain it;

children.text: yathā tu paśyāmi matistathaiṣā tasyāpi yāsyatyavadhūya buddhim // Bc_7.55 //
children.translated_text: but as I perceive, this mind of yours will go beyond even his understanding. // 7.55 //

children.text: idaṃ hi vaktuṃ tanuraktajivhaṃ jñeyārṇavaṃ pāsyati kṛtsnameva // Bc_7.56 //
children.translated_text: slender red-tinged tongue — will drink the entire ocean of the knowable. // 7.56 //

body.translated_text: 'For this face — with its distinct high nose, large wide eyes, red-copper lower lip, sharp white teeth,

children.text: gambhīratā yā bhavatastvagādhā yā dīptatā yāni ca lakṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: 'The unfathomable profundity that is yours, the radiance, and the [bodily] marks —

children.text: ācāryakaṃ prāpsyasi tatpṛthivyāṃ yannarṣibhiḥ pūrvayuge 'pyavāptam // Bc_7.57 //
children.translated_text: you will attain a teacher-ship on earth that was not attained even by the sages in former ages.' // 7.57 //

children.text: paramamiti tato nṛpātmajastamṛṣijanaṃ pratinandya niryayau /
children.translated_text: 'Excellent!' — thus the prince, having gratified that assembly of sages, departed;

children.text: vidhivadanuvidhāya te 'pi taṃ praviviśurāśramiṇastapovanam // Bc_7.58 //
children.translated_text: and they too, having duly attended to him, re-entered the ascetic grove. // 7.58 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye tapovanapraveśo nāma saptamaḥ sargaḥ // 7 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh canto named 'Entry into the Ascetic Grove' in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>. // 7 //
CANTO VIII

children.text: tatasturaṅgāvacaraḥ sa durmanāstathā vanaṃ bhartari nirmame gate /
children.translated_text: Then the horse-attendant (<s>Chandaka</s>), heavy-hearted, when his master had thus gone indifferently into the forest,

children.text: cakāra yatnaṃ pathi śokanigrahe tathāpi caivāśru na tasya cikṣiye // Bc_8.1 //
children.translated_text: made an effort to restrain his grief on the road, but even so his tears could not be held back. // 8.1 //

children.text: yamekarātreṇa tu bharturājñayā jagāma mārga saha tena vājinā /
children.translated_text: The road that he had traversed in a single night by his master's command with that horse,

children.text: iyāya bharturvirahaṃ vicintayaṃstameva panthānamahobhiraṣṭabhiḥ // Bc_8.2 //
children.translated_text: he traveled in eight days, pondering the separation from his master. // 8.2 //

children.text: hayaśca saujā vicacāra kanthakastatāma bhāvena babhūva nirmadaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the horse <s>Kanthaka</s>, though of noble breed, moved listlessly; with downcast spirit he became without his usual mettle,

children.text: alaṃkṛtaścāpi tathaiva bhūṣaṇairabhūdgataśrīriva tena varjitaḥ // Bc_8.3 //
children.translated_text: and though still adorned with ornaments, he seemed as if stripped of his splendor, bereft of his [master]. // 8.3 //

children.text: nivṛtya caivābhimukhastapovanaṃ bhṛśaṃ jiheṣe karuṇaṃ muhurmuhuḥ /
children.translated_text: And turning back to face the ascetic grove, he neighed piteously again and again;

children.text: kṣudhānvito 'pyadhvani śaṣpamambu vā yathā purā nābhinanda nādade // Bc_8.4 //
children.translated_text: and though hungry on the road, he neither relished nor took grass or water as before. // 8.4 //

children.text: tato vihīnaṃ kapilāvhayaṃ puraṃ mahātmanā tena jagaddhitātmanā /
children.translated_text: Then the two slowly approached that city called <s>Kapilā</s> (<s>Kapilavastu</s>), bereft of that great-souled one devoted to the welfare of the world,

children.text: krameṇa tau śūnyamivopajagmaturdivākareṇeva vinākṛtaṃ nabhaḥ // Bc_8.5 //
children.translated_text: as if it were empty, like the sky deprived of the sun. // 8.5 //

children.text: sapuṇḍarīkairapi śobhitaṃ jalairalaṃkṛtaṃ puṣpadharairnagairapi /
children.translated_text: Though adorned with waters bearing lotuses and beautiful with flower-laden trees,

children.text: tadeva tasyopavanaṃ vanopamaṃ gatapraharṣairna rarāja nāgaraiḥ // Bc_8.6 //
children.translated_text: that very pleasure-garden of his looked like a wilderness, with its citizens bereft of joy. // 8.6 //

children.text: tato bhramadbhirdiśi dīnamānasairanujjvalairbāṣpahatekṣaṇairnaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, with men wandering about in the quarters, their spirits low, without radiance, their eyes clouded by tears,

children.text: nirvāyamāṇāviva tāvubhau puraṃ śanairapasnātamivābhijagmatuḥ // Bc_8.7 //
children.translated_text: the two entered the city slowly, as if being extinguished, as if unwashed. // 8.7 //

children.text: niśāmya ca srastaśarīragāminau vināgatau śākyakularṣabheṇa tau /
children.translated_text: And seeing those two, with drooping gait, returning without the bull of the <s>Śākya</s> family,

children.text: mumoca bāṣpaṃ pathi nāgaro janaḥ pura rathe dāśaratherivāgate // Bc_8.8 //
children.translated_text: the city folk shed tears on the road, as when the chariot of <s>Dāśarathi</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) returned to the city [empty]. // 8.8 //

children.text: atha bruvantaḥ samupetamanyavo janāḥ pathi cchandakamāgatāśravaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the people, having come together with rising anger and tears flowing, said to <s>Chandaka</s> on the road:

children.text: kva rājaputraḥ purarāṣṭranandano hṛtastvayāsāviti pṛṣṭhato 'nvayuḥ // Bc_8.9 //
children.translated_text: 'Where is the king's son, the delight of the city and realm? He has been carried off by you!' — thus they followed from behind. // 8.9 //

children.text: tataḥ sa tān bhaktimato 'bravījjanānnarendraputraṃ na parityajāmyaham /
children.translated_text: Then he said to those devoted people: 'I did not abandon the prince;

children.text: rudannahaṃ tena tu nirjane vane gṛhasthaveśaśca visarjitāviti // Bc_8.10 //
children.translated_text: but weeping, I was sent away by him in the lonely forest, along with the householder's garb.' // 8.10 //

children.text: idaṃ vacastasya niśamya te janāḥ suduṣkaraṃ khalviti niścayaṃ yayuḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of his, those people arrived at the conclusion: 'This is truly supremely difficult!';

children.text: pataddhi jahruḥ salilaṃ na netrajaṃ mano nininduśca phalotthamātmanaḥ // Bc_8.11 //
children.translated_text: for they shed tears that fell, not born from the eyes [alone], and they blamed the fate born of their own [past actions]. // 8.11 //

children.text: athocuradyaiva viśāma tadvanaṃ gataḥ sa yatra dviparājavikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then they said: 'Let us enter that very forest today, to which he has gone, he of the prowess of the king of elephants;

children.text: jijīviṣā nāsti hi tena no vinā yathendriyāṇāṃ vigame śarīriṇām // Bc_8.12 //
children.translated_text: for there is no desire to live for us without him, as for embodied beings when their senses have departed.' // 8.12 //

children.text: idaṃ puraṃ tena vivarjitaṃ vanaṃ vanaṃ ca tattena samanvitaṃ puram /
children.translated_text: 'This city, bereft of him, is a wilderness; and that wilderness, graced by him, is a city;

children.text: na śobhate tena hi no vinā puraṃ marutvatā vṛtravadhe yathā divam // Bc_8.13 //
children.translated_text: for our city does not shine without him, like heaven without <s>Indra</s> after the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>.' // 8.13 //

children.text: punaḥ kumāro vinivṛtta ityatho gavākṣamālāḥ pratipedire 'ṅganāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, [hearing] 'The prince has returned!' the women rushed to the lattice-windows;

children.text: viviktapṛṣṭhaṃ ca niśāmya vājinaṃ punargavākṣāṇi pidhāya cukruśuḥ // Bc_8.14 //
children.translated_text: but seeing the horse's back empty, they closed the windows again and wailed. // 8.14 //

children.text: praviṣṭadīkṣastu sutopalabdhaye vratena śokena ca khinnamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the king, his mind afflicted by grief and by a vow undertaken for the recovery of his son,

children.text: jajāpa devāyatane narādhipaścakāra tāstāśca yathāśayāḥ kriyāḥ // Bc_8.15 //
children.translated_text: chanted prayers in the temple of the gods and performed those various rites as befitted his desire. // 8.15 //

children.text: tataḥ sa bāṣpapratipūrṇalocanasturaṅgamādāya turaṅgamānugaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the horse-attendant, with eyes filled with tears, leading the horse,

children.text: viveśa śokābhihato nṛpakṣayaṃ yudhāpinīte ripuṇeva bhartari // Bc_8.16 //
children.translated_text: entered the royal palace, stricken with grief, as when a master has been captured by the enemy in battle. // 8.16 //

children.text: vigāhamānaśca narendramandiraṃ vilokayannaśruvahena cakṣuṣā /
children.translated_text: And entering the king's dwelling, gazing about with tear-streaming eyes,

children.text: svareṇa puṣṭena rurāva kanthako janāya duḥkhaṃ prativedayanniva // Bc_8.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kanthaka</s> neighed with a full voice, as if announcing the sorrow to the people. // 8.17 //

children.text: tataḥ khagāśca kṣayamadhyagocarāḥ samīpabaddhāsturagāśca satkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the birds in the grounds of the inner apartments and the well-tended horses tethered nearby

children.text: hayasya tasya pratisasvanuḥ svanaṃ narendrasūnorupayānaśaṅkinaḥ // Bc_8.18 //
children.translated_text: echoed the neighing of that horse, suspecting the arrival of the king's son. // 8.18 //

children.text: janāśca harṣatiśayena vañcitā janādhipāntaḥpurasaṃnikarṣagāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the people near the inner apartments of the lord of men, deceived by excessive joy,

children.text: yathā hayaḥ kanthaka eṣa heṣate dhruvaṃ kumāro viśatīti menire // Bc_8.19 //
children.translated_text: thought: 'Since the horse <s>Kanthaka</s> neighs thus, surely the prince is entering!' // 8.19 //

children.text: atipraharṣādatha śokamūrchitāḥ kumārasaṃdarśanalolalocanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, overcome first by joy and then by grief, with eyes eager for the sight of the prince,

children.text: gṛhādviniścakramurāśayā striyaḥ śaratpayodādiva vidyutaścalāḥ // Bc_8.20 //
children.translated_text: the women rushed out of the palace with hope, like flickering lightning-flashes from an autumn cloud. // 8.20 //

children.text: vilambakeśyo malināṃśukāmbarā nirañjanairbāṣpahatekṣaṇairmukhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With disheveled hair, in soiled garments, their faces with eyes afflicted by tears and without cosmetics,

children.text: striyo na rejurmṛjayā vinākṛtā divīva tārā rajanīkṣayāruṇāḥ // Bc_8.21 //
children.translated_text: the women did not shine, deprived of adornment, like stars in heaven reddened by the waning of night. // 8.21 //

children.text: araktatāmraiścaraṇairanūpurairakuṇḍalairārjavakandharairmukhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With feet not reddened with lac, without anklets; with faces on upright necks, without earrings;

children.text: svabhāvapīnairjaghanairamekhalairahārayoktrairmuṣitairiva stanaiḥ // Bc_8.22 //
children.translated_text: with hips naturally full, without girdles; with breasts as if robbed, without necklace-bands. // 8.22 //

children.text: nirīkṣya tā bāṣpaparītalocanā nirāśrayaṃ chandakamaśvameva ca /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Chandaka</s> with eyes brimming with tears, and the horse without their lord,

children.text: viṣaṇṇavaktrā rurudurvarāṅganā vanāntare gāva ivarṣabhojjhitāḥ // Bc_8.23 //
children.translated_text: the noble women, with sorrowful faces, wept — like cows in the forest forsaken by the bull. // 8.23 //

children.text: tataḥ sabāṣpā mahīṣī mahīpateḥ pranaṣṭavatsā mahiṣīva vatsalā /
children.translated_text: Then the chief queen of the king, tearful, like an affectionate she-buffalo whose calf is lost,

children.text: pragṛhya bāhū nipapāta gautamī vilolaparṇā kadalīva kāñcanī // Bc_8.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gautamī</s>, stretching out her arms, fell to the ground — like a golden plantain tree with trembling leaves. // 8.24 //

children.text: hatatviṣo 'nyāḥ śithilāṃsabāhavaḥ striyo viṣādena vicetanā iva /
children.translated_text: Other women, their radiance destroyed, their shoulders and arms gone limp,

children.text: na cukruśurnāśru jahurna śaśvasurna celurāsurlikhitā iva sthitāḥ // Bc_8.25 //
children.translated_text: as if senseless from despair, neither cried out, nor shed tears, nor sighed — they did not move, but stood as if painted. // 8.25 //

children.text: adhīramanyāḥ patiśokamūrcchitā vilocanaprasravaṇairmukhaiḥ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Other women, unsteady, overcome by grief for their lord,

children.text: siṣiñcire proṣitacandanān stanāndharādharaḥ prasravaṇairivopalān // Bc_8.26 //
children.translated_text: with faces that were fountains of tears from their eyes, sprinkled their breasts — devoid of their customary sandalwood — like waterfalls moistening rocks. // 8.26 //

children.text: mukhaiśca tāsāṃ nāyanāmbutāḍitaiṃ rarāja tadrājaniveśanaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: And with their faces struck by the tears from their eyes,

children.text: navāmbukāle 'mbudavṛṣṭitāḍitaiḥ sravajjalaistāmarasairyathā saraḥ // Bc_8.27 //
children.translated_text: that royal dwelling shone at that time like a lake with lotuses struck by the rain from newly arrived clouds, dripping with water. // 8.27 //

children.text: suvṛttapiṇāḍagulibhirnirantarairabhūṣaṇairgūḍhasirairvarāṅganāḥ /
children.translated_text: The noble women struck their lotus-like chests with their hands, with fingers well-rounded and closely set, their ornaments hidden by their joints,

children.text: urāṃsi jaghnuḥ kamalopamaiḥ karaiḥ svapallavairvātacalā latā iva // Bc_8.28 //
children.translated_text: like creepers shaken by the wind, striking with their own tendrils. // 8.28 //

children.text: karaprahārapracalaiśca tā babhustathāpi nāryaḥ sahitonnataiḥ stanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And those women, with breasts raised and set in motion by the blows of their hands,

children.text: vanānilāghūrṇitapadmakampitai rathāṅganāmnāṃ mithunairivāpagāḥ // Bc_8.29 //
children.translated_text: appeared like rivers with pairs of <s>cakravāka</s> birds set trembling by lotuses swayed by the forest wind. // 8.29 //

children.text: yathā ca vakṣāṃsi karairapīḍayaṃstathaiva vakṣobhirapīḍayan karān /
children.translated_text: And as they pressed their chests with their hands, so too their hands were pressed by their chests;

children.text: akārayaṃstatra parasparaṃ vyathāḥ karāgravakṣāṃsyabalā dayālasāḥ // Bc_8.30 //
children.translated_text: those weak and compassionate women thus caused mutual pain to their hands and breasts. // 8.30 //

children.text: tatastu roṣapraviraktalocanā viṣādasaṃbandhikaṣāyagadgadam /
children.translated_text: Then, with eyes reddened by anger, with voice choked, hoarse, and mingled with sorrow,

children.text: uvāca niśvāsacalatpayodharā vigāḍhaśokāśrudharā yaśodharā // Bc_8.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśodharā</s>, whose bosom heaved with sighs, bearing a stream of tears from deep grief, spoke: // 8.31 //

children.text: niśi prasuptāmavaśāṃ vihāya māṃ gataḥ kva sa chandaka manmanorathaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Leaving me helpless, asleep in the night — where has he gone, <s>Chandaka</s>, that desire of my heart?

children.text: upāgate ca tvayi kanthake ca me samaṃ gateṣu triṣu kampate manaḥ // Bc_8.32 //
children.translated_text: at your return, and <s>Kanthaka</s>'s, and mine — with three [now] gone together — my mind trembles. // 8.32 //

children.text: anāryamasnigdhamamitrakarma me nṛśaṃsa kṛtvā kimihādya rodiṣi /
children.translated_text: 'What you have done is ignoble, heartless, the act of an enemy — O cruel one, having done this, why do you weep now?

children.text: niyaccha bāṣpaṃ bhava tuṣṭamānaso na saṃvadatyaśru ca tacca karma te // Bc_8.33 //
children.translated_text: Restrain your tears, be of contented mind — for tears and such a deed of yours do not agree.' // 8.33 //

children.text: priyeṇa vaśyena hitena sādhunā tvayā sahāyena yathārthakāriṇā /
children.translated_text: 'With a dear, obedient, well-meaning, virtuous companion such as you, who acts as one wishes —

children.text: gato 'ryaputro hyapunarnivṛttaye ramasva diṣṭyā saphalaḥ śramastava // Bc_8.34 //
children.translated_text: the noble son has gone, never to return — rejoice! How fortunate — your labor has borne fruit!' // 8.34 //

children.text: varaṃ manuṣyasya vicakṣaṇo ripurna mitramaprājñamayogapeśalam /
children.translated_text: 'Better for a man to have a discerning enemy than a friend who is foolish and unskilled in [proper] means;

children.text: suhṛdbruveṇa hyavipaścitā tvayā kṛtaḥ kulasyāsya mahānupaplavaḥ // Bc_8.35 //
children.translated_text: for by you, claiming to be a friend yet being unwise, a great calamity has been wrought upon this family.' // 8.35 //

children.text: imā hi śocyā vyavamuktabhūṣaṇāḥ prasaktabāṣpāvilaraktalocanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For these women are to be pitied — their ornaments cast aside, their reddened eyes blurred with ceaseless tears —

children.text: sthite 'pi patyau himavanmahīsame pranaṣṭaśobhā vidhavā iva striyaḥ // Bc_8.36 //
children.translated_text: though their lord still lives, firm as <s>Himavat</s> — their beauty destroyed, they are like widows.' // 8.36 //

children.text: imāśca vikṣiptaviṭaṅkabāhavaḥ prasaktapārāvatadīrghanisvanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And these rows of palaces, with their turret-arms flung out, with the prolonged moaning sounds of pigeons clinging [to them],

children.text: vinākṛtāstena sahāvarodhanairbhṛśaṃ rudantīva vimānapaṅktayaḥ // Bc_8.37 //
children.translated_text: separated from him along with the inmates of the harem — they seem to weep aloud.' // 8.37 //

children.text: anarthakāmo 'sya janasya sarvathā turaṅgamo 'pi dhruvameṣa kanthakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This horse <s>Kanthaka</s> too surely desires the ruin of this people in every way;

children.text: jahāra sarvasvamitastathā hi me jane prasupte niśi ratnacauravat // Bc_8.38 //
children.translated_text: for he thus carried away all my wealth from here while the people slept at night, like a thief of jewels.' // 8.38 //

children.text: yadā samarthaḥ khalu soḍhumāgatāniṣuprahārānapi kiṃ punaḥ kaśāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Since he is indeed able to endure the blows of arrows coming toward him, how much more whip-strokes —

children.text: gataḥ kaśāpātabhayātkathaṃ nvayaṃ śriyaṃ gṛhītvā hṛdayaṃ ca me samam // Bc_8.39 //
children.translated_text: how then did this one, out of fear of a whip-stroke, carry away my glory and my heart at once?' // 8.39 //

children.text: anāryakarmā bhṛśamadya heṣate narendradhiṣṇyaṃ pratipūrayanniva /
children.translated_text: 'The doer of an ignoble deed, he now neighs loudly today, as if filling the royal courtyard;

children.text: yadā tu nirvāhayati sma me priyaṃ tadā hi mūkasturagādhamo 'bhavat // Bc_8.40 //
children.translated_text: but when he was carrying away my beloved, then he was mute — the vilest of horses!' // 8.40 //

children.text: yadi hyaheṣiṣyata bodhayan janaṃ khuraiḥ kṣitau vāpyakariṣyata dhvanim /
children.translated_text: 'For if he had neighed, rousing the people, or had made a sound on the ground with his hooves,

children.text: hanusvanaṃ vājanayiṣyaduttamaṃ na cābhaviṣyanmama duḥkhamīdṛśam // Bc_8.41 //
children.translated_text: or had produced a loud noise with his jaw — then this grief of mine would not have come to be!' // 8.41 //

children.text: itīha devyāḥ paridevitāśrayaṃ niśamya bāṣpagrathitākṣaraṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the queen, this lamentation uttered in syllables choked with tears,

children.text: adhomukhaḥ sāśrukalaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ śanairidaṃ chandaka uttaraṃ jagau // Bc_8.42 //
children.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s>, with downcast face, tear-drops, and joined palms, slowly sang this reply: // 8.42 //

children.text: vigarhituṃ nārhasi devi kanthakaṃ na cāpi roṣaṃ mayi kartumarhasi /
children.translated_text: 'You should not reproach <s>Kanthaka</s>, O queen, nor is it right to direct your anger at me;

children.text: anāgasau svaḥ samavehi sarvaśo gato nṛdevaḥ sa hi devi devavat // Bc_8.43 //
children.translated_text: know that we are both blameless in every way — for the god among men departed, O queen, like a god. // 8.43 //

children.text: ahaṃ hi jānannapi rājaśāsanaṃ balātkṛtaḥ kairapi daivatairiva /
children.translated_text: 'For I, though knowing the king's command, was compelled as if by certain divine powers;

children.text: upānayaṃ tūrṇamimaṃ turaṅgamaṃ tathānvagacchaṃ vigataśramo 'dhvani // Bc_8.44 //
children.translated_text: I brought this steed swiftly, and likewise I followed along the road without fatigue. // 8.44 //

children.text: vrajannayaṃ vajivaro 'pi nāspṛśanmahī khurāgrairvidhṛtairivāntarā /
children.translated_text: 'As this best of horses walked, he did not even touch the earth with his hooftips — as if [they were] held up in between;

children.text: tathaiva daivādiva saṃyatānano hanusvanaṃ nākṛta nāpyaheṣata // Bc_8.45 //
children.translated_text: and likewise, as if by divine will, with mouth restrained, he made no jaw-sound nor did he neigh. // 8.45 //

children.text: yato bahirgacchati pārthivātmaje tadābhavaddvāramapāvṛtaṃ svayam /
children.translated_text: 'When the prince went forth, the gate opened of its own accord,

children.text: tamaśca naiśaṃ raviṇeva pāṭitaṃ tapo 'pi daivo vidhireṣa gṛhyatām // Bc_8.46 //
children.translated_text: and the darkness of night was split as if by the sun — let this too be understood as divine ordinance. // 8.46 //

children.text: yadapramatto 'pi narendraśāsanād gṛhe pure civa sahasraśo janaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Though the people in the palace and in the city — thousands — were vigilant by the king's command,

children.text: tadā sa nābudhyata nidrayā hṛtastato 'pi daivo vidhireṣa gṛhyatām // Bc_8.47 //
children.translated_text: at that time they did not wake, seized by sleep — let this too be understood as divine ordinance. // 8.47 //

children.text: yataśca vāso vanavāsasaṃmataṃ nisṛṣṭamasmai samaye divaukasā /
children.translated_text: 'And since a garment suitable for forest-dwelling was released to him at that moment by a celestial being,

children.text: divi praviddhaṃ mukuṭaṃ ca taddhṛtaṃ tato 'pi daivo vidhireṣa gṛhyatām // Bc_8.48 //
children.translated_text: and his diadem, cast into the sky, was received [there] — let this too be understood as divine ordinance. // 8.48 //

children.text: tadevamāvāṃ naradevi doṣato na tatprayātaṃ prati gantumarhasi /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, O queen among men, you should not ascribe fault to us regarding his departure;

children.text: na kāmakāro mama nāsya vājinaḥ kṛtānuyātraḥ sa hi daivatairgataḥ // Bc_8.49 //
children.translated_text: it was not by my will, nor by this horse's — for he departed accompanied by the gods.' // 8.49 //

children.text: iti prayāṇaṃ bahudevamadbhūtaṃ niśamya tāstasya mahātmanaḥ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing of his departure — marvelous, attended by many gods — those women of that great soul,

children.text: pranaṣṭaśokā iva vismayaṃ yayurmanojvaraṃ pravrajanāttu lebhire // Bc_8.50 //
children.translated_text: their grief, as it were, vanished, were filled with wonder — yet from his going forth, they received the fever of the heart. // 8.50 //

children.text: viṣādapāriplavalocanā tataḥ pranaṣṭapotā kurarīva duḥkhitā /
children.translated_text: Then, her eyes swimming with despondency, grieving like an <s>osprey</s> whose chicks are lost,

children.text: vihāya dhairya virurāva gautamī tatāma caivāśrumukhī jagāda ca // Bc_8.51 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gautamī</s>, abandoning composure, wailed aloud, and with tear-streaked face, also spoke: // 8.51 //

children.text: mahormimanto mṛdavo 'sitāḥ śubhāḥ pṛthakpṛthaṅmūlaruhāḥ samudgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Great-waved, soft, dark, and beautiful, springing individually from each root, rising high —

children.text: praveritāste bhuvi tasya murdhajā narendramaulīpariveṣṭanakṣamāḥ // Bc_8.52 //
children.translated_text: those locks of his have been cast upon the ground — [locks] worthy of encircling the crown of a king!' // 8.52 //

children.text: pralambabāhurmṛgarājavikramo maharṣabhākṣaḥ kanakojjvaladyutiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With long arms, the prowess of a lion-king, eyes like those of a great bull, radiance blazing like gold,

children.text: viśālavakṣā ghanadundubhisvanastathāvidho 'pyāśramavāsamarhati // Bc_8.53 //
children.translated_text: broad-chested, with a voice like a deep drum — one such as he deserves to dwell in a hermitage?' // 8.53 //

children.text: abhāginī nūnamiyaṃ vasuṃdharā tamāryakarmāṇamanuttamaṃ patim /
children.translated_text: 'Truly, this earth is without fortune, [to have lost] him — that performer of noble deeds, that supreme lord;

children.text: gatastato 'sau guṇavān hi tādṛśo nṛpaḥ prajābhāgyaguṇaiḥ prasūyate // Bc_8.54 //
children.translated_text: since one of such virtues has departed, for a king of such kind is born by the fortune and merit of his subjects.' // 8.54 //

children.text: sujātajālāvatatāṅgulī mṛdū nigūḍhagulphau bisapuṣpakomalau /
children.translated_text: 'Those two feet, with well-formed webs and extended toes, soft, with hidden ankles, tender as lotus-stalks and blossoms,

children.text: vanāntabhūmiṃ kaṭhināṃ kathaṃ nu tau sacakramadhyau caraṇau gamiṣyataḥ // Bc_8.55 //
children.translated_text: with wheel-marks on their soles — how shall those feet walk upon the rough forest ground?' // 8.55 //

children.text: vimānapṛṣṭhe śayanāsanocitaṃ mahārhavastrāgurucandanārcitam /
children.translated_text: 'That body, accustomed to couches and seats on palace-rooftops, honored with precious garments, <s>aguru</s> (aloe), and sandalwood —

children.text: kathaṃ nu śītoṣṇajalāgameṣu taccharīramojasvi vane bhaviṣyati // Bc_8.56 //
children.translated_text: how will that vigorous body fare in the forest, in [seasons of] cold, heat, and rain?' // 8.56 //

children.text: kulena sattvena balena varcasā śrutena lakṣmyā vayasā ca garvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He, who is proud of his lineage, noble nature, strength, radiance, learning, fortune, and youth,

children.text: pradātumevābhyucito na yācituṃ kathaṃ sa bhikṣāṃ parataścariṣyati // Bc_8.57 //
children.translated_text: accustomed to give, not to beg — how will he wander [begging] alms from others?' // 8.57 //

children.text: śucau śayitvā śayane hiraṇmaye prabodhyamāno niśi tūryanisvanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having slept upon a pure golden couch, being awakened at night by the sounds of instruments,

children.text: kathaṃ bata svapsyati so 'dya me vratī paṭaikadeśāntarite mahītale // Bc_8.58 //
