children.translated_text: how, alas, will he, my vow-keeper, sleep today upon the surface of the earth, with only a piece of cloth [as shelter]?' // 8.58 //

children.text: imaṃ pralāpaṃ karuṇaṃ niśamya tā bhujaiḥ pariṣvajya parasparaṃ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing this piteous lament, those women, embracing one another with their arms,

children.text: vilocanebhyaḥ salilāni tatyajurmadhūni puṣpebhya iveritā latāḥ // Bc_8.59 //
children.translated_text: shed water from their eyes — like creepers shaken [by the wind] dropping honey from their blossoms. // 8.59 //

children.text: tato dharāyāmapatadyaśodharā vicakravākeva rathāṅgasāvhayā /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yaśodharā</s> fell upon the ground, like a <s>cakravākī</s> (ruddy goose) named <s>Rathāṅga</s>,

children.text: śanaiśca tattadvilalāpa viklavā muhurmuhurgadgadaruddhayā girā // Bc_8.60 //
children.translated_text: and slowly, in distress, she lamented this and that, in a voice repeatedly choked with sobs: // 8.60 //

children.text: sa māmanāthāṃ sahadharmacāriṇīmapāsya dharma yadi kartumicchati /
children.translated_text: 'If he, casting aside me — his helpless wife and companion in <s>dharma</s> — wishes to practice <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: kuto 'sya dharmaḥ sahadharmacāriṇī vinā tapo yaḥ paribhoktumicchati // Bc_8.61 //
children.translated_text: then how can he have <s>dharma</s>, who wishes to enjoy <s>tapas</s> without his companion in <s>dharma</s>?' // 8.61 //

children.text: śṛṇoti nūnaṃ sa na pūrvapārthivānmahāsudarśaprabhṛtīn pitāmahān /
children.translated_text: 'Surely he has not heard of the ancient kings, grandfathers such as <s>Mahāsudarśa</s> and others,

children.text: vanāni patnīsahitānupeyuṣastathā hi dharma madṛte cikīrṣīte // Bc_8.62 //
children.translated_text: who went to the forests accompanied by their wives — for thus he wishes to practice <s>dharma</s> without me.' // 8.62 //

children.text: makheṣu vā vedavidhānasaṃskṛtau na daṃpatī paśyati dīkṣitābubhau /
children.translated_text: 'Or does he not see in sacrifices, purified by Vedic rites, both husband and wife consecrated?

children.text: samaṃ bubhukṣū parato 'pi tatphalaṃ tato 'sya jāto mayi dharmamatsaraḥ // Bc_8.63 //
children.translated_text: As they wish to enjoy its fruit together even hereafter, he has therefore developed jealousy of <s>dharma</s> toward me!' // 8.63 //

children.text: dhruvaṃ sa jānanmama dharmavallabho manaḥ priyerṣyākalahaṃ muhurmithaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Surely, knowing that my heart — dear as <s>dharma</s> itself — [is prone to] the quarrel of jealousy regarding a beloved, again and again,

children.text: sukhaṃ vibhīrmāmapahāya roṣaṇāṃ mahendraloke 'psaraso jighṛkṣati // Bc_8.64 //
children.translated_text: he happily desires to seize the <s>Apsarases</s> in the world of great <s>Indra</s>, abandoning me, the angry one!' // 8.64 //

children.text: iyaṃ tu cintā mama kīdṛśaṃ nu tā vapurguṇaṃ bibhrati tatra yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But this is my concern: what kind of beauty and qualities do the women there possess,

children.text: vane yadartha sa tapāṃsi tapyate śriyaṃ ca hitvā mama bhaktimeva ca // Bc_8.65 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of which he practices austerities in the forest, abandoning both my glory and my devotion?' // 8.65 //

children.text: na khalviyaṃ svargasukhāya me spṛhā na tajjanasyātmavato 'pi durlabham /
children.translated_text: 'Truly, this longing of mine is not for the pleasures of heaven — for that is not difficult to obtain even for a self-possessed person of such birth;

children.text: sa tu priyo māmiha vā paratra vā kathaṃ na jahyāditi me manorathaḥ // Bc_8.66 //
children.translated_text: but that my beloved should not abandon me, here or hereafter — this is my heart's desire.' // 8.66 //

children.text: abhāginī yadyahamāyatekṣaṇaṃ śucismitaṃ bharturudīkṣituṃ mukham /
children.translated_text: 'If I am so unfortunate as not to gaze upon the long-eyed, brightly smiling face of my lord,

children.text: na mandabhāgyo 'rhati rāhulo 'pyayaṃ kadācidaṅke parivartituṃ pituḥ // Bc_8.67 //
children.translated_text: does not even this ill-fated <s>Rāhula</s> deserve to turn in his father's lap, even once?' // 8.67 //

children.text: aho nṛśaṃsaṃ sukumāravarcasaḥ sudāruṇaṃ tasya manasvino manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, how cruel, how terribly hard is the mind of that tender-complexioned, proud-spirited one,

children.text: kalapralāpaṃ dviṣato 'pi harṣaṇaṃ śiśuṃ sutaṃ yastyajatīdṛśaṃ bata // Bc_8.68 //
children.translated_text: who could abandon such a son — a child whose babbling would delight even an enemy!' // 8.68 //

children.text: mamāpi kāmaṃ hṛdayaṃ sudāruṇaṃ śilāmayaṃ vāpyayaso 'pi vā kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, my heart too must be terribly hard — made of stone, or perhaps fashioned of iron —

children.text: anāthavacchrīrahite sukhocite vanaṃ gate bhartari yanna dīryate // Bc_8.69 //
children.translated_text: that it does not break when my lord, accustomed to comfort, has gone like one without protection to the forest, bereft of glory!' // 8.69 //

children.text: itīha devī patiśokamūrchitā ruroda dadhyau vilalāpa cāsakṛt /
children.translated_text: Thus the queen, overcome by grief for her husband, wept, brooded, and lamented again and again;

children.text: svabhāvadhīrāpi hi sā satī śucā dhṛtiṃ na sasmāra cakāra no hriyam // Bc_8.70 //
children.translated_text: for she — though steadfast and virtuous by nature — from sorrow, remembered neither composure nor modesty. // 8.70 //

children.text: tatastathā śokavilāpaviklavāṃ yaśodharāṃ prekṣya vasuṃdharāgatām /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Yaśodharā</s> in such distress — distraught with grief and lamentation — fallen upon the ground,

children.text: mahāravindairiva vṛṣṭitāḍitairmukhaiḥ sabāṣpairvanitā vicukruśuḥ // Bc_8.71 //
children.translated_text: the women cried out, with tear-stained faces like great lotuses struck by rain. // 8.71 //

children.text: samāptajāpyaḥ kṛtahomamaṅgalo nṛpastu devāyatanādviniryayau /
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, the king, having completed his prayers and performed the auspicious fire-rite, came forth from the temple;

children.text: janasya tejārtaraveṇa cāhataścacāla vajradhvanineva vāraṇaḥ // Bc_8.72 //
children.translated_text: and struck by the anguished cries of the people, he staggered like an elephant [struck] by the sound of a thunderbolt. // 8.72 //

children.text: niśāmya ca cchandakakanthakāvubhau sutasya saṃśrutya ca niścayaṃ sthiram /
children.translated_text: And learning about both <s>Chandaka</s> and <s>Kanthaka</s>, and hearing of his son's firm resolve,

children.text: papāta śokābhihato mahīpatiḥ śacīpatervṛtta ivotsave dhvajaḥ // Bc_8.73 //
children.translated_text: the king, stricken by grief, fell — like a festival banner of <s>Śacī</s>'s lord (<s>Indra</s>) when [the festival] is over. // 8.73 //

children.text: tato muhūrta sutaśokamohito janena tulyābhijanena dhāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, for a moment bewildered by grief for his son, supported by attendants of equal birth,

children.text: nirīkṣya dṛṣṭyā jalapūrṇayā hayaṃ mahītalastho vilalāpa pārthivaḥ // Bc_8.74 //
children.translated_text: gazing with eyes full of water at the horse, the king, [seated] upon the ground, lamented: // 8.74 //

children.text: bahūni kṛtvā samare priyāṇi me mahattvayā kanthaka vipriyaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Having done me many favors in battle, you, <s>Kanthaka</s>, have done me a great disfavor;

children.text: guṇapriyo yena vane sa me priyaḥ priyo 'pi sannapriyavatpraveritaḥ // Bc_8.75 //
children.translated_text: for that beloved of mine, who is dear to virtue — though dear, was carried away by you as if [he were] not dear.' // 8.75 //

children.text: tadadya māṃ vā naya tatra yatra sa vraja drutaṃ vā punarenamānaya /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, either take me now to where he is, or bring him back swiftly;

children.text: ṛte hi tasmānmama nāsti jīvitaṃ vigāḍharogasya sadauṣadhādiva // Bc_8.76 //
children.translated_text: for without him, there is no life for me — like one deeply ill without his constant medicine.' // 8.76 //

children.text: suvarṇaniṣṭhīvini mṛtyunā hṛte suduṣkaraṃ yanna mamāra saṃjayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When <s>Suvarṇaniṣṭhīvī</s> (Gold-spitter) was carried off by death, it was a very difficult thing that <s>Saṃjaya</s> did not die;

children.text: ahaṃ punardharmaratau sute gate mumukṣurātmānamanātmavāniva // Bc_8.77 //
children.translated_text: but I, when my son devoted to <s>dharma</s> has departed, wish to die — like one without self-control!' // 8.77 //

children.text: vibhordaśakṣatrakṛtaḥ prajāpateḥ parāparajñasya vivasvadātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of the mighty <s>Prajāpati</s> (lord of creation), born of the ten <s>Kṣatras</s>, knower of the near and far, of the lineage of <s>Vivasvat</s> (the Sun) —

children.text: priyeṇa putreṇa satā vinākṛtaṃ kathaṃ na muhyeddhi mano manorapi // Bc_8.78 //
children.translated_text: how would the mind not be bewildered, even that of <s>Manu</s> — being separated from his dear, virtuous son?' // 8.78 //

children.text: ajasya rājñastanayāya dhīmate narādhipāyendrasakhāya me spṛhā /
children.translated_text: 'I envy the wise son of King <s>Aja</s>, the lord of men, the friend of <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: gate vanaṃ yastanaye divaṃ gato na moghabāṣpaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ jijīva ha // Bc_8.79 //
children.translated_text: who, when his son went to the forest, went to heaven — and did not live on pitifully, shedding tears in vain.' // 8.79 //

children.text: pracakṣva me bhadra tadāśramājiraṃ hṛtastvayā yatra sa me jalāñjaliḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Point out to me, O good one, that hermitage-grounds where he — my water-offering — was taken by you;

children.text: ime parīpsanti hi taṃ pipāsavo mamāsavaḥ pretagatiṃ yiyāsavaḥ // Bc_8.80 //
children.translated_text: for these thirsty vital breaths of mine desire him, wishing to go the way of the departed.' // 8.80 //

children.text: iti tanayaviyogajātaduḥkha kṣitisadṛśaṃ sahajaṃ vihāya dhairyam /
children.translated_text: Thus, the king — his grief born from separation from his son — abandoning his innate, earth-like steadfastness,

children.text: daśaratha iva rāmaśokavaśyo bahu vilalāpa nṛpo visaṃjñakalpaḥ // Bc_8.81 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Daśaratha</s> overcome by grief for <s>Rāma</s>, lamented much, nearly unconscious. // 8.81 //

children.text: śrutavinayaguṇānvitastatastaṃ matisacivaḥ pravayā purohitaśca /
children.translated_text: Then the wise counselor, endowed with learning, discipline, and virtues, and the aged royal priest,

children.text: samadhṛtamidamūcaturyathāvanna ca pariptamukhau na cāpyaśokau // Bc_8.82 //
children.translated_text: spoke to him these measured words, in a fitting manner — neither with downcast faces, nor yet without sorrow: // 8.82 //

children.text: tyaja naravara śokamehi dhairya kudhṛtirivārhasi dhīra nāśru moktum /
children.translated_text: 'Abandon grief, O best of men, and come to steadfastness; you should not shed tears, O steadfast one, like one of weak resolve;

children.text: srajamiva mṛditāmapāsya lakṣmīṃ bhuvi bahavo hi nṛpā vanānyabhīyuḥ // Bc_8.83 //
children.translated_text: for many kings upon the earth, casting aside sovereignty like a trampled garland, have gone to the forests.' // 8.83 //

children.text: api ca niyata eṣa tasya bhāvaḥ smara vacanaṃ tadṛṣeḥ purāsitasya /
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, his disposition is firmly fixed — remember the words of that ancient sage <s>Asita</s>;

children.text: na hi sa divi na cakravartirājye kṣaṇamapi vāsayituṃ sukhena śakyaḥ // Bc_8.84 //
children.translated_text: for he cannot be made to dwell contentedly even for a moment, either in heaven or in a world-emperor's kingdom.' // 8.84 //

children.text: yadi tu nṛvara kārya eva yatnastvaritamudāhara yāvadatra yāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But if, O best of men, effort must indeed be made, then declare it swiftly, while we are still here;

children.text: bahuvidhimiha yuddhamastu tāvattava tanayasya vidheśca tasya tasya // Bc_8.85 //
children.translated_text: let there be a battle of many strategies here between your son and his various [resolutions].' // 8.85 //

children.text: narapatiratha tau śaśāsa tasmād drutamita eva yuvāmabhiprayātam /
children.translated_text: The king then commanded them: 'Go swiftly, the two of you, in that very direction;

children.text: na hi mama hṛdayaṃ prayāti śāntiṃ vanaśakuneriva putralālasasya // Bc_8.86 //
children.translated_text: for my heart does not find peace — like a forest bird longing for its young.' // 8.86 //

children.text: paramamiti narendraśāsanāttau yayaturamātyapurohitau vanaṃ tat /
children.translated_text: 'Very well!' — thus, by the king's command, the minister and the royal priest went to that forest;

children.text: kṛtamiti savadhūjanaḥ sadāro nṛpatirapi pracakāra śeṣakāryam // Bc_8.87 //
children.translated_text: and the king, along with his daughters-in-law and his wife, attended also to the remaining duties. // 8.87 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth canto, named 'The Lament of the Inner Chambers,' in the <s>Buddhacarita</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>. // 8 //
CANTO IX

children.text: tatastadā mantripurohitau tau bāṣpapratodābhihatau nṛpeṇa /
children.translated_text: Then the minister and the royal priest, those two, goaded by the king's tears,

children.text: viddhau sadaśvāviva sarvayatnātsauhārdaśīghraṃ yayaturvanaṃ tat // Bc_9.1 //
children.translated_text: like two good horses struck [by the whip], went with all speed to that forest, swift with affection. // Bc_9.1 //

children.text: tamāśramaṃ jātapariśramau tāvupetya kāle sadṛśānuyātrau /
children.translated_text: Those two, having endured the fatigue, arrived at that hermitage at the proper time, with a retinue befitting [their rank],

children.text: rājarddhimutsṛjya vinītaceṣṭāvupeyaturbhārgavadhiṣṇyameva // Bc_9.2 //
children.translated_text: and setting aside royal splendor, with modest conduct, approached the seat of <s>Bhārgava</s> alone. // Bc_9.2 //

children.text: tau nyāyatastaṃ pratipūjya vipraṃ tenārcitau tāvapi cānurūpam /
children.translated_text: They duly honored that Brahmin, and he in turn honored them appropriately;

children.text: kṛtāsanau bhārgavamāsanasthaṃ chittvā kathāmūcaturātmakṛtyam // Bc_9.3 //
children.translated_text: having taken their seats, they addressed <s>Bhārgava</s>, seated [before them], cutting to the matter at hand: // Bc_9.3 //

children.text: śuddhaujasaḥ śuddhaviśālakīrterikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhavasya rājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Of the king of pure might, of pure and vast fame, born of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage —

children.text: imaṃ janaṃ vettu bhavānadhītaṃ śrutagrahe mantraparigrahe ca // Bc_9.4 //
children.translated_text: may Your Holiness know these men as learned in the grasp of scripture and in the command of counsel. // Bc_9.4 //

children.text: tasyendrakalpasya jayantakalpaḥ putro jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ titīrṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: "His son, equal to <s>Jayanta</s> as the king is equal to <s>Indra</s>, wishing to cross beyond the fear of old age and death,

children.text: ihābhyutepaḥ kila tasya hetorāvāmupetau bhagavānavaitu // Bc_9.5 //
children.translated_text: has reportedly come here — for his sake we two have come. May the Blessed One know this." // Bc_9.5 //

children.text: tau so 'bravīdasti sa dīrghabāhuḥ prāptaḥ kumāro na tu nāvabuddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: He told them: "That long-armed prince has indeed arrived, but he has not remained unenlightened;

children.text: dharmo 'yamāvartaka ityavetya yātastvarāḍābhimukho mumukṣuḥ // Bc_9.6 //
children.translated_text: knowing that this <s>dharma</s> of return [to worldly life] is cyclic, he has gone, the seeker of liberation, toward <s>Arāḍa</s>." // Bc_9.6 //

children.text: tasmāttatastāvupalabhya tattvaṃ taṃ vipramāmantrya tadaiva sadyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having ascertained the truth from that Brahmin and having taken leave of him, those two, that very moment,

children.text: khinnāvakhinnāviva rājabhaktyā prasasratustena yataḥ sa yātaḥ // Bc_9.7 //
children.translated_text: set out — though weary, as if unwearied through devotion to the king — in the direction he had gone. // Bc_9.7 //

children.text: yāntau tatastau mṛjayā vihīnamapaśyatāṃ taṃ vapuṣojjvalantam /
children.translated_text: Going thus, they saw him, deprived of adornment yet blazing with his natural splendor,

children.text: upopaviṣṭaṃ pathi vṛkṣamūle sūrya ghanābhogamiva praviṣṭam // Bc_9.8 //
children.translated_text: seated at the foot of a tree by the roadside, like the sun that has entered the mass of clouds. // Bc_9.8 //

children.text: yānaṃ vihāyopayayau tatastaṃ purohito mantradhareṇa sārdham /
children.translated_text: Then the royal priest, leaving his vehicle, approached him together with the minister,

children.text: yathā vanasthaṃ sahavāmadevo rāmaṃ didṛkṣurmunirāvairvaśeyaḥ // Bc_9.9 //
children.translated_text: just as the sage <s>Vāmadeva</s>, wishing to see <s>Rāma</s> dwelling in the forest, [approached him] together with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s descendant. // Bc_9.9 //

children.text: tāvarcayāmāsaturarhatastaṃ divīva śukrāṅgirasau mahendram /
children.translated_text: Those two honored him who was worthy, as <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> [honor] great <s>Indra</s> in heaven;

children.text: pratyarcayāmāsa sa cārhatastau divīva śukrāṅgirasau mahendraḥ // Bc_9.10 //
children.translated_text: and he in turn honored those two who were worthy, as great <s>Indra</s> in heaven [honors] <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>. // Bc_9.10 //

children.text: kṛtābhyanujñāvabhitastatastau niṣedatuḥ śākyakuladhvajasya /
children.translated_text: Having received permission, those two then sat on either side of the banner of the <s>Śākya</s> clan,

children.text: virejatustasya ca saṃnikarṣe punarvasū yogagatāvivendoḥ // Bc_9.11 //
children.translated_text: and they shone in his proximity like the two stars of <s>Punarvasu</s> in conjunction with the moon. // Bc_9.11 //

children.text: taṃ vṛkṣamūlasthamabhijvalantaṃ purohito rājasutaṃ babhāṣe /
children.translated_text: The royal priest addressed the prince seated at the tree-root, radiant,

children.text: yathopaviṣṭaṃ divi pārijāte bṛhaspatiḥ śakrasutaṃ jayantam // Bc_9.12 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [would address] <s>Jayanta</s>, the son of <s>Śakra</s>, seated in heaven upon the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree: // Bc_9.12 //

children.text: tvacchokaśalye hṛdayāvagāḍhe mohaṃ gato bhūmitale muhūrtam /
children.translated_text: "The king, his heart pierced by the arrow of grief for you, swooning upon the ground for a moment,

children.text: kumāra rājā nayanāmbuvarṣo yattvāmavocattadidaṃ nibodha // Bc_9.13 //
children.translated_text: O prince, shedding a rain of tears — what he said to you, hear this: // Bc_9.13 //

children.text: jānāmi dharma prati niścayaṃ te paraimi te bhāvinametamartham /
children.translated_text: 'I know your resolve regarding <s>dharma</s>; I foresee that this goal will come to fruition for you;

children.text: ahaṃ tvakāle vanasaṃśrayātte śokāgnināgnipratimena dahye // Bc_9.14 //
children.translated_text: but because you have taken to the forest at an untimely [age], I am being burned by the fire of sorrow, like fire itself. // Bc_9.14 //

children.text: tadehi dharmapriya matpriyārtha dharmārthameva tyaja buddhimetām /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore come, O lover of <s>dharma</s>, for my sake; for the sake of <s>dharma</s> itself, abandon this intention;

children.text: ayaṃ hi mā śokarayaḥ pravṛddhau nadīrayaḥ kūlamivābhihanti // Bc_9.15 //
children.translated_text: for this flood of sorrow, swelling, strikes me as the flood of a river strikes its bank. // Bc_9.15 //

children.text: meghāmbukakṣādriṣu yā hi vṛttiḥ samīraṇārkāgnimahāśanīnām /
children.translated_text: 'The action that wind, sun, fire, and great thunderbolts perform upon clouds, water, brushwood, and mountains —

children.text: tāṃ vṛttimasmāsu karoti śoko vikarṣaṇocchoṣaṇadāhabhedaiḥ // Bc_9.16 //
children.translated_text: that very action sorrow performs upon us, through tearing, drying, burning, and splitting. // Bc_9.16 //

children.text: tadbhuṅkṣva tāvadvasudhādhipatyaṃ kāle vanaṃ yāsyāsi śāstradṛṣṭe /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, enjoy the sovereignty of the earth for now; you shall go to the forest at the time prescribed by scripture;

children.text: aniṣṭabandhau kuru mayyapekṣāṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu dayā hi dharmaḥ // Bc_9.17 //
children.translated_text: show consideration for me, even if your attachment is not desired — for compassion toward all beings is <s>dharma</s>. // Bc_9.17 //

children.text: na caiṣa dharmo vana eva siddhaḥ pure 'pi siddhirniyatā yatīnām /
children.translated_text: 'Nor is this <s>dharma</s> accomplished only in the forest; liberation is certain even in the city for the self-controlled;

children.text: buddhiśca yatnaśca nimittamatra vana ca liṅgaṃ ca hi bhīrucinham // Bc_9.18 //
children.translated_text: intellect and effort are the means here — the forest and the [ascetic] garb are the mark of the timid. // Bc_9.18 //

children.text: maulīdharairasaviṣaktahāraiḥ keyūraviṣṭabdhabhujairnarendraiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By kings bearing crowns, adorned with necklaces, with arms encircled by armlets,

children.text: lakṣbhyaṅkamadhye parivartamānaiḥ prāpto gṛhasthairapi mokṣadharmaḥ // Bc_9.19 //
children.translated_text: reclining in the lap of <s>Lakṣmī</s> — the <s>dharma</s> of liberation has been attained even by householders. // Bc_9.19 //

children.text: dhruvānujau yau balivajrabāhū vaibhrājamāṣāḍhamathāntidevam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dhruva</s> and his two brothers, <s>Bali</s> and <s>Vajrabāhu</s>, <s>Vaibhrāja</s>, <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, and then <s>Antideva</s>,

children.text: videharājaṃ janakaṃ tathaiva śālvadrumaṃ senajitaśca rājñaḥ // Bc_9.20 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Videha</s> king <s>Janaka</s>, and likewise king <s>Śālvadruma</s> and <s>Senajit</s> — // Bc_9.20 //

children.text: etān gṛhasthānnṛpatīnavehi naiḥśreyase dharmavidhau vinītān /
children.translated_text: 'Know these kings, though householders, as trained in the discipline of <s>dharma</s> leading to the highest good;

children.text: ubhe 'pi tasmādyugapadbhajasva cittādhipatyaṃ ca nṛpaśriyaṃ ca // Bc_9.21 //
children.translated_text: therefore, embrace both simultaneously — mastery over the mind and the glory of kingship.' // Bc_9.21 //

children.text: icchāmi hi tvāmupaguhya gāḍhaṃ kṛtābhiṣekaṃ salilārdrameva /
children.translated_text: 'For I wish to embrace you tightly, freshly anointed with the waters of consecration,

children.text: dhṛtātapattraṃ samudīkṣamāṇastenaiva harṣeṇa vanaṃ praveṣṭum // Bc_9.22 //
children.translated_text: to gaze upon you holding the royal parasol — and with that very joy, to enter the forest. // Bc_9.22 //

children.text: ityabravīdbhūmipatirbhavantaṃ vākyena bāṣpagrathitākṣareṇa /
children.translated_text: 'Thus the king spoke to you, with words whose syllables were choked with tears;

children.text: śrutvā bhavānarhati tatpriyārtha snehena tasnehamanuprayātum // Bc_9.23 //
children.translated_text: having heard this, you should — for his sake and out of affection — return that affection.'" // Bc_9.23 //

children.text: śokāmbhasi tvatprabhave hyagādhe duḥkhārṇave majjati śākyarājaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For the <s>Śākya</s> king is drowning in the fathomless ocean of sorrow arising from you, in the sea of suffering;

children.text: tasmāttamuttāraya nāthahīnaṃ nirāśrayaṃ magnamivārṇave nauḥ // Bc_9.24 //
children.translated_text: therefore, rescue him who is without a protector — like a ship [rescuing] one sinking helplessly in the ocean. // Bc_9.24 //

children.text: bhīṣmeṇa gaṅgodarasaṃbhavena rāmeṇa rāmeṇa ca bhārgaveṇa /
children.translated_text: "Having heard of the deeds done for a father's sake by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, born from the womb of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, by <s>Rāma</s>, and by <s>Rāma</s> of <s>Bhārgava</s>'s line —

children.text: śrutvā kṛtaṃ karma pituḥ priyārtha pitustvamaopyarhasi kartumiṣṭam // Bc_9.25 //
children.translated_text: you too should do what is pleasing for your father. // Bc_9.25 //

children.text: saṃvardhayitrī samavehi devīmagastyajuṣṭāṃ diśamaprayātām /
children.translated_text: "Consider the queen who raised you, who has not departed to the quarter favored by <s>Agastya</s> (the south, i.e., death),

children.text: pranaṣṭavatsāmiva vatsalāṃ gāmajasramārtā karuṇaṃ rudantīm // Bc_9.26 //
children.translated_text: weeping piteously, ceaselessly afflicted, like an affectionate cow whose calf has been lost. // Bc_9.26 //

children.text: haṃsena haṃsīmiva viprayuktāṃ tyaktāṃ gajeneva vane kareṇum /
children.translated_text: "Like a female goose separated from a gander, like a female elephant abandoned by the bull in the forest —

children.text: artā sanāthāmapi nāthahīnāṃ trātuṃ vadhūmarhasi darśanena // Bc_9.27 //
children.translated_text: though she has a protector, she is as if without one — you should rescue your bride through your presence. // Bc_9.27 //

children.text: ekaṃ sutaṃ bālamanarhaduḥkhaṃ saṃtāpamantargatamudvahantam /
children.translated_text: "Your one son, a child, undeserving of suffering, bearing an inner grief,

children.text: taṃ rāhulaṃ mokṣaya bandhuśokādrāhūpasargādeva pūrṇacandram // Bc_9.28 //
children.translated_text: free that <s>Rāhula</s> from the sorrow of [losing] his kinsman — as the full moon [is freed] from the affliction of <s>Rāhu</s>. // Bc_9.28 //

children.text: tvaddarśanāmbvicchati dahyamānamantaḥpuraṃ caiva puraṃ ca kṛtsnam // Bc_9.29 //
children.translated_text: being consumed, the inner chambers and the entire city seek the water of your presence. // Bc_9.29 //

body.translated_text: "By the fire of sorrow, whose fuel is your absence, whose smoke is sighing, whose flame is darkness,

children.text: sa bodhisattvaḥ paripūrṇasattvaḥ śrutvā vacastasya purohitasya /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, of perfect being, having heard the words of that royal priest,

children.text: dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ guṇavadguṇajñaḥ pratyuttaraṃ praśritamityuvāca // Bc_9.30 //
children.translated_text: reflecting for a moment, the knower of virtues, endowed with virtue, spoke this modest reply: // Bc_9.30 //

children.text: avaimi bhāvaṃ tanaye pitṝṇāṃ viśeṣato yo mayi bhūmipasya /
children.translated_text: "I know the affection of parents toward a son, and especially that of the king toward me;

children.text: jānannapi vyādhijarāvipadbhyo bhītastvagatyā svajanaṃ tyajāmi // Bc_9.31 //
children.translated_text: yet, knowing [this], terrified by disease, old age, and calamity, I helplessly abandon my kinsmen. // Bc_9.31 //

children.text: draṣṭuṃ priyaṃ kaḥ svajanaṃ hi necchennānte yadi syātpriyaviprayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For who would not wish to see his dear kinsmen, if in the end there were no separation from the beloved?

children.text: yadā tu bhūtvāpi ciraṃ viyogastato guruaṃ snindhamapi tyajāmi // Bc_9.32 //
children.translated_text: But since, even after long [togetherness], separation is inevitable, therefore I abandon even the most cherished affection. // Bc_9.32 //

children.text: maddhetukaṃ yattu narādhipasya śokaṃ bhavānāha na tatpriyaṃ me /
children.translated_text: "As for the sorrow of the lord of men on my account, which you have mentioned — that is not pleasing to me;

children.text: yatsvapnabhūteṣu samāgameṣu saṃtapyate bhāvini viprayoge // Bc_9.33 //
children.translated_text: that one grieves over meetings that are dream-like, when separation is bound to come. // Bc_9.33 //

children.text: evaṃ ca te niścayametu buddhirdṛṣṭvā vicitraṃ jagataḥ pracāram /
children.translated_text: "Let your understanding come to this conclusion, having seen the wondrous course of the world:

children.text: saṃtāpaheturna suto na bandhurajñānanaimittika eṣa tāpaḥ // Bc_9.34 //
children.translated_text: the cause of anguish is not a son, nor a kinsman — this suffering is rooted in ignorance. // Bc_9.34 //

children.text: yathādhvagānamiha saṃgatānāṃ kāle viyogo niyataḥ prajānām /
children.translated_text: "Just as for travelers who have met here, separation at the proper time is certain for beings —

children.text: prājño janaḥ ko tu bhajeta śokaṃ bandhupratijñātajanairvihīnaḥ // Bc_9.35 //
children.translated_text: what wise person would embrace grief, being deprived of those merely acknowledged as kinsmen? // Bc_9.35 //

children.text: ihaiti hitvā svajanaṃ paratra pralabhya cehāpi punaḥ prayāti /
children.translated_text: "Leaving his own people, he goes to the other world; and having obtained [companions] there, he departs again here;

children.text: gatvāpi tatrāpyaparatra gacchatyevaṃ jane tyāgini ko 'nurodhaḥ // Bc_9.36 //
children.translated_text: having gone there too, he goes yet elsewhere — in beings who are thus always departing, what [reason is there for] attachment? // Bc_9.36 //

children.text: yadā ca garbhātprabhṛti pravṛttaḥ sarvāsvavasthāsu vadhāya mṛtyuḥ /
children.translated_text: "And since death, active from the womb onward, is engaged in destruction at every stage,

children.text: kasmādakāle vanasaṃśrayaṃ me putrapriyastatrabhavānavocat // Bc_9.37 //
children.translated_text: why did His Honor, fond of his son, speak of my forest-dwelling as 'untimely'? // Bc_9.37 //

children.text: bhavatyakālo viṣayābhipattau kālastathaivārthavidhau pradiṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: "There may be an untimely moment for the pursuit of sense-objects, and a proper time is prescribed for the pursuit of wealth;

children.text: kālo jagatkarṣati sarvakālānnirvāhake śreyasi nāsti kālaḥ // Bc_9.38 //
children.translated_text: but time drags all beings at all times — there is no [fixed] time for pursuing the enduring good. // Bc_9.38 //

children.text: rājyaṃ mumukṣurmayi yacca rājā tadapyudāraṃ sadṛśaṃ pituśca /
children.translated_text: "That the king wishes to bestow the kingdom upon me — that too is noble and befitting a father;

children.text: pratigrahītuṃ mama na kṣamaṃ tu lobhādapathyānnamivāturasya // Bc_9.39 //
children.translated_text: but for me to accept it would not be proper — like unwholesome food for a sick man, out of greed. // Bc_9.39 //

children.text: kathaṃ nu mohāyatanaṃ nṛpatvaṃ kṣamaṃ prapattuṃ viduṣā nareṇa /
children.translated_text: "How could a wise man deem it proper to embrace kingship, which is the abode of delusion —

children.text: sodvegatā yatra madaḥ śramaśca parāpacāreṇa ca dharmapīḍā // Bc_9.40 //
children.translated_text: where there is anxiety, intoxication, and toil, and injury to <s>dharma</s> through harming others? // Bc_9.40 //

children.text: jāmbūnadaṃ harmyamiva pradīptaṃ viṣeṇa saṃyuktamivottamānnam /
children.translated_text: "Like a golden palace that is ablaze, like the finest food mixed with poison,

children.text: grāhākulaṃ cāmbviva sāravindaṃ rājyaṃ hi ramyaṃ vyasanāśrayaṃ ca // Bc_9.41 //
children.translated_text: like a lake with lotuses infested with crocodiles — kingship is delightful and yet the abode of calamity. // Bc_9.41 //

children.text: itthaṃ ca rājyaṃ na sukhaṃ na dharmaḥ pūrve yathā jātaghṛṇā narendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Thus indeed, kingship brings neither happiness nor <s>dharma</s> — just as former kings, having developed compassion,

children.text: vayaḥprakarṣe 'parihāryaduḥkhe rājyāni muktvā vanameva jagmuḥ // Bc_9.42 //
children.translated_text: when unavoidable suffering [came] in the advance of age, abandoned their kingdoms and went to the forest. // Bc_9.42 //

children.text: varaṃ hi bhuktāni tṛṇānyaraṇye toṣaṃ paraṃ ratnamivopagṛhya /
children.translated_text: "Better indeed to eat grass in the forest, embracing supreme contentment as if it were a gem,

children.text: sahoṣitaṃ śrīsulabhairna caiva doṣairadṛśyairiva kṛṣṇasarpaiḥ // Bc_9.43 //
children.translated_text: than to dwell with the easily-acquired [pleasures] of royal fortune, attended by invisible faults like black serpents. // Bc_9.43 //

children.text: ślādhyaṃ hi rājyāni vihāya rājñāṃ dharmābhilāṣeṇa vanaṃ praveṣṭum /
children.translated_text: "It is praiseworthy for kings to abandon their kingdoms and enter the forest with a desire for <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: bhagnapratijñasya na tūpapannaṃ vanaṃ parityajya gṛhaṃ praveṣṭum // Bc_9.44 //
children.translated_text: but it is not proper for one who has broken his vow to abandon the forest and enter the household. // Bc_9.44 //

children.text: jātaḥ kule ko hi naraḥ sasattvo dharmābhilāṣeṇa vanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: "What man of noble birth and noble character, having entered the forest with desire for <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: kāṣāyamutsṛjya vimuktalajjaḥ puraṃdarasyāpi puraṃ śrayeta // Bc_9.45 //
children.translated_text: would cast off the ochre robe, abandon all shame, and resort to the city — even the city of <s>Purandara</s> (Indra)? // Bc_9.45 //

children.text: lobhāddhi mohādathavā bhayena yo vāntamannaṃ punarādadīta /
children.translated_text: "One who out of greed, or delusion, or fear would eat again food that has been vomited —

children.text: lobhātsa mohādathavā bhayena saṃtyajya kāmān punarādadīta // Bc_9.46 //
children.translated_text: he, out of greed, or delusion, or fear, would take up again the desires he had renounced. // Bc_9.46 //

children.text: yaśca pradīptāccharaṇātkathaṃcinniṣkramya bhūyaḥ praviśettadeva /
children.translated_text: "And one who, having somehow escaped from a burning house, would enter it again —

children.text: gārhasthyamutsṛjya sa dṛṣṭadoṣo mohena bhūyo 'bhilaṣedgrahītum // Bc_9.47 //
children.translated_text: he, having renounced household life after seeing its faults, would in delusion desire to take it up again. // Bc_9.47 //

children.text: yā ca śrutirmokṣamavāptavanto nṛpā gṛhasthā iti naitadasti /
children.translated_text: "As for the report that kings while [remaining] householders have attained liberation — that is not so;

children.text: śamapradhānaḥ kva ca mokṣadharmo daṇḍapradhānaḥ kva ca rājadharmaḥ // Bc_9.48 //
children.translated_text: for where is the <s>dharma</s> of liberation, whose foundation is tranquility, and where is the <s>dharma</s> of kingship, whose foundation is punishment? // Bc_9.48 //

children.text: śame ratiścecchithilaṃ ca rājyaṃ rājye matiścecchamaviplavaśca /
children.translated_text: "If one delights in tranquility, then the kingdom is lax; if the mind is set on kingship, then tranquility is undermined;

children.text: śamaśca taikṣṇyaṃ ca hi nopapannaṃ śītoṣṇayoraikyamivodakāgnyoḥ // Bc_9.49 //
children.translated_text: for tranquility and severity are not compatible — like the unity of cold and hot, of water and fire. // Bc_9.49 //

children.text: tanniścayādvā vasudhādhipāste rājyāni muktvā śamamāptavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, either those lords of the earth, having truly abandoned their kingdoms, attained tranquility;

children.text: rājyāṅgitā vā nibhṛtendriyatvādanaiṣṭhike mokṣakṛtābhimānāḥ // Bc_9.50 //
children.translated_text: or, marked by kingship, due to the subduing of their senses, they harbored a [false] pride of [having achieved] the non-ultimate liberation. // Bc_9.50 //

children.text: teṣāṃ ca rājye 'stu śamo yathāvatprāpto vanaṃ nāhamaniścayena /
children.translated_text: "Let tranquility be duly [achieved] by them in their kingship — I, for my part, have not come to the forest with uncertainty;

children.text: chittvā hi pāśaṃ gṛhabandhusaṃjñaṃ muktaḥ punarna pravivikṣurasmi // Bc_9.51 //
children.translated_text: for having cut the bond called home and kinsmen, I am free and do not wish to enter [bondage] again. // Bc_9.51 //"

children.text: ityātmavijñānaguṇānurūpaṃ muktaspṛhaṃ hetumadūrjitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having heard the prince's reply — fitting his self-knowledge and virtue, free from longing, reasoned, and firm —

children.text: śrutvā narendrātmajamuktavantaṃ pratyuttaraṃ mantradharo 'pyuvāca // Bc_9.52 //
children.translated_text: the minister also spoke: // Bc_9.52 //

children.text: yo niścayo dharmavidhau tavāyaṃ nāyaṃ na yukto na tu kālayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This resolve of yours regarding the discipline of <s>dharma</s> is not improper, yet it is not timely;

children.text: śokāya dattvā pitaraṃ vayaḥsthaṃ syāddharmakāmasya hi te na dharmaḥ // Bc_9.53 //
children.translated_text: for having given your aged father over to sorrow, this would not be <s>dharma</s> for one desirous of <s>dharma</s>. // Bc_9.53 //

children.text: nūnaṃ ca buddhistava nātisūkṣmā dharmārthakāmeṣvavicakṣaṇā vā /
children.translated_text: "Surely your intelligence is not very subtle, or is undiscriminating in matters of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> —

children.text: hetoradṛṣṭasya phalasya yastvaṃ pratyakṣamartha paribhūya yāsi // Bc_9.54 //
children.translated_text: since you, for the sake of an unseen fruit, are disregarding a purpose that is present before your eyes. // Bc_9.54 //

children.text: punarbhavo 'stīti ca kecidāhurnāstīti kecinniyatapratijñāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Some say there is rebirth; others, of firm conviction, say there is not;

children.text: evaṃ yadā saṃśayito 'yamarthastasmātkṣamaṃ bhoktumupasthitā śrīḥ // Bc_9.55 //
children.translated_text: since this matter is thus doubtful, therefore it is proper to enjoy the fortune that has presented itself. // Bc_9.55 //

children.text: bhūyaḥ pravṛttiryadi kācidasti raṃsyāmahe tatra yathopapattau /
children.translated_text: "If there is any further existence [after death], we shall enjoy ourselves there as it comes;

children.text: atha pravṛttiḥ parato na kācitsiddhau 'prayatnājjagato 'sya mokṣaḥ // Bc_9.56 //
children.translated_text: and if there is no further existence beyond, then without effort, liberation of this world is accomplished. // Bc_9.56 //

children.text: astīti kecitparalokamāhurmokṣasya yogaṃ na tu varṇayanti /
children.translated_text: "Some declare that the other world exists, but do not describe the means to liberation;

children.text: agneryathā hyauṣṇyamapāṃ dravatvaṃ tadvatpravṛttau prakṛtiṃ vadanti // Bc_9.57 //
children.translated_text: just as heat belongs to fire and fluidity to water, they declare [repeated] existence to be the nature [of things]. // Bc_9.57 //

children.text: kecitsvabhāvāditi varṇayanti śubhāśubhaṃ caiva bhavābhavau ca /
children.translated_text: "Some explain it as arising from inherent nature — both the auspicious and the inauspicious, and both being and non-being.

children.text: svābhāvikaṃ sarvamidaṃ ca yasmādato 'pi mogho bhavati prayatnaḥ // Bc_9.58 //
children.translated_text: and since all this is natural, therefore too, effort is futile. // Bc_9.58 //

children.text: yadindriyāṇāṃ niyataḥ pracāraḥ priyāpriyatvaṃ viṣayeṣu caiva /
children.translated_text: If the activity of the senses is fixed, and if pleasure and displeasure in objects [are fixed],

children.text: saṃyujyate yajjarayārtibhiśca kastatra yatno nanu sa svabhāvaḥ // Bc_9.59 //
children.translated_text: and if one is conjoined with old age and suffering — what effort is there? Is it not just nature? // Bc_9.59 //

children.text: adbhirhutāśaḥ śamamabhyupaiti tejāṃsi cāpo gamayanti śoṣam /
children.translated_text: Fire is quenched by water, and fire causes water to evaporate;

children.text: bhinnāni bhūtāni śarīrasaṃsthānyaikyaṃ ca gatvā jagadudvahanti // Bc_9.60 //
children.translated_text: the elements, though distinct, when dwelling in a body, come together and sustain the world. // Bc_9.60 //

children.text: yatpāṇipādodarapṛṣṭhamūrdhnā nirvartate garbhagatasya bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: When, in the womb, the condition arises of hands, feet, belly, back, and head,

children.text: yadātmanastasya ca tena yogaḥ svābhāvikaṃ tatkathayanti tajjñāḥ // Bc_9.61 //
children.translated_text: and when there is a connection of these with the self — those who know call that natural. // Bc_9.61 //

children.text: kaḥ kaṇṭakasya prakaroti taikṣṇyaṃ vicitrabhāvaṃ mṛgapakṣiṇāṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Who makes the sharpness of the thorn, or the varied nature of beasts and birds?

children.text: svabhāvataḥ sarvamidaṃ pravṛttaṃ na kāmakāro 'sti kutaḥ prayatnaḥ // Bc_9.62 //
children.translated_text: All this proceeds from nature; there is no free will — whence then effort? // Bc_9.62 //

children.text: sarga vadantīśvaratastathānye tatra paryatne puruṣasya ko 'rthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Others say creation is from God — then what is the use of a man's effort?

children.text: ya eva heturjagataḥ pravṛttau heturnivṛttau niyataḥ sa eva // Bc_9.63 //
children.translated_text: The very cause that sets the world in motion is necessarily the cause of its cessation too. // Bc_9.63 //

children.text: kecidvadantyātmanimittameva prādurbhavaṃ caiva bhavakṣayaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Some say that both arising and the destruction of existence are from the self alone as cause;

children.text: prādurbhavaṃ tu pravadantyayatnādyatnena mokṣādhigamaṃ bruvanti // Bc_9.64 //
children.translated_text: but they say arising is without effort, while they declare that the attainment of liberation requires effort. // Bc_9.64 //

children.text: naraḥ pitṛṇāmanṛṇaḥ prajābhirvedaiṛṣīṇāṃ kratubhiḥ surāṇām /
children.translated_text: A man is born with three debts — to the ancestors through offspring, to the sages through the <s>Vedas</s>, to the gods through sacrifices;

children.text: utpadyate sārdhamṛṇaistribhistairyasyāsti mokṣaḥ kila tasya mokṣaḥ // Bc_9.65 //
children.translated_text: one who has liberation, they say, has liberation [only] when freed from these three debts. // Bc_9.65 //

children.text: ityevametena vidhikrameṇa mokṣaṃ sayatnasya vadanti tajjñāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, by this procedural sequence, those who know declare liberation for the one who strives;

children.text: prayatnavanto 'pi hi vikrameṇa mumukṣavaḥ khedamavāpnuvanti // Bc_9.66 //
children.translated_text: for even those who strive with effort, seeking liberation, attain weariness. // Bc_9.66 //

children.text: tatsaumya mokṣe yadi bhaktirasti nyāyena sevasva vidhiṃ yathoktam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, gentle one, if you are devoted to liberation, follow the prescribed method rightly as stated;

children.text: evaṃ bhaviṣyatyupapattirasya saṃtāpanāśaśca narādhipasya // Bc_9.67 //
children.translated_text: thus will there be the attainment of this goal and the destruction of grief for the lord of men. // Bc_9.67 //

children.text: yā ca pravṛttā tava doṣabuddhistapovanebhyo bhavanaṃ praveṣṭum /
children.translated_text: And as for the fault-finding thought that has arisen in you, to enter the palace from the ascetic groves —

children.text: tatrāpi cintā tava tāta mā bhūta pūrve 'pi jagmuḥ svagṛhānvanebhyaḥ // Bc_9.68 //
children.translated_text: let there be no worry about that, my child; for even in ancient times, [sages] went from forests to their homes. // Bc_9.68 //

children.text: tapovanastho 'pi vṛtaḥ prajābhirjagāma rājā puramambarīṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: King <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, though dwelling in an ascetic grove, chosen by the people, went to the city;

children.text: tathā mahīṃ viprakṛtāmanāryaistapovanādetya rarakṣa rāmaḥ // Bc_9.69 //
children.translated_text: likewise <s>Rāma</s>, coming from the ascetic grove, protected the earth that had been oppressed by the ignoble. // Bc_9.69 //

children.text: tathaiva śālvādhipatirdrumākhyo vanātsasūranurnagaraṃ viveśa /
children.translated_text: Likewise the lord of the <s>Śālvas</s>, named <s>Druma</s>, entered the city from the forest with his army;

children.text: brahmārṣibhūtaśca munervasiṣṭhāddadhre śriyaṃ sāṃkṛtirantidevaḥ // Bc_9.70 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Antideva</s> of the <s>Sāṃkṛti</s> lineage, having become a <s>brahmarṣi</s>, received sovereignty from the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. // Bc_9.70 //

children.text: evaṃvidhā dharmayaśaḥpradīptā vanāni hitvā bhavanānyatīyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Such men, blazing with the glory of <s>dharma</s>, left the forests and entered their palaces;

children.text: tasmānna doṣo 'sti gṛhaṃ prayātuṃ tapovanāddharmanimittameva // Bc_9.71 //
children.translated_text: therefore there is no fault in going home from the ascetic grove for the very sake of <s>dharma</s>. // Bc_9.71 //

children.text: tato vacastasya niśamya mantriṇaḥ priyaṃ hitaṃ caiva nṛpasya cakṣuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the words of the minister — dear and beneficial, and as if the eyes of the king —

children.text: anūnamavyastamasaktamadrutaṃ dhṛtau sthito rājasuto 'bravīdvacaḥ // Bc_9.72 //
children.translated_text: complete, unconfused, unattached, and unhurried, the king's son, firm in resolve, spoke these words: // Bc_9.72 //

children.text: ihāsti nāstīti ya eṣa saṃśayaḥ parasya vākyairna mamātra niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This doubt — whether it exists or does not exist — I shall not resolve by the words of another;

children.text: avetya tattvaṃ tapasā śamena ca svayaṃ grahīṣyāmi yadatra niścitam // Bc_9.73 //
children.translated_text: having ascertained the truth through austerity and tranquility, I myself shall grasp what is certain in this matter. // Bc_9.73 //

children.text: na me kṣamaṃ saṃśayajaṃ hi darśanaṃ grahītumavyaktaparasparāhatam /
children.translated_text: It is not fitting for me to adopt a view born of doubt, struck by unclear mutual contradictions;

children.text: budhaḥ parapratyayato hi ko vrajejjano 'ndhakāre 'ndha ivāndhadeśikaḥ // Bc_9.74 //
children.translated_text: for what wise person would proceed on the faith of another — like a blind man led by a blind guide in the dark? // Bc_9.74 //

children.text: adṛṣṭatattvasya sato 'pi kiṃ tu me śubhāśubhe saṃśayitu śubhe matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Though the truth is not yet seen by me, still, in what is auspicious and inauspicious, my mind inclines toward the auspicious;

children.text: vṛthāpi khedo hi varaṃ śubhātmanaḥ sukhaṃ na tattve 'pi vigarhitātmanaḥ // Bc_9.75 //
children.translated_text: for even fruitless toil is better for one of noble spirit than comfort for one of despicable spirit. // Bc_9.75 //

children.text: imaṃ tu dṛṣṭvāgamamavyavasthitaṃ yaduktamāpttaistadavehi sādhviti /
children.translated_text: But seeing this doctrine to be unsettled, know what is spoken by the trustworthy to be good;

children.text: prahīṇadoṣatvamavehi cāptatāṃ prahīṇadoṣo hyanṛtaṃ na vakṣyati // Bc_9.76 //
children.translated_text: and know that trustworthiness consists in freedom from faults — for one free from faults will not speak untruth. // Bc_9.76 //

children.text: gṛhapraveśaṃ prati yacca me bhavānuvāca rāmaprabhṛtīnnidarśanam /
children.translated_text: And as for your citing the example of <s>Rāma</s> and others regarding entering the household —

children.text: na te pramāṇaṃ na hi dharmaniścayaiṣvalaṃ pramāṇāya parikṣatavratāḥ // Bc_9.77 //
children.translated_text: they are not authoritative; for those whose vows have been impaired are not adequate as authority in matters of determining <s>dharma</s>. // Bc_9.77 //

children.text: tadevamapyeva ravirmahī patedapi sthiratvaṃ himavān giristyajet /
children.translated_text: Even if the sun should fall to earth, even if <s>Himavān</s>, the mountain, should abandon its firmness,

children.text: adṛṣṭatattvo viṣayonmukhendriyaḥ śrayeya na tveva gṛhān pṛthagjanaḥ // Bc_9.78 //
children.translated_text: still I, without having seen the truth, with senses turned toward objects, would never resort to a household as a common person. // Bc_9.78 //

children.text: ahaṃ viśeyaṃ jvalitaṃ hutāśanaṃ na cākṛtārthaḥ praviśeyamālayam /
children.translated_text: I would enter a blazing fire,

children.text: iti pratijñāṃ sa cakāra garvito yatheṣṭamutthāya ca nirmamo yayau // Bc_9.79 //
children.translated_text: but I would not enter a dwelling without having accomplished my purpose.' Thus he made his vow with pride, and rising as he wished, free from attachment, he departed. // Bc_9.79 //

children.text: tataḥ sabāṣpau sacivadvijābubhau niśamya tasya sthirameva niścayam /
children.translated_text: Then the minister and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, both tearful, hearing his firm resolve,

children.text: viṣaṇṇavaktrāvanugamya duḥkhitau śanairagatyā purameva jagmatuḥ // Bc_9.80 //
children.translated_text: with downcast faces, following him in grief, slowly and reluctantly returned to the city. // Bc_9.80 //

children.text: tatsnehādatha nṛpateśca bhaktitastau sāpekṣaṃ pratiyayatuśca tasthatuśca /
children.translated_text: Out of affection for him and devotion to the king, they went and halted with longing glances;

children.text: durdharṣa ravimiva dīptamātmabhāsā taṃ draṣṭuṃ na hi pathi śekaturna moktum // Bc_9.81 //
children.translated_text: blazing with his own radiance like the invincible sun, they could neither bear to look at him on the road nor let him go. // Bc_9.81 //

children.text: tau jñātuṃ paramagatergatiṃ tu tasya pracchannāṃścarapuruṣāñchucīnvidhāya /
children.translated_text: But in order to learn the course of his supreme destination, they stationed pure spies in secret,

children.text: rājānaṃ priyasutalālasaṃ nu gatvā drakṣyāvaḥ kathamiti jagmatuḥ kathaṃcitu // Bc_9.82 //
children.translated_text: and thinking, 'How shall we see the king who yearns for his beloved son?' they went somehow or other. // Bc_9.82 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye kumārānveṣaṇoṃ nāma navamaḥ sargaḥ // 9 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth canto, named 'The Search for the Prince,' in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>. // 9 //
CANTO X

children.text: sa rājavatsaḥ pṛthupīnavakṣāstau havyamantrādhikṛtau vihāya /
children.translated_text: That prince, broad and full of chest, having left behind those two who were charged with oblations and <s>mantras</s>,

children.text: uttīrya gaṅgāṃ pracalattaraṅgāṃ śrīmadgṛhaṃ rājagṛhaṃ jagāma // Bc_10.1 //
children.translated_text: crossed the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with its rolling waves and went to the glorious city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. // Bc_10.1 //

children.text: śailaiḥ suguptaṃ ca vibhūṣitaṃ ca dhṛtaṃ ca pūtaṃ ca śivaistapodaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-protected by hills, adorned, sustained, and purified by auspicious streams of austerity,

children.text: pañcācalāṅkaṃ nagaraṃ prapede śāntaḥ svayaṃbhūriva nākapṛṣṭham // Bc_10.2 //
children.translated_text: he entered that city marked by five mountains, serene, like <s>Svayambhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) [entering] the summit of heaven. // Bc_10.2 //

children.text: gāmbhīryamojaśca niśāmya tasya vapuśca dīptaṃ puruṣānatītya /
children.translated_text: Perceiving his depth, his vigor, and his radiant body surpassing all men,

children.text: visismiye tatra janastadānīṃ sthāṇūvratasyeva vṛṣādhvajāsya // Bc_10.3 //
children.translated_text: the people there were filled with wonder, as at the sight of the bull-bannered one (<s>Śiva</s>) observing his <s>sthāṇu-vrata</s> (pillar-vow). // Bc_10.3 //

children.text: taṃ prekṣya yo 'nyena yayau sa tasthau yastatra tasthau pathi so 'nvagacchat /
children.translated_text: He who was going elsewhere stopped upon seeing him; he who stood there followed him on the road;

children.text: drutaṃ yayau yaḥ sa jagāma dhīraṃ yaḥ kaścidāste sma sa cotpapāta // Bc_10.4 //
children.translated_text: he who was going quickly went slowly; and whoever was seated sprang up. // Bc_10.4 //

children.text: kaścittamānarca janaḥ karābhyāṃ satkṛtya kaścicchirasā vavande /
children.translated_text: Some honored him with joined palms; some reverently saluted with bowed heads;

children.text: snigdhena kaścidvacasābhyanandanainaṃ jagāmāpratipūjya kaścit // Bc_10.5 //
children.translated_text: some greeted him with affectionate words; none went without paying him homage. // Bc_10.5 //

children.text: taṃ jihriyuḥ prekṣya vicitraveṣāḥ prakīrṇavācaḥ pathi maunamīyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Those in gaudy attire were ashamed seeing him; those of scattered speech fell silent;

children.text: dharmasya sākṣādiva saṃnikarṣe na kaścidanyāyamatirbabhūva // Bc_10.6 //
children.translated_text: as if in the direct presence of <s>Dharma</s> himself, no one harbored an unjust thought. // Bc_10.6 //

children.text: anyakriyāṇāmapi rājamārge strīṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ vā bahumānapūrvam /
children.translated_text: On the royal road, even women and men engaged in other activities,

children.text: taṃ devakalpaṃ naradevasūnuṃ nirīkṣamāṇā na tatarpa dṛṣṭiḥ // Bc_10.7 //
children.translated_text: gazing with reverence at that god-like son of a king, their sight was not sated. // Bc_10.7 //

children.text: bhruvau lalāṭaṃ mukhamīkṣaṇe vā vapuḥ karau vā caraṇau gatiṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever part of him anyone beheld there — his brows, his forehead, his face, his eyes,

children.text: yadeva yastasya dadarśa tatra tadeva tasyātha babandha cakṣuḥ // Bc_10.8 //
children.translated_text: his body, his hands, his feet, or his gait — that very thing bound his gaze. // Bc_10.8 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca sorṇabhruvamāyatākṣaṃ jvalaccharīraṃ śubhajālahastam /
children.translated_text: And seeing him with the ūrṇā between his brows, with elongated eyes, with a blazing body, with auspicious marks on his hands,

children.text: ta bhikṣuveṣaṃ kṣitipālanārha saṃcukṣubhe rājagṛhasya lakṣmīḥ // Bc_10.9 //
children.translated_text: yet in a mendicant's garb though worthy of ruling the earth, the glory of <s>Rājagṛha</s> was stirred. // Bc_10.9 //

children.text: śreṇyo 'tha bhartā magadhājirasya bāhyādvimānādvipulaṃ janaugham /
children.translated_text: <s>Śreṇya</s> (<s>Bimbisāra</s>), the lord of the land of <s>Magadha</s>, from the outer terrace, seeing the vast crowd of people,

children.text: dadarśa papraccha ca tasya hetuṃ tatastamasmai puruṣaḥ śaśaṃsa // Bc_10.10 //
children.translated_text: asked the reason for it; and thereupon a man informed him. // Bc_10.10 //

children.text: jñānaṃ paraṃ vā pṛthivīśriyaṃ vā viprairya ukto 'dhigamiṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: 'He who the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> said will attain either supreme knowledge or sovereignty of the earth —

children.text: sa eṣa śākyādhipatestanūjo nirīkṣyate pravrajito janena // Bc_10.11 //
children.translated_text: he, the son of the lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>, is now beheld by the people, having gone forth as a renunciant.' // Bc_10.11 //

children.text: tataḥ śrutārtho manasāgatāstho rājā babhāṣe puruṣaṃ tameva /
children.translated_text: Then the king, having heard the report and taken it to heart,

children.text: vijñāyatāṃ kva pratigacchatīti tathetyathainaṃ puruṣo 'nvagacchat // Bc_10.12 //
children.translated_text: said to that same man, 'Let it be ascertained where he goes'; and so saying, the man followed him. // Bc_10.12 //

children.text: alolacakṣuryugamātradarśī nivṛttavāgyantritamandagāmī /
children.translated_text: With steady gaze, looking only a yoke's length ahead, with speech restrained, walking slowly and measured,

children.text: cacāra bhikṣāṃ sa tu bhikṣuvaryo nidhāya gātrāṇi calaṃ ca cetaḥ // Bc_10.13 //
children.translated_text: that best of mendicants collected alms, having composed his limbs and his restless mind. // Bc_10.13 //

children.text: ādāya bhaikṣaṃ ca yathopapannaṃ yayau gireḥ prasravaṇaṃ viviktam /
children.translated_text: Having received alms as they came, he went to a secluded mountain spring,

children.text: nyāyena tatrābhyavahṛtya cainanmahīdharaṃ pāṇḍavamāruroha // Bc_10.14 //
children.translated_text: and having eaten there in the proper manner, he ascended the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> mountain. // Bc_10.14 //

children.text: tasminnavau lodhravanopagūḍhe mayūranādapratipurṇakuñje /
children.translated_text: On that new mountain, embraced by <s>lodhra</s> groves, with bowers filled with the cries of peacocks,

children.text: kāṣāyavāsāḥ sa babhau nṛsūryo yathodayasyopari bālasūryaḥ // Bc_10.15 //
children.translated_text: clad in ochre robes, that hero among men shone like the young sun over the eastern mountain. // Bc_10.15 //

children.text: tatrainamālokya sa rājabhṛtyaḥ śreṇyāya rājñe kathayāṃcakāra /
children.translated_text: There, the king's servant, having observed him, reported to King <s>Śreṇya</s>;

children.text: saṃśrutya rājā sa ca bāhumānyāttatra pratasthe nibhṛtānuyātraḥ // Bc_10.16 //
children.translated_text: and the king, hearing this, set out there with great reverence and a modest retinue. // Bc_10.16 //

children.text: sa pāṇḍavaṃ pāṇḍavatulyavīryaḥ śailottamaṃ śailasamānavarṣmā /
children.translated_text: Equal to <s>Pāṇḍu</s> in valor, equal to a mountain in stature, he who wore a crown,

children.text: maulīdharaḥ siṃhagatirnṛsiṃhaścalatsaṭaḥ siṃha ivāruroha // Bc_10.17 //
children.translated_text: that lion among men, with the gait of a lion and flowing mane, ascended like a lion that supreme mountain, <s>Pāṇḍava</s>. // Bc_10.17 //

children.text: tataḥ sma tasyopari śṛṅgabhūtaṃ śāntendriyaṃ paśyati bodhisattvam /
children.translated_text: Then, on its summit, he beheld the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his senses at peace,

children.text: paryaṅkamāsthāya virocamānaṃ śaśāṅkamudyantamivābhrakuñjāt // Bc_10.18 //
children.translated_text: seated cross-legged, shining like the rising moon from a cleft in the clouds. // Bc_10.18 //

children.text: taṃ rupalakṣmyā ca śamena caiva dharmasya nirmāṇamivopaviṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Seeing him seated as if the very creation of <s>Dharma</s>, by beauty and by tranquility alike,

children.text: savismayaḥ praśrayavānnarendraḥ svayaṃbhūvaṃ śakra ivopatasthe // Bc_10.19 //
children.translated_text: the king, with wonder and reverence, approached him as <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) [approaches] <s>Svayambhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). // Bc_10.19 //

children.text: taṃ nyāyato nyāyavidāṃ variṣṭhaṃ sametya papraccha ca dhātusāmyam /
children.translated_text: Having met him who was the foremost of those who know justice, he duly inquired after the balance of his bodily humors;

children.text: sa cāpyavocatsadṛśena sāmnā nṛpaṃ manaḥsvāsthyamanāmayaṃ ca // Bc_10.20 //
children.translated_text: and he too, with fitting gentleness, asked the king about his well-being and freedom from illness. // Bc_10.20 //

children.text: tataḥ śucau vāraṇakarṇanīle śilātale saṃniṣasāda rājā /
children.translated_text: Then the king sat down on a clean, dark-as-an-elephant's-ear stone slab;

children.text: upopaviśyānumataśca tasya bhāvaṃ vijijñāsuridaṃ babhāṣe // Bc_10.21 //
children.translated_text: and having sat down near him, with his permission, wishing to learn his disposition, he spoke thus: // Bc_10.21 //

children.text: prītiḥ parā me bhavataḥ kulena kramāgatā caiva parīkṣitā ca /
children.translated_text: 'I have great affection for your family, inherited through succession and tested;

children.text: jātā vivakṣā svavayo yato me tasmādidaṃ snehavaco nibodha // Bc_10.22 //
children.translated_text: because you are of the same age as me, a desire to speak has arisen — therefore hear these words of affection. // Bc_10.22 //

children.text: ādityapūrva vipulaṃ kulaṃ te navaṃ vayo dīptamidaṃ vapuśca /
children.translated_text: Your family, beginning with <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), is illustrious; your youth is fresh, and this body of yours is radiant;

children.text: kasmādiyaṃ te matirakrameṇa bhaikṣāka evābhiratā na rājye // Bc_10.23 //
children.translated_text: why is your mind thus irregularly inclined toward mendicancy rather than kingship? // Bc_10.23 //

children.text: gātraṃ hi te lohitacandanārhaṃ kāṣāyasaṃśleṣamanarhametat /
children.translated_text: This body of yours, worthy of red sandalwood, does not deserve contact with ochre garments;

children.text: hastaḥ prajāpālanayogya eṣa bhoktuṃ na cārhaḥ paradattamannam // Bc_10.24 //
children.translated_text: this hand, fit for ruling the people, should not eat food given by others. // Bc_10.24 //

children.text: tatsaumya rājyaṃ yadi paitṛkaṃ tvaṃ snehātpiturnecchasi vikrameṇa /
children.translated_text: Therefore, gentle one, if you do not wish for the ancestral kingdom out of affection for your father, through seizure,

children.text: na ca kramaṃ marṣayituṃ matiste bhuṅkṣvārdhamasmādviṣayasya śīghram // Bc_10.25 //
children.translated_text: and if you cannot tolerate taking it by force — then take half of this domain of mine at once. // Bc_10.25 //

children.text: evaṃ hi na syātsvajanāvamardaḥ kālakrameṇāpi śamaśrayā śrīḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus there will be no oppression of your kinsmen, and in time, sovereignty resting in peace;

children.text: tasmātkuruṣva praṇayaṃ mayi tvaṃ sadbhiḥ sahīyā hi satāṃ samṛddhiḥ // Bc_10.26 //
children.translated_text: therefore show your favor toward me — for the prosperity of the good is to be shared with the good. // Bc_10.26 //

children.text: atha tvidānī kulagarvitatvādasmāsu viśrambhaguṇo na te 'sti /
children.translated_text: But if now, out of family pride, the quality of trust toward us does not exist in you,

children.text: vyūḍhānyanīkāni vigāhya bāṇairmayā sahāyena parān jigīṣa // Bc_10.27 //
children.translated_text: then plunge into the arrayed battle-ranks with arrows and conquer your enemies with me as your ally! // Bc_10.27 //

children.text: tadbuddhimatrānyatarāṃ vṛṇīṣva dharmārthakāmānvidhivadbhajasva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, set your mind on one or the other; enjoy <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> in the proper way;

children.text: vyatyasya rāgādiha hi trivarga pretyeha ca bhraṃśamavāpnuvanti // Bc_10.28 //
children.translated_text: for those who pursue the triple aim with the wrong ordering, in this world and the next, come to ruin. // Bc_10.28 //

children.text: yo hyarthadharmau paripīḍya kāmaḥ syāddharmakāmau paribhūya cārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For that desire which oppresses <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, or that wealth which overrides <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s>,

children.text: kāmārthayoścoparameṇa dharmastyājyaḥ sa kṛtsno yadi kāṅkṣito 'rthaḥ // Bc_10.29 //
children.translated_text: or that <s>dharma</s> which [requires] the renunciation of <s>kāma</s> and <s>artha</s> — the whole of that is to be rejected, if a [balanced] goal is desired. // Bc_10.29 //

children.text: tasmāttrivargasya niṣevaṇena tvaṃ rūpametatsaphalaṃ kuruṣva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by pursuing the triple aim, make this form of yours bear fruit;

children.text: dharmārthakāmādhigamaṃ hyanūnaṃ nṛṇāmanūnaṃ puruṣārthamāhuḥ // Bc_10.30 //
children.translated_text: for the complete attainment of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>, they say, is the complete aim of man. // Bc_10.30 //

children.text: tanniṣphalau nārhasi kartumetau pīnau bhujau cāpavikarṣaṇārhau /
children.translated_text: Do not render fruitless these powerful arms, worthy of drawing the bow;

children.text: māndhātṛvajjetumimau hi yogyau lokānapi trīniha kiṃ punargām // Bc_10.31 //
children.translated_text: for these are fit to conquer, like <s>Māndhātṛ</s>'s, even the three worlds — how much more the earth alone! // Bc_10.31 //

children.text: snehena khalvetadahaṃ bravīmi naiśvaryarāgeṇa na vismayena /
children.translated_text: I speak this indeed out of affection, not from a desire for sovereignty nor from pride;

children.text: imaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā tava bhikṣuveṣaṃ jātānukampo 'smyapi cāgatāśruḥ // Bc_10.32 //
children.translated_text: for having seen this mendicant guise of yours, I am filled with compassion and also moved to tears. // 10.32 //

children.text: yāvatsvavaṃśapratirūpa rūpaṃ na te jarābhyetyabhibhūya bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'While your beauty, befitting your own lineage, is not yet overcome and vanquished by old age —

children.text: tadbhuṅkṣva bhikṣāśramakāma kāmān kāle 'si kartā priyadharma dharmam // Bc_10.33 //
children.translated_text: enjoy pleasures, O you who desire the mendicant's <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life); in due time, O lover of <s>dharma</s>, you will practice <s>dharma</s>. // 10.33 //

children.text: śaknoti jīrṇaḥ khalu dharmamāptuṃ kāmopabhogeṣvagatirjarāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'An old man is indeed able to attain <s>dharma</s>; old age has no recourse in the enjoyment of pleasures;

children.text: ataśca yūnaḥ kathayanti kāmānmadhyasya vittaṃ sthavirasya dharmam // Bc_10.34 //
children.translated_text: therefore they prescribe pleasures for the young, wealth for the middle-aged, <s>dharma</s> for the elder. // 10.34 //

children.text: dharmasya cārthasya ca jīvaloke pratyarthibhutāni hi yauvanāni /
children.translated_text: 'For in the living world, youths are hostile [by nature] to both <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> (wealth);

children.text: saṃrakṣyamāṇānyapi durgrahāṇi kāmā yatastena pathā haranti // Bc_10.35 //
children.translated_text: even when guarded, they are difficult to restrain — for pleasures lead them away by that path. // 10.35 //

children.text: vayāṃsi jīrṇāni vimarśavanti dhīrāṇyavasthānaparāyaṇāni /
children.translated_text: 'Old ages are reflective, steady, inclined to composure,

children.text: alpena yatnena śamātmakāni bhavantyagatyaiva ca lajjayā ca // Bc_10.36 //
children.translated_text: and with little effort become peaceful-natured — from [sheer] inability and from modesty. // 10.36 //

children.text: ataśca lolaṃ viṣayapradhānaṃ pramattamakṣāntamadīrghadarśi /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, having passed through youth — fickle, dominated by sense-objects, heedless, impatient, short-sighted,

children.text: bahucchalaṃ yauvanamabhyatītya nistīrya kāntāramivāśvasanti // Bc_10.37 //
children.translated_text: and full of pretexts — people breathe easy, as if having crossed through a wilderness. // 10.37 //

children.text: tasmādadhīraṃ capalapramādi navaṃ vayastāvadidaṃ vyapaitu /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, let this new age — unsteady, restless, and heedless — first pass;

children.text: kāmasya pūrva hi vayaḥ śaravyaṃ na śakyate rakṣitumindriyebhyaḥ // Bc_10.38 //
children.translated_text: for youth is the primary target of <s>Kāma</s>'s (love's) arrows, and cannot be guarded from the senses. // 10.38 //

children.text: atho cikīrṣā tava dharma eva yajasva yajñaṃ kuladharma eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Or if your desire is indeed for <s>dharma</s>, then perform the sacrifice — this is the <s>dharma</s> of the lineage;

children.text: yajñairadhiṣṭhāya hi nāgapṛṣṭhaṃ yayau marutvānapi nākapṛṣṭham // Bc_10.39 //
children.translated_text: for by mounting the back of sacrifices, even <s>Marutvat</s> (<s>Indra</s>) went to the pinnacle of heaven. // 10.39 //

children.text: suvarṇakeyūravidaṣṭabāhavo maṇipradīpojjvalacitramaulayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With arms embraced by golden armlets, with bright, jewel-studded, variegated diadems —

children.text: nṛparṣayastāṃ hi gatiṃ gatā makhaiḥ śrameṇa yāmeva maharṣayo yayuḥ // Bc_10.40 //
children.translated_text: the royal sages attained that destination through sacrifices — the very [destination] that the great sages reached through toil.' // 10.40 //

children.text: ityevaṃ magadhapatirvaco babhāṣe yaḥ samyagvalābhidiva bruvan babhāse /
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the lord of <s>Magadha</s>, who as he spoke rightly shone like the [risen] sun;

children.text: tacchrutvā na sa vicacāla rājasūnuḥ kailāso giririva naikacitrasānuḥ // Bc_10.41 //
children.translated_text: but hearing it, the prince did not waver — like Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>, whose variegated slopes are not moved by any [wind]. // 10.41 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye 'śvaghoṣakṛte śreṇyābhigamano nāma daśamaḥ sargaḥ // 10 //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, composed by <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>, [ends] the tenth canto, entitled 'The Approach of <s>Śreṇya</s>' (<s>Śreṇyābhigamana</s>). // 10 //
CANTO XI

children.text: athaivamukto magadhādhipena suhṛnmukhena pratikūlamartham /
children.translated_text: Then, having been thus addressed by the lord of <s>Magadha</s> — words from a friend's mouth, yet contrary in meaning —

children.text: svastho 'vikāraḥ kulaśaucaśuddhaḥ śauddhodanirvākyamidaṃ jagāda // Bc_11.1 //
children.translated_text: self-possessed, unmoved, purified by the purity of his lineage, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s> spoke these words: // 11.1 //

children.text: nāścaryametadbhavato vidhānaṃ jātasya haryaṅkakule viśāle /
children.translated_text: 'This conduct of yours is not surprising, born as you are in the great <s>Haryaṅka</s> lineage;

children.text: yanmitrapakṣe tava mitrakāma syādvṛttireṣā pariśuddhavṛtteḥ // Bc_11.2 //
children.translated_text: that this course should be [adopted] by you, O desirer of friends, toward one on the side of a friend — this befits one of pure conduct. // 11.2 //

children.text: asatsu maitrī svakulānuvṛttā na tiṣṭhati śrīriva viklaveṣu /
children.translated_text: 'Among the ignoble, friendship cultivated in accordance with one's own family does not endure — like fortune among the faint-hearted;

children.text: pūrvaiḥ kṛtāṃ prītiparaṃparābhistāmeva santastu vivardhayanti // Bc_11.3 //
children.translated_text: but the good augment that very [friendship] established by former generations through a succession of affections. // 11.3 //

children.text: ye cārthakṛccheṣu bhavanti loke samānakāryāḥ suhṛdāṃ manuṣyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those people in the world who, in times of adversity, share the same cause with their friends —

children.text: mitrāṇiḥ tānīti paraimi buddhyā svasthasya vṛddhiṣviha ko hi na syāt // Bc_11.4 //
children.translated_text: those I consider friends by my understanding; for who would not [be a friend] to one at ease, in times of prosperity? // 11.4 //

children.text: evaṃ ca ye dravyamavāpya loke mitreṣu dharme ca niyojayanti /
children.translated_text: 'And those who, having obtained wealth in the world, employ it for friends and for <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: avāptasārāṇi dhanāni teṣāṃ bhraṣṭāni nānte janayanti tāpam // Bc_11.5 //
children.translated_text: their wealth, having yielded its essence, when lost at last, causes no distress. // 11.5 //

children.text: suhṛttayā cāryatayā ca rājan khalveṣa yo māṃ prati niścayaste /
children.translated_text: 'This resolve of yours toward me, O king, born of friendliness and nobility —

children.text: atrānuneṣyāmi suhṛttayaiva brūyāmahaṃ nottaramanyadatra // Bc_11.6 //
children.translated_text: here I shall persuade you with friendliness itself; I would say nothing else in reply. // 11.6 //

children.text: ahaṃ jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ viditvā mumukṣayā dharmamimaṃ prapannaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I, knowing the fear of old age and death, and with the desire for liberation, have resorted to this <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: bandhūn priyānaśrumukhānvihāya prāgeva kāmānuśubhasya hetūn // Bc_11.7 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned kinsmen, dear ones with tearful faces — let alone pleasures, which are causes of the inauspicious! // 11.7 //

children.text: nāśīviṣebhyo hi tathā bibhemi naivāśanibhyo gaganāccyutebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For I do not fear poisonous serpents so much, nor thunderbolts fallen from the sky,

children.text: na pāvakebhyo 'nilasaṃhitebhyo yathā bhayaṃ me viṣayebhya eva // Bc_11.8 //
children.translated_text: nor fires combined with wind — as I fear sense-objects. // 11.8 //

children.text: kāmā hyanityāḥ kuśalārthacaurā riktāśca māyāsadṛśāśca loke /
children.translated_text: 'For pleasures are impermanent, thieves of what is wholesome, empty, and like illusions in the world;

children.text: āśāsyamānā api mohayanti cittaṃ nṛṇāṃ kiṃ punarātmasaṃsthāḥ // Bc_11.9 //
children.translated_text: even when merely hoped for, they delude the minds of men — how much more when established within one! // 11.9 //

children.text: kāmābhibhūtā hi na yānti śarma tripiṣṭape kiṃ bata martyaloke /
children.translated_text: 'Those overpowered by pleasures do not find peace even in the triple heaven, let alone in the mortal world;

children.text: kāmaiḥ satṛṣṇasya hi nāsti tṛptiryathendhanairvātasakhasya vanheḥ // Bc_11.10 //
children.translated_text: for one who thirsts, there is no satisfaction in pleasures — as there is none for fire, whose friend is the wind, with fuel. // 11.10 //

children.text: jagatyanartho na samo 'sti kāmairmohācca teṣveva janaḥ prasaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the world, there is no misfortune equal to pleasures, yet from delusion people are attached to them;

children.text: tattvaṃ viditvaivamanarthabhīruḥ prājñaḥ svayaṃ ko 'bhilaṣedanartham // Bc_11.11 //
children.translated_text: knowing the truth of this, what wise person, fearful of misfortune, would desire misfortune of his own accord? // 11.11 //

children.text: samudravaktrāmapi gāmavāpya pāraṃ jigīṣanti mahārṇavasya /
children.translated_text: 'Even after obtaining the earth bounded by the ocean, [people] desire to cross the far shore of the great sea;

children.text: lokasya kāmairna vitṛptirasti patidbhirambhobhirivārṇavasya // Bc_11.12 //
children.translated_text: there is no contentment in the world with pleasures — as there is none for the ocean with waters that flow [into it]. // 11.12 //

children.text: devena vṛṣṭe 'pi hiraṇyavarṣe dvīpānsamagrāṃścaturo 'pi jitvā /
children.translated_text: 'Even when a god rained down showers of gold, even having conquered all four continents,

children.text: śakrasya cārdhāsanamapyavāpya māndhāturāsīdviṣayeṣvatṛptiḥ // Bc_11.13 //
children.translated_text: even having obtained half the seat of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — <s>Māndhātṛ</s> was not satisfied with sense-objects. // 11.13 //

children.text: bhuktvāpi rājyaṃ divi devatānāṃ śatakratau vṛtrabhayātpranaṣṭe /
children.translated_text: 'Even having enjoyed the kingship of the gods in heaven, when <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>) was lost from fear of <s>Vṛtra</s>,

children.text: darpānmaharṣīnapi vāhayitvā kāmeṣvatṛpto nahuṣaḥ papāta // Bc_11.14 //
children.translated_text: and having, in his arrogance, even made the great sages serve as his vehicles — <s>Nahuṣa</s>, unsatisfied with pleasures, fell. // 11.14 //

children.text: aiḍaśca rājā tridivaṃ vigāhya nītvāpi devī vaśamurvaśī tām /
children.translated_text: 'And King <s>Aiḍa</s> (<s>Purūravas</s>), having entered the triple heaven, having brought even the goddess <s>Urvaśī</s> under his sway —

children.text: lobhādṛṣibhyaḥ kanakaṃ jihīrṣurjagāma nāśaṃ viṣayeṣvatṛptaḥ // Bc_11.15 //
children.translated_text: from greed, wishing to steal gold from the sages, went to destruction — unsatisfied with sense-objects. // 11.15 //

children.text: balermahendraṃ nahuṣaṃ mahendrādindraṃ punarye nahuṣādupeyuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those who ousted <s>Bali</s> in favor of great <s>Indra</s>, <s>Nahuṣa</s> in favor of great <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Indra</s> again in place of <s>Nahuṣa</s> —

children.text: svarge kṣitau vā viṣayeṣu teṣu ko viśvasedbhāgyakulākuleṣu // Bc_11.16 //
children.translated_text: who would place trust in those sense-objects — restless in the fortunes and misfortunes [they bring] — whether in heaven or on earth? // 11.16 //

children.text: cīrāmbarā mūlaphalāmbubhakṣā jaṭā vahanto 'pi bhujaṅgadīrghāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Wearing bark-garments, eating roots, fruits, and water, bearing matted locks as long as serpents —

children.text: yairnānyakāryā munayo 'pi bhagnāḥ kaḥ kāmasaṃjñānmṛgayeta śatrūn // Bc_11.17 //
children.translated_text: sages, by whom no other deeds were left undone — even they were broken [by desire]; who then would seek out the enemies known as pleasures? // 11.17 //

children.text: ugrāyudhaścogradhṛtāyudho 'pi yeṣāṃ kṛte mṛtyumavāpa bhīṣmāt /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ugrāyudha</s>, though he had taken up terrible weapons — for whose sake he met death from <s>Bhīṣma</s> —

children.text: cintāpi teṣāmaśivā vadhāya sadvṛttināṃ kiṃ punaravratānām // Bc_11.18 //
children.translated_text: even the thought of them is inauspicious, leading to the ruin of the virtuous — how much more of those without vows! // 11.18 //

children.text: āsvādamalpaṃ viṣayeṣu matvā saṃyojanotkarṣamatṛptimeva /
children.translated_text: 'Knowing that the savor in sense-objects is small, that the affliction of their conjunction is [a source of] non-satisfaction,

children.text: sadbhyaśca garhā niyataṃ ca pāpaṃ kaḥ kāmasaṃjñaṃ viṣamādadīta // Bc_11.19 //
children.translated_text: that censure from the good and sin are certain — who would take the poison called pleasure? // 11.19 //

children.text: kṛṣyādibhiḥ karmabhirarditānāṃ kāmātmakānāṃ ca niśamya duḥkham /
children.translated_text: 'Having observed the suffering of those who are desire-natured, tormented by actions such as ploughing and such,

children.text: svāsthyaṃ ca kāmeṣvakutūhalānāṃ kāmānvihātuṃ kṣamamātmavadbhiḥ // Bc_11.20 //
children.translated_text: and the well-being of those who are without curiosity for pleasures — it is fitting for the self-possessed to abandon pleasures. // 11.20 //

children.text: jñeyā vipatkāmini kāmasaṃpatsiddheṣu kāmeṣu madaṃ hyupaiti /
children.translated_text: 'The attainment of pleasures should be known as disaster, O desire-seeker; for upon success in pleasures, one falls into intoxication;

children.text: madādakārya kurute na kārya yena kṣato durgatimabhyupaiti // Bc_11.21 //
children.translated_text: from intoxication, one does what should not be done, not what should; whereby, injured, one arrives at a bad destination. // 11.21 //

children.text: yatnena labdhvāḥ parirakṣitāśca ye vipralabhya pratiyānti bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those [pleasures] which, obtained with effort and carefully guarded, cheat [the owner] and depart again —

children.text: teṣvātmavānyācitakopameṣu kāmeṣu vidvāniha ko rameta // Bc_11.22 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures — which invite self-collected anger — what wise person of self-mastery would delight? // 11.22 //

children.text: anviṣya cādāya ca jātatarṣā yānatyajantaḥ pariyānti duḥkham /
children.translated_text: 'Those who, having sought out and seized [pleasures], with thirst aroused, unable to relinquish them, go about in suffering —

children.text: loke tṛṇolkāsadṛśeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.23 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling torches of straw in the world, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.23 //

children.text: anātmavanto hṛdi yairvidaṣṭā vināśamarchanti na yānti śarma /
children.translated_text: 'Those by which the self-less, bitten in their hearts, seek destruction and do not find peace —

children.text: kuddhograsarpapratimeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.24 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling angry fierce serpents, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.24 //

children.text: asthi kṣudhārtā iva sārameyā bhuktvāpi yānnaiva bhavanti tṛptāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Like dogs tormented by hunger gnawing a bone, who are never satisfied even after chewing —

children.text: jīrṇasthikaṅkālasameṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.25 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling a worn-out skeleton of bones, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.25 //

children.text: ye rājacaurodakapāvakebhyaḥ sādhāraṇatvājjanayanti duḥkham /
children.translated_text: 'Those which, because of being common to kings, thieves, water, and fire, produce suffering —

children.text: teṣu praviddhāmiṣasanibheṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.26 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling a piece of cast-off meat, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.26 //

children.text: yatra sthitānāmabhito vipattiḥ śatroḥ sakāśādapi bāndhavebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where, for those who possess them, ruin comes from all sides — from enemies as well as from kinsmen —
