children.text: hiṃsreṣu teṣvāyatanopameṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.27 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling violent dwellings, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.27 //

children.text: girau vane cāpsu ca sāgare ca yān bhraṃśamarchanti vilaṅghamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'On mountains, in forests, in waters, and in the sea — those for which people fall to destruction while grasping —

children.text: teṣu drumaprāgraphalopameṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.28 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling the fruit at the tip of a tree, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.28 //

children.text: tīvraiḥ prayatnairvividhairavāptāḥ kṣaṇena ye nāśamiha prayānti /
children.translated_text: 'Those which, obtained through intense and varied efforts, perish in an instant here —

children.text: svapnopabhogapratimeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.29 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling enjoyments in a dream, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.29 //

children.text: yānarjayitvāpi na yānti śarma vivardhayitvā paripālayitvā /
children.translated_text: 'Those which, even after acquiring, guarding, and augmenting, bring no peace —

children.text: aṅgārakarṣūpratimeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.30 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling a pit of burning coals, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.30 //

children.text: vināśamīyuḥ kuravo yadartha vṛṣṇyandhakā mekhaladaṇḍakāśca /
children.translated_text: 'For the sake of which the <s>Kurus</s> went to destruction, the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Andhakas</s>, and the <s>Mekhalas</s> and <s>Daṇḍakas</s> —

children.text: sūnāsikāṣṭhapratimeṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.31 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, resembling the wooden block of a butcher's shop, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.31 //

children.text: sundopasundāvasurau yadarthamanyonyavairaprasṛtau vinaṣṭau /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Asura</s> brothers <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, for whose sake they perished in mutual enmity —

children.text: sauhārdīvaśleṣakareṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.32 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, which destroy the embrace of friendship, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.32 //

body.text: yeṣāṃ kṛte vāriṇi pāvake ca / kravyātsu cātmānamihotsṛjanti /

children.text: sapatnabhūteṣvaśiveṣu teṣu kāmeṣu kasyātmavato ratiḥ syāt // Bc_11.33 //
children.translated_text: in those pleasures, inauspicious and like adversaries, what person of self-mastery would find delight? // 11.33 //

body.translated_text: 'Those for whose sake people here cast themselves into water, fire, and among carnivorous beasts —

children.text: kāmārthamajñaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ karoti prāpnoti duḥkhaṃ vadhabandhanādi /
children.translated_text: 'The ignorant one acts pitiably for the sake of pleasures, and obtains suffering — killing, bondage, and such;

children.text: kāmārthamāśākṛpaṇastapasvī mṛtyuṃ śramaṃ cārchati jīvalokaḥ // Bc_11.34 //
children.translated_text: pitiable with longing for pleasures, the ascetic world of the living strives for death and hardship. // 11.34 //

children.text: gītairhiyante hi mṛgā vadhāya rūpārthamagnau śalabhāḥ patanti /
children.translated_text: 'Deer are lured by songs to their slaughter; moths, for the sake of form, fall into fire;

children.text: matsyo giratyāyasamāmiṣārthī tasmādanartha viṣayāḥ phalanti // Bc_11.35 //
children.translated_text: the fish swallows the iron hook for the sake of the bait — therefore sense-objects bear fruit as misfortune. // 11.35 //

body.text: kāmāstu bhogā iti yanmatiḥ syādbhogā na kecitparigaṇyamānāḥ

children.text: vastrādayo dravyaguṇā hi loke duḥkhapratīkāra iti pradhāryāḥ // Bc_11.36 //
children.translated_text: for material qualities such as clothing and such in the world are to be understood as remedies for suffering.' // 11.36 //

body.translated_text: 'If one thinks that pleasures are enjoyments — no enjoyments are to be counted [as such] upon examination;

children.text: iṣṭaṃ hi tarṣapraśamāya toyaṃ kṣunnāśahetoraśanaṃ tathaiva /
children.translated_text: 'For water is desired for the quenching of thirst; food likewise for the elimination of hunger;

children.text: vātātapāmbvāvaraṇāya veśma kaupīnaśītāvaraṇāya vāsaḥ // Bc_11.37 //
children.translated_text: a house for protection from wind, heat, and rain; clothing for covering nakedness and warding off cold. // 11.37 //

children.text: nidrāvighātāya tathaiva śayyā yānaṃ tathādhvaśramanāśanāya /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise, a bed for the removal of sleepiness; a vehicle for the removal of the fatigue of travel;

children.text: tathāsanaṃ sthānavinodanāya snānaṃ mṛjarogyabalāśrayāya // Bc_11.38 //
children.translated_text: likewise, a seat for the alleviation of the discomfort of standing; bathing as a basis for cleanliness, health, and strength. // 11.38 //

children.text: duḥkhapratīkāranimittabhūtāstasmātprajānāṃ viṣayā na bhogāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, since sense-objects exist for the purpose of remedying suffering, they are not enjoyments for creatures;

children.text: aśnāmi bhogāniti ko 'bhyupeyātprājñaḥ pratīkāravidhau pravṛttaḥ // Bc_11.39 //
children.translated_text: what wise person, engaged in the method of remedying [suffering], would claim: "I am enjoying pleasures"? // 11.39 //

children.text: yaḥ pittadāhena vidahyamānaḥ śītakriyāṃ bhoga iti vyavasyet /
children.translated_text: 'One who, being burned by the fever of bile, would designate the cooling treatment as an enjoyment —

children.text: duḥkhapratīkāravidhau pravṛttaḥ kāmeṣu kuryātsa hi bhogasaṃjñām // Bc_11.40 //
children.translated_text: he, engaged in the method of remedying suffering, would apply the designation "enjoyment" to pleasures. // 11.40 //

children.text: kāmeṣvanaikāntikatā ca yasmādato 'pi me teṣu na bhogasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: 'And since there is no constancy in pleasures, for this reason too I do not designate them as enjoyments;

children.text: ya eva bhāvā hi sukhaṃ diśanti ta eva duḥkhaṃ punarāvahanti // Bc_11.41 //
children.translated_text: for the very things that give happiness also in turn bring suffering. // 11.41 //

children.text: gurūṇi vāsāṃsyagurūṇi caiva sukhāya śīte hyusukhāya dharme /
children.translated_text: 'Heavy garments and light ones — the former for comfort in cold, the latter for discomfort in heat;

children.text: candrāṃśavaścandanameva coṣṇe sukhāya duḥkhāya bhavanti śīte // Bc_11.42 //
children.translated_text: moonbeams and sandalwood — for comfort in heat, for suffering in cold. // 11.42 //

children.text: dvandvāni sarvasya yataḥ prasaktānyalābhalābhaprabhṛtīni loke /
children.translated_text: 'Since pairs of opposites are always present for everyone — loss and gain and such — in the world,

children.text: ato 'pi naikāntasukho 'sti kaścinnaikāntaduḥkha puruṣaḥ pṛthivyām // Bc_11.43 //
children.translated_text: therefore there is no one exclusively happy, nor any person exclusively miserable on earth. // 11.43 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vimiśrāṃ sukhaduḥkhatāṃ me rājyaṃ ca dāsyaṃ ca mataṃ samānam /
children.translated_text: 'Having seen this mixed nature of pleasure and pain, kingship and servitude are equal in my estimation;

children.text: nityaṃ hasatyeva hi naiva rājā na cāpi saṃtapyata eva dāsaḥ // Bc_11.44 //
children.translated_text: for a king does not always laugh, nor does a servant always grieve. // 11.44 //

children.text: ājñā nṛpatve 'bhyadhiketi yatsyānmahānti duḥkhānyata eva rājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If it be said that command is supreme in kingship — therefore the sufferings of a king are great;

children.text: āsaṅgakāṣṭhapratimo hi rājā lokasya hetoḥ parikhedameti // Bc_11.45 //
children.translated_text: for a king is like a piece of wood used as a prop — he undergoes exhaustion for the sake of the world. // 11.45 //

children.text: rājye nṛpastyāgini bavhamitre viśvāsamāgacchati cedvipannaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If, in his kingdom, a king with many friends who [may] desert [him] places his trust — he is ruined;

children.text: athāpi viśrambhamupaiti neha kiṃ nāma saukhyaṃ cakitasya rājñaḥ // Bc_11.46 //
children.translated_text: but if he does not place trust here — then what happiness can there be for a frightened king? // 11.46 //

children.text: yadā ca jitvāpi mahīṃ samagrāṃ vāsāya dṛṣṭaṃ puramekameva /
children.translated_text: 'And when, even after conquering the entire earth, only one city is seen to serve as a dwelling,

children.text: tatrāpi caikaṃ bhavanaṃ niṣevyaṃ śramaḥ parārthe nanu rājabhāvaḥ // Bc_11.47 //
children.translated_text: and even therein only one palace is to be inhabited — is not the state of king a toil for the sake of others? // 11.47 //

children.text: rājño 'pi vāsoyugamekameva kṣutsaṃnirodhāya tathānnamātrā /
children.translated_text: 'Even a king has only one pair of garments to wear, and only a measure of food for staving off hunger,

children.text: śayyā tathaikāsanamekameva śeṣā viśeṣā nṛpatermadāya // Bc_11.48 //
children.translated_text: and likewise only one bed and one seat — the rest of a king's distinctions are for the sake of [his] pride.' // 11.48 //

children.text: tuṣṭyarthametacca phalaṃ yadīṣṭamṛte 'pi rājyānmama tuṣṭirasti /
children.translated_text: "And if this fruit is desired for the sake of contentment, I have contentment even without a kingdom;

children.text: tuṣṭau ca satyāṃ puruṣasya loke sarve viśeṣā nanu nirviśeṣāḥ // Bc_11.49 //
children.translated_text: and when contentment exists, are not all distinctions of a man in this world without distinction? // Bc_11.49 //

children.text: tannāsmi kāmān prati saṃpratāryaḥ kṣemaṃ śivaṃ mārgamanuprapannaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, I am not to be led back toward desires, having attained the auspicious, safe path;

children.text: smṛtvā suhṛttvaṃ tu punaḥ punarmā brūhi pratijñāṃ khalu pālayeti // Bc_11.50 //
children.translated_text: but remembering your friendship, tell me again and again: 'Keep your vow!' // Bc_11.50 //

children.text: na hyasmyamarṣeṇa vanaṃ praviṣṭo na śatrubāṇairavadhūtamauliḥ /
children.translated_text: "For I have not entered the forest through resentment, nor with my crown struck off by enemy arrows,

children.text: kṛtaspṛho nāpi phalādhikebhyo gṛhṇāmi naitadvacanaṃ yataste // Bc_11.51 //
children.translated_text: nor have I conceived desire for those with greater rewards — therefore I do not accept these words of yours. // Bc_11.51 //

children.text: yo dandaśūkaṃ kupitaṃ bhujaṅgaṃ muktvā vyavasyeddhi punargrahītum /
children.translated_text: "For one who, having released an enraged serpent, a venomous snake, would resolve to seize it again —

children.text: dāhātmikāṃ vā jvalitāṃ tṛṇolkāṃ saṃtyajya kāmānsa punarbhajeta // Bc_11.52 //
children.translated_text: or, having cast aside a blazing torch of grass whose nature is burning — he would take up desires again. // Bc_11.52 //

children.text: andhāya yaśca spṛhayedanandho baddhāya mukto vidhanāya cāḍhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "One who is not blind would covet blindness, one free would covet bondage, one wealthy would covet destitution,

children.text: unmattacittāya ca kalyacittaḥ spṛhāṃ sa kuryādviṣayātmakāya // Bc_11.53 //
children.translated_text: and one of sound mind would covet one of deranged mind — he who would covet the nature of sense-objects. // Bc_11.53 //

children.text: bhaikṣopabhogīti ca nānukampyaḥ kṛtī jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ titīrṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Nor is one who lives on alms to be pitied — he is a man of accomplishment, seeking to cross beyond the fear of old age and death;

children.text: ihottamaṃ śāntisukhaṃ ca yasya paratra duḥkhāni ca saṃvṛtāni // Bc_11.54 //
children.translated_text: for he has the supreme bliss of tranquility here, and his sufferings hereafter are also closed off. // Bc_11.54 //

children.text: lakṣmyāṃ mahatyāmapi vartamānastṛṣṇābhibhūtastvanukampitavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Rather, one who, even while abiding in great fortune, is overcome by craving — he is to be pitied,

children.text: prāpnoti yaḥ śāntisukhaṃ na ceha paratra duḥkhai pratigṛhyate ca // Bc_11.55 //
children.translated_text: who does not attain the bliss of tranquility here, and hereafter is received by sufferings. // Bc_11.55 //

children.text: evaṃ tu vaktuṃ bhavato 'nurūpaṃ sattvasya vṛttasya kulasya caiva /
children.translated_text: "It is fitting for you to speak thus, befitting your character, conduct, and lineage;

children.text: mamāpi voḍhuṃ sadṛśaṃ pratijñāṃ sattvasya vṛttasya kulasya caiva // Bc_11.56 //
children.translated_text: and it is fitting for me to uphold my vow, befitting my character, conduct, and lineage. // Bc_11.56 //

children.text: ahaṃ hi saṃsāraśareṇa viddho viniḥsṛtaḥ śāntimavāptukāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For I, pierced by the arrow of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclical existence), have come forth wishing to attain peace;

children.text: neccheyamāptuṃ tridive 'pi rājyaṃ nirāmayaṃ kiṃ bata mānuṣeṣu // Bc_11.57 //
children.translated_text: I would not wish to obtain kingship even in the three heavens, free from affliction — how much less among mortals! // Bc_11.57 //

children.text: trivargasevāṃ nṛpa yattu kṛtsnataḥ paro manuṣyārtha iti tvamāttha mām /
children.translated_text: "As for what you say to me, O king, that the complete service of the triple aim (<s>trivarga</s>) is the supreme aim of man —

children.text: anartha ityeva mamātra darśanaṃ kṣayī trivargo hi na cāpi tarpakaḥ // Bc_11.58 //
children.translated_text: my view here is that it is rather a non-aim — for the <s>trivarga</s> is subject to decay and never satisfying. // Bc_11.58 //

children.text: pade tu yasminna jarā na bhīrna rūṅ na janma naivoparamo na cādhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "But that state in which there is no old age, no fear, no sickness, no birth, no cessation, and no sorrows —

children.text: tameva manye puruṣārthamuttamaṃ na vidyate yatra punaḥ punaḥ kriyā // Bc_11.59 //
children.translated_text: that alone I consider the supreme aim of man, where there is no action again and again. // Bc_11.59 //

children.text: yadapyavoca paripālyatāṃ jarā nava vayo gacchati vikriyāmiti /
children.translated_text: "As for what you said — 'let old age be watched for, youth does not undergo change' —

children.text: aniścayo 'ya capalaṃ hi dṛśyate jarāpyadhīrā dhṛtimacca yauvanam // Bc_11.60 //
children.translated_text: this is uncertain, for fickleness is seen: old age too is unsteady, and youth can be resolute. // Bc_11.60 //

children.text: svakarmadakṣaśca yadāntako jagad vayasu sarveṣvavaśa vikarṣati /
children.translated_text: "And since Death, skilled in his own work, drags the world helplessly at every age,

children.text: vināśakāle kathamavyavasthite jarā pratīkṣyā viduṣā śamepsunā // Bc_11.61 //
children.translated_text: when the time of destruction is so uncertain, how should the wise one seeking peace wait for old age? // Bc_11.61 //

children.text: jarāyudho vyādhivikīrṇasāyako yadāntako vyādha ivāśivaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "When Death stands like an inauspicious hunter, with old age as his weapon and diseases as his scattered arrows,

children.text: prajāmṛgān bhāgyavanāśritāṃstudan vayaḥprakarṣa prati ko manorathaḥ // Bc_11.62 //
children.translated_text: striking the deer-like beings who dwell in the forest of fortune — what hope is there for the advance of age? // Bc_11.62 //

children.text: ato yuvā vā sthaviro 'thavā śiśustathā tvarāvāniha kartumarhati /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, whether young, or old, or a child, one should act here with equal urgency,

children.text: yathā bhaveddharmavataḥ kṛtātmanaḥ pravṛttiriṣṭā vinivṛttireva vā // Bc_11.63 //
children.translated_text: so that the desired course — whether engagement or withdrawal — may be that of one who possesses <s>dharma</s> and self-mastery. // Bc_11.63 //

children.text: yadāttha cāpīṣṭaphalāṃ kulocitāṃ kuruṣva dharmāya makhakriyāmiti /
children.translated_text: "As for what you said — 'perform the sacrificial rite, befitting your lineage, with its desired fruits, for the sake of <s>dharma</s>' —

children.text: namo makhebhyo na hi kāmaye sukhaṃ parasya duḥkhakriyayā yadiṣyate // Bc_11.64 //
children.translated_text: I bow to sacrifices [in refusal], for I do not desire happiness that is obtained through causing suffering to another. // Bc_11.64 //

children.text: paraṃ hi hantuṃ vivaśaṃ phalepsayā na yuktarūpa karuṇātmanaḥ sataḥ /
children.translated_text: "For to kill another being, helpless, for the sake of obtaining a fruit, is not fitting for one of compassionate nature who is good;

children.text: kratoḥ phalaṃ yadyapi śāśvataṃ bhavettathāpi kṛttvā kimu yatkṣayātmakam // Bc_11.65 //
children.translated_text: even if the fruit of the sacrifice were eternal, what use is that which is of the nature of destruction? // Bc_11.65 //

children.text: bhavecca dharmo yadi nāparo vidhirvratena śīlena manaḥśamena vā /
children.translated_text: "And if <s>dharma</s> were not achievable by another means — by vows, by moral conduct, or by the calming of the mind —

children.text: tathāpi naivārhati sevituṃ kratuṃ viśasya yasmin paramucyate phalam // Bc_11.66 //
children.translated_text: even then, the sacrifice should not be performed, in which the fruit is obtained through slaughter. // Bc_11.66 //

children.text: ihāpi tāvatpuruṣasya tiṣṭhataḥ pravartate yatparahiṃsayā sukham /
children.translated_text: "Even here and now, for a person living [in the world], the happiness that proceeds from harming others —

children.text: tadapyaniṣṭaṃ saghṛṇasya dhīmato bhavāntare kiṃ bata yanna dṛśyate // Bc_11.67 //
children.translated_text: even that is unwanted by the compassionate wise one; how much more what cannot be seen in the next existence! // Bc_11.67 //

children.text: na ca pratāryo 'smi phalapravṛttaye bhaveṣu rājan ramate na me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Nor am I to be led toward activity for the sake of [worldly] fruits; my mind does not delight in existences, O king;

children.text: latā ivāmbhodharavṛṣṭitāḍitāḥ pravṛttayaḥ sarvagatā hi cañcalāḥ // Bc_11.68 //
children.translated_text: for all activities are unstable, like creepers struck by the rain of a cloud. // Bc_11.68 //

children.text: ihāgataścahamito didṛkṣayā munerarāḍasya vimokṣavādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "I have come here with the desire to see the sage <s>Arāḍa</s>, the proponent of liberation;

children.text: prayāmi cādyaiva nṛpāstu te śivaṃ vacaḥ kṣamethā mama tattvaniṣṭhuram // Bc_11.69 //
children.translated_text: and I depart this very day — may there be auspiciousness for you, O king; pardon my speech, though it be harsh in its truthfulness. // Bc_11.69 //

children.text: avendravaddivyava śaśvadarkavad guṇairava śreya ihāva gāmava /
children.translated_text: "May you flourish like <s>Indra</s>, may you be divine like <s>Śiva</s>, may you ever [shine] like the sun, may you increase in virtues, may you prosper like the earth,

children.text: avāyurāryairava satsutānava śriyaśca rājannava dharmamātmanaḥ // Bc_11.70 //
children.translated_text: may you have long life like the noble ones, may you have good sons like the virtuous, and may you possess royal glory, O king, and the <s>dharma</s> of the self. // Bc_11.70 //

children.text: himāriketūdbhavasaṃbhavāntare yathā dvijo yāti vimokṣayaṃstanum /
children.translated_text: "Just as a bird, between the rising and setting of the enemy of snow (the sun), releases its body,

children.text: himāriśatrukṣayaśatrughātane tathāntare yāhi vimokṣayanmanaḥ // Bc_11.71 //
children.translated_text: so too, in the interval between the destruction of the enemy of the cold and the slaying of enemies, go forth, liberating your mind." // Bc_11.71 //

children.text: nṛpo 'bravītsāñjalirāgataspṛho yatheṣṭamāpnotu bhavānavighnataḥ /
children.translated_text: The king, with palms joined, his longing aroused, said: "May Your Honor attain what is desired without obstruction;

children.text: avāpya kāle kṛtakṛtyatāmimāṃ mamāpi kāryo bhavatā tvanugrahaḥ // Bc_11.72 //
children.translated_text: and when in time you have attained this fulfilled state, you must show your grace to me also." // Bc_11.72 //

children.text: sthiraṃ pratijñāya tatheti pārthive tataḥ sa vaiśvaṃtaramāśramaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: Having firmly promised 'So be it' to the king, he then went to the hermitage of <s>Vaiśvantara</s>;

children.text: parivrajantaṃ tamudīkṣya vismito nṛpo 'pi vavrāja puri girivrajam // Bc_11.73 //
children.translated_text: and the king, gazing in wonder at him as he wandered forth, also returned to the city of <s>Girivraja</s> (<s>Rājagṛha</s>). // Bc_11.73 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye kāmavigarhaṇo nāmaikādaśa sargaḥ // 11 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh canto, named 'The Censure of Desire,' in the <s>Buddhacarita</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>. // 11 //
CANTO XII

children.text: tataḥ śamavihārasya munerikṣvākucandramāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the moon of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> dynasty, dwelling in the abode of tranquility,

children.text: arāḍasyāśramaṃ bheje vapuṣā pūrayanniva // Bc_12.1 //
children.translated_text: resorted to the hermitage of <s>Arāḍa</s>, as if filling it with his splendor. // Bc_12.1 //

children.text: sa kālāmasagotreṇa tenālokyaiva dūrataḥ /
children.translated_text: Espied from afar by that one of the <s>Kālāma</s> lineage,

children.text: uccaiḥ svāgatamityuktaḥ samīpamupajagmivān // Bc_12.2 //
children.translated_text: he was addressed aloud with 'Welcome!' and approached near. // Bc_12.2 //

children.text: tāvubhau nyāyataḥ pṛṣṭvā dhātusāmyaṃ parasparam /
children.translated_text: Those two, having duly inquired about each other's balance of bodily humors,

children.text: dāravyormedhyayorvṛṣyoḥ śucau deśe niṣedatuḥ // Bc_12.3 //
children.translated_text: sat down in a clean spot, on two seats made of wood, pure and fit. // Bc_12.3 //

children.text: tamāsīnaṃ nṛpasutaṃ so 'bravīnmunisattamaḥ /
children.translated_text: The best among sages addressed the prince who was seated,

children.text: bahumānaviśālābhyāṃ darśanābhyāṃ pibanniva // Bc_12.4 //
children.translated_text: as if drinking him in with his wide eyes of great reverence: // Bc_12.4 //

children.text: viditaṃ me yathā saumya niṣkrānto bhavanādasi /
children.translated_text: "It is known to me, O gentle one, that you have departed from your dwelling,

children.text: chittvā snehamayaṃ pāśaṃ pāśaṃ dṛpta iva dvipaḥ // Bc_12.5 //
children.translated_text: having cut the bond made of affection — like a proud elephant [breaking] its tether. // Bc_12.5 //

children.text: sarvathā dhṛtimaccaiva prājñaṃ caiva manastava /
children.translated_text: "Your mind is certainly steadfast and wise in every way,

children.text: yastvaṃ prāptaḥ śriyaṃ tyaktvā latāṃ viṣaphalāmiva // Bc_12.6 //
children.translated_text: since you, having abandoned fortune, have arrived — as one [discards] a vine bearing poisonous fruit. // Bc_12.6 //

children.text: nāścarya jīrṇavayaso yajjagmuḥ pārthivā vanam /
children.translated_text: "It is no wonder that kings in their old age have gone to the forest,

children.text: apatyebhyaḥ śriyaṃ dattvā bhuktocchiṣṭāmiva srajam // Bc_12.7 //
children.translated_text: having given their fortune to their children — like a garland that has been worn and discarded. // Bc_12.7 //

children.text: idaṃ me matamāścaryaṃ nave vayasi yadbhavān /
children.translated_text: "This is what I find wondrous in my view — that you, in your fresh youth,

children.text: abhuktvaiva śriyaṃ prāptaḥ sthito viṣayagocare // Bc_12.8 //
children.translated_text: have arrived without even enjoying fortune, though standing within the range of sense-objects. // Bc_12.8 //

children.text: tadvijñātumimaṃ dharma paramaṃ bhājanaṃ bhavān /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, you are the supreme vessel for knowing this <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: jñānaplamavadhiṣṭhāya śīghraṃ duḥkhārṇavaṃ tara // Bc_12.9 //
children.translated_text: mounting the raft of knowledge, quickly cross the ocean of suffering. // Bc_12.9 //

children.text: śiṣye yadyapi vijñāte śāstraṃ kālena varṇyate /
children.translated_text: "Although the teaching is normally expounded to a disciple only after a period of testing,

children.text: gāmbhīryādvyavasāyācca na parīkṣyo bhavānmama // Bc_12.10 //
children.translated_text: due to your depth and your resolve, you need not be examined by me. // Bc_12.10 //"

children.text: iti vākyamarāḍasya vijñāya sa nararṣabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Understanding the words of <s>Arāḍa</s>, that bull among men

children.text: babhūva paramaprītaḥ provācottarameva ca // Bc_12.11 //
children.translated_text: became supremely delighted and spoke this reply: // Bc_12.11 //

children.text: viraktasyāpi yadidaṃ saumukhyaṃ bhavataḥ param /
children.translated_text: "This supreme graciousness of yours, even though you are detached,

children.text: akṛtārtho 'pyanenāsmi kṛtārtha iva saṃprati // Bc_12.12 //
children.translated_text: [makes me feel] — even though I have not attained my purpose — as if I have attained it right now. // Bc_12.12 //

children.text: didṛkṣuriva hi jyotiryiyāsuriva daiśikam /
children.translated_text: "Like one wishing to see light, like one wishing to travel [seeking] a guide,

children.text: tvaddarśanamahaṃ manye titīrṣuriva ca plavam // Bc_12.13 //
children.translated_text: I consider the sight of you as one wishing to cross [seeks] a raft. // Bc_12.13 //

children.text: tasmādarhasi tadvaktuṃ vaktavyaṃ yadi manyase /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, please speak that which you think should be spoken —

children.text: jarāmaraṇarogebhyo yathāyaṃ parimucyate // Bc_12.14 //
children.translated_text: how this [person] may be freed from old age, death, and disease." // Bc_12.14 //

children.text: ityarāḍaḥ kumārasya māhātmyādeva coditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Arāḍa</s>, impelled by the greatness of the prince alone,

children.text: saṃkṣiptaṃ kathayāṃcakre svasya śāstrasya niścayam // Bc_12.15 //
children.translated_text: briefly recounted the conclusion of his own teaching: // Bc_12.15 //

children.text: śrūyatāmayamasmākaṃ siddhāntaḥ śṛṇvatāṃ vara /
children.translated_text: "Hear, O best of listeners, this doctrine of ours —

children.text: yathā bhavati saṃsāro yathā caiva nivartate // Bc_12.16 //
children.translated_text: how <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclical existence) comes about and how it ceases. // Bc_12.16 //

children.text: prakṛtiśca vikāraśca janma mṛtyurjareva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>vikāra</s> (modification), birth, death, and old age —

children.text: tattāvatsattvamituktaṃ sthirasattva parehi tat // Bc_12.17 //
children.translated_text: this much is called <s>sattva</s> (being/existence); understand that, O one of firm resolve. // Bc_12.17 //

children.text: tatra tu prakṛtiṃ nāma viddhiṃ prakṛtikovida /
children.translated_text: "Therein, know that which is called <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), O knower of <s>prakṛti</s>:

children.text: pañca bhūtānyahaṃkāraṃ buddhimavyaktameva ca // Bc_12.18 //
children.translated_text: the five elements, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and the <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest). // Bc_12.18 //

children.text: vikāra iti budhyasva viṣayānindriyāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: "And understand as <s>vikāra</s> (modifications): the sense-objects and the sense organs,

children.text: pāṇipādaṃ ca vādaṃ ca pāyūpasthaṃ tathā manaḥ // Bc_12.19 //
children.translated_text: hands, feet, speech, the organ of excretion, the organ of generation, and the mind. // Bc_12.19 //

children.text: asya kṣetrasya vijñānātkṣetrajña iti saṃjñi ca /
children.translated_text: "Through the knowledge of this field (<s>kṣetra</s>), the term <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower) is applied;

children.text: kṣetrajña iti cātmānaṃ kathayantyātmacintakāḥ // Bc_12.20 //
children.translated_text: and those who contemplate the self call the self <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the field-knower). // Bc_12.20 //

children.text: saśiṣyaḥ kapilaśceha pratibuddha iti smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Kapila</s>, together with his disciples, is remembered here as 'the awakened one';

children.text: saputro 'pratibuddhastu prajāpatirihocyate // Bc_12.21 //
children.translated_text: but <s>Prajāpati</s>, together with his sons, is here called 'the unawakened.' // Bc_12.21 //

children.text: jāyate jīryate caiva bādhyate mriyate ca yat /
children.translated_text: "What is born, grows old, is afflicted, and dies —

children.text: tadvyaktamiti vijñeyamavyaktaṃ tu viparyayāt // Bc_12.22 //
children.translated_text: that is to be known as the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>); the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is the opposite. // Bc_12.22 //

children.text: ajñānaṃ karma tṛṣṇā ca jñeyāḥ saṃsārahetavaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), and craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) — these should be known as the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: sthito 'smiṃstritaye jantustatsattvaṃ nātivartate // Bc_12.23 //
children.translated_text: a being established in this triad does not transcend that existence. // Bc_12.23 //

children.text: vipratyayādahaṃkārātsaṃdehādabhisaṃplavāt /
children.translated_text: "Through false conception, through egoism, through doubt, through conflation,

children.text: aviśeṣānupāyābhyāṃ saṅgādabhyavapātataḥ // Bc_12.24 //
children.translated_text: through non-discrimination, through wrong means, through attachment, and through downfall — // Bc_12.24 //

children.text: tatra vipratyayo nāma viparītaṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: "Therein, what is called false conception operates in an inverted manner;

children.text: anyathā kurute kāryaṃ mantavyaṃ manyate 'nyathā // Bc_12.25 //
children.translated_text: one performs an action in one way, while thinking of what should be done in another way. // Bc_12.25 //

children.text: bravīmyahamahaṃ vedmi gacchāmyahamahaṃ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "'I speak,' 'I know,' 'I go,' 'I stand' —

children.text: itīhaivamahaṃkārastvanahaṃkāra vartate // Bc_12.26 //
children.translated_text: thus here egoism operates, O one free from egoism. // Bc_12.26 //

children.text: yastu bhāvānasaṃdigdhānekībhāvena paśyati /
children.translated_text: "One who sees undoubted realities as unified,

children.text: mṛtpiṇḍavadasaṃdeha saṃdehaḥ sa ihocyate // Bc_12.27 //
children.translated_text: like a lump of clay — that is called doubt. // Bc_12.27 //

children.text: ya evāhaṃ sa evedaṃ mano buddhiśca karma ca /
children.translated_text: "'I myself am this — mind, intellect, and action,

children.text: yaścaivaiṣa gaṇaḥ so 'hamiti yaḥ so 'bhisaṃplavaḥ // Bc_12.28 //
children.translated_text: and this aggregate is myself' — that is what is called conflation. // Bc_12.28 //

children.text: aviśeṣaṃ viśeṣajña pratibuddhāprabuddhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: "O knower of distinctions, the non-distinction between the awakened and the unawakened,

children.text: prakṛtīnāṃ ca yo veda so 'viśeṣa iti smṛtaḥ // Bc_12.29 //
children.translated_text: and of the <s>prakṛtis</s> — one who knows [but ignores] this is said to be [in the state of] non-discrimination. // Bc_12.29 //

children.text: namaskāravaṣaṭkārau prokṣaṇābhyukṣaṇādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Salutations, oblations, ritual sprinkling, consecration, and such —

children.text: anupāya iti prājñairupāyajña praveditaḥ // Bc_12.30 //
children.translated_text: these are declared by the wise, O knower of [true] means, to be wrong means. // Bc_12.30 //

children.text: sajjate yena durmedhā manovāgbuddhikarmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "That by which the foolish-minded one clings through acts of mind, speech, and body

children.text: viṣayeṣvanabhiṣvaṅga so 'bhiṣvaṅga iti smṛtaḥ // Bc_12.31 //
children.translated_text: to sense-objects without detachment — that is remembered as attachment. // Bc_12.31 //

children.text: mamedamahamasyeti yadduḥkhamabhimanyate /
children.translated_text: "The suffering that one imagines as 'mine is this, I belong to this' —

children.text: vijñeyo 'bhyavapātaḥ sa saṃsāre yena pātyate // Bc_12.32 //
children.translated_text: that should be known as downfall, by which one falls into <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Bc_12.32 //

children.text: ityavidyāṃ hi vidvānsa pañcaparvā samīhate /
children.translated_text: "Thus the wise one understands this ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) as having five branches:

children.text: tamo mohaṃ mahāmohaṃ tāmisradvayameva ca // Bc_12.33 //
children.translated_text: darkness (<s>tamas</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), great delusion (<s>mahāmoha</s>), and the two [forms of] gloom (<s>tāmisra</s>). // Bc_12.33 //

children.text: tatrālasyaṃ tamo viddhi mohaṃ mṛtyuṃ ca janma ca /
children.translated_text: "Therein, know <s>tamas</s> as sloth; <s>moha</s> as death and birth;

children.text: mahāmohastvasaṃmoha kāma ityeva gamyatām // Bc_12.34 //
children.translated_text: and <s>mahāmoha</s> — let it be understood as unfailing: desire (<s>kāma</s>) itself. // Bc_12.34 //

children.text: yasmādatra ca bhūtāni pramuhyanti mahāntyapi /
children.translated_text: "Since even great beings are deluded here by it,

children.text: tasmādeṣa mahābāho mahāmoha iti smṛtaḥ // Bc_12.35 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O mighty-armed one, it is remembered as <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion). // Bc_12.35 //

children.text: tāmisramiti cākrodha krodhamevādhikurvate /
children.translated_text: "And they designate anger as <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom), increasing anger;

children.text: viṣādaṃ cāndhatāmisramaviṣāda pracakṣate // Bc_12.36 //
children.translated_text: and they call despair <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness), O one free from despair. // Bc_12.36 //

children.text: anayāvidyayā bālaḥ saṃyuktaḥ pañcaparvayā /
children.translated_text: "The foolish one, conjoined with this five-branched ignorance,

children.text: saṃsāre duḥkhabhūyiṣṭhe janmasvabhiniṣicyate // Bc_12.37 //
children.translated_text: is poured into births in <s>saṃsāra</s>, which abounds in suffering. // Bc_12.37 //

children.text: draṣṭā śrotā ca mantā ca kāryakaraṇameva ca /
children.translated_text: "As 'I am the seer, the hearer, the thinker, and the agent of action' —

children.text: ahamityevamāgamya saṃsāre parivartate // Bc_12.38 //
children.translated_text: thus, having arrived [at this identification], one revolves in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Bc_12.38 //

children.text: ihaibhirhetubhirdhīman janmastrotaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: "By these causes here, O wise one, the stream of births proceeds;

children.text: hetvabhāvātphalābhāva iti vijñātumarhasi // Bc_12.39 //
children.translated_text: from the absence of causes, the absence of fruit — you should understand this. // Bc_12.39 //

children.text: tatra samyaṅmatirvidyānmokṣakāma catuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: "Therein, one of right understanding, desiring liberation, should know the fourfold [truth]:

children.text: pratibuddhāprabuddhau ca vyaktamavyaktameva ca // Bc_12.40 //
children.translated_text: the awakened and the unawakened, and the manifest and the unmanifest. // Bc_12.40 //

children.text: yathāvadetadvijñāya kṣetrajño hi catuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: "Having properly known this fourfold [truth], the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower),

children.text: ājavaṃjavatāṃ hitvā prāpnoti padamakṣaram // Bc_12.41 //
children.translated_text: abandoning the continuous cycle, attains the imperishable state. // Bc_12.41 //

children.text: ityartha brāhmaṇā loke paramabrahmavādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For this purpose, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in the world, proponents of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: brahmacarya carantīha brāhmaṇānvāsayanti ca // Bc_12.42 //
children.translated_text: practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline) and accommodate <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // Bc_12.42 //

children.text: iti vākyamidaṃ śrutvā munestasya nṛpātmajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard these words of the sage, the prince

children.text: abhyupāyaṃ ca papraccha padameva ca naiṣṭhikam // Bc_12.43 //
children.translated_text: asked about both the method and the ultimate goal. // Bc_12.43 //

children.text: brahmacaryamidaṃ caryaṃ yathā yāvacca yatra ca /
children.translated_text: 'How this celibate discipline is to be practiced, for how long, and where —

children.text: dharmasyāsya ca paryantaṃ bhavānvyākhyātumarhati // Bc_12.44 //
children.translated_text: and the final limit of this <s>dharma</s> — you should kindly explain.' // Bc_12.44 //

children.text: ityarāḍo yathāśāstraṃ vispaṣṭārtha samāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Ārāḍa</s>, according to scripture, with clear meaning, in brief,

children.text: tamevānyena kalpena dharmamasmai vyabhāṣata // Bc_12.45 //
children.translated_text: expounded this <s>dharma</s> to him in yet another way: // Bc_12.45 //

children.text: ayamādau gṛhānmuktvā bhaikṣākaṃ liṅgamāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the beginning, having left the household, one takes up the mendicant's garb;

children.text: samudācāravistīrṇa śīlamādāya vartate // Bc_12.46 //
children.translated_text: one adopts a moral conduct that is extensive in its observances and carries on. // Bc_12.46 //

children.text: saṃtoṣaṃ paramāsthāya yena tena yatastataḥ /
children.translated_text: Abiding in supreme contentment, with whatever and from wherever [one obtains],

children.text: viviktaṃ sevate vāsaṃ nirdvandvaḥ śāstravitkṛtī // Bc_12.47 //
children.translated_text: the knower of scripture, skilled, free from pairs of opposites, resorts to a secluded dwelling. // Bc_12.47 //

children.text: tato rāgādbhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā vairāgyācca paraṃ śivam /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing danger in attachment and supreme well-being in dispassion,

children.text: nigṛhṇannindriyagrāmaṃ yatate manasaḥ śame // Bc_12.48 //
children.translated_text: restraining the group of senses, one strives for the calming of the mind. // Bc_12.48 //

children.text: atho viviktaṃ kāmebhyo vyāpādādibhya eva ca /
children.translated_text: Then, secluded from desires and from ill-will and such,

children.text: vivekajamavāpnoti pūrvadhyānaṃ vitarkavat // Bc_12.49 //
children.translated_text: one attains the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), born of seclusion, endowed with discursive thought. // Bc_12.49 //

children.text: tacca dhyānasukhaṃ prāpya tattadeva vitarkayān /
children.translated_text: And having attained that bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>, continuing to engage in discursive thought on that very subject,

children.text: apūrvasukhalābhena hriyate bāliśo janaḥ // Bc_12.50 //
children.translated_text: the foolish person is carried away by the attainment of a previously unknown happiness. // Bc_12.50 //

children.text: śamenaivaṃvidhenāyaṃ kāmadveṣavigarhiṇā /
children.translated_text: By such tranquility, which condemns desire and hatred,

children.text: brahmalokamavāpnoti paritoṣeṇa vañcitaḥ // Bc_12.51 //
children.translated_text: he attains the <s>Brahma</s>-world, deceived by complacency. // Bc_12.51 //

children.text: jñātvā vidvānvitarkāstu manaḥsaṃkṣobhakārakān /
children.translated_text: But the wise one, knowing discursive thoughts to be disturbers of the mind,

children.text: tadviyuktamavāpnoti dhyānaṃ prītisukhānvitam // Bc_12.52 //
children.translated_text: attains <s>dhyāna</s> free from them, endowed with joy and bliss. // Bc_12.52 //

children.text: hriyamāṇastayā prītyā yo viśeṣaṃ na paśyati /
children.translated_text: He who, carried away by that joy, does not perceive the distinction,

children.text: sthānaṃ bhāsvaramāpnoti deveṣvābhāsvareṣu saḥ // Bc_12.53 //
children.translated_text: attains a radiant abode among the radiant (<s>Ābhāsvara</s>) gods. // Bc_12.53 //

children.text: yastu prītisukhāttasmādvivecayati mānasam /
children.translated_text: But he who separates the mind from that joy and bliss

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ labhate dhyānaṃ sukhaṃ prītivivarjitam // Bc_12.54 //
children.translated_text: attains the third <s>dhyāna</s>, which has bliss but is free from joy. // Bc_12.54 //

children.text: yastu tasminsukhe magno na viśeṣāya yatnavān /
children.translated_text: He who is immersed in that bliss and does not strive for distinction

children.text: śubhakṛtsnaiḥ sa sāmānyaṃ sukhaṃ prāpnoti daivataiḥ // Bc_12.55 //
children.translated_text: attains a common happiness with the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (all-good) deities. // Bc_12.55 //

children.text: caturtha dhyānamāpnoti sukhaduḥkhavivarjitam // Bc_12.56 //
children.translated_text: attains the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, free from both pleasure and pain. // Bc_12.56 //

body.translated_text: But he who, having attained such bliss, is not attached and remains equanimous,

children.text: tatra kecidvyavasyanti mokṣa ityabhimāninaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some who are self-assured resolve that this is liberation,

children.text: sukhaduḥkhaparityāgādavyāpārācca cetasaḥ // Bc_12.57 //
children.translated_text: because of the abandonment of pleasure and pain and the cessation of mental activity. // Bc_12.57 //

children.text: asya dhyānasya tu phalaṃ samaṃ devairbṛhatphalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: But the fruit of this <s>dhyāna</s>, they say, is equality with the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (great-fruited) gods,

children.text: kathayanti bṛhatkālaṃ bṛhatprajñāparīkṣakāḥ // Bc_12.58 //
children.translated_text: for a great duration — so say those of great wisdom who examine [the matter]. // Bc_12.58 //

children.text: samādhervyutthitastasmād dṛṣtvā doṣāṃścharīriṇām /
children.translated_text: Having risen from that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), seeing the faults of embodied beings,

children.text: jñānamārohati prājñaḥ śarīravinivṛttaye // Bc_12.59 //
children.translated_text: the wise one ascends to knowledge for the cessation of embodiment. // Bc_12.59 //

children.text: tatastaddhyānamutsṛjya viśeṣe kṛtaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, abandoning that <s>dhyāna</s>, having resolved on distinction,

children.text: kāmebhya iva sa prājño rūpādapi virajyate // Bc_12.60 //
children.translated_text: the wise one becomes dispassionate toward form itself, just as toward desires. // Bc_12.60 //

children.text: śarīre khāni yānyasmintānyādau parikalpayan /
children.translated_text: First, contemplating the apertures that exist in this body,

children.text: ghaneṣvapi tato dravyeṣvākāśamadhimucyate // Bc_12.61 //
children.translated_text: he then becomes convinced of space even in solid substances. // Bc_12.61 //

children.text: ākāśagatamātmānaṃ saṃkṣipya tvaparo budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Another wise one, having condensed the self that has entered space,

children.text: tadevānantataḥ paśyanviśeṣamadhigacchati // Bc_12.62 //
children.translated_text: seeing that very [space] as infinite, attains distinction. // Bc_12.62 //

children.text: adhyātmakuśalastvanyo nivartyātmānamātmanā /
children.translated_text: But another, skilled in the inner self, withdrawing the self by the self,

children.text: kiṃcinnāstīti saṃpaśyannākiṃcanya iti smṛtaḥ // Bc_12.63 //
children.translated_text: perceiving 'there is nothing at all,' is known as [one abiding in] <s>ākiṃcanya</s> (nothingness). // Bc_12.63 //

children.text: tato muñjādiṣīkeva śakuniḥ pañjarādiva /
children.translated_text: Then, like a reed [drawn] from its sheath, or like a bird from its cage,

children.text: kṣetrajño niḥsṛto dehānmukta ityabhidhīyate // Bc_12.64 //
children.translated_text: the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), having come forth from the body, is called liberated. // Bc_12.64 //

children.text: etattatparamaṃ brahma nirliṅga dhruvamakṣaram /
children.translated_text: This is that supreme <s>Brahman</s>, without marks, permanent, imperishable,

children.text: yanmokṣa iti tattvajñāḥ kathayanti manīṣiṇaḥ // Bc_12.65 //
children.translated_text: which the wise who know reality call liberation. // Bc_12.65 //

children.text: ityupāyaṃśca mokṣaśca mayā saṃdarśitastava /
children.translated_text: Thus the method and liberation have been shown to you by me;

children.text: yadi jñātaṃ yadi ruciryathāvatpratipadyatām // Bc_12.66 //
children.translated_text: if it is understood and pleases you, let it be practiced as it should be. // Bc_12.66 //

children.text: jaigīṣavyo 'tha janako vṛddhaścaiva parāśaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, and the aged <s>Parāśara</s> —

children.text: imaṃ panthānamāsādya muktā hyanye ca mokṣiṇaḥ // Bc_12.67 //
children.translated_text: having reached this path, they and other seekers of liberation have been liberated.' // Bc_12.67 //

children.text: iti tasya sa tadvākyaṃ gṛhītvā tu vicārya ca /
children.translated_text: He, having received and examined those words,

children.text: pūrvahetubalaprāptaḥ pratyuttaramuvāca ha // Bc_12.68 //
children.translated_text: impelled by the force of prior causes, spoke this reply: // Bc_12.68 //

children.text: śrutaṃ jñānamidaṃ sūkṣmaṃ parataḥ parataḥ śivam /
children.translated_text: 'I have heard this subtle knowledge, progressively more auspicious;

children.text: kṣetrajñasyāparityāgādavaimyetadanaiṣṭhikam // Bc_12.69 //
children.translated_text: but since the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) is not abandoned, I understand this to be non-final. // Bc_12.69 //

children.text: vikāraprakṛtibhyo hi kṣetrajñaṃ muktamapyaham /
children.translated_text: For even when the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is freed from modifications and <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), I consider it

children.text: manye prasavadharmāṇaṃ bījadharmāṇameva ca // Bc_12.70 //
children.translated_text: to be of the nature of production, of the nature of a seed. // Bc_12.70 //

children.text: viśuddho yadyapi hyātmā nirmukta iti kalpyate /
children.translated_text: Even if the self is pure and is conceived as liberated,

children.text: bhūyaḥ pratyayasadbhāvādamuktaḥ sa bhaviṣyati // Bc_12.71 //
children.translated_text: because conditions still exist, it will become unliberated again. // Bc_12.71 //

children.text: ṛtubhūmyambuvirahādyathā bījaṃ na rohati /
children.translated_text: Just as a seed does not sprout when deprived of season, soil, and water,

children.text: rohati pratyayaistaistaistadvatso 'pi mato mama // Bc_12.72 //
children.translated_text: but sprouts when those conditions [return] — so too, in my opinion, is that [self]. // Bc_12.72 //

children.text: yatkarmājñānatṛṣṇānāṃ tyāgānmokṣaśca kalpyate /
children.translated_text: And when liberation is conceived through the abandonment of <s>karma</s>, ignorance, and craving,

children.text: atyantastatparityāgaḥ satyātmani na vidyate // Bc_12.73 //
children.translated_text: the absolute abandonment of these does not exist as long as the self exists. // Bc_12.73 //

children.text: hitvā hitvā trayamidaṃ viśeṣastūpalabhyate /
children.translated_text: By progressively abandoning these three, distinction is indeed obtained;

children.text: ātmanastu sthitiryatra tatra sūkṣmamidaṃ trayam // Bc_12.74 //
children.translated_text: but where the self abides, there this triad [exists] in subtle form. // Bc_12.74 //

children.text: sūkṣmatvāccaiva doṣāṇāmavyāpārācca cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Due to the subtlety of the faults, and the cessation of mental activity,

children.text: dīrghatvādāyuṣaścaiva mokṣastu parikalpyate // Bc_12.75 //
children.translated_text: and the length of the lifespan, liberation is merely imagined. // Bc_12.75 //

children.text: ahaṃkāraparityāgo yaścaiṣa parikalpyate /
children.translated_text: As for the abandonment of ego-sense that is conceived,

children.text: satyātmani parityāgo nāhaṃkārasya vidyate // Bc_12.76 //
children.translated_text: the abandonment of ego-sense does not exist as long as the self exists. // Bc_12.76 //

children.text: saṃkhyādibhiramuktaśca nirguṇo na bhavatyayam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, being not freed according to <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other [systems], this [self] does not become quality-less;

children.text: tasmādasati nairguṇye nāsya mokṣo 'bhidhīyate // Bc_12.77 //
children.translated_text: therefore, in the absence of quality-lessness, its liberation is not declared. // Bc_12.77 //

children.text: guṇino hi guṇānāṃ ca vyatireko na vidyate /
children.translated_text: For there is no separation between a possessor of qualities and the qualities;

children.text: rūpoṣṇābhyāṃ virahito na hyagnirupalabhyate // Bc_12.78 //
children.translated_text: fire, for instance, is not apprehended apart from form and heat. // Bc_12.78 //

children.text: prāgdehānna bhaveddehī prāgguṇebhyastathā guṇī /
children.translated_text: Before the body there would be no embodied one; before the qualities, likewise no possessor of qualities;

children.text: tasmādādau vimuktaḥ san śarīrī badhyate punaḥ // Bc_12.79 //
children.translated_text: therefore, having been free at first, the embodied one is bound again. // Bc_12.79 //

children.text: kṣetrajño viśarīraśca jño vā syādajña eva vā /
children.translated_text: Either the <s>kṣetrajña</s> without a body is a knower, or it is a non-knower;

children.text: yadi jño jñeyamasyāsti jñeye sati na mucyate // Bc_12.80 //
children.translated_text: if it is a knower, it has a knowable, and as long as there is a knowable, it is not liberated. // Bc_12.80 //

children.text: athājña iti siddho vaḥ kalpitena kimātmanā /
children.translated_text: If it is established as a non-knower, then what is the use of this imagined self?

children.text: vināpi hyātmanājñānaṃ prasiddhaṃ kāṣṭhakuḍyavat // Bc_12.81 //
children.translated_text: For even without a self, non-knowing is well established, as in a log of wood or a wall. // Bc_12.81 //

children.text: parataḥ paratastyāgo yasmāttu guṇavān smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since progressive abandonment is held to be meritorious,

children.text: tasmātsarvaparityāgānmanye kṛtsnāṃ kṛtārthatām // Bc_12.82 //
children.translated_text: therefore I consider complete accomplishment to consist in the abandonment of everything. // Bc_12.82 //'

children.text: iti dharmamarāḍasya viditvā na tutoṣa saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having understood the <s>dharma</s> of <s>Ārāḍa</s>, he was not satisfied;

children.text: akṛtsnamiti vijñāya tataḥ pratijagāma ha // Bc_12.83 //
children.translated_text: knowing it to be incomplete, he thereupon departed. // Bc_12.83 //

children.text: viśeṣamatha śuśrūṣurudrakasyāśramaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: Then, wishing to hear [something] superior, he went to the hermitage of <s>Udraka</s>;

children.text: ātmagrāhācca tasyāpi jagṛhe na sa darśanam // Bc_12.84 //
children.translated_text: but he did not adopt his doctrine either, due to its clinging to a self. // Bc_12.84 //

children.text: saṃjñāsaṃjñitvayordoṣaṃ jñātvā hi munirudrakaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the sage <s>Udraka</s>, knowing the fault in both perception and non-perception,

children.text: ākiṃcanyātparaṃ lebhe'saṃjñāsaṃjñātmikāṃ gatim // Bc_12.85 //
children.translated_text: attained beyond nothingness a state characterized by neither-perception-nor-non-perception. // Bc_12.85 //

children.text: yasmāccālambane sūkṣme saṃjñāsaṃjñe tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: Since, in that subtle object — perception-and-non-perception — beyond that,

children.text: nāsaṃjñī naiva saṃjñīti tasmāttatragataspṛhaḥ // Bc_12.86 //
children.translated_text: [the being] is neither non-perceiving nor perceiving — therefore he was free from desire for that [state]. // Bc_12.86 //

children.text: yataśca buddhistatraiva sthitānyatrāpracāriṇī /
children.translated_text: And since awareness abides in that very [state], not operating elsewhere,

children.text: sūkṣmāpaṭvī tatastatra nāsaṃjñitvaṃ na saṃjñitā // Bc_12.87 //
children.translated_text: subtle and inactive — therefore, there is neither non-perception nor perception in it. // Bc_12.87 //

children.text: yasmācca tadapi prāpya punarāvartate jagat /
children.translated_text: And since, even having attained that, the world returns again,

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ paraṃ prepsustasmādudrakamatyajat // Bc_12.88 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeking the supreme, therefore left <s>Udraka</s>. // Bc_12.88 //

children.text: tato hitvāśramaṃ tasya śreyo 'rthī kṛtaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, leaving his hermitage, seeking the highest good, firm in resolve,

children.text: bheje gayasya rājarṣernagarīsaṃjñamāśramam // Bc_12.89 //
children.translated_text: he betook himself to the hermitage bearing the name of the royal sage <s>Gaya</s>. // Bc_12.89 //

children.text: atha nairañjanātīre śucau śuciparākramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, on the bank of the <s>Nairañjanā</s> river, pure and of pure prowess,

children.text: cakāra vāsamekāntavihārābhiratirmuniḥ // Bc_12.90 //
children.translated_text: the sage, delighting in solitary retreat, took up his abode. // Bc_12.90 //

children.text: āgatān tatra tatpūrvapañcendriyavaśoddhatān /
children.translated_text: There he observed five mendicants who had come before him,

children.text: tapaḥpravṛttān vratino bhikṣūn pañca niraikṣata // Bc_12.91 //
children.translated_text: their senses formerly unrestrained, now engaged in austerity and vows. // Bc_12.91 //

children.text: te copatastthurdṛṣṭvātra bhikṣavastaṃ mumukṣavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those mendicants, seekers of liberation, seeing him there, attended upon him,

children.text: puṇyārjitadhanārogyamindriyārthā iveśvaram // Bc_12.92 //
children.translated_text: like the sense-faculties attending upon a lord endowed with wealth and health won by merit. // Bc_12.92 //

children.text: saṃpūjyamānastaiḥ pravhairvinayādanuvartibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Honored by those noble ones who followed him out of discipline,

children.text: tadvaśasthāyibhiḥ śiṣyairlolairmana ivendriyaiḥ // Bc_12.93 //
children.translated_text: who remained under his control like the restless senses of the mind — // Bc_12.93 //

children.text: mṛtyujanmāntakaraṇe syādupāyo 'yamityatha /
children.translated_text: thinking, 'This may be the means of putting an end to death and birth,'

children.text: duṣkarāṇi samārebhe tapāṃsyanaśanena saḥ // Bc_12.94 //
children.translated_text: he then undertook difficult austerities through fasting. // Bc_12.94 //

children.text: upavāsavidhīnnaikān kurvannaradurācarān /
children.translated_text: Performing various fasting observances, difficult for men to endure,

children.text: varṣāṇi ṣaṭ śamaprepsurakarotkārśyamātmanaḥ // Bc_12.95 //
children.translated_text: seeking tranquility, he reduced himself to emaciation for six years. // Bc_12.95 //

children.text: annakāleṣu caikaikaiḥ sa kolatilataṇḍulaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And at mealtimes, with single jujube fruits, sesame seeds, and grains of rice,

children.text: apārapārasaṃsārapāraṃ prepsurapārayat // Bc_12.96 //
children.translated_text: he who sought to reach the far shore of the boundless ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> sustained himself. // Bc_12.96 //

children.text: dehādapacayastena tapasā tasya yaḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wasting away of the body that was caused by his austerity

children.text: sa evopacayo bhūyastejasāsya kṛto 'bhavat // Bc_12.97 //
children.translated_text: became in turn an increase of his spiritual radiance. // Bc_12.97 //

children.text: kṛśo 'pyakṛśakīrtiśrīrlhādaṃ cakre 'nyacakṣuṣām /
children.translated_text: Though emaciated, with fame and glory undiminished, he delighted the eyes of others,

children.text: kumudānāmiva śaracchuklapakṣādicandramāḥ // Bc_12.98 //
children.translated_text: like the moon at the beginning of the bright fortnight [delights] white lotuses in autumn. // Bc_12.98 //

children.text: tvagasthiśeṣo niḥśeṣairmedaḥpiśitaśoṇitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With only skin and bones remaining, his fat, flesh, and blood entirely gone,

children.text: kṣīṇo 'pyakṣīṇagāmbhīryaḥ samudra iva sa vyabhāt // Bc_12.99 //
children.translated_text: though diminished, with depth undiminished, he appeared like an ocean. // Bc_12.99 //

children.text: atha kaṣṭatapaḥspaṣṭavyarthakliṣṭatanurmuniḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that sage, his body plainly afflicted by severe and fruitless austerity,

children.text: bhavabhīrurimāṃ cakre buddhiṃ buddhatvakāṅkṣayā // Bc_12.100 //
children.translated_text: fearing continued existence, formed this resolve out of desire for Buddhahood: // Bc_12.100 //

children.text: nāyaṃ dharmo virāgāya na bodhāya na muktaye /
children.translated_text: 'This is not the <s>dharma</s> for dispassion, nor for enlightenment, nor for liberation;

children.text: jambumūle mayā prāpto yastadā sa vidhirdhruvaḥ // Bc_12.101 //
children.translated_text: that method which I attained formerly beneath the <s>jambu</s> tree — that is the sure one. // Bc_12.101 //

children.text: na cāsau durbalenāptuṃ śakyamityāgatādaraḥ /
children.translated_text: And that cannot be attained by one who is weak.' With this conviction,

children.text: śarīrabalavṛddhyarthamidaṃ bhūyo 'nvacintayat // Bc_12.102 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of increasing bodily strength, he reflected further: // Bc_12.102 //

children.text: kṣutpipāsāśramaklāntaḥ śramādasvasthamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Exhausted by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, with a mind unsettled from exertion —

children.text: prāpnuyānmanasāvāpyaṃ phalaṃ kathamanirvṛtaḥ // Bc_12.103 //
children.translated_text: how could one who is not at ease attain a fruit that is to be attained by the mind? // Bc_12.103 //

children.text: nirvṛtiḥ prāpyate samyak satatendriyatarpaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Ease is properly attained through the constant nourishment of the senses;

children.text: saṃtarpitendriyatayā manaḥsvāsthyamavāpyate // Bc_12.104 //
children.translated_text: through the nourishment of the senses, well-being of mind is attained. // Bc_12.104 //

children.text: svasthaprasannamanasaḥ samādhirupapadyate /
children.translated_text: For one whose mind is at ease and clear, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) arises;

children.text: samādhiyuktacittasya dhyānayogaḥ pravartate // Bc_12.105 //
children.translated_text: for one whose mind is endowed with <s>samādhi</s>, the practice of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) proceeds. // Bc_12.105 //

children.text: dhyānapravartanāddharmāḥ prāpyante yairavāpyate /
children.translated_text: Through the practice of <s>dhyāna</s>, those <s>dharmas</s> (qualities) are attained by which is obtained

children.text: durlabhaṃ śāntamajaraṃ paraṃ tadamṛtaṃ padam // Bc_12.106 //
children.translated_text: that hard-to-attain, peaceful, ageless, supreme, immortal state. // Bc_12.106 //

children.text: tasmādāhāramūlo 'yamupāya itiniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this method is rooted in food — this is the conclusion.'

children.text: āhārakaraṇe dhīraḥ kṛtvāmitamatirmatim // Bc_12.107 //
children.translated_text: The resolute one, of immeasurable wisdom, having set his mind on taking food, // Bc_12.107 //

children.text: snāto nairañjanātīrāduttatāra śanaiḥ kṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: having bathed, slowly rose from the bank of the <s>Nairañjanā</s>, emaciated,

children.text: bhaktyāvanataśākhāgrairdattahastastaṭadrumaiḥ // Bc_12.108 //
children.translated_text: with the trees on the bank offering their hands — branches that reverently bent low. // Bc_12.108 //

children.text: atha gopādhipasutā daivatairabhicoditā /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nandabalā</s>, the daughter of the chief of cowherds, impelled by the gods,

children.text: udbhutahṛdayānandā tatra nandabalāgamat // Bc_12.109 //
children.translated_text: her heart filled with surging joy, came there. // Bc_12.109 //

children.text: sitaśaṅkhojjvalabhujā nīlakambalavāsinī /
children.translated_text: With arms radiant as white conch shells, clad in a dark garment,

children.text: saphenamālānīlāmburyamuneva saridvarā // Bc_12.110 //
children.translated_text: she was like the noble river <s>Yamunā</s>, with its dark waters and garlands of foam. // Bc_12.110 //

children.text: sā śraddhāvardhitaprītirvikasallocanotpalā /
children.translated_text: She, her joy increased by faith, her lotus-eyes blooming,

children.text: śirasā praṇipatyainaṃ grāhayāmāsa pāyasam // Bc_12.111 //
children.translated_text: bowing her head before him, offered him milk-rice. // Bc_12.111 //

children.text: kṛtvā tadupabhogena prāptajanmaphalāṃ sa tām /
children.translated_text: Having made her birth fruitful by his partaking of it,

children.text: bodhiprāptau samartho 'bhūtsaṃtarpitaṣaḍindriyaḥ // Bc_12.112 //
children.translated_text: he became capable of attaining enlightenment, his six senses nourished. // Bc_12.112 //

children.text: paryāptāpyānamūrtiśca sārdha svayaśasā muniḥ /
children.translated_text: With his body filled and nourished, along with his glory, the sage

children.text: kāntidhairye babhāraikaḥ śaśāṅkārṇavayordvayoḥ // Bc_12.113 //
children.translated_text: bore alone the beauty and steadfastness of both the moon and the ocean. // Bc_12.113 //

children.text: āvṛtta iti vijñāya taṃ jahuḥ pañca bhikṣavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing him to have turned back [from austerity], the five mendicants abandoned him,

children.text: manīṣiṇamivātmānaṃ nirmuktaṃ pañca dhātavaḥ // Bc_12.114 //
children.translated_text: like the five elements [abandoning] one who is wise and freed from them. // Bc_12.114 //

children.text: vyavasāyadvitīyo 'tha śādvalāstīrṇabhūtalam /
children.translated_text: Then, with determination as his second companion, [he proceeded] over ground spread with green grass;

children.text: so 'śvatthamūlaṃ prayayau bodhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ // Bc_12.115 //
children.translated_text: he went to the foot of an <s>aśvattha</s> (pipal) tree, firm in his resolve for enlightenment. // Bc_12.115 //

children.text: tatastadānīṃ gajarājavikramaḥ padasvanenānupamena bodhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, at that moment, awakened by the incomparable sound of his footsteps, with the stride of the king of elephants,

children.text: mahāmunerāgatabodhiniścayo jagāda kālo bhujagottamaḥ stutim // Bc_12.116 //
children.translated_text: a great serpent, certain that the enlightenment of the great sage was at hand, uttered a hymn of praise: // Bc_12.116 //

children.text: yathā mune tvaccaraṇāvapīḍitā muhurmuhurniṣṭanatīva medinī /
children.translated_text: 'Just as the earth resounds again and again, as it were, pressed by your feet, O sage,

children.text: yathā ca te rājati sūryavatprabhā dhrūvaṃ tvamiṣṭaṃ phalamadya bhokṣyase // Bc_12.117 //
children.translated_text: and just as your radiance shines like the sun — surely you will enjoy the desired fruit today. // Bc_12.117 //

children.text: yathā bhramantyo divi cāṣapaṅktayaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ tvāṃ kamalākṣa kurvate /
children.translated_text: Just as rows of blue jays circle around you in the sky, turning to the right, O lotus-eyed one —

children.text: yathā ca saumyā divi vānti vāyavastvamadya buddho niyataṃ bhaviṣyasi // Bc_12.118 //
children.translated_text: and just as the gentle breezes blow in heaven — you will surely become a <s>Buddha</s> today. // 12.118 //

children.text: tato bhujaṅgapravareṇa saṃstutastṛṇānyupādāya śucīni lāvakāt /
children.translated_text: Then, praised by the chief of serpents, receiving pure grass from a grass-cutter,

children.text: kṛtapratijño niṣasāda bodhaye mahātarormūlamupāśritaḥ śuceḥ // Bc_12.119 //
children.translated_text: having made his resolve, he sat down for enlightenment at the root of a great, pure tree. // 12.119 //

children.text: tataḥ sa paryaṅkamakampyamuttamaṃ babandha suptoragabhogapiṇḍitam /
children.translated_text: Then he bound the supreme, unshakable cross-legged posture, compact as the coils of a sleeping serpent,

children.text: bhinadmi tāvadbhuvi naitadāsanaṃ na yāmi yāvatkutakṛtyatāmiti // Bc_12.120 //
children.translated_text: [vowing:] 'I shall not break this seat upon the earth until I have accomplished what must be done.' // 12.120 //

children.text: tato yayurmadamatulāṃ divaukaso vavāśire na mṛgagaṇā na pakṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the sky-dwellers went to incomparable joy; the herds of deer did not cry, nor the birds;

children.text: na sasvanurvanataravo 'nilāhatāḥ kṛtāsane bhagavati niścitātmani // Bc_12.121 //
children.translated_text: the forest-trees, struck by the wind, did not rustle — when the Blessed One, firm in resolve, had taken his seat. // 12.121 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye 'rāḍadarśano nāma dvādaśaḥ sargaḥ // 12 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth canto named 'The Encounter with <s>Arāḍa</s>' in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>. // 12 //
CANTO XIII

children.text: tasminvimokṣāya kṛtapratijñe rājarṣivaṃśaprabhave maharṣau /
children.translated_text: When that great sage, born of a lineage of <s>rājarṣis</s> (royal sages), sat there having made his resolve for liberation,

children.text: tatropaviṣṭe prajaharṣa lokastatrāsa saddharmaripustu māraḥ // Bc_13.1 //
children.translated_text: the world rejoiced; but <s>Māra</s>, the enemy of the true <s>Dharma</s>, was terrified. // 13.1 //

children.text: yaṃ kāmadevaṃ pravadanti loke citrāyudhaṃ puṣpaśaraṃ tathaiva /
children.translated_text: He whom they call in the world <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the god of desire), bearing a variegated bow with flower-arrows —

children.text: kāmapracārādhipatiṃ tameva mokṣadviṣaṃ māramudāharanti // Bc_13.2 //
children.translated_text: that very lord of the domain of desire — they call him <s>Māra</s>, the enemy of liberation. // 13.2 //

children.text: tasyātmajā vibhramaharṣadarpāstisro 'ratiprītitṛṣaśca kanyāḥ /
children.translated_text: His three daughters — <s>Arati</s> (Discontent), <s>Prīti</s> (Delight), and <s>Tṛṣā</s> (Craving) — with their allure, joy, and pride,

children.text: papracchurenaṃ manaso vikāraṃ sa tāṃśca tāścaiva vaco 'bhyuvāca // Bc_13.3 //
children.translated_text: asked him the cause of his mental disturbance; and he spoke these words to both his sons and daughters: // 13.3 //

children.text: asau munirniścayavarma bibhratsattvāyudhaṃ buddhiśaraṃ vikṛṣya /
children.translated_text: 'That sage, wearing the armor of resolve, drawing the arrow of intellect fitted to the bow of truth,

children.text: jigīṣurāste viṣayānmadīyāntasmādayaṃ me manaso viṣādaḥ // Bc_13.4 //
children.translated_text: sits desiring to conquer my domains — that is the cause of my mind's dejection. // 13.4 //

children.text: yadi hyasau māmabhibhūya yāti lokāya cākhyātyapavargamārgam /
children.translated_text: 'For if he conquers me and proclaims to the world the path of liberation,

children.text: śūnyastato 'yaṃ viṣayo mamādya vṛttāccyutasyeva videhabhartuḥ // Bc_13.5 //
children.translated_text: then this domain of mine will be empty today — like the realm of the lord of <s>Videha</s> who fell from his [proper] conduct. // 13.5 //

children.text: tadyāvadevaiṣa na labdhacakṣurmadrocare tiṣṭhati yāvadeva /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, while he has not yet attained the eye [of enlightenment], while he still remains in my domain,

children.text: yāsyāmi tāvadvratamasya bhettuṃ setuṃ nadīvega ivātivṛddhaḥ // Bc_13.6 //
children.translated_text: I shall go to break his vow — like a swollen river-current [breaking] a dam.' // 13.6 //

children.text: tato dhanuḥ puṣpamayaṃ gṛhītvā śarān jaganmohakarāṃśca pañca /
children.translated_text: Then, taking up the flower-bow and five arrows that delude the world,

children.text: so 'śvatthamūlaṃ sasuto 'bhyagacchadasvāsthyakārī manasaḥ prajānām // Bc_13.7 //
children.translated_text: he advanced with his sons to the root of the <s>Aśvattha</s> tree — he who causes unease in the minds of beings. // 13.7 //

children.text: atha praśāntaṃ munimāsanasthaṃ pāraṃ titīrṣu bhavasāgarasya /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the serene sage seated at his seat, wishing to cross to the far shore of the ocean of <s>bhava</s> (existence),

children.text: viṣajya savyaṃ karamāyudhāgre krīḍan śareṇedamuvāca māraḥ // Bc_13.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>, placing his left hand on the tip of his weapon, playing with an arrow, said this: // 13.8 //

children.text: uttiṣṭha bhoḥ kṣatriya mṛtyubhīta cara svadharma tyaja mokṣadharmam /
children.translated_text: 'Arise, O <s>Kṣatriya</s>, fearful of death! Follow your own <s>dharma</s>, abandon the <s>dharma</s> of liberation!

children.text: bāṇaiśca yajñaiśca vinīya lokaṃ lokātpadaṃ prāpnuhi vāsavasya // Bc_13.9 //
children.translated_text: Having subdued the world by arrows and sacrifices, win the seat of <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) beyond the world! // 13.9 //

children.text: panthā hi niryātumayaṃ yaśasyo yo vāhitaḥ pūrvatamairnarendraiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For this is the glorious path of departure that was trodden by the earliest kings;

children.text: jātasya rājarṣikule viśāle bhaikṣākamaślādhyamidaṃ prapattum // Bc_13.10 //
children.translated_text: born in a great lineage of royal sages, it is unseemly to take up begging. // 13.10 //

children.text: athādya nottiṣṭhasi niścitātman bhava sthiro mā vimucaḥ pratijñām /
children.translated_text: 'But if you will not rise today, O one of firm resolve, be steadfast — do not release your vow;

children.text: mayodyato hyeṣa śaraḥ sa eṃva yaḥ śūrpake mīnaripau vimuktaḥ // Bc_13.11 //
children.translated_text: for this arrow raised by me is the very one that was released at <s>Śūrpaka</s>, the enemy of fish. // 13.11 //

children.text: spṛṣṭaḥ sa cānena kathaṃcidaiḍaḥ somasya naptāpyabhavadvicittaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And struck by it, <s>Aiḍa</s> — grandson of <s>Soma</s> — though barely touched, became bewildered;

children.text: sa cābhavacchantanurasvatantraḥ kṣīṇe yuge kiṃ bata durbalo 'nyaḥ // Bc_13.12 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Śantanu</s> too was rendered powerless — in a degenerate age, what then of another, still weaker? // 13.12 //

children.text: tatkṣipramuttiṣṭha labhasva saṃjñāṃ bāṇo hyayaṃ tiṣṭhati lelihānaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore arise quickly, regain your senses — for this arrow stands licking [its lips];

children.text: priyāvidheyeṣu ratipriyeṣu yaṃ cakravākeṣviva notsṛjāmi // Bc_13.13 //
children.translated_text: this arrow which I do not release even upon the <s>cakravāka</s> birds, who are devoted to their beloved and fond of love.' // 13.13 //

children.text: ityevamukto 'pi yadā nirāstho naivāsanaṃ śākyamunirbibheda /
children.translated_text: Yet even when thus addressed, the <s>Śākya</s> sage, being free from attachment, did not at all break his seat;

children.text: śaraṃ tato 'smai visasarja māraḥ kanyāśca kṛtvā purataḥ sutāṃśca // Bc_13.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> then released the arrow at him, and placed his daughters and sons before him. // 13.14 //

children.text: tasmiṃstu bāṇe 'pi sa vipramukte cakāra nāsthāṃ na dhṛteścacāla /
children.translated_text: But even when that arrow was released, he paid it no heed, nor did he waver in his firmness;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tathainaṃ viṣasāda māraścintāparītaśca śanairjagāda // Bc_13.15 //
children.translated_text: seeing him thus, <s>Māra</s> was dejected, and slowly said, surrounded by anxiety: // 13.15 //

children.text: śailendraputrīṃ prati yena viddho devo 'pi śambhuścalito babhūva /
children.translated_text: 'The very arrow by which even the god <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) was struck and became agitated with regard to the daughter of the Mountain-lord —

children.text: na cintayatyeṣa tameva bāṇaṃ kiṃ syādacitto na śaraḥ sa eṣaḥ // Bc_13.16 //
children.translated_text: this one does not heed that very arrow — is he perhaps without consciousness? Or is it not the [same] arrow? // 13.16 //

children.text: tasmādayaṃ nārhati puṣpabāṇaṃ na harṣaṇaṃ nāpi raterniyogam /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore this one does not deserve the flower-arrow, nor enticement, nor the assignment of love;

children.text: arhatyayaṃ bhūtagaṇairasaumyaiḥ saṃtrāsanātarjanatāḍanāni // Bc_13.17 //
children.translated_text: this one deserves from fierce ghostly hosts — terrorizing, threatening, and striking.' // 13.17 //

children.text: sasmāra māraśca tataḥ svasainyaṃ vighnaṃ śame śākyamuneścikīrṣan /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> recalled his army, desiring to create an obstacle to the <s>Śākya</s> sage's tranquility;

children.text: nanāśrayāścānucarāḥ parīyuḥ śaladrumaprāsagadāsihastāḥ // Bc_13.18 //
children.translated_text: and his attendants of various abodes came around, holding darts, spears, clubs, swords, and maces in hand. // 13.18 //

children.text: varāhamīnāśvakharoṣṭravaktrā vyāghrarkṣasiṃhadviradānanāśca /
children.translated_text: With faces of boars, fish, horses, donkeys, and camels; with faces of tigers, bears, lions, and elephants;

children.text: ekekṣaṇā naikamukhāstriśīrṣā lambodarāścaiva pṛṣodarāśca // Bc_13.19 //
children.translated_text: one-eyed, many-faced, three-headed; with pot-bellies and spotted bellies. // 13.19 //

children.text: ajānusakthā ghaṭajānavaśca daṃṣṭrāyudhāścaiva nakhāyudhāśca /
children.translated_text: With thighs extending to the knees, with knees like pots; armed with fangs and armed with claws;

children.text: karaṅkavaktrā bahumūrtayaśca bhagnārdhavaktrāśca mahāmukhāśca // Bc_13.20 //
children.translated_text: with skull-faces, many-formed; with half-shattered faces and enormous mouths. // 13.20 //

children.text: bhasmāruṇā lohitabinducitrāḥ khaṭvāṅgahastā haridhūmrakeśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Ash-red, speckled with drops of blood, holding skull-topped staffs (<s>khaṭvāṅga</s>), with green-grey hair;

children.text: lambasrajo vāraṇalambakarṇāścarmāmbarāścaiva nirambarāśca // Bc_13.21 //
children.translated_text: with hanging garlands, with elephant-like drooping ears; wearing hides as garments, and some naked. // 13.21 //

children.text: śvetārdhavaktrā haritārdhakāyāstāmrāśca dhrūmrā harayo 'sitāśca /
children.translated_text: With half-white faces, half-green bodies; copper-colored, smoky, tawny, and dark;

children.text: vyālottarāsaṅgabhujāstathaiva praghuṣṭāghaṇṭākulamekhalāśca // Bc_13.22 //
children.translated_text: with serpents as upper garments on their arms; with girdles clanging with loudly-ringing bells. // 13.22 //

children.text: tālapramāṇāśca gṛhītaśūlā daṃṣṭrākarālāśca śiśupramāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Tall as palm trees, grasping tridents; small as infants, with terrible fangs;

children.text: urabhravaktrāśca vihaṃgamākṣā mārjāravaktrāśca manuṣyakāyāḥ // Bc_13.23 //
children.translated_text: with ram-faces and bird-eyes; with cat-faces and human bodies. // 13.23 //

children.text: prakīrṇakeśāḥ śikhino 'rdhamuṇḍā raktāmbarā vyākulaveṣṭanāśca /
children.translated_text: With disheveled hair, crested, half-shaved; in red garments, with disordered wrappings;

children.text: prahṛṣṭavaktrā bhṛkuṭīmukhāśca tejoharāścaiva manoharāśca // Bc_13.24 //
children.translated_text: with exultant faces and scowling faces; those that steal splendor and those that steal the mind. // 13.24 //

children.text: kecidvrajanto bhṛśamāvavalguranyo 'nyamāpupluvire tathānye /
children.translated_text: Some went striding violently; others leapt upon each other;

children.text: cikrīḍurākāśagatāśca kecitkecicca cerustarumastakeṣu // Bc_13.25 //
children.translated_text: some sported while going through the sky; some roamed on the treetops. // 13.25 //

children.text: nanarta kaścidbhramayaṃstriśūlaṃ kaścidvipuṣphūrja gadāṃ vikarṣan /
children.translated_text: One danced whirling a trident; another roared while brandishing a mace;

children.text: harṣeṇa kaścidvṛṣavannanarda kaścicatprajajvāla tanūnaruhebhyaḥ // Bc_13.26 //
children.translated_text: one bellowed with joy like a bull; another burst into flame from every hair of his body. // 13.26 //

children.text: evaṃvidhā bhūtagaṇāḥ samantāttadbodhimūlaṃ parivārya tasthuḥ /
children.translated_text: Such hosts of spirits, surrounding that root of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree from all sides, stood

children.text: jighṛkṣavaścaiva jighāṃsavaśca bharturniyogaṃ paripālayantaḥ // Bc_13.27 //
children.translated_text: desiring to seize and desiring to slay, carrying out their master's command. // 13.27 //

children.text: taṃ prekṣya mārasya ca pūrvarātre śākyarṣabhasyaiva ca yuddhakālam /
children.translated_text: Seeing that battle-time of <s>Māra</s> and the bull of the <s>Śākyas</s> in the first watch of the night,

children.text: na dyauścakāśe pṛthivī cakampe prajajvaluścaiva diśaḥ saśabdāḥ // Bc_13.28 //
children.translated_text: heaven did not shine, the earth trembled, and the quarters blazed forth with sound. // 13.28 //

children.text: viṣvagvavau vāyurudīrṇavegastārā na rejurna babhau śaśāṅkaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wind blew violently in all directions; the stars did not gleam, the moon did not shine;

children.text: tamaśca bhūyo vitatāna rātriḥ sarve ca saṃcukṣubhire samudrāḥ // Bc_13.29 //
children.translated_text: and the night spread even denser darkness, and all the oceans were agitated. // 13.29 //

children.text: mahībhṛto dharmaparāśca nāgā mahāmunervighnamamṛṣyamāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Dharma</s>-devoted <s>Nāgas</s>, the mountain-bearers, unable to tolerate the obstacle to the great sage,

children.text: māraṃ prati krodhavivṛttanetrā niḥśaśvasuścaiva jajṛmbhire ca // Bc_13.30 //
children.translated_text: rolled their eyes in anger toward <s>Māra</s>, and sighed and yawned. // 13.30 //

children.text: śuddhādhivāsā vibudharṣayastu saddharmasiddhyarthamabhipravṛttāḥ /
children.translated_text: But the divine sages of pure abodes, engaged in the accomplishment of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: māre 'nukampāṃ manasā pracakrurvirāgabhāvāttu na roṣamīyuḥ // Bc_13.31 //
children.translated_text: felt compassion toward <s>Māra</s> in their minds, but did not come to anger, due to their state of dispassion. // 13.31 //

children.text: tadbodhimūlaṃ samavekṣya kīrṇa hiṃsātmanā mārabalena tena /
children.translated_text: Seeing that root of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree strewn by that army of <s>Māra</s> intent on harm,

children.text: dharmātmabhirlokavimokṣakāmairbabhūva hāhākṛtamantarīkṣe // Bc_13.32 //
children.translated_text: by the <s>Dharma</s>-minded ones desiring the liberation of the world, a cry of 'Alas! Alas!' arose in the sky. // 13.32 //

children.text: upaplavaṃ dharmavidhestu tasya dṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ mārabalaṃ maharṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: But seeing the army of <s>Māra</s> standing as an obstacle to that seeker of <s>Dharma</s>, the great sage

children.text: na cukṣubhe nāpi yayau vikāraṃ madhye gavāṃ siṃha ivopaviṣṭaḥ // Bc_13.33 //
children.translated_text: was neither agitated nor underwent any change — like a lion seated amidst cattle. // 13.33 //

children.text: mārastato bhūtacamūmudīrṇāmājñāpayāmāsa bhayāya tasya /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> commanded his excited army of spirits to terrify him;

children.text: svaiḥ svaiḥ prabhāvairatha sāsya senā taddhairyabhedāya matiṃ cakāra // Bc_13.34 //
children.translated_text: and with their various powers, his army set their minds to breaking his firmness. // 13.34 //

children.text: keciccalannaikavilambijivhāstīkṣṇāgradaṃṣṭrā harimaṇḍalākṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some, with tongues flickering and dangling, with sharp-pointed fangs, with tawny ring-eyes,

children.text: vidāritāsyāḥ sthiraśaṅkukarṇāḥ saṃtrāsayantaḥ kila nāma tasthuḥ // Bc_13.35 //
children.translated_text: with mouths rent apart, with ears [sharp as] fixed stakes — stood there, supposedly trying to terrify. // 13.35 //

children.text: tebhyaḥ sthitebhyaḥ sa tathāvidhebhyaḥ rūpeṇa bhāvena ca dāruṇebhyaḥ /
