children.translated_text: From those who stood thus, terrible in form and in nature,

children.text: na vivyathe nodvivije maharṣiḥ krīḍatsubālebhya ivoddhatebhyaḥ // Bc_13.36 //
children.translated_text: the great sage was neither frightened nor disturbed — as [he would not be] from unruly children at play. // 13.36 //

children.text: kaścittato roṣavivṛttadṛṣṭistasmai gadāmudyamayāṃcakāra /
children.translated_text: Then one, with eyes rolling in rage, raised a mace against him;

children.text: tastambha bāhuḥ sagadastato 'sya puraṃdarasyeva pura savajraḥ // Bc_13.37 //
children.translated_text: but his arm with the mace froze in place — like the thunderbolt-bearing arm of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) of old. // 13.37 //

children.text: kecitsamudyamya śilāstarūṃśca viṣehire naiva munau vimoktum /
children.translated_text: Some, having raised rocks and trees, were unable to hurl them at the sage;

children.text: petuḥ savṛkṣāḥ saśilāstathaiva vajrāvabhagnā iva vindhyapādāḥ // Bc_13.38 //
children.translated_text: they fell together with the trees and rocks — like the slopes of the <s>Vindhya</s> struck by thunderbolts. // 13.38 //

children.text: kaiścitsamutpatya nabho vimuktāḥ śilāśca vṛkṣāśca paraśvadhāśca /
children.translated_text: By some, having leapt into the sky, rocks, trees, and axes were released;

children.text: tasthurnabhayasyeva na cāvapetuḥ saṃdhyābhrapādā iva naikavarṇāḥ // Bc_13.39 //
children.translated_text: but they stood in the sky and did not fall — like many-colored cloud-masses at twilight. // 13.39 //

children.text: cikṣepa tasyopari dīptamanyaḥ kaḍaṅgaraṃ parvataśṛṅgamātram /
children.translated_text: Another hurled from above a blazing firebrand, massive as a mountain peak;

children.text: yanmuktapātraṃ gaganasthameva tasyānubhāvācchatadhā paphāla // Bc_13.40 //
children.translated_text: but released from his hand, remaining in the sky itself, it burst into a hundred pieces by [the sage's] spiritual power. // 13.40 //

children.text: kaścijjvalannarka ivoditaḥ khādaṅgāravarṣa mahadutsasarja /
children.translated_text: Another, blazing like the risen sun in the sky, let fall a great shower of burning coals,

children.text: cūrṇāni cāmīkarakandarāṇāṃ kalpātyaye meruriva pradīptaḥ // Bc_13.41 //
children.translated_text: and [showers of] golden mountain-dust — like blazing <s>Meru</s> at the end of a cosmic age. // 13.41 //

children.text: tadbodhimūle pravikīryamāṇamaṅgāravarṣa tu savisphuliṅgam /
children.translated_text: But that shower of coals, with sparks, being scattered at the root of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree,

children.text: maitrīvihārādṛṣisattamasya babhūva raktotpalapattravarṣaḥ // Bc_13.42 //
children.translated_text: by the power of the loving-kindness meditation (<s>maitrī-vihāra</s>) of that best of sages, became a shower of red-lotus petals. // 13.42 //

children.text: śarīracittavyasanātapaistairevaṃvidhaistaiśca nipātyamānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Though struck by those torments of body, mind, and various afflictions of such a kind,

children.text: naivāsanācchākyamuniścacāla svaniścayaṃ bandhumivopaguhya // Bc_13.43 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Śākya</s> sage did not stir from his seat — embracing his own resolve as if it were a kinsman. // 13.43 //

children.text: athāpare nirjigilurmukhebhyaḥ sarpānvijīrṇebhya iva drumebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then others disgorged serpents from their mouths, as from decayed trees;

children.text: te mantrabaddhā iva tatsamīpe na śaśvasurnotsasṛpurna celuḥ // Bc_13.44 //
children.translated_text: but those [serpents], as if bound by <s>mantras</s>, near him neither breathed, nor crept, nor moved. // 13.44 //

children.text: bhūtvāpare vāridharā bṛhantaḥ savidyutaḥ sāśanicaṇḍaghoṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others, becoming great rain-clouds, with lightning, with terrible thunder and thunderbolts,

children.text: tasmindrume tatyajuraśmavarṣaṃ tatpuṣpavarṣaṃ ruciraṃ babhūva // Bc_13.45 //
children.translated_text: released a shower of stones upon that tree; but it became a beautiful shower of flowers. // 13.45 //

children.text: cāpe 'tha bāṇo nihito 'pareṇa jajvāla tatraiva na niṣpapāta /
children.translated_text: Then an arrow placed upon a bow by another blazed there but did not fall;

children.text: anīśvarasyātmani dhūyamāno durmarṣaṇasyeva narasya manyuḥ // Bc_13.46 //
children.translated_text: consumed in [the archer's] own self though powerless — like the anger of an intolerable man. // 13.46 //

children.text: pañceṣavo 'nyena tu vipramuktāstasthurnabhasyeva munau na petuḥ /
children.translated_text: Five arrows released by another stood in the sky and did not fall upon the sage —

children.text: saṃsārabhīrorviṣayapravṛttau pañcendriyāṇīva parikṣakasya // Bc_13.47 //
children.translated_text: like the five senses of an examiner, [holding back] from engagement with sense-objects, for one who fears <s>saṃsāra</s>. // 13.47 //

children.text: jighāsayānyaḥ prasasāra ruṣṭo gadāṃ gṛhītvābhimukho maharṣeḥ /
children.translated_text: Another, desiring to kill, rushed forward in anger, seizing a mace, facing the great sage;

children.text: so 'prāptakāmo vivaśaḥ papāta doṣeṣvivānarthakareṣu lokaḥ // Bc_13.48 //
children.translated_text: but he fell, powerless, having failed in his aim — like the world into harmful faults. // 13.48 //

children.text: strī meghakālī tu kapālahastā kartu maharṣeḥ kila cittamoham /
children.translated_text: And a woman, <s>Meghakālī</s> (Dark-as-a-Cloud), holding a skull in her hand, desiring to create delusion in the great sage's mind,

children.text: babhrāma tatrāniyataṃ na tasthau calātmano buddhirivāgameṣu // Bc_13.49 //
children.translated_text: wandered there erratically, unable to stand still — like the unsteady mind of a passion-driven person in [matters of] scripture. // 13.49 //

children.text: kaścitpradīptaṃ praṇidhāya cakṣurnetrāgnināśīviṣavaddidhakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: One, fixing his blazing eye, wishing to burn [the sage] with the fire of his gaze like a venomous serpent,

children.text: tatraiva nāsīnamṛṣiṃ dadarśa kāmātmakaḥ śreya ivopadiṣṭam // Bc_13.50 //
children.translated_text: saw the sage sitting right there [unmoved] — like a passion-driven person [confronting but unable to heed] a teaching of the good. // 13.50 //

children.text: gurvī śilāmudyamayaṃstathānyaḥ śaśrāma moghaṃ vihataprayatnaḥ /
children.translated_text: And another, heaving up a heavy rock, toiled in vain with thwarted effort —

children.text: niḥśreyasaṃ jñānasamādhigamyaṃ kāyaklamairdharmamivāptukāmaḥ // Bc_13.51 //
children.translated_text: like one desiring to attain through bodily exertion the <s>Dharma</s> of the supreme good that is attainable through knowledge and <s>samādhi</s>. // 13.51 //

children.text: tarakṣusiṃhākṛtayastathānye praṇeduruccairmahataḥ praṇādān /
children.translated_text: And others, with forms of hyenas and lions, uttered great roars,

children.text: sattvāni yaiḥ saṃcukucuḥ samantādvajrāhatā dyauḥ phalatīti mattvā // Bc_13.52 //
children.translated_text: by which all creatures shrank on every side, thinking 'The sky, struck by thunderbolts, is splitting!' // 13.52 //

children.text: mṛgā gajāścārtaravān sṛjanto vidudruvuścaiva nililyire ca /
children.translated_text: And deer and elephants, emitting distressed cries, fled in all directions and hid;

children.text: rātrau ca tasyāmahanīva digbhyaḥ khagā ruvantaḥ paripeturārtāḥ // Bc_13.53 //
children.translated_text: and in that night, as if it were day, birds flew crying from every quarter in distress. // 13.53 //

children.text: teṣāṃ praṇādaistu tathāvidhaistai sarveṣu bhūteṣvapi kampiteṣu /
children.translated_text: But though all beings trembled at those various roars of theirs,

children.text: munirna tatrāsa na saṃcukoca ravairgarutmāniva vāyasānām // Bc_13.54 //
children.translated_text: the sage was neither frightened nor contracted — like <s>Garuḍa</s> at the cries of crows. // 13.54 //

children.text: bhayāvahebhyaḥ pariṣadgaṇebhyo yathā yathā naiva munirbibhāya /
children.translated_text: the more the sage felt no fear of the terrible hosts of his retinue,

children.text: tathā tathā dharmabhṛtāṃ sapatnaḥ śokācca roṣācca sasāda māraḥ // Bc_13.55 //
children.translated_text: the more <s>Māra</s>, the adversary of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>, sank down — from sorrow and from rage. // 13.55 //

children.text: bhūtaṃ tataḥ kiṃciddṛśyarūpaṃ viśiṣṭabhūtaṃ gaganasthameva /
children.translated_text: Then a certain being of visible form, a distinguished being, standing in the sky,

children.text: dṛṣṭavarṣaye dugdhamavairaruṣṭaṃ māraṃ babhāṣe mahatā svareṇa // Bc_13.56 //
children.translated_text: addressed <s>Māra</s> in a mighty voice — without anger, pouring down milk [of compassion], as it were: // 13.56 //

children.text: moghaṃ śramaṃ nārhasi māra kartuṃ hiṃsrātmatāmutsṛja gaccha śarma /
children.translated_text: 'You should not exert yourself in vain labor, O <s>Māra</s>; abandon your violent nature and go to peace;

children.text: naiṣa tvayā kampayituṃ hi śakyo mahāgirirmerurivānilena // Bc_13.57 //
children.translated_text: for this one cannot be shaken by you — as the great mountain <s>Meru</s> cannot be moved by the wind. // 13.57 //

children.text: apyuṣṇabhāvaṃ jvalanaḥ prajahyādāpo dravatvaṃ prathivī sthiratvam /
children.translated_text: 'Fire might abandon its hot nature, water its fluidity, the earth its stability,

children.text: anekakalpācitapuṇyakarmā na tveva jahyādvyavasāyameṣaḥ // Bc_13.58 //
children.translated_text: but this one, whose meritorious deeds have been accumulated through many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), would never abandon his resolve. // 13.58 //

children.text: yo niścayo hyasya parākramaśca tejaśca yadyā ca dayā prajāsu /
children.translated_text: 'For his determination, his valor, his splendor, and his compassion for all beings —

children.text: aprāpya notthāsyati tattvameṣa tamāṃsyahatveva sahasraraśmiḥ // Bc_13.59 //
children.translated_text: without attaining the truth, he will not rise from this [seat] — like the thousand-rayed [sun] that has dispelled the darkness. // 13.59 //

children.text: kāṣṭhaṃ hi mathnan labhate hutāśaṃ bhūmiṃ khananvindati cāpi toyam /
children.translated_text: 'For by rubbing wood, one obtains the sacrificial fire; by digging the earth, one also finds water;

children.text: nirbandhinaḥ kiṃcana nāstyasādhyaṃ nyāyena yuktaṃ ca kṛtaṃ ca sarvam // Bc_13.60 //
children.translated_text: for one who perseveres, nothing is unachievable — everything is accomplished that is done with right method. // 13.60 //

children.text: tallokamārta karuṇāyamāno rogeṣu rāgādiṣu vartamānam /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, having compassion for this world — afflicted, ailing with the diseases of <s>rāga</s> (passion) and such —

children.text: mahābhiṣaṅga nārhati vighnameṣa jñānauṣadhārtha parikhidyamānaḥ // Bc_13.61 //
children.translated_text: it is not right to obstruct this great physician, who is exerting himself for the sake of the medicine of knowledge. // 13.61 //

children.text: hṛte ca loke bahubhiḥ kumārgaiḥ sanmārgamanvicchati yaḥ śrameṇa /
children.translated_text: 'When the world has been led astray by many wrong paths, he who with effort seeks the right path —

children.text: sa daiśikaḥ kṣobhayituṃ na yuktaṃ sudeśikaḥ sārtha iva pranaṣṭe // Bc_13.62 //
children.translated_text: it is not right to disturb that guide — like a good guide when a caravan is lost. // 13.62 //

children.text: sattveṣu naṣṭeṣu mahāndhakāre jñānapradīpaḥ kriyamāṇa eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Among beings lost in great darkness, this one is being fashioned as a lamp of knowledge;

children.text: āryasya nirvāpayituṃ na sādhu prajvālyamānastamasīva dīpaḥ // Bc_13.63 //
children.translated_text: it is not good to extinguish a noble one — like [extinguishing] a lamp being lit in darkness. // 13.63 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca saṃsāramaye mahaughe magnaṃ jagatpāramavindamānam /
children.translated_text: 'And seeing the world submerged in the great flood of <s>saṃsāra</s>, unable to find the far shore —

children.text: yaścedamuttārayituṃ pravṛttaḥ kaścintayettasya tu pāpamāryaḥ // Bc_13.64 //
children.translated_text: what noble person would conceive evil toward one who has undertaken to rescue it? // 13.64 //

children.text: kṣamāśipho dhairyavigāḍhamūlaścāritrapuṣpaḥ smṛtibuddhiśākhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The tree of knowledge, whose tip is forbearance, whose root is firmly fixed by steadfastness, whose flowers are good conduct, whose branches are mindfulness and wisdom,

children.text: jñānadrumo dharmaphalapradātā notpāṭanaṃ hyarhati vardhamānaḥ // Bc_13.65 //
children.translated_text: the giver of the fruit of <s>dharma</s> — it does not deserve to be uprooted while it is growing. // 13.65 //

children.text: baddhāṃ dṛḍhaiścetasi mohapāśairyasya prajāṃ mokṣayituṃ manīṣā /
children.translated_text: 'He whose intention is to liberate these beings, whose minds are bound by the firm bonds of delusion —

children.text: tasmin jighāṃsā tava nopapannā śrānte jagadbandhanamokṣahetoḥ // Bc_13.66 //
children.translated_text: your desire to harm him is unfitting — him who toils for the sake of loosening the bonds of the world. // 13.66 //

children.text: bodhāya karmāṇi hi yānyanena kṛtāni teṣāṃ niyato 'dya kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the deeds that this one has performed for the sake of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) — the appointed time for those is today;

children.text: sthāne tathāsminnupaviṣṭa eṣa yathaiva pūrve munayastathaiva // Bc_13.67 //
children.translated_text: he is seated in this very spot, just as the former sages [sat] — in the same way. // 13.67 //

children.text: eṣā hi nābhirvasudhātalasya kṛtsnena yuktā parameṇa dhāmnā /
children.translated_text: 'For this is the navel of the surface of the earth, united with the supreme abode in its entirety;

children.text: bhūmerato 'nyo 'sti hi na pradeśo vegaṃ samādherviṣaheta yo 'sya // Bc_13.68 //
children.translated_text: there is no other spot on earth that could withstand the force of his <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). // 13.68 //

children.text: tanmā kṛthā śokamupehi śāntiṃ mā bhūnmahimnā tava māra mānaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, do not grieve; go to peace. Let there not be pride in you from your power, O <s>Māra</s>;

children.text: viśrambhituṃ na kṣamamadhuvā śrīścale pade vismayamabhyupaiṣi // Bc_13.69 //
children.translated_text: you should not feel confident — for fortune is fickle; are you amazed at [standing on] an unstable footing?' // 13.69 //

children.text: tataḥ sa saṃśrutya ca tasya tadvaco mahāmuneḥ prekṣya ca niṣprakampatām /
children.translated_text: Then, having heard those words and having seen the unwavering composure of the great sage,

children.text: jagāma māro vimano hatodyamaḥ śarairjagaccetasi yairvihanyate // Bc_13.70 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> departed — downcast, his effort defeated — with those arrows by which the hearts of all the world are pierced. // 13.70 //

children.text: gatapraharṣā viphalīkṛtaśramā praviddhapāṣāṇakaḍaṅgaradrumā /
children.translated_text: Their joy gone, their effort made fruitless, their rocks, cudgels, and trees cast aside,

children.text: diśaḥ pradudrāva tato 'sya sā camūrhatāśrayeva dviṣatā dviṣaccamūḥ // Bc_13.71 //
children.translated_text: that army of his fled in all directions — like the army of an enemy whose refuge has been destroyed by the foe. // 13.71 //

children.text: dravati saparipakṣe nirjitai puṣpaketau jayatijitamaske nīrajaske maharṣau /
children.translated_text: As the flower-bannered [<s>Māra</s>] fled with his retinue, defeated, and as the great sage triumphed — his darkness conquered, his dust removed —

children.text: yuvatiriva sahāsā dyauścakāśe sacandrā surabhi ca jalagarbha puṣpavarṣa papāta // Bc_13.72 //
children.translated_text: the sky suddenly shone with the moon, like a woman; and a fragrant rain of flowers, water-laden, fell. // 13.72 //

body.text: iti buddhacarite mahākāvye 'śvaghoṣakṛte māravijayo nāma trayodaśaḥ sargaḥ // 13 //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the great poem <s>Buddhacarita</s>, composed by <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>, [ends] the thirteenth canto, entitled 'The Victory over <s>Māra</s>' (<s>Māravijaya</s>). // 13 //
CANTO XIV

children.text: tato mārabalaṃ jitvā dhairyeṇa ca śamena ca /
children.translated_text: Then, having conquered the army of <s>Māra</s> by steadfastness and by calm,

children.text: paramārtha vijijñāsuḥ sa dadhyau dhyānakovidaḥ // Bc_14.1 //
children.translated_text: he, skilled in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), desiring to know the supreme truth, meditated. // 14.1 //

children.text: sarveṣu dhyānavidhiṣu prāpya caiśvaryamuttamam /
children.translated_text: Having attained supreme mastery in all the methods of <s>dhyāna</s>,

children.text: sasmāra prathame yāme pūrvajanmaparaṃparām // Bc_14.2 //
children.translated_text: in the first watch of the night, he remembered the succession of his former births: // 14.2 //

children.text: amutrāhamayaṃ nāma cyutastasmādihāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There I was, of such-and-such a name; fallen from that [life], I came here' —

children.text: uiti janmasahastrāṇi sasmārānubhavanniva // Bc_14.3 //
children.translated_text: thus he remembered thousands of births, as if experiencing them again. // 14.3 //

children.text: smṛtvā janma ca mṛtyuṃ ca tāsu tāsūpapattiṣu /
children.translated_text: Remembering birth and death in those various existences,

children.text: tataḥ sattveṣu kāruṃṇyaṃ cakāra karuṇātmakaḥ // Bc_14.4 //
children.translated_text: he then felt compassion for all beings, he whose nature was compassion: // 14.4 //

children.text: kṛtveha svajanotsarga punaranyatra ca kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned their own people here, and performing rites elsewhere again —

children.text: atrāṇaḥ khalu loko 'yaṃ paribhramati cakravat // Bc_14.5 //
children.translated_text: this world, without protection, revolves like a wheel!' // 14.5 //

children.text: ityevaṃ smaratastasya babhūva niyatātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, as he remembered, for him whose self was restrained,

children.text: kadalīgarbhaniḥsāraḥ saṃsāra iti niścayaḥ // Bc_14.6 //
children.translated_text: this certainty arose: '<s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) is without essence, like the pith of a plantain tree.' // 14.6 //

children.text: dvitīye tvāgate yāme so 'dvitīyaparākramaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when the second watch arrived, he, of unrivaled valor,

children.text: divyaṃ lebhe paraṃ cakṣuḥ sarvacakṣuṣmatāṃ varaḥ // Bc_14.7 //
children.translated_text: obtained the supreme divine eye — the best among all those who possess sight. // 14.7 //

children.text: tatastena sa divyena pariśuddhena cakṣuṣā /
children.translated_text: Then with that divine, perfectly purified eye,

children.text: dadarśa nikhilaṃ lokamādarśa iva nirmale // Bc_14.8 //
children.translated_text: he saw the entire world, as if in a spotless mirror. // 14.8 //

children.text: sattvānāṃ paśyatastasya nikṛṣṭotkṛṣṭakarmaṇām /
children.translated_text: As he beheld beings — of low and exalted deeds —

children.text: pracyutiṃ copapattiṃ ca vavṛdhe karuṇātmatā // Bc_14.9 //
children.translated_text: their falling away and their rebirth, his compassionate nature grew: // 14.9 //

children.text: ime duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ prāṇino yāni durgatim /
children.translated_text: 'These beings of evil deeds go to a bad destination;

children.text: ime 'nye śubhakarmāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhante tripiṣṭape // Bc_14.10 //
children.translated_text: these others, of wholesome deeds, are established in the triple heaven. // 14.10 //

children.text: upapannāḥ pratibhaye narake bhṛśadāruṇe /
children.translated_text: 'Born in the dreadful, exceedingly terrible hell,

children.text: amī duḥkhairbahuvidhaiḥ pīḍyante kṛpaṇaṃ bata // Bc_14.11 //
children.translated_text: these ones are tormented by manifold sufferings — pitiable, alas! // 14.11 //

children.text: pāyyante kvathitaṃ kecidagnivarṇamayorasam /
children.translated_text: 'Some are made to drink boiling molten iron, fire-colored;

children.text: āropyante ruvānto 'nye niṣṭaptastambhamāyasam // Bc_14.12 //
children.translated_text: others, screaming, are mounted upon heated iron pillars. // 14.12 //

children.text: pacyante piṣṭavatkecidayaskumbhīṣvavāṅmukhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Some are cooked like flour, face-down in iron cauldrons;

children.text: dahyante karuṇaṃ keciddīpteṣvaṅgārarāśiṣu // Bc_14.13 //
children.translated_text: some are pitiably burned on heaps of blazing coals. // 14.13 //

children.text: kecittīkṣṇairayodaṃṣṭrairbhakṣyante dāruṇaiḥ śvabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Some are devoured by fierce dogs with sharp iron teeth;

children.text: keciddhṛṣṭairayastuṇḍairvāyasairāyasairiva // Bc_14.14 //
children.translated_text: some by bold iron-beaked crows — like iron [birds]. // 14.14 //

children.text: keciddāhapariśrāntāḥ śītacchāyābhikāṅikṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Some, exhausted by burning, longing for the shade of cool [trees],

children.text: asipattravanaṃ nīlaṃ baddhā iva viśantyamī // Bc_14.15 //
children.translated_text: enter the dark <s>Asipattravana</s> (sword-leaf forest) — bound, as it were. // 14.15 //

children.text: pāṭyante dāruvatkecitkuṭhārairbaddhabāhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Some, with arms bound, are split like wood with axes;

children.text: duḥkhe 'pi na vipacyante karmabhirdhāritāsavaḥ // Bc_14.16 //
children.translated_text: yet even in suffering they do not expire, their lives sustained by [the force of] their <s>karmas</s>. // 14.16 //

children.text: sukhaṃ syāditi yatkarma kṛtaṃ duḥkhanivṛttaye /
children.translated_text: 'Thinking "there will be happiness," the <s>karma</s> that was done for the removal of suffering —

children.text: phalaṃ tasyedamavaśairduḥkhamevopabhujyate // Bc_14.17 //
children.translated_text: its fruit is helplessly experienced [here] as nothing but suffering itself. // 14.17 //

children.text: sukhārthamaśubhaṃ kṛtvā ya ete bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These who, having performed unwholesome [deeds] for the sake of happiness, are exceedingly pained —

children.text: āsvādaḥ sa kimeteṣāṃ karoti sukhamaṇvapi // Bc_14.18 //
children.translated_text: does that [former] savor produce even the slightest happiness for them? // 14.18 //

children.text: hasadbhiryatkṛtaṃ karma kaluṣaṃ kaluṣātmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The impure deed that was done laughingly, by those of impure selves —

children.text: etatpariṇate kāle krośadbhiranubhūyate // Bc_14.19 //
children.translated_text: that, when its time ripens, is experienced while weeping. // 14.19 //

children.text: yadyevaṃ pāpakarmāṇaḥ paśyeyuḥ karmaṇāṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: 'If evil-doers could see the fruit of their deeds,

children.text: vameyuruṣṇaṃ rudhiraṃ marmasvabhihatā iva // Bc_14.20 //
children.translated_text: they would vomit hot blood, as if struck in their vital parts. // 14.20 //

children.text: ime 'nye karmabhiścitraiścittavispandasaṃbhavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These others, by various <s>karmas</s> born from the quivering of the mind,

children.text: tiryagyonau vicitrāyāḥmupapannāstapasvinaḥ // Bc_14.21 //
children.translated_text: have been born in the animal womb, of manifold variety — unfortunate ones! // 14.21 //

children.text: māṃsatvagbāladantārtha vairādapi madādapi /
children.translated_text: 'For the sake of flesh, skin, hair, or tusks, out of enmity, or out of madness,

children.text: hanyante kṛpaṇaṃ yatra bandhūnāṃ paśyatāmapi // Bc_14.22 //
children.translated_text: they are pitifully slain there, even before the eyes of their kinsmen. // 14.22 //

children.text: aśaknuvanto 'pyavaśāḥ kṣuttarṣaśramapīḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Though unable [to resist], helpless, tormented by hunger, thirst, and exhaustion,

children.text: go 'śvabhūtāśca vāhyante pratodakṣatamūrtayaḥ // Bc_14.23 //
children.translated_text: having become oxen and horses, they are driven along — their bodies scarred by goads. // 14.23 //

children.text: vāhyante gajabhūtāśca valīyāṃso 'pi durbalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having become elephants, though stronger, they are driven by the weak,

children.text: aṅkaśakliṣṭamūrdhānastāḍitāḥ pādapāṣṇibhiḥ // Bc_14.24 //
children.translated_text: with heads afflicted by the <s>aṅkuśa</s> (hook), struck by heels and feet. // 14.24 //

children.text: satsvapyanyeṣu duḥkheṣu duḥkhaṃ yatra viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even though other sufferings exist, the suffering here is especially [great],

children.text: parasparavirodhācca parādhīnatayaiva ca // Bc_14.25 //
children.translated_text: both from mutual hostility and from being subject to others' control. // 14.25 //

children.text: khasthāḥ khasthairhi bādhyante jalasthā jalacāribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those in the sky are harassed by those in the sky; those in the water, by water-dwellers;

children.text: sthalasthāḥ sthalasaṃsthaiśca prāpya caivetaretaraiḥ // Bc_14.26 //
children.translated_text: those on land, by those on land — and each is seized and [consumed] by the other. // 14.26 //

children.text: upapannāstathā ceme mātsaryākrāntacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And these others, born with minds seized by envy,

children.text: pitṛloke nirāloke kṛpaṇaṃ bhuñjate phalam // Bc_14.27 //
children.translated_text: experience their fruit pitifully in the lightless world of the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors). // 14.27 //

children.text: sūcīchidropamamukhāḥ parvatopamakukṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With mouths like the eye of a needle, and bellies like mountains,

children.text: kṣuttarṣajanitairduḥkhai pīḍyante duḥkhabhāginaḥ // Bc_14.28 //
children.translated_text: the sharers of suffering are tormented by pains born of hunger and thirst. // 14.28 //

children.text: āśayā samatikrāntā dhāryamāṇāḥ svakarmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Their expectations surpassed, sustained by their own <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: labhante na hyamī bhoktuṃ praviddhānyaśucīnyapi // Bc_14.29 //
children.translated_text: these ones cannot even eat things that have been cast away and are impure. // 14.29 //

children.text: puruṣo yadi jānīta mātsaryasyedṛśaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: 'If a person knew that such is the fruit of envy,

children.text: sarvathā śibivaddadyāccharīrāvayavānapi // Bc_14.30 //
children.translated_text: he would in all ways give even the parts of his body, like <s>Śibi</s>. // 14.30 //

children.text: ime 'nye narakaprakhye garbhasaṃjñe 'śucihrade /
children.translated_text: 'These others — beings born among humans — in an impure pool',

children.text: upapannā manuṣyeṣu duḥkhamarchanti jantavaḥ // Bc_14.31 //
children.translated_text: called the womb, resembling a hell, arrive at suffering. // 14.31 //
